# Historical Analysis: What 154 Years of Symmetry-Programme Physics Did Not Do, and What the McGucken Principle Does

> *"More intellectual curiosity, versatility and yen for physics than Elliot McGucken's I have never seen in any senior or graduate student... I gave him as an independent task to figure out the time factor in the standard Schwarzschild expression around a spherically-symmetric center of attraction... 'Can you, by poor-man's reasoning, derive what I never have, the time part?' He could and did, and wrote it all up in a beautifully clear account... But he revels in Shakespeare, too. Acting the part of Prospero in the Tempest."*
> --- John Archibald Wheeler, Princeton University, Recommendation for the author, 1990

The dual-channel derivation of all principal symmetries from dx₄/dt = ic raises an unavoidable historical question. The symbol x₄ = ict --- the integrated form of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic --- has been in the foundational literature of physics since Minkowski's 1908 Cologne lecture *Raum und Zeit*. Generations of physicists --- including Sommerfeld, Eddington, Pauli, Weyl, Dirac, Wheeler, and Feynman --- have manipulated x₄ = ict and the closely related dx₄² =  − c²dt² in their writing. None of them treated dx₄/dt = ic as the foundational dynamical postulate of physics. Why? And what specifically does the McGucken Principle do that none of these predecessors did?

This section provides the answer. The argument has two parts. First, we trace the lineage from Klein 1872 through the modern symmetry programme and identify, at each stage, the specific commitment that prevented physicists from reading x₄ = ict as a physical fact rather than a coordinate convention. Second, we state precisely what the McGucken Principle adds that none of these predecessors supplied. The novelty resides in a methodological transformation: the McGucken Principle is treated as a *physical, geometric, dynamical* statement about the world (x₄ is a real fourth coordinate that physically expands, with the factor i encoding perpendicularity and the rate fixed at c), and from this single statement the Lorentzian metric, Poincaré group, canonical commutation relation, Schrödinger equation, Maxwell theory, Yang-Mills theory, Einstein field equations, Second Law, and all principal symmetries of physics descend as theorems. The symbol x₄ = ict was visible in the literature since Minkowski 1908; what no predecessor in the 154-year arc did was treat it as the integrated form of a physical dynamical law. The McGucken Principle does precisely this.

## Twelve Features Distinguishing the McGucken Programme from the 154-Year Symmetry Arc

Before the detailed lineage analysis, we state in formal register the twelve most distinctive features of the McGucken programme --- features that distinguish it methodologically from the Klein--Einstein--Minkowski--Noether--Wigner--Cartan--Wheeler arc that precedes it. Each feature is a formal property of the construction articulated in §§4--17 of the present paper, anchored to the specific theorems, lemmas, and propositions that establish it. The features are stated in summary form here; the supporting proofs occupy the body of the paper.

**Feature 1 (Father-Symmetry priority: every named symmetry of physics, including Noether's theorem itself, descends from dx₄/dt = ic).** The standard foundations of physics treat the following as ten independent foundational commitments: (i) Lorentz invariance of the spacetime metric (Einstein 1905, Minkowski 1908); (ii) Poincaré covariance of the field equations (Poincaré 1905, Wigner 1939); (iii) the canonical commutation relation [q̂,p̂] = iℏ (Heisenberg 1925, Born--Jordan 1925, Dirac 1925); (iv) U(1) gauge invariance of electromagnetism (Weyl 1929); (v) unitary evolution of the quantum state (Dirac 1930, von Neumann 1932); (vi) the CPT theorem or its axiomatic predecessors (Lüders 1954, Pauli 1955, Jost 1957, Bargmann--Hall--Wightman 1958); (vii) diffeomorphism invariance of the gravitational action (Einstein 1916, Hilbert 1915); (viii) the variational principle for physical action (Hamilton 1834, Lagrange 1788; Noether 1918 establishing the symmetry-conservation theorem as standalone machinery for the variational framework); (ix) the Born rule for quantum probabilities (Born 1926); and (x) the separable-Hilbert-space arena of quantum mechanics (Dirac 1930, von Neumann 1932). The McGucken programme establishes the *Father-Symmetry priority*: the McGucken Symmetry dx₄/dt = ic is prior to each of these ten commitments, including Noether's theorem itself. [MG-FatherSymmetry, Theorem 32] states the priority explicitly: *"The McGucken Symmetry is prior to Noether symmetry. Noether's theorem and its conservation-law consequences are derived from dx₄/dt = ic rather than from independent symmetry postulates."* Theorem 30 of the present paper extends the claim to its full scope: *all three ingredients of Noether's theorem --- the Lagrangian, the symmetries, and the currents --- descend as theorems of dx₄/dt = ic*. The consolidation ratio is ten foundational postulates to one Father Symmetry, with each of the named symmetries (Lorentz, Poincaré, Noether, Wigner, U(1) gauge, non-Abelian gauge, quantum-unitary evolution, CPT, diffeomorphism, supersymmetry, string dualities) descending as a theorem rather than entering as an independent postulate of the variational, group-theoretic, or analytic framework. The compression is, to the author's knowledge, the most aggressive among the major foundational programmes of the past 154 years; the Father-Symmetry priority of the McGucken Principle over every named symmetry of physics is the content of the consolidation.

**Feature 2 (Forcing rather than postulation: the Disjunctive Forcing Theorem).** Every other foundational framework in the 154-year arc begins by *positing* its starting point: Einstein 1905's two postulates, the Wightman axioms of axiomatic QFT (Wightman 1956, Streater--Wightman 1964), the gauge-group selection SU(3)_(c) × SU(2)_(L) × U(1)_(Y) in the Standard Model (Glashow 1961, Weinberg 1967, Salam 1968), the worldsheet conformal invariance underlying perturbative string theory (Nambu 1970, Polyakov 1981), the path-integral measure in lattice QCD (Wilson 1974), and the Tomita--Takesaki modular structure of algebraic QFT (Haag--Kastler 1964, Bisognano--Wichmann 1975). The Disjunctive Forcing Theorem (§4.1, Theorem 21) instead proves that dx₄/dt = ic is the unique configuration of the four-manifold consistent with the joint empirical record of quantum mechanics and relativity. The proof is case-exhaustion: the principle is shown to follow from the conjunction of five independently-confirmed empirical strands --- Tsirelson saturation $|\langle\mathrm{CHSH}\rangle| = 2\sqrt{2}$ (Tsirelson 1980, BIG Bell Test 2018); rotational invariance of entanglement correlations (Aspect 1982, Hensen 2015, Giustina 2015, Shalm 2015); the absence of any entanglement-distance limit observed to 1, 400 km (Micius 2017, Yin 2017); the Lorentz invariance of c to one part in 10¹⁷ (Michelson--Morley 1887 through MICROSCOPE 2017); and Huygens self-replication of wavefronts (Huygens 1690, Kirchhoff 1882) --- exhausted along three orthogonal classification axes (geometric kinematic type, propagation rate, complex-versus-real signature) through five failure modes. The negation of each failure mode is empirically established to the precision indicated; their conjunction forces dx₄/dt = ic by classical disjunction-elimination. The principle proves itself from empirical data, rather than being assumed.

**Feature 3 (Dual-channel convergent overdetermination).** Each principal symmetry of physics is derived through two disjoint routes. *Algebraic Channel* is the algebraic-symmetry reading via Lie groups and Lie algebras, generators and operator algebras, Stone's theorem on one-parameter unitary groups (Stone 1932), Mackey induction from little-group representations (Mackey 1952), Bargmann--Hall--Wightman analytic continuation through the complex Lorentz group (Bargmann--Hall--Wightman 1957), Schur's lemma on irreducible representations (Schur 1905), and Noether's first and second theorems (Noether 1918). *Geometric Channel* is the geometric-propagation reading via the McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) at every event, iterated Huygens-type propagation along the active expansion dx₄ = ic dt (Huygens 1690), parallel transport on the McGucken-generated bundle structure, and the McGucken--Wick rotation τ = x₄/c (Wick 1954, McGucken 2026). The two channels share no intermediate machinery. Their convergence on the same canonical objects is demonstrated theorem by theorem: the canonical commutator [q̂,p̂] = iℏ from Stone's theorem (Algebraic Channel; §11, Theorem 42) and from iterated propagator composition (Geometric Channel); the Lorentzian interval ds² =  − c²dt² + dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² from the solution space of X^(T)η + ηX = 0 (Algebraic Channel; §5, Theorem 24) and from the null-cone structure of Σ⁺(p) (Geometric Channel; §5, Proposition 25); the Einstein equations G_(μν) = 8πGT_(μν)/c⁴ from Lovelock's 1971 uniqueness theorem applied to the McGucken-generated metric (Algebraic Channel; §13, Theorem 48) and from the variational principle on S_(EH)[g] with g generated by the McGucken Principle (Geometric Channel); the CPT operator Θ from Bargmann--Hall--Wightman complex-Lorentz analytic continuation (Algebraic Channel; §12, Theorem 45) and from geometric reflection of Σ⁺(p) (Geometric Channel). ## How dx₄/dt = ic Derives the Conservation Laws: Novelty and Channel Distribution

The content of the McGucken programme is the *Father-Symmetry priority*: the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is prior to every named symmetry of physics. The Father-Symmetry paper [MG-FatherSymmetry, Theorem 32] states it directly: *"The McGucken Symmetry is prior to Noether symmetry. Noether's theorem and its conservation-law consequences are derived from dx₄/dt = ic rather than from independent symmetry postulates."* Theorem 30 of the present paper extends the claim to its full scope: *all three ingredients of Noether's theorem --- the Lagrangian, the symmetries, and the currents --- descend as theorems of dx₄/dt = ic rather than as independent postulates*. The same priority structure applies to Lorentz invariance (§5, Theorem 24, descends from Lemma 1), Poincaré covariance (§6, Theorem 27, forced by Lemma 1 plus event homogeneity), Wigner classification (§8, Theorem 33, descends from the forced Poincaré group), U(1) gauge invariance (§9, Theorem 36, forced by the absence of preferred x₄-orientation phase), CPT (§12, Theorem 45, descends from analytic continuation of the forced complex Lorentz group), diffeomorphism invariance (§13, Theorem 48, descends from the forced metric structure plus Lovelock 1971), supersymmetry (§14, Theorem 51, conditional on Haag--Łopuszański--Sohnius hypotheses), and the eight forms of entropy (§4.2, Theorems 22a--22h, descend from the McGucken Sphere expansion).

This subsection addresses three specific questions about the source of the Father-Symmetry priority: (i) what features of dx₄/dt = ic make this priority possible; (ii) whether Algebraic Channel or Geometric Channel carries the more novel derivations; (iii) whether the McGucken programme derives some laws through the Algebraic Channel or the Geometric Channel routes that have no prior precedent in the standard literature. Each answer is anchored to specific theorems, lemmas, and propositions of the present paper, and to specific historical citations in the standard foundational literature.

### Question 1: What features of dx₄/dt = ic make the Father-Symmetry priority possible

Six features of the McGucken Principle, taken jointly, suffice for the derivation of every conservation law of physics as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic. Each feature is novel in the foundational literature.

**Feature N1 (Dynamical-law reading rather than static coordinate substitution).** Minkowski 1908's coordinate identity x₄ = ict is the integrated form of dx₄/dt = ic with the initial condition x₄(0) = 0. The static substitution renders the indefinite Lorentzian form  − c²dt² + dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² as the positive-definite form dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄² on ℝ⁴; it is algebraically equivalent to the (−,+,+,+) signature, and Minkowski 1908 treated it as a calculational device without physical content beyond the sign convention. The dynamical reading converts the substitution into an active substrate generator: x₄ is a real fourth direction undergoing physical expansion at rate ic at every spacetime event. The conservation-law apparatus of Noether's theorem requires inputs --- an action functional, a foliation by Cauchy hypersurfaces, an integration measure, a translation invariance, an orientation supplying the strict Second Law --- that the static substitution does not generate. The dynamical reading does generate them. The 154-year delay between Minkowski's 1908 introduction of the symbol x₄ = ict and the recognition of dx₄/dt = ic as a physical dynamical law (the present author's 1998--99 UNC Chapel Hill dissertation Appendix B; the five FQXi essay-contest papers 2008--2013; the present corpus 2026) is the delay between having the notation and having the law.

**Feature N2 (Lemma 1 generates the Lorentzian metric, supplying the variational background Noether's theorem requires).** The pulled-back form of Lemma 1 substitutes dx₄ = ic dt into the auxiliary Euclidean inner product g_(E) = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄² to produce η = diag(−,+,+,+) directly: the Frobenius-forced i² =  − 1 algebraically converts the dx₄² term to  − c²dt². The McGucken-generated metric η is therefore the structure that the action functional S[ϕ] = ∫_(M)ℒ(ϕ,∂ϕ) dvol_(η) integrates against, rather than a postulate of the variational framework. The volume form $d\mathrm{vol}_\eta = \sqrt{-g}\,d^4 x$, the index-raising operations η^(μν) and η_(μν), the d'Alembertian operator □ = η^(μν)∂_(μ)∂_(ν), and the integration-by-parts identity ∫_(M)(∂_(μ)A)B dvol_(η) =  − ∫_(M)A (∂_(μ)B) dvol_(η) (under support conditions) all inherit from Lemma 1. Standard derivations of Noether's theorem (Noether 1918, *Invariante Variationsprobleme*; modern formal treatments in Olver 1986, *Applications of Lie Groups to Differential Equations*; Saunders 1989, *The Geometry of Jet Bundles*) postulate the spacetime metric as an external input alongside the action functional. The McGucken programme derives the metric from dx₄/dt = ic via Lemma 1 and then builds the action on top of the derived metric.

**Feature N3 (Event homogeneity, Hypothesis A4, supplies the translation invariance generating the Poincaré group).** The principle dx₄/dt = ic holds at every event of spacetime with no preferred origin. Event homogeneity is part of the principle's content (the active expansion is identical at every event), rather than a separate postulate added to the principle. Event homogeneity forces [P^(μ),P^(ν)] = 0 as the algebraic statement of translation invariance, and produces the four translation generators P⁰, P¹, P², P³ as theorems (§6, Theorem 27). Noether's first theorem applied to these four translation generators yields energy conservation (from P⁰) and momentum conservation (from P¹, P², P³). **Feature N4 (The  + ic orientation, Hypothesis A5, supplies both the Cauchy foliation for Noether charges and the strict Second Law).** Noether's conserved charge Q_(X)(Σ) = ∫_(Σ)j_(X)^(μ)n_(μ) dΣ is defined as an integral over a Cauchy hypersurface Σ. The McGucken Principle's strict  + ic orientation supplies a canonical foliation: at each event p, the spacelike hypersurface Σ_(t(p)) is the spatial three-plane orthogonal (with respect to η) to the  + ic-oriented x₄-axis. By Hypothesis A6 (flatness), the global foliation {Σ_(t)}_(t ∈ ℝ) is well-defined; the Noether charge Q_(X)(Σ_(t)) is therefore independent of t. *The same  + ic orientation that supplies the Noether foliation supplies the strict-monotonic Second Law of thermodynamics through the Geometric Channel* (§4.2, Theorem 22). Loschmidt's 1876 reversibility objection (Loschmidt, *Über den Zustand des Wärmegleichgewichts eines Systems von Körpern mit Rücksicht auf die Schwerkraft*) --- that time-reversal-symmetric microscopic dynamics cannot generate a time-asymmetric macroscopic law --- is dissolved as a separation theorem: the Algebraic Channel's variational dynamics is time-reversal symmetric, so Noether's currents are time-reversal symmetric; the Geometric Channel's  + ic orientation is not time-reversal symmetric, so the Second Law is strict-monotonic. Both descend from the same equation dx₄/dt = ic. The 124-year-old reversibility objection becomes a theorem about the dual-channel structure of the McGucken Principle.

**Feature N5 (Frobenius forcing of i unifies the imaginary unit across Lie algebra brackets, canonical commutators, and unitary evolution).** The factor i appearing in (i) the Hermitian-generator convention of the Lorentz Lie algebra brackets [J^(μν),J^(ρσ)] = i(η^(μρ)J^(νσ)−η^(νρ)J^(μσ)+η^(νσ)J^(μρ)−η^(μσ)J^(νρ)); (ii) the canonical commutator [q̂,p̂] = iℏ that converts classical Noether charges into self-adjoint quantum operators; (iii) the Schrödinger evolution operator U(t) = e^(−iĤt/ℏ) under which probability is conserved; (iv) the path-integral weight e^(iS/ℏ) in the Feynman propagator; (v) the Dirac equation (iγ^(μ)∂_(μ)−m)ψ = 0 from which probability conservation as a continuity equation ∂_(μ)J^(μ) = 0 follows; and (vi) the Bargmann--Hall--Wightman forward-tube prescription ζ = ξ − iη for the CPT theorem is *the same i* --- the Frobenius-forced generator of complex structure on the orthogonal-to-spatial subspace of the McGucken manifold (§4.3, Theorem 23). Frobenius 1878 (*Über lineare Substitutionen und bilineare Formen*) classified finite-dimensional associative real division algebras as ℝ, ℂ, ℍ; among these, ℂ is the unique algebra in which a single one-parameter rotation subgroup with i² =  − 1 exists (ℝ admits no such subgroup; ℍ admits a two-sphere S² of such elements). **Feature N6 (The cogeneration cascade ℳ_(G) → 𝕄_(1, 3) → 𝒱 → ℋ generates the Hilbert-space arena on which Stone's theorem converts classical Noether charges into self-adjoint quantum operators).** Dirac 1930 (*The Principles of Quantum Mechanics*) and von Neumann 1932 (*Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik*) postulate the separable complex Hilbert space ℋ as the arena of quantum mechanics. The joint content of features N1 through N6 is the Father-Symmetry priority of the McGucken Principle: each of the three classical ingredients of Noether's theorem --- Lagrangian, symmetries, currents --- and each of the inputs to those ingredients --- the metric (via Lemma 1), the foliation (via  + ic orientation), the imaginary unit (via Frobenius forcing), the Hilbert space (via cogeneration cascade) --- descend from dx₄/dt = ic as theorems rather than entering as postulates of an external variational framework.

### Question 2: Are the novel derivations more in the Algebraic Channel or the Geometric Channel

The novel derivations are distributed across both channels, but the *role* each channel plays in establishing the Father-Symmetry priority is materially different.

**Algebraic Channel makes the Father-Symmetry priority visible algebraically.** Each algebraic step in deriving a conservation law requires a McGucken-generated input: (i) the metric solution space of X^(T)η + ηX = 0 yielding the Lorentz Lie algebra 𝔰𝔬(1,3) requires η from Lemma 1; (ii) the Hermitian-generator conventions in the Lie algebra brackets [J^(μν),J^(ρσ)] = i(η^(μρ)J^(νσ)−...) require the Frobenius-forced i from §4.3; (iii) the symplectic form Ω = ∫_(Σ)δp_(A) ∧ δϕ^(A) d³x on field-theoretic phase space requires the foliation by Σ from the  + ic orientation (A5); (iv) the Poisson bracket {Q_(X), Q_(Y)}_(PB) = Q_([X,Y]) requires the symplectic form just constructed; (v) the operator-algebraic conversion of classical charges into self-adjoint quantum operators via Stone's theorem requires the Hilbert space from the cogeneration cascade (Theorem 116). The Algebraic Channel machinery (Lie groups, Lie algebras, Stone's theorem 1932, Mackey induction 1952, Bargmann--Hall--Wightman analytic continuation 1957, Noether's first and second theorems 1918, Schur's lemma 1905) is standard 20th-century mathematical apparatus. What is novel in the Algebraic Channel is that *every input the standard machinery operates on* is now a McGucken-derived theorem rather than an external postulate.

**Geometric Channel makes the Father-Symmetry priority visible geometrically.** Each geometric step in deriving a conservation law is the McGucken Principle in its native form: (i) the active foliation by Cauchy hypersurfaces Σ_(t) *is* the active expansion at  + ic; (ii) the McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) *is* the geometric content of dx₄ = ic dt at each event; (iii) the McGucken--Wick rotation τ = x₄/c *is* the integrated form of the principle viewed as a parameter substitution; (iv) the iterated Huygens-type propagation *is* the dx₄/dt = ic active expansion seen as wavefront composition; (v) the eight forms of entropy *are* the same McGucken-Sphere expansion read at eight different scales of resolution. The Geometric Channel machinery (geometric flows, Cauchy foliations, Huygens propagation 1690, exterior calculus, Stokes's theorem, holographic-area arguments) is also standard mathematical apparatus. What is novel in the Geometric Channel is that *the geometric structures the machinery operates on* are produced by dx₄/dt = ic rather than postulated as Riemannian, pseudo-Riemannian, or Lorentzian inputs.

## The 154-Year Lineage and Where Each Stage Stopped Short

### Klein 1872: The Erlangen Programme as Mathematical Framework Without Physical Generator

In his 1872 *Vergleichende Betrachtungen über neuere geometrische Forschungen* , Felix Klein proposed that geometry is to be characterised by its transformation group and the invariants of that group. A geometry is, on this account, the pair (G,H) where G is a Lie group of transformations acting transitively on a homogeneous space X = G/H, with H the stabiliser of a base point. Euclidean geometry is (ISO(n),O(n)) on ℝ^(n); affine geometry is (GA(n),GL(n)) on ℝ^(n); projective geometry is (PGL(n+1),⋅) on ℝP^(n).

Klein's programme is the foundational rule for the symmetry approach to geometry: *specify the group, and the geometry follows*. It is a mathematical principle, not a physical one. Klein does not address which group is realised in Nature, or why. The programme is silent on the physical generator of the Lorentzian Kleinian structure that would, after 1905, be discovered to govern relativistic physics. What Klein supplied was the rule of correspondence between group and geometry; what he did not supply was the physical fact selecting one Kleinian pair from another.

### Einstein 1905, Minkowski 1908: The Lorentzian Geometry Without Its Physical Source

Einstein's 1905 derivation of special relativity proceeded from two postulates: the principle of relativity (the laws of physics take the same form in all inertial frames) and the invariance of the speed of light. From these postulates Einstein obtained the Lorentz transformations, time dilation, length contraction, and the equivalence of mass and energy. Einstein did not use a fourth dimension in his 1905 derivation; the framework was purely operational, expressed in terms of rods, clocks, and light signals.

In 1908, Hermann Minkowski supplied the geometric reformulation. In his Cologne lecture *Raum und Zeit*, Minkowski proposed that "henceforth space by itself, and time by itself, are doomed to fade away into mere shadows, and only a kind of union of the two will preserve an independent reality." The technical device was a four-dimensional space with coordinates (x₁,x₂,x₃,x₄) where x₄ = ict. With this substitution, the indefinite Lorentzian quadratic form

ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c²dt²

becomes the formally Euclidean four-form

dℓ² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄².

Minkowski's choice of x₄ = ict --- the integrated form of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic when read as a physical and geometric statement --- was used by Minkowski as a *calculational gauge*: it made the Lorentzian quadratic form look formally Euclidean, allowing the use of Euclidean techniques for Lorentzian calculations. Minkowski did not assert that x₄ is a physical coordinate, that it expands, that its expansion rate is c, or that the factor i has geometric meaning. The symbol x₄ = ict was a notational device.

This is the crucial misreading. Minkowski had in his hands the exact mathematical object --- the integrated form of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic --- whose physical content is that the fourth dimension expands as a spherically-symmetric wavefront at velocity c, but he treated it as a coordinate convention. The factor i was for him a sign-flipper for the metric, not a geometric encoder of perpendicularity. The rate of x₄-advance with respect to t, which is ic in Minkowski's own substitution, was not interpreted as a physical fact. There was no ẋ₄ = ic in Minkowski 1908 in any *dynamical* sense. The relation x₄ = ict was the static statement of a coordinate identification, not the time-derivative of a physical evolution.

By the 1920s and 1930s, even Minkowski's x₄ = ict notation was supplanted in much of the literature by the now-standard (t,x,y,z) with metric signature (−,+,+,+) or (+,−,−,−). The factor i was absorbed into the metric tensor. The fourth coordinate became simply t (with units chosen to absorb c), and Lorentzian structure was encoded entirely in the indefinite metric. The substrate dimension --- a real fourth coordinate x₄ along which physical evolution occurs --- disappeared from the formalism. What remained was an indefinite quadratic form on a four-manifold of coordinates (t,x,y,z).

### Weyl 1918: Gauge Invariance as Mathematical Generalisation Without Physical Substrate

Hermann Weyl's 1918 *Gravitation and Electricity* introduced the concept of gauge invariance, originally as a local rescaling of lengths in attempt to unify general relativity and electromagnetism. The proposal was rejected on physical grounds by Einstein (the resulting theory would produce position-dependent atomic spectra contrary to observation), but the mathematical concept was preserved and, after Weyl's 1929 work and the rise of quantum mechanics, became the basis of modern gauge theory.

Weyl's central contribution was the recognition that a phase factor e^(iα(x)) multiplying a complex wavefunction can be made local, and that local phase invariance forces the introduction of a connection A_(μ)(x) transforming as A_(μ) ↦ A_(μ) + ∂_(μ)α. This is the geometric basis of U(1) gauge theory, of Maxwell electromagnetism, and (by generalisation) of the non-abelian Yang-Mills theories of the Standard Model.

What Weyl did not do was identify the *physical source* of the factor i in the phase e^(iα). The factor i is the same factor that appears in the Schrödinger equation, in the canonical commutation relation, in the unitary evolution operator, and (per Minkowski's 1908 notation) in the relation x₄ = ict. It is the same algebraic object across all of these contexts. But Weyl treated the phase-factor i as a mathematical given; he did not ask why the wavefunction is complex-valued in the first place.

The McGucken answer is that the wavefunction is complex-valued because dx₄/dt = ic: the same i that encodes the perpendicularity of x₄ to the spatial three appears in the Schrödinger equation, in U(1) gauge transformations, in SU(N) generators, in the unitary group U(t) = e^(−iĤt/ℏ), and in the Wick rotation underlying the CPT theorem. Weyl had the phase factor; he did not have its source. The McGucken Principle supplies the source.

### Noether 1918: Conservation from Symmetry Without Physical Generator

Emmy Noether's 1918 *Invariante Variationsprobleme* proved that every continuous symmetry of a variational problem produces a conserved current. The theorem is a triumph of mathematical structure: it converts symmetry information into conservation information without any further physical input. From spacetime translations, Noether's theorem yields energy and momentum conservation; from rotations, angular-momentum conservation; from internal U(1), electric charge conservation.

Noether's theorem requires, as input, a Lagrangian and a continuous symmetry. It does not generate either of these from a deeper principle. The Lagrangian must be supplied; the symmetry must be supplied. The theorem then converts them into a conserved current. In the standard formulation, both the Lagrangian and the symmetry are postulated --- they are not theorems of a foundational physical principle.

The McGucken Principle changes this. The Lagrangian is fixed by the McGucken construction (cf. , ℒ_(McGucken) = ℒ_(kin) + ℒ_(Dirac) + ℒ_(YM) + ℒ_(EH)). The symmetries are theorems of dx₄/dt = ic (cf. Sections `<a href="#sec:lorentz" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:lorentz">`{=html}3`</a>`{=html}--`<a href="#sec:string" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:string">`{=html}13`</a>`{=html}). Noether's theorem then operates on inputs that are themselves theorems, not postulates. This shifts Noether's theorem from a free-standing mathematical principle to a derivable consequence of a deeper physical structure.

### Wigner 1939: Particle Classification Without Selection Principle

E. P. Wigner's 1939 *On Unitary Representations of the Inhomogeneous Lorentz Group* classified the unitary irreducible representations of the Poincaré group. The classification is by orbit of P^(μ) under the Lorentz subgroup: timelike (massive particles, m > 0), null (massless particles, m = 0), spacelike (tachyons, m² < 0), and zero (vacuum). Within each orbit type, the irreducible representations are labelled by the irreducible representations of the corresponding little group: SU(2) for massive, ISO(2) for massless, SO(2,1) for spacelike, trivial for zero. The labels are the Casimirs of the Poincaré algebra: P^(μ)P_(μ) =  − m²c² and W^(μ)W_(μ) where W is the Pauli-Lubanski pseudovector.

Wigner's classification is exhaustive: it gives all UIRs of $\widetilde{\mathrm{ISO}}(1,3)$. It does not, however, select among them. The classification produces tachyonic UIRs alongside massive and massless ones; the standard physics exclusion of tachyons is imposed by hand on stability and causality grounds, not derived from the Poincaré algebra itself.

The McGucken Principle supplies the selection. The temporal orientation  + ic of dx₄/dt = ic picks out the future-oriented half of the Lorentz group, eliminating tachyonic orbits from the physical spectrum (cf. Section `<a href="#sec:wigner" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:wigner">`{=html}6`</a>`{=html}). What was an external exclusion in the standard formulation becomes a theorem of the foundational principle in the McGucken formulation.

### Cartan and Ehresmann: Geometric Apparatus Without Physical Source

Élie Cartan's 1922--1925 method of moving frames and his theory of differential forms supplied the geometric language for general relativity and Yang-Mills theory. Charles Ehresmann's 1950 construction of principal bundles and Ehresmann connections supplied the modern mathematical setting for gauge theory: a principal G-bundle P → M with connection 1-form A and curvature 2-form F = dA + A ∧ A. These constructions are the geometric backbone of every modern presentation of gauge field theory.

The Cartan-Ehresmann apparatus is mathematically definitive. It does not, however, specify which bundles or which structure groups are realised in Nature. The choices of U(1) × SU(2) × SU(3) in the Standard Model, of the Lorentz frame bundle in general relativity, of the spin structure for fermions --- all of these are physical inputs that the apparatus organises but does not derive.

The McGucken Principle, by specifying the Kleinian pair (ISO(1,3),SO⁺(1,3)) and the complex structure of the wavefunction, supplies the missing physical inputs. The base manifold of the gauge bundles is the McGucken-generated Minkowski space; the structure group U(1) is the algebraic image of the McGucken-generated i in ψ; the Clifford-algebraic extensions to SU(2)_(L) and SU(3)_(c) are organised through the McGucken complexification of 𝔰𝔬(1,3) (cf. Section `<a href="#sec:lorentz" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:lorentz">`{=html}3`</a>`{=html}). The geometric apparatus is supplied by Cartan-Ehresmann; the physical content is supplied by the McGucken Principle.

### Wheeler's Geometrodynamic Programme: Geometry as Physics Without the Generator

John Archibald Wheeler's programme of geometrodynamics --- developed in his Princeton years from the 1950s through the 1980s --- pursued the thesis that "physics is geometry." In Wheeler's vision, particles, fields, and forces would all emerge from the geometry of spacetime. The programme included his proposal of the "it from bit" relation between information and physical reality, his development of the ADM formalism with Arnowitt and Deser, his work on quantum foam, and his sustained interest in the question "Why the quantum?"

Wheeler's programme is the closest predecessor to the McGucken Principle in spirit. Wheeler asked whether physics could be derived from a geometric foundation, and he sustained the question through six decades of work. Wheeler's commission to McGucken at Princeton --- to find the geometric source of the time part of the Schwarzschild metric --- is the direct historical antecedent of the McGucken Principle.

What Wheeler did not produce was the specific foundational equation. Wheeler had the methodological commitment (physics is geometry) and he had specific questions (the time part of Schwarzschild, the source of quantum behaviour). He did not find the single dynamical principle that simultaneously generates the Lorentzian metric, the unitary structure of quantum mechanics, the temporal orientation of thermodynamics, and the gauge structure of the Standard Model. The McGucken Principle is the answer to Wheeler's programme: dx₄/dt = ic is the geometric, dynamical principle from which the Schwarzschild time component, the Schrödinger phase, and the entropy arrow all descend as theorems.

### The Modern Programme: Postulating Symmetries Rather Than Deriving Them

The dominant approach in modern foundational physics --- visible in the Standard Model, in canonical quantum gravity, in string theory, and in the various extensions of the modern programme --- is to postulate symmetries and derive their consequences. The Standard Model postulates Lorentz invariance, gauge invariance under U(1) × SU(2) × SU(3), and the Higgs mechanism for symmetry breaking. General relativity postulates diffeomorphism invariance and the equivalence principle. String theory postulates worldsheet conformal invariance and supersymmetry. Loop quantum gravity postulates the existence of spin-network states. In each case, the symmetries are inputs; the dynamics are derived from them through Lagrangian or Hamiltonian constructions.

This methodological choice has been enormously productive. It has also been epistemically unsatisfying: at the end of every modern derivation lies a postulated symmetry. The 154-year arc from Klein 1872 to the present has built the mathematical apparatus for organising symmetries (Klein, Noether, Wigner, Cartan, Ehresmann) and for connecting them to topology (Chern, Atiyah-Singer); this apparatus organises symmetries after they have been postulated, rather than generating them from a physical principle.

The McGucken Principle is the proposed resolution. The principal symmetries of physics are theorems of a single physical, geometric, dynamical fact dx₄/dt = ic, rather than postulates. The fourth dimension expands at the velocity of light c in a spherically symmetric manner; the factor i encodes the perpendicularity of x₄ to the spatial three; the positive sign of  + ic encodes temporal orientation. From this one statement, the Lorentzian metric (Lemma `<a href="#lem:master" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:master">`{=html}1`</a>`{=html}), the Poincaré group (Theorem `<a href="#thm:poincare" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:poincare">`{=html}27`</a>`{=html}), Noether's theorem (Theorem `<a href="#thm:noether" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:noether">`{=html}30`</a>`{=html}), the Wigner classification (Theorem `<a href="#thm:wigner" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:wigner">`{=html}33`</a>`{=html}), U(1) gauge invariance (Theorem `<a href="#thm:u1" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:u1">`{=html}36`</a>`{=html}), non-abelian gauge invariance (Theorem `<a href="#thm:nonabel" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:nonabel">`{=html}39`</a>`{=html}), quantum-unitary symmetry (Theorem `<a href="#thm:unitary" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:unitary">`{=html}42`</a>`{=html}), CPT (Theorem `<a href="#thm:cpt" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:cpt">`{=html}45`</a>`{=html}), diffeomorphism invariance (Theorem `<a href="#thm:diff" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:diff">`{=html}48`</a>`{=html}), and the algebraic content of supersymmetry and the string dualities (Theorems `<a href="#thm:susy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:susy">`{=html}51`</a>`{=html} and `<a href="#thm:string" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:string">`{=html}55`</a>`{=html}) all descend as theorems.

### Georgi--Glashow 1974 -- Present: Grand Unification as Postulate Migration

The Grand Unified Theory programme, initiated by Georgi and Glashow 1974 (*Unity of All Elementary Particle Forces*, Phys. Rev. Lett. 32, 438--441), embeds the Standard Model gauge group G_(SM) = U(1)_(Y) × SU(2)_(L) × SU(3)_(c) in a larger simple Lie group G_(GUT), with the observed G_(SM) recovered as the residual after spontaneous symmetry breaking at an intermediate scale M_(GUT) ∼ 10^(15--16) GeV. The principal candidates are SU(5) (Georgi--Glashow 1974), SO(10) (Fritzsch--Minkowski 1975; Georgi 1975), E₆ (Gürsey--Ramond--Sikivie 1976), flipped SU(5), the Pati--Salam SU(4) × SU(2)_(L) × SU(2)_(R) scheme (Pati--Salam 1974, *Lepton Number as the Fourth Color*, Phys. Rev. D 10, 275--289), and their supersymmetric extensions (MSSM-GUTs, 1980s--present). The strategic motivation is that the three Standard Model gauge couplings, run via renormalization-group equations to high energy, approximately meet near 10^(16) GeV, suggesting that they descend from a unified coupling.

The principal empirical prediction is proton decay via GUT-scale X and Y gauge bosons that couple quarks to leptons, with lifetime approximately τ_p^(GUT) ∼ M_X^4 / (m_p^5 α_(GUT)^2). Non-supersymmetric minimal SU(5) gives τ_p ∼ 10^(29--31) years, excluded by Super-Kamiokande which sets τ_p/B(p → e⁺π⁰) > 2.4 × 10^(34) years at 90% CL (Super-Kamiokande Collaboration 2020, Phys. Rev. D 102, 112011). Minimal supersymmetric SU(5) gives τ_p ∼ 10^(32--34) years and is in significant tension with current bounds; SO(10) and flipped SU(5) remain viable but increasingly constrained.

The GUT programme's stopping-short, from the standpoint of the McGucken programme, is that it does not derive the gauge group from a deeper principle. It postulates a larger gauge group as primitive and breaks it down to G_(SM); the question "why this group?" is migrated up one level rather than answered. After fifty-two years, no GUT has uniquely emerged as compelling, and no principle has been supplied that selects among SU(5), SO(10), E₆, E₇, E₈, Pati--Salam, or their supersymmetric extensions. The empirical evidence (proton stability) is increasingly hostile to the programme's central prediction.

The McGucken framework's response to the GUT programme is developed at full rigour in the companion paper [MG-SMGauge2026], which establishes Theorem 303 (the No-GUT Theorem): within the McGucken framework the internal algebra 𝒜_F = ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M_3(ℂ) is the maximal algebra realisable from the substrate-scale features of dx₄/dt = ic; no fourth summand is available; therefore G_(SM) does not embed in any larger simple Lie group within the framework, and no GUT scenario is available. The empirical consequence is the sharp prediction τ_p = ∞ (no proton decay), distinguishing the McGucken framework from every GUT scenario. See [MG-SMGauge2026] Theorem 303 (No-GUT Theorem), the No-Proton-Decay Prediction section, and Master Comparison Tables A, B, and C for the full framework-by-framework analysis across GUTs, Connes--Chamseddine noncommutative geometry, string theory, Pati--Salam, and the McGucken framework.

### Polyakov 1974 and the Modern Conformal Bootstrap: Symmetry as Consistency Condition

The bootstrap programme, initiated by Ferrara, Gatto, and Grillo 1973 (*Conformal Algebra in Space-Time and Operator Product Expansion*, Springer Tracts in Modern Physics 67) and Polyakov 1974 (*Nonhamiltonian Approach to Conformal Quantum Field Theory*, Sov. Phys. JETP 39, 10--18), and revived in modern form by Rattazzi, Rychkov, Tonni, and Vichi 2008 (*Bounding Scalar Operator Dimensions in 4D CFT*, JHEP 12, 031), proceeds by imposing conformal symmetry, unitarity, and crossing symmetry as consistency conditions on correlation functions and deriving the spectrum of scaling dimensions of local operators from these conditions. No Lagrangian is postulated. The methodological content: symmetry is used as an algebraic constraint whose consistency-closure with unitarity and crossing determines the operator spectrum, rather than to generate a Lagrangian dynamics from which the spectrum then follows.

The modern conformal-bootstrap literature has produced record-precision results on the three-dimensional Ising critical point (Kos, Poland, and Simmons-Duffin 2014, JHEP 06, 091; 2016, JHEP 08, 036, giving critical exponents Δ_σ = 0.5181489(10), Δ_ε = 1.412625(10) at the current best precision), on O(N) models, on the three-dimensional 𝒩=2 superconformal fixed point, on 4d 𝒩=4 super Yang--Mills, and on higher-dimensional conformal field theories. The achievements demonstrate that conformal symmetry together with unitarity and crossing determines, at critical points, quantities previously accessible only through perturbative expansion, Monte Carlo simulation, or renormalization-group flow.

The bootstrap's stopping-short, from the standpoint of the McGucken programme, has two parts. First, the bootstrap takes conformal symmetry as its starting input rather than deriving it. The conformal group SO(d,2) (in d spacetime dimensions), the operator product expansion, and the Ward identities enforcing conformal covariance are all assumed; no physical principle is supplied that generates them. Second, the bootstrap operates in the fixed-point limit where a mass scale drops out; the physical mass gap of the underlying theory (the deviation from the conformal fixed point) is what the bootstrap does not address.

The McGucken framework's engagement with the bootstrap programme is developed at full rigour in the companion paper [MG-QFT2026] via two theorems.

First, the bootstrap-as-QFT-presentation status is a theorem. The Maturity-Test Passage Theorem ([MG-QFT2026], §4.3) states: every presentation of QFT --- Lagrangian, Hamiltonian, Wightman-axiomatic, Haag-Kastler algebraic, lattice, bootstrap, holomorphy, scattering-amplitudes --- factors through a specific extraction operation on the substrate field object φ̂ on the hybrid measure ℝ³ × ℓ_P·ℤ. Bootstrap is one of the eight standard presentations that factors through the substrate; the bootstrap's assumed conformal symmetry, unitarity, and crossing symmetry are the algebraic content surviving when the extraction operation is applied to substrate correlators at a conformal fixed point.

Second, the algebraic characterization of exact bootstrap solvability is a theorem. Theorem S2 of [MG-QFT2026] §5.2 states: *a QFT admits exact solution by bootstrap, holomorphy, integrability, or supersymmetric localization if and only if the Algebraic Channel symmetry algebra acts transitively on the substrate's configuration space modulo gauge equivalence.* The empirical successes of the modern conformal-bootstrap programme (the 3d Ising fixed point, O(N) models, the 3d 𝒩=2 superconformal fixed point, 4d 𝒩=4 super Yang--Mills) fall on the transitivity-satisfied side of the biconditional; theories at generic couplings away from fixed points, and theories with insufficient symmetry, fall on the transitivity-failed side. Verification of the transitivity condition for any specific case is a separate calculation not carried out in the present corpus.

Two matters remain open. Whether the full conformal group SU(2,2) ≅ Spin(4,2) descends as an additional theorem of dx₄/dt = ic beyond the Poincaré subgroup established by Theorem 27 is not addressed in the present corpus and is flagged as a research item. The massless sector on the McGucken background carries Sphere-tangent share v_{x₄} = 0 on null worldlines (Appendix A, reading (R2)); whether the associated massless conformal enhancement is a substrate theorem or an emergent large-scale symmetry is likewise open.

### Wick 1954 -- Present: The Euclidean-Rotation Programme and the Missing Coordinate Interpretation

The Wick-rotation programme originates with Wick 1954 (*Properties of Bethe-Salpeter Wave Functions*, Phys. Rev. 96, 1124--1134), which introduced the "rotation of the integration path in the complex plane of the [energy] variable" as a computational technique for continuing bound-state Bethe-Salpeter wavefunctions to complex relative-time values. The substitution t → −iτ carries the Minkowski metric with signature (−, +, +, +) into the Euclidean metric with signature (+, +, +, +), the oscillatory factor e^(iS/ℏ) into the real-positive weight e^(−S_E/ℏ), and the unitary group U(t) = e^(−iĤt/ℏ) into the contractive semigroup T(τ) = e^(−Ĥτ/ℏ) for Ĥ ≥ 0. The Wick-τ here is Wick's Euclidean-time parameter, distinct from the proper time τ of Appendix A reading (R3); both symbols use τ by convention and their identity is fixed by context.

The programme received its axiomatic development in Osterwalder and Schrader 1973 (*Axioms for Euclidean Green's Functions*, Comm. Math. Phys. 31, 83--112) and 1975 (Comm. Math. Phys. 42, 281--305), which established the reconstruction theorem: the Wightman axioms W0--W7 governing correlation functions on Minkowski spacetime and the Euclidean-Green's-function axioms governing Schwinger functions on Euclidean spacetime are equivalent theories, with the passage between them mediated by the OS reflection-positivity condition. Reflection positivity is what allows the Euclidean semigroup T(τ) to be inverted back to the unitary group U(t) on the physical Hilbert space; without it the analytic continuation fails.

The subsequent development produced seventy years of empirical success across constructive quantum field theory (Glimm and Jaffe 1987, *Quantum Physics: A Functional Integral Point of View*, Springer 2nd ed.), Euclidean lattice QCD (Wilson 1974; Kogut and Susskind 1975 and successors), imaginary-time thermal field theory (Matsubara 1955, Kubo 1957, Martin and Schwinger 1959), and Feynman-Kac path integrals across every scale of physically realistic field theory. Every standard treatment (Peskin-Schroeder 1995, Weinberg 1995, Srednicki 2007, Glimm-Jaffe 1987) presents Wick rotation as a formal analytic-continuation device justified by holomorphicity theorems about the behaviour of correlation functions in the complex time plane.

The programme's stopping-short is that the physical meaning of τ has remained absent from the standard treatment. Visser 2017 (*How to Wick rotate generic curved spacetime*, arXiv:1702.05572 [gr-qc]; originally 1991 Gravity Research Foundation essay) makes the puzzle explicit for the curved-spacetime case: *"After Wick rotating from Minkowski space to Euclidean space these causality constraints survive in a modified form as 'Osterwalder-Schrader positivity' (OS positivity) of the Euclidean version of the field theory. On the other hand, in the usual formulation of the transition from Lorentzian signature gravity to Euclidean signature quantum gravity the effects of the causal structure of the Lorentzian signature theory seem to disappear completely as no analogue of OS positivity is manifest. This circumstance is profoundly disturbing, and suggests that something crucial is missing in the naive analysis."* Kontsevich and Segal 2021 (*Wick Rotation and the Positivity of Energy in Quantum Field Theory*, Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. 72, 673--699, arXiv:2105.10161 [hep-th]) rigorously extended the connection between Wick rotation and Hamiltonian positivity to a complex-metric axiom system in which ordinary Riemannian metrics are contained in the allowable domain and Lorentzian metrics lie on its boundary. Woit 2023 (*Spacetime is Right-handed*, arXiv:2311.00608 [hep-th]) formulated an asymmetric Wick rotation: *"We describe the relation between vectors and spinors in complex spacetime in an unconventional chirally asymmetric manner, using purely right-handed spinors, with Minkowski spacetime getting Wick rotated to a four-dimensional Euclidean spacetime with a distinguished direction."*

Across these seven decades the programme has produced correct physical predictions without answering three specific questions: (W1) what is the coordinate τ physically; (W2) why does the substitution work --- why should rotating into a mathematical direction in the complex plane produce correct answers about real physical processes; (W3) why is the specific rotation angle π/2 the one that produces the convergent Euclidean theory.

The McGucken framework supplies the coordinate reading. The companion paper [MG-QFT2026] §14.18, Theorem 14.18.1 states: under the McGucken Principle in integrated form x₄ = ict, define the Euclidean-time coordinate

τ ≡ x₄/c   (Wick-τ, distinct from proper time of Appendix A (R3)).   (W1′)

Then the substitution t → −iτ is equivalent to the coordinate change τ = it, and Wick rotation is the operational realisation of the coordinate reparametrisation from the Algebraic Channel real-time t to the Geometric Channel's fourth coordinate x₄/c. The seventy-year empirical success of Wick rotation across physically realistic QFTs becomes direct empirical evidence for x₄ = ict as the correct substrate coordinate identification.

Theorem 14.19.1 of [MG-QFT2026] establishes the Wick response of the McGucken Principle itself: under t → −iτ, the McGucken Principle in Minkowski parametrisation dx₄/dt = ic transforms to

dx₄/dτ = c   (real rate in real Wick-τ)   (W2′)

by dx₄ = ic dt = ic · (−i dτ) = c dτ. The imaginary factor i in the Minkowski-parametrised rate ic is absorbed by the imaginary factor −i in the Wick substitution t → −iτ, leaving a real Euclidean expansion rate c. The physical content of the McGucken Principle --- expansion of the fourth coordinate at rate c from every event --- is preserved through Wick rotation; the parametrisation of the rate changes from imaginary (in real time t) to real (in real Wick-τ), which addresses question (W2) at the substrate level.

The Lorentzian light-cone under the same Wick rotation collapses to a point: the null-vector equation η(v, v) = 0 with signature (−, +, +, +) becomes δ(v, v) = v₀² + v₁² + v₂² + v₃² = 0 with signature (+, +, +, +), whose only solution by positive-definiteness of δ is v = 0. The Sphere (upstream substrate primitive) is Wick-covariant; the light cone (downstream coordinate shadow of the Minkowski-signature metric) is Wick-non-invariant. The Visser puzzle --- *"the effects of the causal structure of the Lorentzian signature theory seem to disappear completely"* --- receives a specific derivational reading: the light cone vanishes under Wick because it is coordinate bookkeeping, and the substrate physics (Sphere expansion at rate c) persists because it is the physical primitive.

The specific McGucken framing --- Wick rotation as substrate-coordinate reparametrisation τ = x₄/c, with the Sphere as the Wick-covariant upstream primitive and the light cone as the Wick-non-invariant downstream coordinate shadow --- is not found in Visser, Kontsevich-Segal, or Woit. Visser identifies the destruction of causal structure under Wick as a defect to be repaired by a complex metric deformation of the spacetime; Kontsevich-Segal complexify the metric while preserving the Riemannian → Lorentzian boundary relation; Woit identifies the chirality asymmetry as a signature motivating a right-handed spacetime programme. The McGucken framework reads the asymmetry as a derivational signature of substrate primacy, with the coordinate identification τ = x₄/c supplying the physical interpretation of the parameter τ that the seventy-year programme has lacked.


## How the Standard Textbook Literature Organizes the Material

The graduate textbook literature on group theory and symmetries in physics organises its material by one of two principles: mathematical structure first, or physical principle first. The two organisations produce distinct pedagogical arcs.

The mathematical-structure-first tradition proceeds in a canonical order: finite groups and their representations; Lie groups and Lie algebras via the exponential map; Cartan's classification of simple Lie algebras (the four infinite families A_n, B_n, C_n, D_n and the five exceptional algebras G₂, F₄, E₆, E₇, E₈); root systems, weights, and highest-weight representations; the specific groups relevant to physics (rotation, Lorentz, Poincaré, gauge groups); and applications. Wu-Ki Tung 1985, *Group Theory in Physics* (World Scientific) is the canonical instance: eleven chapters marching from basic group theory (Ch. 2) through group representations (Ch. 3), finite groups (Ch. 4--6), Lie groups and rotations (Ch. 7--8), the Lorentz and Poincaré groups (Ch. 10), tensor operators and the Wigner--Eckart theorem (Ch. 11), and closing with the Wigner classification of Poincaré representations. Howard Georgi 1999, *Lie Algebras in Particle Physics* (Perseus, 2nd ed.) is organised around the Cartan classification with grand unification as the payoff: SU(2), tensor methods, roots and weights, the Cartan matrix, SU(3) and the Eightfold Way, then SU(5) grand unification. Fulton and Harris 1991, *Representation Theory: A First Course* (Springer) is the mathematician's textbook, systematically organised around the Cartan classification and the Weyl character formula. Anthony Zee 2016, *Group Theory in a Nutshell for Physicists* (Princeton) arcs from finite groups through Lie algebras to gauge theory and grand unification, with dedicated chapters on the expanding universe and SO(10) GUTs.

The application-focused variants of the mathematical-structure-first tradition include Hamermesh 1962, *Group Theory and Its Application to Physical Problems* (Addison-Wesley; Dover reprint), organised around molecular vibrations, crystallography, and atomic spectra; Gilmore 1974, *Lie Groups, Lie Algebras and Some of Their Applications* (Wiley; Dover 2005); Cornwell 1984--89, *Group Theory in Physics* (Academic Press, three volumes); and Ludwig and Falter 1996, *Symmetries in Physics: Group Theory Applied to Physical Problems* (Springer 2nd ed.). These are organised by mathematical structure with physics applications following in later chapters.

The physical-principle-first tradition is exemplified by a single textbook: Weinberg 1995, *The Quantum Theory of Fields, Volume I: Foundations* (Cambridge). Weinberg's Chapters 2--5 are the closest existing textbook to the McGucken derivational spirit. The order there is: Chapter 2 Relativistic Quantum Mechanics (with Wigner's theorem on symmetry realisations, quantum Lorentz transformations, the Poincaré algebra, one-particle states derived through Wigner's little-group method, space inversion and time reversal, projective representations); Chapter 3 Scattering Theory (symmetries of the S-matrix as constraints on rates and cross-sections); Chapter 4 The Cluster Decomposition Principle; Chapter 5 Quantum Fields and Antiparticles (fields as covariant assemblies of the Wigner one-particle states). The methodological arc: relativity plus quantum mechanics plus cluster decomposition force quantum field theory, with symmetry as the derivation engine and the Poincaré group as the algebraic input whose irreducible unitary representations classify particles. Weinberg's Chapters 2--5 assume the Poincaré group as input; they do not derive it from a deeper physical principle. The McGucken programme extends this arc one level further back: the Poincaré group descends as Theorem 27 of dx₄/dt = ic, so the input at the start of Weinberg's Chapter 2 becomes a theorem of the McGucken Principle.

The philosophy-of-physics literature on symmetries is anchored by Brading and Castellani (editors) 2003, *Symmetries in Physics: Philosophical Reflections* (Cambridge), which surveys the significance of gauge symmetry, particle identity, parity violation, spontaneous symmetry breaking, and the empirical status of symmetry principles across contributions by Wigner, Weyl, van Fraassen, Earman, Redhead, Butterfield, and others. The Brading--Castellani volume is the philosophical companion to the technical textbook literature; it addresses the interpretive questions the technical texts organise around but do not resolve.

The pattern across the technical textbooks: they organise by mathematical structure (finite groups → Lie groups → Lie algebras → representations → specific groups: SU(N), SO(N), Poincaré, etc.) with applications following, rather than by physical principle deriving the symmetries. Weinberg Chapters 2--5 is the closest textbook to the second style: the material begins from relativity plus quantum mechanics as physical principles and lets the classification of particles follow. The McGucken programme pushes the derivation one level further back: the metric, the Poincaré group, the canonical commutator, the Schrödinger equation, and the principal symmetries all descend as theorems from dx₄/dt = ic. A textbook organised around the McGucken Principle would begin with the one physical fact of x₄ expanding at ic from every event, and derive the Lorentzian signature, the Poincaré group, the Wigner classification, gauge invariance, quantum-unitary evolution, CPT, diffeomorphism invariance, and the algebraic content of supersymmetry as the successive theorems of Sections 5 through 12 of the present paper.


## The Diagnosis: Five Commitments That Prevented the 154-Year Reading

Why did 154 years of mathematically gifted physicists, working with x₄ = ict explicitly in the literature, fail to identify dx₄/dt = ic as the foundational physical principle? The answer is that five specific commitments of twentieth-century physics conspired to prevent the reading.

### Commitment 1: x₄ = ict Read as Notation, Not as Physics

Minkowski 1908 introduced x₄ = ict --- the integrated form of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic --- explicitly as a coordinate device to make the Lorentzian quadratic form look formally Euclidean. The original reading was instrumentalist: a formal trick to enable calculation. When subsequent generations of physicists encountered x₄ = ict, they inherited the instrumentalist interpretation. The factor i was a sign-flipper; the relation x₄ = ict was a coordinate identification. Neither was treated as a physical fact about the world.

The McGucken correction: x₄ is a physical fourth coordinate that exists alongside the spatial three. The relation x₄ = ict is the time-integrated form of the dynamical statement dx₄/dt = ic. The factor i functions as the algebraic marker of the geometric perpendicularity of x₄ to the spatial three, not as a sign-flipper. The rate c is the physical speed of x₄-advance from every event, not a calibration.

### Commitment 2: Background-Independence Doctrine Removed the Substrate

The development of general relativity through the 1910s and the modern programme through the present has emphasised background-independence: the metric is itself dynamical, and there is no fixed background spacetime against which physics occurs. This is a methodological commitment that is correct for the gravitational sector. However, the background-independence doctrine has been applied uniformly across all of physics, including the foundational substrate, in a way that has obscured the existence of a foundational fourth dimension.

The McGucken Principle does not contradict background-independence in the gravitational sector. The Einstein field equations are theorems of dx₄/dt = ic extended to curved spacetime (cf. Section `<a href="#sec:diff" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:diff">`{=html}11`</a>`{=html}). What the McGucken Principle adds is that the underlying substrate is itself dynamical: x₄ expands at rate c from every event, and the spherical expansion of x₄ is the geometric source of the null cone, the McGucken Sphere, and the foundational atom of spacetime. The dynamical substrate is compatible with background-independence at the level of the metric, but it provides the physical generator that pure background-independence does not.

### Commitment 3: The Factor i Treated as Calculational, Not Geometric

The factor i in quantum mechanics is, in the standard formulation, treated as a calculational device whose ultimate physical meaning is left obscure. The Schrödinger equation contains an i; the canonical commutation relation contains an i; the unitary evolution operator contains an i. In the standard pedagogy, students are taught to use these i's correctly without being told why they are there. The factor i is, in effect, a quantum-mechanical mystery: physicists know how to compute with it, but they do not know what it is.

The McGucken correction: the factor i in all of these contexts is the *same factor*, and it is the algebraic marker of the perpendicularity of x₄ to the spatial three. The i in the Schrödinger equation, the i in [q,p] = iℏ, the i in U(t) = e^(−iĤt/ℏ), the i in U(1) gauge transformations, the i in the Wick rotation for CPT, the i in the complexification of 𝔰𝔬(1,3), and the i in dx₄/dt = ic are all the same i. They are unified by their common physical origin: the geometric perpendicularity of the fourth dimension to the spatial three.

### Commitment 4: Time Treated as Parameter, Not as Geometric Coordinate

In the operational tradition descending from Einstein 1905 and reinforced through the canonical formulation of quantum mechanics, time is treated as a parameter --- an external label on which physics depends but which is not itself a physical degree of freedom. The wavefunction ψ(x,t) depends on t; observables are operators on the space of ψ's; t is the parameter of the unitary group U(t). The four-dimensional geometric reading that Minkowski 1908 proposed --- in which t is a coordinate alongside the spatial three --- was preserved in special and general relativity but partially erased in non-relativistic quantum mechanics. Modern textbooks oscillate between the two readings without a consistent foundational stance.

The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic resolves this. The parameter t is the physical parameter of x₄-evolution; the coordinate x₄ = ict, descending from the McGucken Principle by integration, is the geometric coordinate of the fourth dimension. The two are related by the dynamical statement dx₄/dt = ic. There is no conflict between the operational and the geometric readings: t is the parameter of evolution along x₄, and x₄ is the coordinate of the substrate along which evolution occurs.

### Commitment 5: Symmetry as Postulate Rather Than as Theorem

The dominant methodological commitment of twentieth-century theoretical physics has been to postulate symmetries and derive their consequences. Lorentz invariance is postulated; gauge invariance is postulated; diffeomorphism invariance is postulated; supersymmetry is postulated. The Lagrangian is then constructed to be invariant under the postulated symmetries, and the dynamics are derived from the Lagrangian via the principle of least action. This is the modern programme.

The McGucken Principle inverts the methodology. The symmetries are theorems of a single foundational physical fact rather than postulates. The Lagrangian is constructed to be the simplest action compatible with dx₄/dt = ic rather than constructed to be invariant under postulated symmetries. The dynamics are derived from the foundational physical postulate of x₄-expansion rather than from a postulated symmetric Lagrangian, with the symmetries and the Lagrangian both descending as theorems.

## The McGucken Methodological Transformation

The five commitments of Section `<a href="#sec:diagnosis" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:diagnosis">`{=html}2.2`</a>`{=html} together explain why 154 years of physicists, having x₄ = ict explicitly in their notation, did not arrive at dx₄/dt = ic as the foundational principle. The McGucken Principle inverts each of these commitments. The methodological transformation can be stated precisely.

:::
**Thesis 22** (The McGucken Methodological Transformation). *The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic transforms the foundational structure of physics by simultaneously:*

1. *promoting x₄ = ict from coordinate convention to physical and geometric statement, by recognizing it as the integrated form of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic;*

2. *identifying the physical substrate x₄ as a fourth coordinate that expands at rate c from every event;*

3. *identifying the factor i as the unified algebraic marker of x₄-perpendicularity, appearing identically in dx₄/dt = ic, in [q,p] = iℏ, in the Schrödinger equation, in U(t) = e^(−iĤt/ℏ), in U(1) and non-abelian gauge transformations, in the Wick rotation for CPT, and in the complexification of 𝔰𝔬(1,3);*

4. *identifying the rate c as the physical speed of x₄-advance, recovering the invariant speed of relativity;*

5. *identifying the positive sign  + ic as the source of temporal orientation, the thermodynamic arrow, and the breaking of time-reversal at the foundational level;*

6. *generating the principal symmetries of physics --- Lorentz, Poincaré, Noether, Wigner, U(1) gauge, non-abelian gauge, quantum-unitary, CPT, diffeomorphism, supersymmetry, and the standard string dualities --- as theorems through the dual-channel architecture of the Algebraic Channel (algebraic-symmetry) and the Geometric Channel (geometric-propagation);*

7. *closing Klein's 1872 Erlangen Programme by supplying the physical generator of the Lorentzian Kleinian pair (ISO(1,3),SO⁺(1,3)).*

The thesis concerns the framework's overall shape, not exegesis of particular past writers. The claim is not that no individual physicist has ever proposed any of (1)--(7); various items have been proposed in isolated forms (Wheeler's geometrodynamics is the closest predecessor to (1)--(2); Penrose's spinor approach captures some of (3)). What no predecessor has done is the simultaneous transformation: a single physical postulate that performs all seven items at once, with the principal symmetries of physics descending as theorems.
