The novelty of the McGucken Principle, relative to its predecessors, can be stated in five precise items.

### Novelty 1: A Single Physical Equation as Foundational Postulate

No predecessor framework offers a single physical equation as the foundational postulate from which Lorentz, Poincaré, gauge, quantum-unitary, CPT, and diffeomorphism invariance all descend as theorems. Einstein 1905 used two postulates (principle of relativity, invariance of c); the canonical commutation relation is its own independent postulate; gauge invariance is postulated separately for each gauge group; diffeomorphism invariance is postulated separately for general relativity. The McGucken Principle is one equation that simultaneously generates all of these.

### Novelty 2: The Factor i Unified Across Contexts

No predecessor framework identifies the factor i across quantum mechanics, gauge theory, the Wick rotation, and the Minkowski x₄ = ict notation --- the integrated form of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic --- as the *same* algebraic object with a *single* physical origin. In the standard formulation, the i in [q,p] = iℏ is unrelated to the i in x₄ = ict, and both are unrelated to the i in U(1) phase factors. The McGucken Principle identifies all of these as images of one i: the algebraic marker of x₄-perpendicularity.

### Novelty 3: Temporal Orientation as Theorem, Not Postulate

No predecessor framework derives the temporal orientation (the arrow of time, the Second Law of Thermodynamics, the breaking of time-reversal at the foundational level) from a foundational physical principle. The standard formulation introduces these features either by hand (the Past Hypothesis, low-entropy boundary conditions) or as emergent statistical phenomena (Boltzmann's H-theorem, decoherence). The McGucken Principle derives them as theorems of the positive sign of  + ic in dx₄/dt = ic.

### Novelty 4: The Dual-Algebraic Channelrchitecture as Methodological Unification

No predecessor framework systematically presents the principal symmetries of physics as theorems through two simultaneous channels --- the Algebraic Channel (algebraic-symmetry: generators, commutators, representations) and the Geometric Channel (geometric-propagation: manifolds, bundles, wavefronts) --- joined by a shared invariant. The Klein 1872 programme establishes the correspondence between group and geometry at a general mathematical level; the McGucken Principle realises the correspondence at every level of the symmetry hierarchy through the dual-channel architecture (cf. Sections `<a href="#sec:lorentz" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:lorentz">`{=html}3`</a>`{=html}--`<a href="#sec:string" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:string">`{=html}13`</a>`{=html}).

### Novelty 5: The Closure of Klein 1872 with a Physical Generator

No predecessor framework closes Klein's 1872 Erlangen Programme by supplying the physical generator of the Lorentzian Kleinian pair. Klein's programme establishes the rule (geometry is determined by transformation group and invariants); Minkowski 1908 supplies the relevant Kleinian pair (ISO(1,3),SO⁺(1,3)) as a mathematical object; the 154 years from 1908 to the present elaborated the apparatus (Noether 1918, Wigner 1939, Cartan, Ehresmann, Chern, Atiyah-Singer) without supplying the physical generator. The McGucken Principle is the missing physical generator: dx₄/dt = ic is the physical fact that selects (ISO(1,3),SO⁺(1,3)) as the Kleinian pair of relativistic physics.

## The Method as the Novelty

The deepest novelty of the McGucken Principle is methodological rather than calculational. The principal symmetries derived in this paper are the same symmetries that have been postulated and used by twentieth-century physics for a century --- the McGucken Principle does not produce a numerical prediction unavailable to its predecessors. The methodological novelty is that these symmetries are now *theorems* of a foundational physical postulate rather than postulates in their own right.

This methodological transformation has three corollary consequences.

#### First, the explanatory burden shifts.

In the standard formulation, the explanatory burden lies on the symmetries: one must explain why Lorentz invariance holds, why gauge invariance holds, why CPT holds. In the McGucken formulation, the explanatory burden lies on the foundational postulate: one must explain why dx₄/dt = ic holds. The latter is a single physical claim about the world; the former is a list of mathematical postulates. The McGucken Principle reduces the postulational basis of physics to one statement.

#### Second, the uniqueness criterion sharpens.

In the standard formulation, alternative postulational bases are difficult to compare: one cannot easily ask whether the Standard Model gauge group is unique because gauge groups are postulated, not derived. In the McGucken formulation, uniqueness becomes a precise question: is dx₄/dt = ic the unique single-equation physical principle generating the principal symmetries of physics? The uniqueness theorem (Theorem `<a href="#thm:unique" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:unique">`{=html}59`</a>`{=html}) gives the affirmative answer.

#### Third, the empirical signature relocates.

In the standard formulation, the empirical signature of each symmetry is tested separately: Lorentz invariance is tested by photon-velocity experiments, gauge invariance by precision QED, CPT by particle-antiparticle mass equality, etc. In the McGucken formulation, all of these tests are simultaneously tests of dx₄/dt = ic. The empirical evidence for the principal symmetries of physics is, by Theorems `<a href="#thm:lorentz" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:lorentz">`{=html}24`</a>`{=html}--`<a href="#thm:string" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:string">`{=html}55`</a>`{=html}, evidence for the McGucken Principle. The cumulative weight of twentieth-century physics, from atomic spectra through LHC physics, becomes cumulative weight for dx₄/dt = ic.

## Summary: The Historical Position of the McGucken Principle

The McGucken Principle stands in a precise historical position. It generates each prior framework as a theorem rather than contradicting any of them.

- Relative to Klein 1872, it supplies the missing physical generator that selects the Lorentzian Kleinian pair from among all possible Kleinian geometries.

- Relative to Minkowski 1908, it promotes x₄ = ict from coordinate convention to physical and geometric statement by recognizing it as the integrated form of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, and identifies the factor i as a geometric marker rather than a sign-flipper.

- Relative to Weyl 1918, it supplies the physical source of the gauge-theoretic factor i in the phase e^(iα).

- Relative to Noether 1918, it derives the Lagrangian and the symmetries (which Noether's theorem requires as inputs) from a deeper physical principle.

- Relative to Wigner 1939, it supplies the selection principle (the temporal orientation  + ic) that picks out the physical UIRs from the full classification.

- Relative to Cartan and Ehresmann, it supplies the physical content of the bundle structure: which base manifold, which fibre, which structure group, which connection.

- Relative to Wheeler's geometrodynamic programme, it supplies the specific foundational equation that Wheeler sought and that his commission to McGucken at Princeton anticipated.

- Relative to the modern programme, it converts the standard postulates of physics --- Lorentz invariance, gauge invariance, CPT, diffeomorphism invariance --- into theorems of a single physical, geometric, dynamical statement.

The historical position of the McGucken Principle is therefore not as a competitor to its predecessors but as their foundational completion. The 154-year arc built the apparatus; dx₄/dt = ic supplies the physical content for which the apparatus was waiting.

## Woit's Symmetry Critique and the McGucken Response

Peter Woit, in *Not Even Wrong* (2006) [Woit2006] and in subsequent published and recorded discussions including his 2024 *Robinson's Podcast* appearance "String Theory and the Crisis in Physics" [WoitPodcast2024], has articulated a sustained, mathematically literate critique of post-1973 foundational physics. His critique is positioned not as anti-mathematical (Woit is a senior lecturer in mathematics at Columbia, with a research programme on the geometry of spinors and twistors) but as a critique of *how* the symmetry apparatus of physics has been deployed: as a postulational scaffold rather than as a derived structure, with the consequence that the standard model's specific symmetry choices remain without explanation and the post-standard-model programmes (Grand Unification, supersymmetry, string theory) have failed either empirically or predictively. Woit's diagnoses are, to a significant extent, the same diagnoses the present paper addresses. This subsection states each of his seven principal symmetry-related concerns with verbatim source where possible, then maps each concern to the corresponding corpus theorem or, where the corpus does not yet supply a complete derivation, to the open-problem flag carrying that incompleteness. The mapping is conducted to the standard of formal mathematical rigour required throughout the present paper: each item is either a citation to an established corpus theorem, a citation to the open-problem catalogue of [MG-Connes2026, §10.4], or a identification stated as such.

The present subsection makes no claim that Woit has endorsed the McGucken framework. Woit's research programme on Euclidean twistor unification [Woit2021], [Woit2023] is independent of the McGucken programme and proceeds via different technical machinery. What this subsection establishes is that the McGucken framework supplies, for several of the concerns Woit raises, *the kind of answer that the form of the concern demands* --- namely, a derivation of the symmetry content from a single foundational physical principle rather than a postulational reintroduction of the symmetry content at a deeper layer of the theory. Where the McGucken corpus does not currently supply such a derivation, this subsection flags the gap honestly.

### Woit's seven symmetry-related concerns

The principal concerns extractable from [Woit2006] and [WoitPodcast2024] are the following.

**W1 --- The standard model gauge group is not derived.** Woit's framing [WoitPodcast2024, transcript 28:38] is direct: *"You've gotten these three forces and they're described by gauge fields of the group U(1), SU(2), and SU(3), so why? Why three, why U(1), why SU(2), why SU(3)? A lot of effort has gone into ... trying to come up with an improvement in the standard model that would actually answer some of those questions, but that really just kind of has not successfully worked so far."* The standard model picks the gauge group by hand from the empirical record; no proof from a deeper principle has been supplied within the mainstream programme.

**W2 --- The Higgs sector compounds the postulational debt.** Woit's framing [WoitPodcast2024, 30:42] applied to Grand Unification but generalises: *"You have to introduce a new and different kind of Higgs field and tune all of its parameters so it does exactly the right thing to break the SU(5) down to what we see. So you've just traded one set of parameters for another."* The same critique applies to the standard model's own Higgs: the vacuum expectation value, the Mexican-hat potential, and the Yukawa coupling matrix are postulated with their values left to empirical determination.

**W3 --- Supersymmetry's superpartners are unobserved and the framework predicts nothing.** Woit's framing [WoitPodcast2024, 38:30]: *"They for instance say that for every particle there should be a superpartner... and then you have to go start going into contortions to explain why haven't we seen it yet, well it's very massive, it's too massive we haven't seen it yet... that's the fundamental problem with the supersymmetric theories ... they kind of don't really predict anything because what they do naively predict you don't see."* The empirical status as of [ATLAS-SUSY2024] and [CMS-SUSY2024] confirms this: no superpartner has been observed up to gluino mass  ∼ 2 TeV, squark mass  ∼ 1.5 TeV, and various electroweakino mass bounds.

**W4 --- The representations of the gauge symmetries are not understood.** Woit [WoitPodcast2024, 12:56]: *"There's still a lot that we don't understand about the implications of that. We don't understand these gauge symmetries, what their representations are very well. There's a lot of the mathematics which remains undeveloped."*

**W5 --- The distinction between a group and the things it acts on is elided.** Woit [WoitPodcast2024, 16:00]: *"This distinction between the group and the things it is acting on is often kind of all elided when people try and explain this, which I think just makes it more confusing."* This is a precise mathematical point: a Lie group is one mathematical object, and the representations on which it acts are different mathematical objects, and the physical content of a symmetry resides in the representations rather than in the abstract group alone.

**W6 --- Spinors are more fundamental than vectors, and quantum gravity has failed by being formulated in vector terms.** Woit [WoitPodcast2024, 1:50:00]: *"Vectors just are not fundamental, spinors are fundamental ... I would argue that one of the things which has really gone wrong with quantum gravity is that people have not been thinking about it in terms of spinors. There is already something different, more fundamental than regular geometry --- the geometry of spinors."*

**W7 --- Symmetries are treated as postulates rather than as derivations from deeper principles.** Woit [WoitPodcast2024, 29:25] lists as his third major problem with the standard model: *"Larger features such as the symmetries --- where they come from."* The same concern is the central organising frame of [Woit2006].

### Mapping concern by concern: the corpus response

The following seven mappings are stated as formal identifications. Each cites the corpus result that addresses the concern at the level the concern demands, or flags the concern as open. Where the corpus is internally split on whether a given concern is fully addressed or remains open, the split is recorded.

**Response to W1 (the standard model gauge group is not derived).** The McGucken corpus supplies a *form* derivation that is independent of the specific choice of compact gauge group, together with a partial-and-internally-contested derivation of the specific group G_(SM). Both components are recorded explicitly.

Universally agreed within the corpus (no internal dispute): for any compact connected real Lie group G with Lie algebra 𝔤, the form of the Yang--Mills sector is forced by dx₄/dt = ic. Specifically:

- The Yang--Mills Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{YM}} = -\tfrac{1}{4} \mathrm{tr}(F_{\mu\nu} F^{\mu\nu})$ is forced as the unique gauge-and-Lorentz-invariant action functional once G is supplied (Theorem 39 of the present paper; [McGuckenExperimental2026, QM T11]; [MG-Connes2026, D-1]).

- Local rather than merely global U(1) invariance is forced by x₄-phase indeterminacy at the spinor level: the directed sign  + ic supplies a global reference for the x₄-expansion direction but does not supply a global reference for the x₄-orientation phase at the spinor level, so the phase angle α is undetermined pointwise, forcing local invariance ([MG-Connes2026, D-2]; [MG-SMGauge2026, §III.2 of MG-QED2026 citation]).

- The chiral coupling structure of matter fields to the gauge field is forced by the matter-orientation condition (M) of [MG-Dirac]: matter modes carry  + Ikx₄ phase with k > 0 and antimatter modes carry  − Ikx₄, with the chirally-asymmetric Clifford pseudoscalar I =  − iγ⁵ supplying the distinction ([MG-Connes2026, D-3]).

- Bundle triviality (the No-Monopole Theorem) is forced by the globally-defined  + ic section of the x₄-orientation U(1)-bundle: any principal U(1)-bundle admitting a global section is trivial, so the first Chern class vanishes and magnetic monopoles cannot exist ([MG-Connes2026, D-4]; [MG-SMGauge2026, §VIII.3]).

- The tensor-product factorisation 𝒜 = C^(∞)(M) ⊗ 𝒜_(F) of the almost-commutative spectral triple, postulated in Connes--Chamseddine--Marcolli, is forced by the Coleman--Mandula theorem of 1967 ([MG-Connes2026, §10.5]). This is a Grade-1 forcing.

Where the corpus is internally split: [MG-SMGauge2026] (May 16, 2026) frames the specific identification G_(SM) = U(1)_(Y) × SU(2)_(L) × SU(3)_(c) as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via substrate-scale exhaustion (no fourth summand in the internal algebra 𝒜_(F) is available); [MG-Connes2026, §10.3] (May 3, 2026) is explicit that the specific algebra 𝒜_(F) = ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ) is empirical input, with four candidate geometric derivations catalogued in §10.4 (the SU(2)_(L)-as-Spin(4)-stabiliser candidate; the SU(3)_(c)-as-transverse-spatial-structure candidate; the U(1)-hypercharge-as-x₄-phase candidate; the generations-as-x₄-mode-quantisation candidate) under the explicit caveat that *none is currently complete to first-principles derivation status*.

The honest statement is therefore the following. The corpus has converted Woit's W1 from an unstructured open problem into a structured one: the form is a theorem, the bundle triviality is a theorem, the local invariance is a theorem, the tensor-product factorisation is a theorem, and the chiral coupling is a theorem. The specific group identification G_(SM) is a theorem in one corpus paper and an open problem with four candidate derivations in another corpus paper. Within the hypothesis stack of the present paper (Hypotheses A1--A23), the gauge group G remains empirical input (A13), with the deeper derivation flagged as ongoing corpus work.

**Response to W2 (the Higgs sector compounds the postulational debt).** This is the response in which the corpus has the strongest available answer. [MG-SMGauge2026, Part IV] establishes eight Higgs theorems, here stated as the precise responses to W2:

- Theorem H1 (Higgs as pointer to  + ic): the Higgs field H is the field-theoretic encoding of the local  + ic direction at each spacetime event, with four real components splitting as three orientation angles (parametrising the unit-vector direction of  + ic in 4-space) plus one magnitude (the gauge-invariant scalar surviving as the physical Higgs h).

- Theorem H2 (vev non-vanishing and globally homogeneous): the vacuum expectation value satisfies |⟨H⟩|(p) > 0 at every event p ∈ ℳ because |dx₄/dt| = c ≠ 0 everywhere, and $|\langle H\rangle| = v/\sqrt{2}$ globally constant from global uniformity of  + ic. The G_(EW)-bundle is topologically trivial via Steenrod's global-section theorem applied to the constant section pointing in  + ic.

- Theorem H3 (hierarchy-problem trichotomy): topological non-vanishing is preserved under loop corrections. The hierarchy problem splits into a rigorous trichotomy: existence of ⟨H⟩ ≠ 0 (solved topologically via Theorem H2), magnitude |v| ≈ 246 GeV (open), and radiative-correction stability of μ² (open, with three honest-finding routes attempted and reported).

- Theorem H4 (Yukawa as winding rate): each fermion species f acquires Compton frequency $k_{C}^{(f)} = y_{f} v c / (\sqrt{2}\hbar)$ in the broken phase, with y_(f) the species-specific x₄-winding rate.

- Theorem H5 (EWSB as "matter feels x₄" switch): in the unbroken phase (⟨H⟩ = 0) all fermions are massless (k_(C)^((f)) = 0) and wavefunctions are x₄-independent, so matter does not couple to the fourth dimension; in the broken phase each species winds at its species-specific Compton rate and matter "feels" x₄.

- Theorem H6 (Mexican-hat shape): the form V(H) =  − μ²H^(†)H + λ(H^(†)H)² is the unique simplest renormalisable G_(EW)-invariant scalar potential consistent with the pointer-on energetic postulate (local maximum at |H| = 0, global minimum at $|H| = v_{*}/\sqrt{2} > 0$). The values μ² and λ remain empirical parameters; the functional form is uniquely forced.

- Theorem H7 (the 3+1 component split): three orientation angles are absorbed as W^(±), Z Goldstones, one magnitude survives as the physical Higgs h. The count 3 + 1 = 4 is forced by the geometry of recording a direction in 4-space.

- Theorem H8 (No-Higgs-Domain-Wall Theorem): the absolute prohibition on Higgs domain walls, vortices, textures, and magnitude variations follows from the global uniformity of  + ic. The vacuum manifold has a single G_(EW)-orbit regardless of how many Higgs multiplets are added, because multiple disconnected components would require the  + ic direction to differ across spacetime, contradicting dx₄/dt =  + ic uniformly.

The honest statement is therefore the following. Woit's W2 is not a critique that applies to the McGucken framework's treatment of the Higgs. The McGucken Higgs is the field-theoretic encoding of  + ic. The vev's existence is a topological theorem; the Mexican-hat shape is a uniqueness theorem; the 3+1 split is a geometric theorem; the Yukawa coupling is identified with a physical quantity (the x₄-winding rate); EWSB is identified with a physical mechanism (matter coupling to x₄); and an additional prediction (the No-Higgs-Domain-Wall Theorem) is delivered. The empirical magnitude |v| ≈ 246 GeV and the empirical Yukawa values remain inputs; this is honestly flagged in [MG-SMGauge2026, Theorem H3] as the magnitude half of the hierarchy trichotomy.

**Response to W3 (supersymmetry's superpartners are unobserved).** The McGucken position on supersymmetry, stated already in Lemma 54 of the present paper and consistent across the corpus, is the following. The McGucken derivations of the principal symmetries of physics (Lorentz, Poincaré, Noether, Wigner, U(1) gauge, non-Abelian gauge, quantum-unitary, CPT, diffeomorphism) --- Sections 2 through 10 of the present paper --- make no use of supersymmetry. Theorem 51 establishes the claim that *if* supersymmetry is realised, it is necessarily of the Haag--Łopuszański--Sohnius graded-Lie-algebra form; the theorem makes no commitment to supersymmetry being realised in Nature.

This is the right epistemic stance against W3. The McGucken framework neither requires supersymmetry (which would expose it to Woit's no-superpartners critique) nor excludes supersymmetry (which would forbid future accommodation if superpartners are eventually found). If LHC Run 4 or future colliders observe superpartners, the framework accommodates them via Theorem 51 as a extension; if no superpartners are observed, the framework loses nothing because its derivations of the principal symmetries do not depend on supersymmetric content. Woit's W3 critique applies to programmes for which supersymmetry is ; it does not apply to the McGucken Father-Symmetry programme.

**Response to W4 (the representations of the gauge symmetries are not understood).** This is the response that lives most naturally inside Woit's own positive programme and is the closest to first-principles within the present corpus. The corpus supplies origins for each principal representation:

- The doublet representation of SU(2)_(L) is forced by the complex dimension 2 of the irreducible complex representation of Cl(1,3)⁺ on a chirality eigenspace ([MG-SMGauge2026, Lemma 5.2]).

- The three colours of SU(3)_(c) descend from the three transverse spatial directions of the McGucken Sphere ([MG-SMGauge2026, Part III]).

- The hypercharge assignment (−1,+1,−1/3) on the three sectors (ℂ,ℍ,M₃(ℂ)) is forced by the unimodularity condition on U(𝒜_(F)) leaving a unique surviving U(1) subgroup ([MG-SMGauge2026, Theorem U1Y]).

This is --- within the corpus's own most careful articulation [MG-Connes2026, §10.3] --- an incomplete response: the specific fermion representation content (the precise assignment of representations to physical particles across three generations) is honestly catalogued as not yet derived (item N-2 in [MG-Connes2026, §10.3]). But the incompleteness is of a different kind from the standard model's: the standard model has no story at all for *why* these representations rather than others, while the corpus has arguments under active development for each component. The four candidate derivations of [MG-Connes2026, §10.4] are the explicit programme targets.

**Response to W5 (group versus representation distinction is elided).** This is the response that engages most directly with Woit's specific mathematical literacy, and it is the one in which the McGucken framework supplies a categorically structured separation rather than a mere terminological distinction. The Erlangen-Programme-completion content [MG-Erlangen2026] supplies precisely the categorical apparatus that distinguishes the McGucken Symmetry 𝒮_(M) (the algebraic generator of dx₄/dt = ic) from its action on physical structures via four parallel descent functors Π_(Lor), Π_(Hilb), Π_(Bun), Π_(Cstar). Each descent functor sends the source-pair (ℳ_(G),D_(M)) to a category of physical structures --- Lorentzian manifolds, Hilbert spaces, principal G-bundles, C^(*)-algebras --- with the symmetry group and its representations on those structures arising as derived objects.

This categorical separation is the formal apparatus Woit identifies as undeveloped in the standard programme. Klein's original 1872 Erlangen Programme separates a group from its associated geometry; the McGucken extension goes further, separating the foundational physical generator dx₄/dt = ic from each of the four categories of structure on which the derived symmetry groups act. The structure-versus-group distinction Woit emphasises is the categorical content of the Erlangen-completion programme [MG-Erlangen2026], realised through this four-level separation.

**Response to W6 (spinors are more fundamental than vectors).** This is the *deepest* Woit--McGucken convergence and the one for which the corpus is most fully developed. Woit's diagnosis --- that the failure of vectorial quantum gravity is rather than incidental, and that the geometry of spinors must supply the substrate --- is operationalised in the corpus at three independent levels.

First, the spectral-triple level: the McGucken--Dirac spectral triple [MG-Connes2026, Theorem A] is constructed on L²(ℳ,S), the space of square-integrable spinor sections on the McGucken Euclidean four-manifold. The Dirac operator D_(ℳ) = iγ^(μ)∇_(μ) --- the McGucken Operator --- acts on this spinor space from the start. The factor i in D_(ℳ) is identified, via the suppression-map analysis of [Wick34, Lemma 14], with the perpendicularity marker of x₄ in dx₄/dt = ic. Second, the foundational-atom level: the McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) at every event p is, by Theorem H of [MG-Connes2026], derivationally identical to the Chamseddine--Connes--Mukhanov "quantum of geometry" at substrate scale. Two independent foundational frameworks --- the McGucken framework, deriving the McGucken Sphere from Huygens construction at substrate-tick parameter t_(P); and the Chamseddine--Connes--Mukhanov framework, deriving the quantum-of-geometry sphere from the higher Heisenberg commutation relation $\tfrac{1}{4!}\langle Y[D,Y]^{4}\rangle = \gamma$ via the index theorem --- arrive at the same Planckian spherical quantum of spacetime. The substrate atom of spacetime is spinorial in both frameworks.

Third, the Dirac-equation derivation level: the Dirac equation (iγ^(μ)∂_(μ)−m)ψ = 0, the spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ representation, the SU(2) double cover SU(2) → SO(3), and the matter--antimatter pair structure are all derived as theorems of x₄-rotation in [MG-Dirac]. The Cartan square-root identification --- that the Dirac operator is the geometric square root of the d'Alembertian, and that spinors are square roots of vectors --- is the content underlying these derivations.

The Woit--McGucken convergence on W6 is therefore at the level of diagnosis (spinors fundamental, vectors derived) and at the level of operationalisation (McGucken--Dirac spectral triple constructed on spinor sections from the start; the McGucken Sphere identified as the spinorial spacetime atom; the Dirac equation derived as a theorem). The previously-developed corpus paper on Woit's Euclidean Twistor Unification connection takes this further: dx₄/dt = ic supplies the physical selection principle for which Woit's twistor-theoretic programme has explicitly indicated the absence of a mechanism (see [Woit2021], where Woit acknowledges that the Euclidean twistor formulation requires *some* physical principle for selecting SU(2,2) as primary and PT⁺ as physical; dx₄/dt = ic supplies precisely that principle, with the bundle-theoretic identification placing S_(R) on the tautological line bundle 𝒪(−1) as the x₄-advance directions and S_(L) on the normal bundle).

The convergence is at the level of diagnosis and form. Woit has not endorsed the specific McGucken solution; the corpus does not require Woit's endorsement. What the convergence establishes is that two independent research programmes --- Woit's Euclidean twistor unification and the McGucken Father-Symmetry programme --- have arrived at the same conclusion that the substrate of physics is spinorial rather than vectorial, with the McGucken framework supplying the dynamical-geometric mechanism (dx₄/dt = ic) that Woit's framework leaves as primitive data.

**Response to W7 (symmetries are postulates rather than derivations).** This is the central organising concern of the present paper, and the response is the Master Table of Section 1 together with Theorems 24, 27, 30, 33, 36, 39, 42, 45, 48 (Sections 2 through 10) and the conditional Theorems 51 and 55. Within the hypothesis stack A1--A23 of the present paper:

- Noether's first theorem (Theorem 30, with the priority statement) is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic in the sharper sense established in [MG-FatherSymmetry, Theorem 32]: the Lagrangian, the symmetries the theorem maps from, and the conservation laws the theorem maps to are all forced consequences of the McGucken Principle.

- The CPT theorem (Theorem 45) is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via Bargmann--Hall--Wightman analytic continuation, with the i in the analytic-continuation prescription identified as the McGucken i.

The supersymmetry theorem (Theorem 51) and the string-dualities theorem (Theorem 55) are conditional and empirically open/unsettled respectively, as honestly catalogued in Lemma 54 and Remark 56 of the present paper.

Nine of the eleven principal symmetries of contemporary physics are therefore theorems of dx₄/dt = ic within the present paper; two are conditional. The 47-theorem empirical chain of [McGuckenExperimental2026] extends this derivation pattern across General Relativity (Theorems 1--24) and Quantum Mechanics (Theorems 1--23), with Theorem 143 establishing a cumulative Bayesian likelihood ratio  ≳ 10¹⁴¹ in favour of the active-expansion reading over its negation under conservative benchmarks chosen to favour the negation hypothesis (by elementary log comparison: the figure exceeds the Higgs-boson discovery log₁₀ ∼ 6 and the CMB dark-matter inference log₁₀ ∼ 100 under the stated benchmarks). Within the empirical-confirmation domain of those 47 theorems, Woit's W7 is converted from an open problem into a precisely-graded one: forms forced, specific empirical identifications partially derived with the open work catalogued.

### Honest summary of where the corpus does and does not address Woit

The seven Woit concerns are not addressed uniformly. The historical record therefore separates into two layers. The first layer is the established mathematical apparatus: Klein's group-theoretic classification of geometries, Minkowski's Lorentzian union of space and time, Weyl's gauge-geometric extension, Noether's symmetry-conservation theorem, Wigner's representation-theoretic classification, and the Cartan--Ehresmann language of connections and bundles. The McGucken Principle supplies the latter by interpreting the fourth coordinate dynamically: x₄ = ict is the integrated form of the light-speed spherical expansion law dx₄/dt = ic, rather than a formal imaginary coordinate introduced without physical content.

This historical distinction is technically essential. If x₄ = ict is only a convention, then Lorentzian signature, the invariant speed, complex quantum phase, and unitary time evolution remain separately stipulated. If dx₄/dt = ic is the physical-geometric law, then the same symbol i has one role across the paper: it records the perpendicularity of the fourth dimension to the spatial three-plane, and its square produces the negative temporal sign in the interval. The Algebraic Channel then reads the resulting invariants algebraically through groups, algebras, representations, generators, and charges; the Geometric Channel reads the same invariants geometrically through spheres, null cones, bundles, propagation kernels, and variational paths. This is the exact historical point at which the present paper broadens the 154-year lineage rather than replacing it: the inherited apparatus is preserved, but its physical source is made explicit.

## The Disjunctive Forcing Theorem: dx₄/dt = ic is the unique configuration forced by the joint empirical record

The Disjunctive Forcing Theorem (Theorem 21 below; cf. McGucken 2026, *The McGucken Geometric and Algebraic Channels Duality at the Deepest Level*, §X.11) establishes that any candidate dynamics of the fourth coordinate consistent with five independently confirmed empirical features of contemporary physics is forced to coincide with dx₄/dt = ic. This section presents the theorem with full rigor: formal setup of the candidate space (Definition 4.1.1), exhaustiveness lemmas for the classification of candidates (Lemma 4.1.2) and for the modes of departure (Lemma 4.1.3), an orientation-forcing lemma grounded in two empirical inputs independent of the second law of thermodynamics (Lemma 4.1.4), explicit strand-to-mode bridging propositions with empirical bounds (Propositions 4.1.5–4.1.9), the theorem with proof (Theorem 21), and two remarks on the precision and transparency of the argument (Remarks 4.1.10 and 4.1.11).

### Setup: the candidate space of fourth-coordinate dynamics

Let M be a four-dimensional smooth manifold equipped with a foliation by spatial three-slices {S_t}_(t ∈ ℝ) indexed by the lab clock parameter t. At each event p ∈ M, the tangent space T_p M decomposes as V₃(p) ⊕ V₄(p), with V₃(p) = T_p S_{t(p)} and V₄(p) the one-dimensional complement transverse to the spatial slice.

**Definition 4.1.1 (Candidate fourth-coordinate dynamics).** *A candidate fourth-coordinate dynamics is a triple Π = (R, Σ, ε) where:*

*(i) R : M × S² → ℂ is a smooth function assigning to each event p and spatial unit vector n̂ ∈ S² ⊂ V₃(p) a complex rate of x₄-advance, in units of velocity;*

*(ii) Σ : M → 𝒫(M) assigns to each event p a smooth wavefront surface Σ(p) ⊂ M, the set of events declared "x₄-simultaneous" with p;*

*(iii) ε ∈ {+1, −1} is a global orientation of the foliation, selecting future-directed or past-directed propagation of Σ(p).*

*The McGucken configuration is Π_McG = (R_McG, Σ_McG, ε_McG) with R_McG(p, n̂) = ic for every (p, n̂), Σ_McG(p) = {q ∈ M : |𝐱_q − 𝐱_p| = c(t_q − t_p), t_q > t_p}, and ε_McG = +1. The space of all candidate triples is denoted 𝒞.*

### The five empirical strands

The empirical inputs to the theorem are five independently confirmed observational features of contemporary physics.

- **Strand (i): Tsirelson saturation.** The CHSH correlation saturates the Tsirelson bound $|\mathrm{CHSH}|=2\sqrt{2}$ within a few percent in loophole-free Bell tests (Aspect 1982; Hensen et al. 2015 measuring $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2.42 \pm 0.20$; the Big Bell Test 2018; the Pan-group Micius satellite Bell test, Yin et al. 2017).
- **Strand (ii): Rotational invariance of entanglement.** The angular dependence of entanglement correlations is the universal E(â, b̂) = −cos θ_(ab), isotropic under SO(3), verified to better than 1% in the loophole-free Bell tests (Hensen 2015; Giustina 2015; Shalm 2015).
- **Strand (iii): No entanglement-distance limit.** Bell tests at increasing separation — meter scale (Aspect 1982), 10 km optical fibre under Lake Geneva (Tittel et al. 1998), 1200 km between Delingha ground station and the Micius satellite (Pan group 2017; Yin et al. 2017) — continue to find $|\mathrm{CHSH}|=2\sqrt{2}$ within experimental error.
- **Strand (iv): Lorentz invariance of c.** The speed of light is isotropic and frame-invariant to |Δc/c| ≲ 10⁻²⁰ across photon energies separated by orders of magnitude (Vasileiou et al. 2013, gamma-ray-burst timing constraints from GRB 090510); to |Δc/c| ≲ 10⁻¹⁵ in resonator-cavity tests (MICROSCOPE 2017).
- **Strand (v): Wavefront self-replication.** Every point on a wavefront radiates secondary spherical wavelets that combine to form the future wavefront (Huygens 1690; Kirchhoff 1882). Empirically: light from distant astronomical sources reaches Earth by iterated self-replication over megaparsec distances; gravitational waves from GW150914 propagated by self-replication over 1.3 billion light-years (LIGO/Virgo 2015).

### Classification of candidates along three orthogonal axes

The candidate Π = (R, Σ, ε) is classified along three orthogonal axes:

**Axis (α) — Rate.** The rate function R is classified by its deviation δR := R − R_McG = R − ic ∈ C^∞(M × S², ℂ).

**Axis (β) — Surface assignment.** The surface Σ(p) is classified by two quantities: its x₄-coherence width w(p) := sup_{q ∈ Σ(p)} |x₄(q) − x₄(p)|, and the Huygens self-replication bit Huyg(Π) := **1**[Σ(q) ⊆ ⋃_{r ∈ Σ(p)} Σ(r) for all q ∈ Σ(p)].

**Axis (γ) — Orientation.** The sign ε ∈ {+1, −1} selects the temporal branch of Σ(p).

**Lemma 4.1.2 (Classification exhaustiveness).** *The assignment*

$$\Pi \mapsto \bigl(\delta R,\ w,\ \mathrm{Huyg},\ \varepsilon\bigr)$$

*is a bijection between 𝒞 and C^∞(M × S², ℂ) × C^∞(M, [0, ∞]) × {0, 1} × {+1, −1}. Equivalently: every candidate Π is uniquely characterized by its rate deviation, surface coherence width, Huygens bit, and orientation; the four are mutually independent.*

*Proof.* The forward map is constructed componentwise from Definition 4.1.1: δR := R − ic is computed from the rate, w from the surface, Huyg from the surface assignment, ε from the foliation orientation. The inverse map reconstructs R = ic + δR, Σ as the unique surface of x₄-coherence width w satisfying or failing the Huygens condition, and ε as given. The four components are independent: δR controls rate, w controls thickness, Huyg controls propagation, ε controls orientation, and changing any one leaves the others fixed. ◼

### Five failure modes and their exhaustion along axes (α, β)

Departures from Π_McG along axes (α) and (β) are characterized by five failure modes.

- **Mode A (random scatter).** δR is a random field with non-zero variance σ_X²(p) > 0 over an experimental ensemble. The induced x₄-position variance over one Compton time τ_C(m) = ℏ/(mc²) is σ_(x₄)²(m) = τ_C²(m) · σ_X².

- **Mode B (systematic gradient).** δR is deterministic and event-dependent, with non-zero gradient ∇_p δR ≠ 0; the systematic-gradient coupling is g := sup_{p, n̂} |∇_p δR(p, n̂)| · τ_C, of dimensions of action.

- **Mode C (finite thickness).** w(p) > 0 for some p, with empirical x₄-coherence length L_coh := c · sup_p w(p).

- **Mode D (rate anisotropy).** R(p, n̂) − R(p, n̂′) ≠ 0 for some n̂ ≠ n̂′; quantified by the fractional anisotropy |Δc/c| := sup_{p, n̂, n̂′} |R(p, n̂) − R(p, n̂′)| / c.

- **Mode E (no self-replication).** Huyg(Π) = 0.

**Lemma 4.1.3 (Mode exhaustiveness along (α, β)).** *Any candidate Π with Π ≠ Π_McG along axis (α) or axis (β) falls into at least one of Modes A, B, C, D, E.*

*Proof.* By Lemma 4.1.2, deviation along (α) means δR ≠ 0 as a function on M × S². The space of non-zero smooth complex-valued functions on M × S² decomposes by elementary functional classification into: (1) stochastic functions with non-zero ensemble variance (Mode A); (2) deterministic functions with non-zero spatial gradient ∇_p δR (Mode B); (3) deterministic and spatially constant but direction-dependent functions, i.e. δR(n̂) ≠ δR(n̂′) for some n̂ ≠ n̂′ (Mode D); or (4) deterministic, spatially constant, and direction-independent, i.e. δR = const. Case (4) is a constant offset of the rate, which redefines the speed c globally and is excluded by the unit-system fixing c = 299,792,458 m/s as the empirically measured photon velocity (case 4 is a relabeling of units, not a physical deviation). The cases (1)–(3) exhaust physical deviations along (α).

Deviation along (β) means (w, Huyg) ≠ (0, 1), i.e. either w > 0 (Mode C) or w = 0 with Huyg = 0 (Mode E). The cases exhaust deviations along (β).

The five modes A, B, C, D, E together exhaust deviations of Π from Π_McG along axes (α) and (β). ◼

### 1. Boltzmann--Gibbs entropy (1872 / 1902)

The phase-space entropy of statistical mechanics. For a massive particle whose spatial distribution undergoes Brownian motion driven by the McGucken-Sphere isotropic spherical expansion, the Boltzmann--Gibbs entropy is a strict identity:
$$S_{\mathrm{BG}}(t) = \tfrac{3}{2}k_{B}\ln(4\pi e D t) + \mathrm{const}, \qquad \frac{dS_{\mathrm{BG}}}{dt} = \frac{3k_{B}}{2t} > 0.$$
The diffusion constant is the McGucken Compton-coupling D_(x)^((McGucken)) = ε²c²Ω/(2γ_(L)²), supplying species-dependent, temperature-independent geometric diffusion. The monotonicity dS_(BG)/dt = 3k_(B)/(2t) > 0 is **strict** --- not statistical, not on average --- because the Gaussian density of the particle's spatial distribution widens deterministically as ⟨|x|²⟩ = 6Dt, and the Boltzmann--Gibbs entropy of a wider Gaussian is greater by a deterministic function of variance. **Loschmidt's 1876 reversibility objection is dissolved at the level**: strict monotonicity sits in the Geometric Channel's  + ic orientation rather than in the Algebraic Channel's time-symmetric microscopic dynamics, and requires no Algebraic-Channel symmetry breaking.

### 2. Shannon entropy (1948)

The information-theoretic entropy of a continuous distribution on a measurable space. For a photon emitted isotropically from event p₀ and riding the McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p₀) of radius R(t) = c(t−t₀) with uniform angular distribution, the Shannon entropy of the distribution is:
$$S_{\mathrm{Sh}}(t) = k_{B}\ln A(t) + \mathrm{const} = k_{B}\ln\bigl(4\pi c^{2}(t-t_{0})^{2}\bigr) + \mathrm{const}, \qquad \frac{dS_{\mathrm{Sh}}}{dt} = \frac{2k_{B}}{t-t_{0}} > 0.$$
**The entropy grows because the sphere grows; the sphere grows because x₄ advances at rate c.** The Boltzmann--Gibbs entropy (massive particles, (3/2)k_(B)/t rate) and the Shannon entropy (photons, 2k_(B)/(t−t₀) rate) differ only in the prefactor reflecting their distinct kinematic regimes (massive particles diffuse in 3-volume; photons spread on a 2-surface) but trace to the same geometric source: the McGucken Sphere's c-rate isotropic expansion.

## The Frobenius forcing of i: ℂ, not ℝ or ℍ

The principle dx₄/dt = ic carries the imaginary unit i. Why ℂ and not ℝ or ℍ? Frobenius's theorem (1878) settles the question.

**Theorem (Frobenius 1878).** *The only associative finite-dimensional division algebras over ℝ are ℝ, ℂ, and the quaternions ℍ.*

**Theorem (Algebraic forcing of i).** *The generator i in dx₄/dt = ic is the unique element of ℂ --- up to sign --- satisfying: (1) i² =  − 1; (2) |i| = 1; (3) i generates a one-parameter rotation subgroup of ℂ by complex multiplication. The sign + is fixed by the physical content of the four-fold ontology: the active expansion proceeds at  + ic, not  − ic.*

**Theorem (Frobenius forces ℂ, not ℝ, not ℍ).** *In ℝ no element squares to  − 1, so (1) fails. In ℍ the three units i, j, k each square to  − 1; the choice among them is not forced by the geometric content of dx₄/dt = ic, which selects a single one-parameter rotation subgroup. Frobenius's theorem leaves ℂ as the unique remaining real division algebra.*

The Clifford-algebraic identification then closes the question of *which* i. The relativistic Clifford algebra Cℓ(1,3) contains ℂ as a subalgebra. The pseudoscalar ω = γ⁰γ¹γ²γ³ ∈ Cℓ(1,3) satisfies ω² =  − 1 and commutes with even-grade elements; it generates a complex structure on the even subalgebra. The McGucken Principle's i is the pseudoscalar of the spacetime Clifford algebra restricted to the orthogonal-to-spatial subspace.

**Corollary (the unique i across physics).** *The i in dx₄/dt = ic, the i in [q̂,p̂] = iℏ, the i in ψ(t) = ψ(0)e^(−iHt/ℏ), the i in det (η_(μν)) =  − 1 (after Wick rotation), the i in e^(iS/ℏ), and the i in the Dirac equation (iγ^(μ)∂_(μ)−m)ψ = 0 are all the same i: the Frobenius-forced unique generator of x₄-advance in the real division algebra ℂ, identified physically with the pseudoscalar of Cℓ(1,3) restricted to the orthogonal-to-spatial subspace.*

This unification of the various i's of mathematical physics under a single algebraic-geometric primitive is what licenses every symmetry derivation of §§5--16 to use i without further justification. The Wick-rotation i, the canonical-commutation i, the Schrödinger-evolution i, the path-integral-weight i, and the CPT analytic-continuation i (Proposition 45a of §13) are five representations of the one geometric generator rather than five independent insertions of a formal symbol.

The Frobenius-forced i of the preceding subsection is a single algebraic-geometric primitive of the McGucken-generated bundle structure. **Theorem (The physical and geometric reading of dx₄/dt = ic: spherically-symmetric wavefront with twin properties c and ℏ; the spinor on the wavefront).** *The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is the physical and geometric statement that the fourth dimension is expanding as a spherically-symmetric wavefront at velocity c from every event p ∈ M of spacetime. - *(i) Wavelength.* *At every massive source event p of mass m, the McGucken Sphere wavefront carries the Compton wavelength λ_(C)(m) = ℏ/(mc). This is the wavelength the wavefront has as a wavefront, not an externally-imposed quantum-mechanical scale.*
- *(ii) Frequency.* *At every massive source event p of mass m, the McGucken Sphere wavefront carries the Compton frequency ω_(C)(m) = mc²/ℏ. This is the frequency the wavefront has by virtue of being a wavefront with rate c and wavelength λ_(C).*
- *(iii) Phase.* *Every point q on the McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) carries the Compton phase Φ(q;p) = exp (−imc²Δτ(q;p)/ℏ), with Sphere-surface phase uniformity established by Lemma 9.2 of [MG-ProofsQMRel2026]: every point q on the spatial slice of Σ⁺(p) shares the same Compton phase.*
- *(iv) Action.* *Each Planck-frequency oscillation of x₄-advance carries one quantum of action ℏ. The action quantum is the action carried by the wavefront over one oscillation period.*

*The two fundamental constants of physics are twin properties of one advance. c is the rate of x₄-advance on the right-hand side of dx₄/dt = ic; ℏ is the action quantum per Planck-frequency oscillation of that advance ([MG-HilbertBorn2026, Proposition 2.2], Twin Constants). *The Dirac spinor lives on a wavefront that already has the Compton frequency. The Algebraic Channel reads the structure algebraically: the radii of the light cone are null vectors of zero spacetime length under η; two events connected by a null vector are at zero spacetime distance in the Minkowski metric; the connected Lorentz group SO⁺(1,3) is the real-linear isometry group of η in which the null vectors are defined. *Per Theorem 106 of [MG-GRQM2026] (Signature-Bridging Theorem, imported from [Wick34, Theorem 1]) and Lemma 9.3 of [MG-ProofsQMRel2026] (Dual-channel co-failure forcing of the asymmetry), the Geometric Channel and the Algebraic Channel produce theorem-by-theorem equivalent empirical content through disjoint intermediate machinery; the two channels are two readings of one principle dx₄/dt = ic. The Algebraic-Channel empirical signature (Lorentz invariance of c, verified by GRB 090510 photon-timing isotropy to |Δc/c| ≲ 10⁻²⁰) and the Geometric-Channel empirical signature (Tsirelson saturation $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2\sqrt{2}$, verified by Hensen 2015, Big Bell Test 2018, and Micius 2017) co-fail under any perturbation of the McGucken Principle. *Co-identity reading. The light cone of the Algebraic Channel and the McGucken Sphere of the Geometric Channel are the same geometric object --- the spatial slice |x−x₀| = c(t−t₀) at time t > t₀ is at once (i) the null cone of Minkowski's 1908 formalism, the locus of vectors r with η_(μν)r^(μ)r^(ν) = 0, and (ii) the McGucken Sphere of the source event, the active wavefront of x₄-expansion at velocity c. The empirical co-failure follows from Lemma 9.3 of [MG-ProofsQMRel2026]. The co-identity is stronger than causal dependence: the two are two readings of one principle, not separate phenomena that happen to co-fail under perturbation. **Theorem (Symmetry-asymmetry channel diagnosis: the Algebraic Channel is the symmetry-content channel; the Geometric Channel is the asymmetry-generating channel with spherically-symmetric source).** *The dual-channel architecture of the McGucken programme exhibits a asymmetry in its handling of preservation-versus-flow content. **Theorem (External symmetries carry base-i).** *Lorentz invariance, Poincaré covariance, and diffeomorphism invariance --- the three external symmetries of the McGucken programme (Theorems 24, 27, 48 of the present paper) --- carry the Frobenius-forced i in the base-i placement. The i is absorbed into the base metric η via the pulled-back Lorentzian form of Lemma 1: the substitution dx₄ = ic dt converts the auxiliary Euclidean inner product g_(E) = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄² to the Lorentzian metric η = diag(−,+,+,+), with the  − 1 in the time-time component being the algebraic image of i² =  − 1 for the Frobenius-forced i. The external symmetries act on the base manifold M by preserving η --- and therefore by preserving the absorbed base-i --- without altering any fiber structure over M.*

*Proof.* The Lorentz group SO⁺(1,3) is defined by Theorem 24 as the connected real-linear isometry group of η, i.e., the connected component of the solution space of X^(T)η + ηX = 0. Any element Λ ∈ SO⁺(1,3) acts on the base via x^(μ) ↦ Λ_( ν)^(μ)x^(ν) and preserves η_(μν) by construction. Since η₀₀ =  − 1 is the algebraic image of i² =  − 1 via the Lemma 1 substitution, preservation of η entails preservation of the base-i placement. The Lorentz action does not touch any fiber over the base --- gauge phases of matter fields, internal-symmetry indices, and tangent-space spinor decompositions all remain at the same fiber point under a base Lorentz transformation, transforming only by the induced representation of SO⁺(1,3) on the fiber. The same argument applied to the affine isometries of (ℝ^(1, 3),η) (i.e., the Poincaré group ISO⁺(1,3) = ℝ^(1, 3) ⋊ SO⁺(1,3) of Theorem 27) and to the smooth diffeomorphisms of (M,g) preserving the McGucken-generated Lorentzian structure (Theorem 48) yields the same conclusion: each acts on the base, preserves the absorbed base-i, and does not introduce fiber-acting content. ◼

**Theorem (Internal symmetries carry fiber-i).** *The U(1) gauge symmetry (Theorem 36 of §9), the non-Abelian gauge symmetries SU(N) (Theorem 39 of §10), and any compact internal symmetry group G admitted in the principal-bundle structure of A14 --- the three classes of internal symmetries of the McGucken programme --- carry the Frobenius-forced i in the fiber-i placement. The i appears as the generator of the fiber group acting on matter fields ψ^(a) at fixed base point x ∈ M: for U(1), the gauge transformation is ψ(x) ↦ e^(iα(x))ψ(x) with i in the exponent; for SU(N), the transformation is ψ^(a)(x) ↦ [e^(iθ^(b)(x)T^(b))]_( c)^(a)ψ^(c)(x) with i in the Lie-algebra-valued exponent. The base point x is fixed; the fiber acts independently of the base coordinate.*

*Proof.* The U(1) gauge group is the structure group of the complex line bundle L → M of Hypothesis A12. A gauge transformation is a section of the associated bundle L×_(U(1))U(1), written explicitly as the map ψ(x) ↦ e^(iα(x))ψ(x) for α : M → ℝ smooth. The exponent iα(x) has i as its Frobenius-forced generator (Theorem 23 establishes that the i in e^(iα) is the same algebraic primitive as the i in dx₄/dt = ic). The base coordinate x is unchanged by the gauge action; only the fiber over x is rotated. For non-Abelian SU(N), the same structure holds with 𝔰𝔲(N)-valued generators T^(a) in place of the U(1) generator; the i in exp (iθ^(a)T^(a)) remains the Frobenius-forced i (the Hermitian-generator convention of the Lie algebra brackets [T^(a),T^(b)] = if^(abc)T^(c) uses the same i). The fiber action is by definition independent of the base coordinate. ◼

**Theorem (Coleman--Mandula as the algebraic shadow of the geometric perpendicular-versus-parallel substrate decomposition).** *The Coleman--Mandula no-go theorem (Coleman and Mandula 1967, *All Possible Symmetries of the S-Matrix*) --- which states that the most general Lie algebra of symmetries of the S-matrix in (3+1)-dimensional relativistic quantum field theory, under technical hypotheses (massive particles, finite particle types, analytic S-matrix), is the direct sum of the Poincaré algebra and a Lie algebra of internal symmetries that commute with Poincaré --- is the algebraic shadow of the geometric decomposition of the McGucken substrate into perpendicular-to-spatial and parallel-to-spatial features. Specifically: the internal symmetries (fiber-i placement; descending from the i on the right-hand side of dx₄/dt = ic per the two-source theorem) act on the x₄-perpendicular substrate features (the phase of x₄-winding for U(1)_(Y); the doublet structure of x₄-orientation for SU(2)_(L); the substrate-scale spatial-direction bimodule for SU(3)_(c)). The external symmetries (base-i placement; descending from the c on the right-hand side per the same theorem) act on the parallel-to-spatial substrate features (the three-space coordinates of the McGucken Sphere wavefront, with translations shifting the wavefront's centre event, rotations rotating its spatial directions, and boosts changing the worldline through it). The commutators [P^(μ),T^(a)] = 0 and [J^(μν),T^(a)] = 0 of the Coleman--Mandula decomposition are the infinitesimal algebraic statement that the perpendicular substrate features and the parallel substrate features are geometrically disjoint on the McGucken-generated bundle; their symmetries commute by necessity. The Haag--Łopuszański--Sohnius 1975 graded extension corresponds to the conditional adjunction of a Grassmann-odd direction to the perpendicular substrate features, treated in §14 of the present paper as conditional on auxiliary hypotheses.*

*Proof sketch.* Under the McGucken-generated bundle structure of the present subsection, the perpendicular-to-spatial substrate features (the x₄-orientation phase, the spinor doublet structure, the colour bimodule) and the parallel-to-spatial substrate features (the three-space coordinates of the McGucken Sphere wavefront, the spatial-rotation SO(3) symmetry of the sphere, the timelike worldline parameterised by t = x₄/(ic)) are geometrically orthogonal in the substrate decomposition: the perpendicular features sit in the x₄-direction algebraic structure (which carries the Frobenius-forced i as the perpendicularity marker of Theorem 23); the parallel features sit in the three-space-and-time structure of the McGucken Sphere (which carries the velocity c as the wavefront-propagation rate). The two-source theorem above established that the i generates the internal-symmetry transformation content (acting on perpendicular features) and the c generates the external-symmetry wavefront-propagation content (acting on parallel features). For any smooth field ψ(x) defined on the McGucken-generated bundle, the composition of an internal action T^(a) (rotating the perpendicular features at fixed base point x) and a base action P^(μ) (translating the parallel features along the wavefront) commute as operators: [(P^(μ)⋅T^(a))ψ](x) = T^(a)[ψ(x+a^(μ))] = (T^(a)⋅P^(μ))ψ(x), since T^(a) acts only on the perpendicular fibre indices of ψ at a given base point, and P^(μ) acts only on the parallel coordinate of ψ. The vanishing commutators [P^(μ),T^(a)] = 0 and [J^(μν),T^(a)] = 0 at the Lie-algebra level are the infinitesimal statement of this commutativity. The Coleman--Mandula 1967 result therefore arises as the reading of the perpendicular-versus-parallel substrate decomposition of the McGucken-generated bundle. ## Setup: the time-reversal operator $T$ and the channel projection $\Pi_{A}$

Let $M$ denote the four-manifold of spacetime events with the McGucken foliation by spatial three-slices $\{S_{t}\}_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$. Let $\mathcal{B}$ denote the full geometric content of the McGucken Principle: the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma^{+}(p)$ at every event $p \in M$ with $+ic$ orientation, the iterated Huygens-propagation rule of the McGucken→Huygens Theorem of §3, the $+ic$-directed McGucken–Wick rotation $\tau = x_{4}/c$, the McGucken-Sphere Brownian-coupling diffusion $D_{x} = \varepsilon^{2}c^{2}\Omega/(2\gamma_{L}^{2})$, the eight forms of entropy on $\Sigma^{+}(p)$, the Born-rule Haar measure on the spatial slice, the cosmological McGucken Sphere driving Hubble expansion, and all derived geometric structure. Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote Algebraic Channel's algebraic content: the Lorentzian metric $\eta = \mathrm{diag}(-,+,+,+)$, the Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^{+}(1,3)$, the Poincaré algebra $\mathfrak{iso}(1,3) = \mathbb{R}^{1,3} \rtimes \mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, the Wigner UIR classification by mass and spin, the canonical commutator $[\widehat{q}, \widehat{p}] = i\hbar$, the unitary one-parameter group $U(t) = e^{-i\widehat{H}t/\hbar}$, the McGucken Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{McGucken}}$, Noether currents $j^{\mu}_{X}$, the $CPT$ operator $\Theta$, the Wightman field axioms, and all derived algebraic structure.

### Definition PT1 (Wigner's antiunitary time-reversal operator $T$)

The operator $T : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}$ is the involution defined as the geometric and algebraic content of Wigner 1932's antiunitary time-reversal operator, with the following properties:

*(i) Sphere reversal:* $T \cdot \Sigma^{+}(p) \cdot T^{-1} = \Sigma^{-}(p)$, where $\Sigma^{-}(p)$ is the past-directed light cone of $p$.

*(ii) Orientation reversal:* $T \cdot (+ic) \cdot T^{-1} = -ic$.

*(iii) Antilinearity on complex amplitudes:* $T \cdot i \cdot T^{-1} = -i$, i.e. $T$ anti-commutes with the Frobenius-forced imaginary unit (Wigner 1932 antilinear convention).

*(iv) Spatial invariance:* $T \cdot x_{j} \cdot T^{-1} = x_{j}$ for $j = 1, 2, 3$.

*(v) Temporal reversal:* $T \cdot t \cdot T^{-1} = -t$.

*(vi) Momentum and angular-momentum reversal:* $T \cdot \widehat{p}_{j} \cdot T^{-1} = -\widehat{p}_{j}$, $T \cdot \widehat{J}_{jk} \cdot T^{-1} = -\widehat{J}_{jk}$.

*(vii) Hamiltonian invariance:* $T \cdot \widehat{H} \cdot T^{-1} = \widehat{H}$ (the Hamiltonian is $T$-invariant for time-translation-invariant systems; this is the content of Stone's theorem applied to the time-translation symmetry being preserved under $T$).

*(viii) Square:* $T^{2} = (-1)^{2s}$ where $s$ is the spin of the system ($T^{2} = +1$ for integer spin, $T^{2} = -1$ for half-integer spin; Kramers 1930).

Equivalently in algebraic terms: $T$ is the antiunitary operator on the McGucken-generated Hilbert space $\mathcal{H} \cong L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{3}, d^{3}x)$ of [HilbertBorn2026, Theorem 6.1] satisfying $T \cdot i \cdot T^{-1} = -i$ and reversing the McGucken-Sphere orientation.

### Definition PT2 (The channel projection $\Pi_{A} : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$)

The channel projection $\Pi_{A}$ is the forgetful functor sending each Geometric-Channel object $X \in \mathcal{B}$ to its $T$-invariant content. Three equivalent formulations:

*(a) Restriction to the $T$-invariant subalgebra.*
$$\Pi_{A}(X) := X\bigr|_{\mathrm{Fix}(T)}$$
where $\mathrm{Fix}(T) = \{X \in \mathcal{B} : T X T^{-1} = X\}$ is the $T$-invariant subalgebra of $\mathcal{B}$.

*(b) Quotient by the $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ time-reversal involution.*
$$\Pi_{A} : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}/T = \mathcal{A}$$
where $T$ is treated as the $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ involution $+ic \leftrightarrow -ic$ on the geometric content.

*(c) Forgetful functor on the orientation triple $+ic = (+) \cdot (i) \cdot (c)$.*
$$\Pi_{A} : (+\,,\,i\,,\,c) \mapsto (i\,,\,c)$$
The projection retains the magnitude content $(c)$ and the perpendicularity content $(i)$ of $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ while forgetting the orientation content $(+)$.

The three formulations are equivalent. Formulation (a) is the cleanest for algebraic-QFT contexts where $T$ is already a defined operator on the Hilbert space; formulation (b) is the cleanest for categorical contexts where the $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$-quotient is the natural construction; formulation (c) is the cleanest for emphasizing what is preserved versus what is forgotten.

### Lemma PT2.1 (Π_A is well-defined)

*The map $\Pi_{A} : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$ is well-defined: $T$-invariant content of $\mathcal{B}$ is recognizable as Algebraic-Channel content of $\mathcal{A}$, and the operation respects the algebraic structure of $\mathcal{B}$.*

*Proof.* Every Algebraic-Channel object is $T$-invariant by direct inspection:

- The Lorentzian metric $\eta$ is $T$-invariant: $T (-c^{2}\,dt^{2} + d\mathbf{x}^{2}) T^{-1} = -c^{2}\,dt^{2} + d\mathbf{x}^{2}$ since $T$ flips $dt$ but $dt^{2}$ is even under the flip.
- The Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^{+}(1,3)$ is $T$-invariant: $T$ acts on the connected isometry group by inducing the involution that maps the connected component to itself (the future light cone and the past light cone are both invariant under $T$ as sets, even though their orientations flip).
- The Poincaré algebra $\mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$ is $T$-invariant under simultaneous flipping of all signs (translation generators $P^{\mu}$ flip with $t$; rotation generators preserve; boost generators flip).
- The canonical commutator $[\widehat{q}, \widehat{p}] = i\hbar$ is $T$-invariant: $T [\widehat{q}, \widehat{p}] T^{-1} = T \widehat{q} T^{-1} \cdot T \widehat{p} T^{-1} - T \widehat{p} T^{-1} \cdot T \widehat{q} T^{-1} = \widehat{q} \cdot (-\widehat{p}) - (-\widehat{p}) \cdot \widehat{q} = -[\widehat{q}, \widehat{p}]$, but $T (i\hbar) T^{-1} = -i\hbar$ by antilinearity, so both sides flip and the equation is preserved.
- The unitary one-parameter group $U(t) = e^{-i\widehat{H}t/\hbar}$ is $T$-related: $T U(t) T^{-1} = U(-t) = U(t)^{-1}$. Stone's theorem produces the same Hamiltonian from either direction of $t$.
- The Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{McG}}$ is $T$-invariant: $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{kin}}$, $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Dirac}}$, $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{YM}}$, $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{EH}}$ are each $T$-invariant by inspection of their term structure.
- Noether currents $j^{\mu}_{X}$ are $T$-related: $T j^{\mu}_{X} T^{-1} = j^{\mu}_{TXT^{-1}}$ (currents transform as $X$ transforms under $T$), so the conserved-charge content is $T$-invariant.
- The $CPT$ operator $\Theta = CPT$ is $T$-invariant: $T \Theta T^{-1} = T(CPT)T^{-1} = (T C T^{-1})(T P T^{-1})(T T T^{-1}) = C P T = \Theta$, since $C$ and $P$ commute with $T$.

So every Algebraic-Channel object is $T$-invariant. Conversely, every $T$-invariant element of $\mathcal{B}$ corresponds to a Algebraic-Channel object: the McGucken-Sphere $\Sigma^{+}(p) \cup \Sigma^{-}(p)$ symmetrized over orientation is the full light cone of $p$, which is the Algebraic-Channel null-cone content of $p$; the time-translation-invariant content of the McGucken-Sphere expansion gives the Hamiltonian content; etc. The map $\Pi_{A}$ sends each $T$-invariant element to its Algebraic-Channel counterpart, preserving algebraic structure (commutators, brackets, currents). $\blacksquare$

## Theorem PT1 (Constructive Independence of the Algebraic Channel)

**Theorem PT1 (Constructive Independence of the Algebraic Channel from the Geometric Channel).** *Algebraic Channel's apparatus — the Lorentzian metric, the Lorentz and Poincaré groups, Stone's theorem and the canonical commutator, the Wigner UIR classification, the Lagrangian and Noether currents, the $CPT$ operator, the Wightman field axioms — can be developed constructively from algebraic foundations alone, with no reference to the McGucken Sphere, no reference to the iterated Huygens propagation, and no reference to the $+ic$ orientation.*

*Proof.* The historical record is the constructive proof. The Algebraic Channel's apparatus was developed by the following chain of works without any McGucken-Sphere input:

(i) *Lorentzian metric and Lorentz group:* Lorentz 1904 (length-contraction calculations); Poincaré 1905 (relativity principle, group structure); Einstein 1905 (special relativity from two postulates); Minkowski 1908 (geometric four-dimensional formulation). None of these works invoked the McGucken Sphere as an input; the Lorentzian metric was extracted from Maxwell's equations via the requirement of frame-independence of the speed of light.

(ii) *Poincaré group and algebra:* Wigner 1939 (*On Unitary Representations of the Inhomogeneous Lorentz Group*) constructed $\widetilde{\mathrm{ISO}}(1,3)$ and classified its UIRs by orbit and little group, using only the algebraic structure of the metric and the translation/rotation/boost generators. No Sphere input.

(iii) *Stone's theorem and the canonical commutator:* Stone 1932 (*On one-parameter unitary groups in Hilbert space*) proved that every strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group has a unique self-adjoint infinitesimal generator. Heisenberg 1925 and Born–Jordan 1925 introduced the canonical commutator $[\widehat{q}, \widehat{p}] = i\hbar$ as a foundational algebraic relation; Dirac 1925 derived it from the Poisson bracket via the correspondence principle. (iv) *Wightman field axioms:* Wightman 1956 (*Quantum Field Theory in Terms of Vacuum Expectation Values*) axiomatized relativistic QFT in terms of operator-valued distributions, the spectrum condition, locality, Poincaré covariance, and vacuum cyclicity. No Sphere input.

(v) *$CPT$ theorem:* Pauli 1955 (*Exclusion principle, Lorentz group and reflexion of space-time and charge*), Lüders 1954 (*On the equivalence of invariance under time reversal and under particle-antiparticle conjugation for relativistic field theories*), Jost 1957 (*Eine Bemerkung zum CTP-Theorem*), and Bargmann–Hall–Wightman 1957 derived $CPT$ from Lorentz invariance, locality, and spin-statistics using only the analytic continuation of Lorentz transformations to the complex Lorentz group. No Sphere input.

(vi) *Lagrangian and Noether currents:* Hamilton 1834 (principle of stationary action); Lagrange 1788 (calculus of variations); Noether 1918 (*Invariante Variationsprobleme*) established the symmetry-conservation theorem. The Standard Model's $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SM}}$ and its Noether currents (Glashow 1961, Weinberg 1967, Salam 1968) were constructed by gauge-symmetry imposition without any McGucken-Sphere input.

(vii) *Mackey induction and irreducible representation theory:* Mackey 1952 (*Induced representations of locally compact groups, I*) developed the induced-representation machinery for non-compact groups, enabling Wigner's classification. No Sphere input.

(viii) *Bargmann–Hall–Wightman analytic continuation:* Bargmann–Hall–Wightman 1957 established the analytic continuation of the Lorentz group to the complex Lorentz group, enabling the $CPT$ theorem. No Sphere input.

The historical record establishes that the Algebraic Channel's apparatus is constructively independent: every Algebraic-Channel theorem can be reached from algebraic foundations (Hilbert space, operator algebra, variational calculus, group theory, analytic continuation) without invoking the McGucken Sphere or its $+ic$ orientation. ## Theorem PT3 (The Projection Theorem: the Algebraic Channel is the T-Invariant Image of the Foundational Geometric Channel)

**Theorem PT3 (The Projection Theorem: $\mathcal{A} = \Pi_{A}(\mathcal{B})$).** *Algebraic Channel's content equals the $T$-invariant image of the Geometric Channel's content under the forgetful functor $\Pi_{A}$. Every Algebraic-Channel theorem $T_{A} \in \mathcal{A}$ satisfies $T_{A} = \Pi_{A}(T_{B})$ for some $T_{B} \in \mathcal{B}$; conversely every $T$-invariant element $T_{B} \in \mathcal{B}$ projects to a Algebraic-Channel theorem $\Pi_{A}(T_{B}) \in \mathcal{A}$. The map $\Pi_{A}$ is surjective onto $\mathcal{A}$ and respects the algebraic structure (commutators, brackets, currents, conservation laws).*

*Proof.* In four steps.

*Step 2 (Surjectivity of $\Pi_{A}$).* For every Algebraic-Channel theorem $T_{A}$ — Lorentzian metric, Lorentz/Poincaré algebra, $[\widehat{q}, \widehat{p}] = i\hbar$, Stone's theorem, $CPT$, Noether's first theorem, the Lagrangian — there exists a Geometric-Channel counterpart $T_{B} \in \mathcal{B}$ that projects to $T_{A}$:
