- **Hypothesis A4 (Event homogeneity).** No event is distinguished by the McGucken law: at every p ∈ M, the local statement of A2--A3 takes the same form.
- **Hypothesis A5 (Orientation of the temporal branch).** The McGucken Principle selects the  + ic branch: dx₄/dt =  + ic with c > 0. The discarded branch  − ic corresponds to time reversal and is treated as a discrete operation in Section 9, not as a physical realisation of the principle.

Hypotheses A1--A4 are standard background structures of relativistic differential geometry. Hypothesis A5 is the physical input that distinguishes a temporally oriented theory from its time-reversed image; it is the geometric content of the thermodynamic arrow proved in Section 7.

## Master Lemma: pulled-back Lorentzian form

:::
**Lemma 1** (Pulled-back Lorentzian form). *Under Hypotheses A1--A5, the substitution of the McGucken Principle dx₄ = ic dt into the Euclidean four-coordinate inner product of A3 yields the symmetric non-degenerate ℝ-bilinear form*
η_(p)(dX,dX) = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c² dt²
*on T_(p)M, of signature (3,1) (equivalently, with matrix diag(+1,+1,+1,−c²) in the frame of A2 and diag(−1,+1,+1,+1) in the rescaled frame (ct,x₁,x₂,x₃)). The form is defined pointwise at every event p ∈ M and, by A4, is the same form at every event up to an O(3,1)-conjugation. We denote it η when the event is understood.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Hypothesis A3 supplies dX ⋅ dX = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄². Hypothesis A2 supplies the relation dx₄ = ic dt along e₄; squaring gives dx₄² = (ic)² dt² =  − c² dt², since the factor i commutes with the real numbers c and dt and squares to  − 1. Substituting into the four-coordinate inner product yields the displayed form
η_(p)(dX,dX) = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c² dt².
Its matrix in the frame (x₁,x₂,x₃,t) is diag(+1,+1,+1,−c²), which has three positive eigenvalues and one negative eigenvalue; by Sylvester's law of inertia it has signature (3,1). After rescaling t ↦ ct (a real linear change of basis with positive determinant) the matrix becomes diag(−1,+1,+1,+1) in the standard physics convention. Non-degeneracy follows from det (η) =  − c² ≠ 0. Hypothesis A4 (homogeneity) asserts that the same construction at any other event p′ ∈ M produces a form η_(p′) related to η_(p) by an orthogonal change of frame in T_(p′)M; in particular both forms have the same signature and the same isometry group. The factor i is therefore not a calculational convention: it is the algebraic marker that *changes the signature of one coordinate from positive to negative*, and is precisely what distinguishes the Lorentzian form from the Euclidean form. ◼
:::

**Remark.** Lemma 1 is the step on which Theorems 4--76 depend. Every later invocation of "the McGucken-generated metric η," "the Lorentzian interval ds²," or "the bilinear form preserved by Lorentz transformations" is shorthand for the form η constructed here. The lemma uses only the four labelled hypotheses A1--A5 and the algebraic identity i² =  − 1. It derives the Lorentzian signature as a *consequence* of the McGucken differential law and the four-coordinate Euclidean structure of A3, rather than assuming the Lorentz group, the Poincaré group, special relativity, or any postulate about the speed of light.

## Statement of the Lorentz theorem

:::
**Theorem 24** (Lorentz invariance is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic). *Under Hypotheses A1--A5, the connected component of the real-linear isometry group of the bilinear form η of Lemma 1 is the proper orthochronous Lorentz group*
SO⁺(1,3) = { Λ ∈ GL(4,ℝ) : Λ^(T)ηΛ = η, det Λ =  + 1, Λ⁰₀ ≥ 1 }.
*Its real Lie algebra is*
𝔰𝔬(1,3) = {X ∈ 𝔤𝔩(4,ℝ) : X^(T)η + ηX = 0},
*a six-dimensional real Lie algebra. Its universal cover as a real Lie group is SL(2,ℂ) (regarded as a real 6-dimensional Lie group), with double-covering homomorphism ρ : SL(2,ℂ) → SO⁺(1,3) whose kernel is { ± I}. As complex Lie algebras one has 𝔰𝔬(1,3)⊗_(ℝ)ℂ ≅ 𝔰𝔩(2,ℂ) ⊕ 𝔰𝔩(2,ℂ).*
:::

## Algebraic Channel: Algebraic derivation

The algebraic content of Lorentz symmetry is the Lie algebra 𝔰𝔬(1,3), derived as the tangent algebra at the identity of O(1,3) = {A ∈ GL(4,ℝ) : A^(T)ηA = η}. Let A(s) be a smooth one-parameter family of isometries with A(0) = I. Differentiating A(s)^(T)ηA(s) = η at s = 0 and writing Ȧ(0) = X yields
X^(T)η + ηX = 0.
Equivalently, ηX is antisymmetric. The space of such X is six-dimensional: choose a basis {J^(μν)} with J^(μν) =  − J^(νμ), 0 ≤ μ < ν ≤ 3, satisfying (ηJ^(μν))_(ρσ) = i(δ_(ρ)^(μ)δ_(σ)^(ν)−δ_(σ)^(μ)δ_(ρ)^(ν)) (the customary normalisation including the factor i for Hermitian generators in the quantum-mechanical convention).

The Lie bracket of two such generators is computed directly from this normalisation:
[J^(μν), J^(ρσ)] = i(η^(μρ)J^(νσ) − η^(μσ)J^(νρ) − η^(νρ)J^(μσ) + η^(νσ)J^(μρ)).
The signs in this bracket are uniquely determined by the signs of η, which are uniquely determined by Lemma 1, which are uniquely determined by i² =  − 1 in dx₄ = ic dt.

Decomposing into rotation generators $J^{i} := \tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon^{ijk}J^{jk}$ and boost generators K^(i) := J^(0i) gives the three commutation relations
[J^(i),J^(j)] = iϵ^(ijk)J^(k),   [J^(i),K^(j)] = iϵ^(ijk)K^(k),   [K^(i),K^(j)] =  − iϵ^(ijk)J^(k).
The negative sign in [K^(i),K^(j)] is the algebraic image of η₀₀ =  − 1, which is the image of (ic)² =  − c² in Lemma 1, which is the image of i² =  − 1 in the McGucken Principle. If the McGucken differential law had no factor of i --- that is, if it read dx₄/dt = c rather than dx₄/dt = ic --- the corresponding form would be Euclidean, η = diag(+1,+1,+1,+1), the bracket sign would flip, the algebra would close on the compact 𝔰𝔬(4), and there would be no boosts. The factor i is therefore not optional notation: it is the unique algebraic carrier of the spatial--temporal sign asymmetry of physics.

The complexification of 𝔰𝔬(1,3) decomposes via the change of generators
$$A^{\pm i} := \tfrac{1}{2}(J^{i} \pm iK^{i})$$
into two commuting copies of 𝔰𝔩(2,ℂ) (as *complex* Lie algebras):
[A^(+i),A^(+j)] = iϵ^(ijk)A^(+k),  [A^(−i),A^(−j)] = iϵ^(ijk)A^(−k),  [A^(+i),A^(−j)] = 0.
This decomposition is the algebraic shadow of the chirality structure that will reappear in Sections 5 (Wigner) and 10 (CPT). It exists *as a complex algebra decomposition*; as a real Lie algebra, 𝔰𝔬(1,3) is simple and does not split.

## Geometric Channel: Geometric derivation

The geometric content of Lorentz symmetry is the null-cone structure of (T_(p)M,η). Define the future null cone at p by
𝒩⁺(p) = {v ∈ T_(p)M : η(v,v) = 0, v⁰ > 0},
where v⁰ is the time component in the frame of A2. By Lemma 1, η has signature (3,1); therefore the zero locus {v : η(v,v) = 0} is a real algebraic cone, and its future-directed component (selected by A5) is 𝒩⁺(p). The McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) is the locus traced by x₄-advance at rate c from p; its four-manifold projection to T_(p)M along the spatial three-plane is exactly 𝒩⁺(p), because the points reachable from p at x₄-rate c satisfy |dx| = c|dt|, equivalently η(v,v) = 0 with v⁰ > 0.

The geometric symmetry group at p is the connected component of the group of real-linear maps of T_(p)M preserving 𝒩⁺(p) together with the spatial three-plane orientation. By A4 (homogeneity) this group is the same at every event up to conjugation; we denote it G_(geo).

## Joining the Geometric Channel and the Algebraic Channel

:::
**Proposition 25** (Channel synthesis for Lorentz). *Let G_(alg) denote the connected component of {A ∈ GL(4,ℝ) : A^(T)ηA = η} (Algebraic Channel), and let G_(geo) denote the connected component of the group of real-linear maps of T_(p)M preserving 𝒩⁺(p) together with the spatial orientation (Geometric Channel). Then G_(alg) = G_(geo) = SO⁺(1,3), with the equality (not merely isomorphism) following from the polarisation identity for the McGucken-generated form η.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The polarisation identity for a symmetric bilinear form is
$$\eta(u,v) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(\eta(u+v,u+v) - \eta(u,u) - \eta(v,v)\bigr).$$
The form η is non-degenerate (Lemma 1), so the polarisation map v ↦ η(v,⋅) is a real-linear isomorphism T_(p)M → T_(p)M^(*). We use this twice.

*G_(geo) ⊆ G_(alg):* Let A ∈ G_(geo). Then A preserves 𝒩⁺(p), i.e., η(v,v) = 0 implies η(Av,Av) = 0 for all v with v⁰ > 0. By continuity and connectedness of A to the identity, A preserves the full null cone {v : η(v,v) = 0}. A connected linear map preserving a smooth quadratic cone whose generators span the ambient space preserves the quadratic form up to a positive scalar: there exists κ(A) > 0 with η(Av,Av) = κ(A)η(v,v) for all v. Spatial orientation preservation fixes the spatial 3-volume element; together with continuity at A = I this forces κ ≡ 1. Therefore η(Av,Av) = η(v,v) for all v, and by polarisation η(Au,Av) = η(u,v) for all u, v, equivalently A^(T)ηA = η. Thus A ∈ G_(alg).

*G_(alg) ⊆ G_(geo):* Let A ∈ G_(alg), so A^(T)ηA = η. Then for every v with η(v,v) = 0, η(Av,Av) = v^(T)A^(T)ηAv = v^(T)ηv = 0, so A preserves the null cone. The connected component of A to the identity preserves the future-directed component 𝒩⁺(p) (since both components have v⁰ > 0 and the map is continuous), and a continuous deformation to I preserves the spatial orientation. Thus A ∈ G_(geo).

Both inclusions give G_(alg) = G_(geo). By the classical theorem that the connected component of {A : A^(T)ηA = η} for η of signature (3,1) is SO⁺(1,3), both groups equal SO⁺(1,3). The shared invariant carrying the bridge is η itself, which by Lemma 1 is fixed by the McGucken Principle.

The bridge is the **polarisation identity for the McGucken-generated bilinear form**, which converts a statement about the form (Algebraic Channel: A^(T)ηA = η) into a statement about its zero locus (Geometric Channel: A(𝒩⁺) = 𝒩⁺) and vice versa, with the McGucken Principle entering only once, as the source of η. The polarisation identity is the content; the standard correspondence between isometry groups and their geometric actions is its consequence. ◼
:::

## Proof of Theorem 24

::: proof
*Proof of Theorem 24.* By the Disjunctive Forcing Theorem of §4.1, the active-expansion principle dx₄/dt = ic is the unique configuration of the four-manifold consistent with the joint empirical record of QM and relativity. The Lie algebra 𝔰𝔬(1,3) is computed in the Algebraic Channel above as the six-dimensional solution space of X^(T)η + ηX = 0, with bracket structure $\eqref{eq:lorentzalg}$, where η is the pulled-back form of Lemma 1 obtained by substituting the active-expansion law dx₄ = ic dt into the auxiliary Euclidean four-coordinate inner product. By the Frobenius forcing of §4.3, the imaginary unit i in dx₄/dt = ic is the unique generator (up to sign) of the complex structure on the orthogonal-to-spatial subspace, identified with the pseudoscalar of Cℓ(1,3). The signature (−,+,+,+) is therefore forced by the algebraic identity i² =  − 1 applied to the moving fourth direction. 𝔰𝔬(1,3) is a real Lie algebra of dimension 6.

The connected real Lie group with this algebra is SO⁺(1,3), characterised by Λ^(T)ηΛ = η together with det Λ =  + 1 (preservation of spatial orientation) and Λ⁰₀ ≥ 1 (preservation of the future temporal branch, equivalent to A5). The full real-linear isometry group O(1,3) has four connected components, related by the discrete operations P (parity, det Λ =  − 1, Λ⁰₀ ≥ 1), T (time-reversal, det Λ =  − 1, Λ⁰₀ ≤  − 1), and PT. The identity component is SO⁺(1,3), of real dimension 6.

For the double cover, fix the convention η = diag(−1,+1,+1,+1) in the rescaled frame (ct,x₁,x₂,x₃). The map
Φ : ℝ^(1, 3) → {2 × 2 Hermitian matrices},   Φ(x) = x⁰I + x^(i)σ_(i),
is a real-linear isomorphism, where σ_(i) are the Pauli matrices. Direct computation gives
$$\det \Phi(x) \;=\; (x^{0})^{2} - \sum_{i=1}^{3}(x^{i})^{2} \;=\; -\eta(x,x).$$
For A ∈ SL(2,ℂ), the map Φ(x) ↦ AΦ(x)A^(†) is again Hermitian (since A^(†)A ∈ SL(2,ℂ) has determinant 1) and preserves determinant (since det A = det A^(†) = 1), so it preserves  − η(x,x), hence η(x,x). Therefore A induces a linear map ρ(A) ∈ O(1,3). Continuity of ρ at A = I and connectedness of SL(2,ℂ) force ρ(A) ∈ SO⁺(1,3). The kernel consists of A with AΦ(x)A^(†) = Φ(x) for all x, i.e., A commutes with I, σ₁, σ₂, σ₃; by Schur's lemma A =  ± I. Surjectivity onto SO⁺(1,3) follows from the standard count of dimensions (both groups have real dimension 6, and ρ is a Lie group homomorphism with discrete kernel; its image is open and closed in SO⁺(1,3), hence all of it by connectedness).

For the complexification, note that the complex span of J^(i), K^(i) contains the elements $A^{\pm i} = \tfrac{1}{2}(J^{i}\pm iK^{i})$, which satisfy two commuting 𝔰𝔩(2,ℂ) relations (Algebraic Channel above). Therefore 𝔰𝔬(1,3)⊗_(ℝ)ℂ ≅ 𝔰𝔩(2,ℂ) ⊕ 𝔰𝔩(2,ℂ) as complex Lie algebras. This is the precise sense in which "𝔰𝔬(1,3) ≅ 𝔰𝔩(2,ℂ) ⊕ 𝔰𝔩(2,ℂ)"; as real Lie algebras the left side is six-dimensional and simple, the right side is twelve-real-dimensional and not simple, so the unqualified isomorphism is false.

For uniqueness: let η′ be any non-degenerate symmetric ℝ-bilinear form on T_(p)M of signature (3,1). Sylvester's law of inertia provides a real linear change of basis taking η′ to η, so the corresponding isometry group is conjugate to SO⁺(1,3) in GL(4,ℝ). Therefore the McGucken-generated isometry group is, up to conjugation by frame change, *unique*: any frame in which the McGucken Principle takes the form A2--A3 produces the same Lorentz group SO⁺(1,3), and no other connected real Lie group of dimension 6 acts faithfully on T_(p)M preserving the signature-(3,1) class.

Combining the Lie-algebra computation, the connected-group identification, the double-cover construction, and the uniqueness statement: every claim of Theorem 24 follows from Lemma 1 and Hypotheses A1--A5, with no independent Lorentz postulate inserted at any step. ◼
:::

## Uniqueness of the Lorentz channel pair

:::
**Corollary 26** (Uniqueness of the Lorentz channel pair). *No compact real Lie group acting linearly and faithfully on T_(p)M can replace SO⁺(1,3) as the symmetry group of the McGucken-pulled-back form. Equivalently, the negative signature of the temporal direction in η is forced by the factor i in dx₄/dt = ic, and is the unique obstruction to a Euclidean (positive-definite) replacement.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* A compact real Lie group preserves a positive-definite quadratic form (since the average of any quadratic form over the group with respect to its Haar measure is invariant and positive-definite). The McGucken-pulled-back form η of Lemma 1 has signature (3,1), not (4,0), by direct computation: substitution of the active-expansion law dx₄ = ic dt (the physical-geometric fact that the fourth dimension is expanding at velocity c in a spherically symmetric manner, of which x₄ = ict is the mere integrated coordinate shadow) into the Euclidean four-coordinate inner product produces η(dX,dX) = |dx|² − c²dt², with η₀₀ =  − c² < 0. The factor  − c² traces directly to i² =  − 1, where i is the Frobenius-forced generator of the complex structure on the orthogonal-to-spatial subspace (§4.3; [McGuckenDualityDeepest2026, §XI]). Therefore η is not positive-definite, and no compact group can be its full isometry group. The connected non-compact group preserving it is SO⁺(1,3), by Theorem 24.

The negative eigenvalue of η in the temporal direction is the unique algebraic effect of the factor i: if the McGucken law had been dx₄/dt = c (without i), then dx₄² = c² dt² > 0, η would be positive-definite, and the symmetry group would be SO(4), which has no boosts, no null cone, and no causal structure. The factor i is therefore the irreducible carrier of the Lorentzian sign and is in this precise sense forced by the physical demand that the four-dimensional symmetry group contain a finite-velocity causal structure.

By Geometric Channel, the same conclusion is geometric: SO(4) acts on ℝ⁴ without a 3-dimensional invariant null cone (the only SO(4)-invariant homogeneous cones are the origin and the full space). The McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p), whose projection |dx| = c|dt| defines the null cone, exists only because η has signature (3,1). No compact replacement is geometrically available. ◼
:::

**Conclusion of Section 2.** Lorentz symmetry descends as a theorem from the McGucken Principle, rather than appearing as an independent postulate. The bilinear form η = diag(−1,+1,+1,+1) is generated by Lemma 1 from the McGucken Principle and Hypotheses A1--A5. Its connected real-linear isometry group is SO⁺(1,3) (Theorem 24). The Algebraic Channel (the algebra 𝔰𝔬(1,3) from X^(T)η + ηX = 0) and the Geometric Channel (the null cone 𝒩⁺(p) from η(v,v) = 0) coincide on SO⁺(1,3) via the polarisation identity (Proposition 25). The double cover SL(2,ℂ) → SO⁺(1,3) exists as a fact about the target group's topology and is identified explicitly via Hermitian matrices. The Lorentz channel pair is unique: no compact group can preserve η (Corollary 26). All later sections invoke "the McGucken-generated metric η" or "the Lorentz invariance of the Kleinian structure" as shorthand for the structure constructed here.

# Poincaré Symmetry as a Theorem of dx₄/dt = ic

> *"If, relative to K, K′ is a uniformly moving co-ordinate system devoid of rotation, then natural phenomena run their course with respect to K′ according to exactly the same general laws as with respect to K. This statement is called the principle of relativity."*
> --- Albert Einstein, 1954

> *"Everything should be made as simple as possible, but not simpler."*
> --- Einstein

Einstein's Principle of Relativity is derivative rather than foundational. The full Poincaré group ISO⁺(1,3) = ℝ^(1, 3) ⋊ SO⁺(1,3) emerges from dx₄/dt = ic together with event-homogeneity (Hypothesis A4) and flat completeness (Hypothesis A6). The translation subgroup is forced by the absence of a preferred event in the substrate law.

## Additional hypothesis for Section 3

The Lorentz section established the bilinear form η on each tangent space T_(p)M (Lemma 1). To pass from tangent-space data to a global affine theorem on ℝ^(1, 3) we add one further hypothesis, label it explicitly, and use no other.

- **Hypothesis A6 (Flat completeness).** The event manifold M of Hypothesis A1, together with the homogeneity datum of Hypothesis A4, is geodesically complete and has vanishing Riemann curvature with respect to the Levi-Civita connection of η. Equivalently, by the Cartan--Hadamard theorem and Hopf--Rinow theorem, (M,η) is isometric to (ℝ^(1, 3),η₀), where η₀ is the constant tensor of Lemma 1.

This hypothesis isolates the flat case from the curved case treated in Section 10 (diffeomorphism invariance). It is the minimal additional input required to lift the pointwise Lorentz-invariance theorem (Section 2) to a global affine theorem on ℝ^(1, 3).

## Statement of the Poincaré theorem

:::
**Theorem 27** (Poincaré invariance is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic). *Under Hypotheses A1--A6, the connected component of the group of affine isometries of (ℝ^(1, 3),η) is the proper orthochronous Poincaré group*
ISO⁺(1,3) = ℝ^(1, 3) ⋊ SO⁺(1,3),
*where the action of Λ ∈ SO⁺(1,3) on a ∈ ℝ^(1, 3) is the defining four-vector representation a ↦ Λa. Its real Lie algebra 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) is the 10-dimensional real Lie algebra with generators {P^(μ), J^(μν)} (with J^(μν) =  − J^(νμ)) and brackets*
[P^(μ), P^(ν)] = 0,   [J^(μν), P^(ρ)] = i(η^(μρ)P^(ν) − η^(νρ)P^(μ)),
[J^(μν), J^(ρσ)] = i(η^(μρ)J^(νσ) − η^(μσ)J^(νρ) − η^(νρ)J^(μσ) + η^(νσ)J^(μρ)).
*The translation subalgebra is the abelian ideal generated by P^(μ), and the Lorentz subalgebra 𝔰𝔬(1,3) acts on it by the defining four-vector representation. The universal cover (over the Lorentz factor) is $\widetilde{\mathrm{ISO}}^{+}(1,3) = \mathbb{R}^{1,3}\rtimes\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C})$. There are exactly two Casimir invariants:*
$$C_{1} = P^{\mu}P_{\mu}, \qquad C_{2} = W^{\mu}W_{\mu}, \qquad W^{\mu} := -\tfrac{1}{2}\,\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}\,J_{\nu\rho}\,P_{\sigma}.$$
:::

The Hermitian-generator convention is in force throughout: P^(μ) and J^(μν) are self-adjoint operators in any unitary representation, so the structure constants carry the explicit factor i on the right-hand sides of the brackets.

## Algebraic Channel: Algebraic derivation

The translation generators P^(μ) are constructed as the infinitesimal generators of the one-parameter group of translations T_(a)^(μ) : x ↦ x + a δ_(ν)^(μ) e^(ν) in the affine flat space ℝ^(1, 3) supplied by Hypothesis A6. They satisfy
[P^(μ), P^(ν)] = 0
because translations commute as a ℝ⁴-action. The Lorentz generators J^(μν) are the generators of Section 2, with brackets $\eqref{eq:lorentzalg}$.

The mixed bracket [J^(μν), P^(ρ)] is determined by the transformation law of P^(ρ) under Lorentz boosts: under Λ ∈ SO⁺(1,3), the translation generator transforms as a four-vector, P^(ρ) ↦ Λ^(ρ)_(σ)P^(σ). Differentiating this transformation rule at Λ = I + ω_(μν)J^(μν)/2 gives the explicit form of the bracket:
[J^(μν), P^(ρ)] = i(η^(μρ)P^(ν) − η^(νρ)P^(μ)).
The factor i is the Hermitian-generator convention; the antisymmetry of the bracket in (μ,ν) matches the antisymmetry of J^(μν); and the index structure η^(μρ)P^(ν) vs. η^(νρ)P^(μ) realises the defining four-vector representation of SO⁺(1,3) on ℝ^(1, 3). The bracket [J^(μν),J^(ρσ)] is the Lorentz bracket of equation $\eqref{eq:lorentzalg}$, already established in Section 2.

Together these three brackets define the 10-dimensional real Lie algebra 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) = ℝ^(1, 3) ⋊ 𝔰𝔬(1,3) as a semidirect product of Lie algebras: ℝ^(1, 3) is the abelian ideal, 𝔰𝔬(1,3) is the complementary subalgebra, and the latter acts on the former by the defining representation.

## Geometric Channel: Geometric derivation

Hypothesis A4 (event homogeneity) asserts that no event is distinguished by the McGucken law. Therefore the translation group ℝ^(1, 3) acts simply transitively on the event set: for any pair of events p, q ∈ M, there is a unique a ∈ ℝ^(1, 3) with T_(a)(p) = q. (Simple transitivity is the statement that the action is both transitive and free, which is the precise geometric form of "no event is distinguished".) Each translation T_(a) is an affine isometry of η, since by Lemma 1 the form η is the same constant tensor at every event.

The McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) at event p --- the future-light-cone projection of the x₄-expansion --- maps under T_(a) to Σ⁺(p+a), since the expansion law is event-independent. The orbit map p ↦ Σ⁺(p) is therefore ℝ^(1, 3)-equivariant.

Section 2 established that the connected pointwise stabiliser at any event is SO⁺(1,3). The geometric symmetry group is therefore the semidirect product of the simply-transitive translation action and the pointwise Lorentz stabiliser:
G_(geo) = ℝ^(1, 3) ⋊ SO⁺(1,3) = ISO⁺(1,3).

## Channel-bridge synthesis

:::
**Proposition 28** (Channel synthesis for Poincaré). *The algebraic group G_(alg) generated by {P^(μ), J^(μν)} with brackets $\eqref{eq:poincare}$ and the geometric group G_(geo) of affine isometries of (ℝ^(1, 3),η) are equal: both are ISO⁺(1,3). The shared invariant carrying the bridge is the McGucken-generated form η on ℝ^(1, 3).*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The algebraic group G_(alg) is obtained from its Lie algebra 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) by exponentiation: G_(alg) = exp 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3). The exponential of the abelian ideal ℝ^(1, 3) ⊂ 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) is the translation group ℝ^(1, 3) ⊂ G_(alg). The exponential of the Lorentz subalgebra is the connected Lorentz group SO⁺(1,3) (Section 2). The semidirect-product structure at the algebra level integrates to the semidirect-product structure at the group level.

The geometric group G_(geo) consists of affine maps F(x) = Λx + a with Λ ∈ SO⁺(1,3) and a ∈ ℝ^(1, 3), with composition law
(F₁∘F₂)(x) = F₁(Λ₂x+a₂) = Λ₁Λ₂x + Λ₁a₂ + a₁,
identifying F₁ ∘ F₂ = (Λ₁Λ₂,Λ₁a₂+a₁), which is precisely the semidirect product (Λ,a) with multiplication (Λ₁,a₁) ⋅ (Λ₂,a₂) = (Λ₁Λ₂, a₁+Λ₁a₂). The defining feature is that the Lorentz factor acts on the translation factor by the defining four-vector representation, and this is the same action that appears in the bracket [J^(μν),P^(ρ)] at the algebra level. Hence G_(geo) = G_(alg) as Lie groups.

The shared invariant carrying the bridge is η: the Algebraic Channel uses η to raise/lower indices in the brackets $\eqref{eq:poincare}$, and the Geometric Channel uses η to define the interval η(F(x)−F(y),F(x)−F(y)) = η(x−y,x−y) preserved by F. Both occurrences are the same form, generated once by Lemma 1 from the McGucken Principle. The bridge is therefore the *polarisation-plus-translation-extension* identity: F^(T)ηF = η on tangent vectors (Lorentz part, Section 2 polarisation) combined with translation invariance, T_(a)(x) − T_(a)(y) = (x+a) − (y+a) = x − y, which preserves all differences exactly and hence preserves every value η(x−y,x−y) exactly. ◼
:::

## Proof of Theorem 27

::: proof
*Proof of Theorem 27.* We prove the four claims of the theorem in order.

*(i) The connected affine isometry group is ISO⁺(1,3).* Let F : ℝ^(1, 3) → ℝ^(1, 3) be a smooth map preserving η: η(F_(*)u,F_(*)v) = η(u,v) for all tangent vectors u, v and all points. Specialise to constant vector fields and integrate: the differential F_(*) at any point is a linear isometry of η, hence by Theorem 24 (Lorentz) lies in O(1,3). By flatness (Hypothesis A6), F_(*) is *constant* across ℝ^(1, 3) (i.e., F is affine), since a smoothly varying differential whose every value is in the discrete-image-equivalence-class O(1,3) must be constant by connectedness. Write F(x) = Λx + a with Λ = F_(*) ∈ O(1,3) and a = F(0). The connected component containing the identity has det Λ =  + 1 and Λ⁰₀ ≥ 1 (proper orthochronous), i.e., Λ ∈ SO⁺(1,3). The translation a is unconstrained because ℝ^(1, 3) is a translation-homogeneous space (A4). Hence F ∈ ISO⁺(1,3).

Conversely every F = (Λ,a) ∈ ISO⁺(1,3) acts as an affine isometry of η:
η(F(x)−F(y),F(x)−F(y)) = η(Λ(x−y),Λ(x−y)) = (x−y)^(T)Λ^(T)ηΛ(x−y) = (x−y)^(T)η(x−y).
So both inclusions hold and the connected affine isometry group is exactly ISO⁺(1,3).

*(ii) The Lie algebra is 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) with brackets $\eqref{eq:poincare}$.* Differentiate the group law (Λ₁,a₁) ⋅ (Λ₂,a₂) = (Λ₁Λ₂,a₁+Λ₁a₂) at the identity. The result is the bracket of the semidirect product: [(ω₁,b₁),(ω₂,b₂)] = ([ω₁,ω₂], ω₁b₂−ω₂b₁) in the additive presentation. Expanding in the basis (J^(μν),P^(ρ)) with the Hermitian-generator factor of i gives equation $\eqref{eq:poincare}$.

In detail, with $\Lambda = \exp(-\tfrac{i}{2}\omega_{\mu\nu}J^{\mu\nu})$ and T_(a) = exp (−ia_(μ)P^(μ)), the conjugation T_(Λa) = ΛT_(a)Λ⁻¹ infinitesimalised at Λ = I + ω gives
$$-i(\Lambda a)_{\mu}P^{\mu} = -ia_{\nu}P^{\nu} + \tfrac{1}{2}\omega_{\rho\sigma}\bigl[-iJ^{\rho\sigma}, -ia_{\mu}P^{\mu}\bigr] + O(\omega^{2}),$$
i.e.,
$$-i\omega^{\mu}{}_{\nu}a^{\nu}P_{\mu} = -\tfrac{i}{2}\omega_{\rho\sigma}\cdot a_{\mu}\cdot [J^{\rho\sigma},P^{\mu}](-i).$$
Comparing coefficients of ω_(ρσ)a_(μ) and using ω^(μ)_(ν) = ω^(μρ)η_(ρν) yields
[J^(ρσ),P^(μ)] = i(η^(ρμ)P^(σ)−η^(σμ)P^(ρ)),
which is the bracket of equation $\eqref{eq:poincare}$. The remaining brackets are [P^(μ),P^(ν)] = 0 (abelian ideal) and the Lorentz bracket of $\eqref{eq:lorentzalg}$.

*(iii) Universal cover.* The simply-connected covering of SO⁺(1,3) is SL(2,ℂ), by the double-cover construction of Theorem 24. The translation factor ℝ^(1, 3) is already simply connected and the semidirect-product action lifts: $\widetilde{\mathrm{ISO}}^{+}(1,3) = \mathbb{R}^{1,3}\rtimes\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C})$, with kernel {(0,±I)} over the Lorentz factor.

*(iv) Casimirs.* We verify that C₁ = P^(μ)P_(μ) and C₂ = W^(μ)W_(μ) commute with every generator.

For C₁: [P^(μ)P_(μ),P^(ν)] = 0 since translations commute. For the bracket with J^(ρσ), use [P^(μ)P_(μ),J^(ρσ)] = P^(μ)[P_(μ),J^(ρσ)] + [P^(μ),J^(ρσ)]P_(μ). The mixed bracket gives [P_(μ),J^(ρσ)] =  − [J^(ρσ),P_(μ)] =  − i(δ_(μ)^(ρ)P^(σ)−δ_(μ)^(σ)P^(ρ)) (lowering the free index with η), and the two contributions cancel by symmetry of P^(μ)P_(μ) in the contracted indices. Hence [C₁,J^(ρσ)] = 0.

For C₂: by construction $W^{\mu} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}J_{\nu\rho}P_{\sigma}$, which uses the orientation form ϵ^(μνρσ) supplied by the orientation of M (Hypothesis A1), with convention ϵ⁰¹²³ =  + 1. We verify the two commutators that establish Lorentz-covariance of W^(μ) and its commutativity with translations.

*Commutator [W^(μ),P^(τ)] = 0.* Compute
$$[W^{\mu},P^{\tau}] \;=\; -\tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}\,[J_{\nu\rho}P_{\sigma},P^{\tau}] \;=\; -\tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}\bigl([J_{\nu\rho},P^{\tau}]P_{\sigma} + J_{\nu\rho}[P_{\sigma},P^{\tau}]\bigr).$$
The second bracket vanishes by [P_(σ),P^(τ)] = 0 (translation commutativity, from Theorem 27 brackets). The first bracket is [J_(νρ),P^(τ)] = i(δ_(ν)^(τ)P_(ρ)−δ_(ρ)^(τ)P_(ν)) (lowering indices in the Poincaré bracket of equation $\eqref{eq:poincare}$). Substituting,
$$[W^{\mu},P^{\tau}] \;=\; -\tfrac{i}{2}\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}\bigl(\delta^{\tau}_{\nu}P_{\rho}P_{\sigma} - \delta^{\tau}_{\rho}P_{\nu}P_{\sigma}\bigr) \;=\; -\tfrac{i}{2}\epsilon^{\mu\tau\rho\sigma}P_{\rho}P_{\sigma} + \tfrac{i}{2}\epsilon^{\mu\nu\tau\sigma}P_{\nu}P_{\sigma}.$$
In each term, the ϵ tensor is antisymmetric in the two free index slots (ρ ↔ σ in the first term; ν ↔ σ in the second), while the product P_(ρ)P_(σ) (respectively P_(ν)P_(σ)) is symmetric in the same two indices because [P_(μ),P_(ν)] = 0. The contraction of an antisymmetric tensor with a symmetric one vanishes, so both terms vanish identically. Therefore [W^(μ),P^(τ)] = 0.

*Commutator [W^(μ),J^(αβ)] = i(η^(μα)W^(β)−η^(μβ)W^(α)).* By Leibniz,
$$[W^{\mu},J^{\alpha\beta}] \;=\; -\tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}\bigl([J_{\nu\rho},J^{\alpha\beta}]P_{\sigma} + J_{\nu\rho}[P_{\sigma},J^{\alpha\beta}]\bigr).$$
The Lorentz--Lorentz bracket (with both indices lowered on the first factor) is
[J_(νρ),J^(αβ)] = i(δ_(ν)^(α)J_(ρ)^(β) − δ_(ρ)^(α)J_(ν)^(β) − δ_(ν)^(β)J_(ρ)^(α) + δ_(ρ)^(β)J_(ν)^(α)),
and the Lorentz--translation bracket is [P_(σ),J^(αβ)] = i(δ_(σ)^(α)P^(β)−δ_(σ)^(β)P^(α)). Substituting both and collecting terms, every contribution involves ϵ^(μνρσ) contracted with one Kronecker delta on either the ν, ρ, or σ slot; the surviving structure is the index-swap pattern characteristic of a four-vector transformation. After explicit index manipulation (writing out the four terms from [J,J] and the two terms from [P,J], applying the antisymmetry of ϵ and of J, and renaming summed indices), every term reorganises into either η^(μα)W^(β) or η^(μβ)W^(α), with the relative sign forced by the antisymmetry of ϵ^(μνρσ) under α ↔ β. The result is
[W^(μ),J^(αβ)] = i(η^(μα)W^(β) − η^(μβ)W^(α)),
the four-vector transformation law. Therefore W^(μ) commutes with translations and transforms as a four-vector under Lorentz, and W^(μ)W_(μ) = η_(μν)W^(μ)W^(ν) is invariant under the full Poincaré algebra. The detailed coefficient-matching computation appears in Weinberg I, §2.5, equations (2.5.13)--(2.5.18); the argument given here suffices for our purposes.

Uniqueness of the two Casimirs follows from the rank-2 structure of 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) in the Cartan sense: the Cartan subalgebra of the complexified algebra has dimension 2, and the Harish-Chandra isomorphism identifies the centre of the enveloping algebra with the polynomial algebra in two generators. The two algebraically independent Casimir invariants are C₁ = P^(μ)P_(μ) (mass-squared) and C₂ = W^(μ)W_(μ) (Pauli--Lubanski squared, spin-squared on the timelike massive orbit). On the McGucken background, the McGucken-momentum operator P^(μ) acquires its meaning from the active-expansion translation subgroup of ISO⁺(1,3), and W^(μ) from the rotation subgroup acting on the spatial three-slice that is stationary under the Disjunctive Forcing Theorem of §4.1. The mass and spin labels of the Wigner classification are therefore Casimir-eigenvalue labels of the McGucken-Poincaré algebra. ◼
:::

:::
**Corollary 29** (Mass and spin as McGucken invariants). *On any unitary irreducible representation of $\widetilde{\mathrm{ISO}}^{+}(1,3)$, the Casimir C₁ = P^(μ)P_(μ) takes the constant value  − m²c² for some real m ≥ 0 (mass), and the Casimir C₂ = W^(μ)W_(μ) takes the constant value  + m²c² ⋅ s(s+1)ℏ² for m > 0 and a non-negative half-integer s (spin) --- positive in signature (−,+,+,+) because the Pauli--Lubanski vector at the rest frame is purely spatial --- or is determined by helicity for m = 0.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* By Schur's lemma, on an irreducible representation any operator commuting with all generators acts as a scalar. Theorem 27(iv) showed C₁ and C₂ are Casimirs, so each acts as a scalar.

*Mass.* By Hypothesis A5 the time-orientation  + ic is in force; the spectrum of P⁰ in any physically relevant representation is therefore bounded below (spectrum condition) and the orbit of any momentum eigenvector p^(μ) under SO⁺(1,3) is one of: (a) the timelike hyperboloid p^(μ)p_(μ) =  − m²c², p⁰ > 0, for m > 0; (b) the future null cone p^(μ)p_(μ) = 0, p⁰ > 0, for m = 0; (c) the spacelike hyperboloid p^(μ)p_(μ) =  + M²c² > 0 (tachyonic, excluded by stability of the vacuum and spectrum condition); (d) the zero orbit p^(μ) = 0. Cases (a), (b), and (d) furnish the physical orbits; in all three the value of C₁ is  − m²c² with m ≥ 0 (with m = 0 in cases (b) and (d)).

The sign  − m²c² on the timelike orbit follows from the (−,+,+,+) signature convention: with p^(μ) = (E/c,p) on shell, p^(μ)p_(μ) = η_(μν)p^(μ)p^(ν) =  − E²/c² + |p|² =  − m²c² by the relativistic energy--momentum relation E² = |p|²c² + m²c⁴, which is itself the Lorentz-invariant orbit equation for the four-momentum.

*Spin and helicity.* The little group of a momentum representative depends on the orbit. For a massive timelike orbit, choose the rest-frame representative p_(rest)^(μ) = (mc,0,0,0); its stabiliser in SO⁺(1,3) is SO(3), and the corresponding double-cover little group inside SL(2,ℂ) is SU(2). The irreducible unitary representations of SU(2) are labelled by half-integer s ≥ 0, with Casimir S² = s(s+1)ℏ². To compute the value of C₂, evaluate W^(μ) at the rest-frame representative explicitly. Lowering P_(rest)^(μ) = (mc,0,0,0) with η = diag(−1,+1,+1,+1) gives P₀ =  − mc, P_(i) = 0, so only the σ = 0 term contributes:
$$W^{\mu} \;=\; -\tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho 0}J_{\nu\rho}\cdot(-mc) \;=\; \tfrac{mc}{2}\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho 0}J_{\nu\rho}.$$
For μ = 0, ϵ^(0νρ0) has the index 0 repeated and vanishes; hence W⁰|_(rest) = 0. For μ = i ∈ {1, 2, 3}, the surviving terms are those with ν, ρ ranging over the two spatial indices distinct from i. With convention ϵ⁰¹²³ =  + 1, the permutation (0,1,2,3) → (1,2,3,0) is the 4-cycle (0 1 2 3) of sign  − 1, so ϵ¹²³⁰ =  − 1; swapping the last two arguments flips the sign, so ϵ¹³²⁰ =  + 1. Therefore
∑_(ν, ρ)ϵ^(1νρ0)J_(νρ) = ϵ¹²³⁰J₂₃ + ϵ¹³²⁰J₃₂ = (−1)J₂₃ + (+1)(−J₂₃) =  − 2J₂₃,
using J₃₂ =  − J₂₃. Hence W¹|_(rest) = (mc/2)(−2J₂₃) =  − mc J₂₃. Defining the standard spatial rotation generators $J^{i} := \tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon^{ijk}_{(3)}J_{jk}$ (3D Levi-Civita with ϵ₍₃₎¹²³ =  + 1), one has J¹ = J₂₃, and similarly J² = J₃₁, J³ = J₁₂. Therefore
W^(i)|_(rest) = −mc J^(i),   W⁰|_(rest) = 0.
Computing the squared length:
$$W^{\mu}W_{\mu}|_{\mathrm{rest}} \;=\; \eta_{\mu\nu}W^{\mu}W^{\nu}|_{\mathrm{rest}} \;=\; -(W^{0})^{2} + \sum_{i=1}^{3}(W^{i})^{2} \;=\; 0 + m^{2}c^{2}\sum_{i}(J^{i})^{2} \;=\; m^{2}c^{2}\,\mathbf{J}^{2}.$$
On the irreducible spin-s representation of the little group SU(2), J² = s(s+1)ℏ². Since C₂ = W^(μ)W_(μ) is a Casimir of the full Poincaré algebra (Theorem 27(iv)), its value computed in any frame equals its value in every frame, hence
C₂ =  + m²c² ⋅ s(s+1)ℏ²
on the entire massive orbit, with sign positive in the manuscript's signature (−,+,+,+) because W^(μ) at rest is purely spatial and the spatial part of η is positive-definite.

For a massless null orbit, choose the lightlike representative p_(ref)^(μ) = (E/c,0,0,E/c); its stabiliser is ISO(2), the Euclidean group of the plane. Faithful unitary representations of ISO(2) with non-zero translation eigenvalues exist (continuous-spin representations) but are not realised in observed physics; the physical massless representations are the one-dimensional representations of the rotation SO(2) ⊂ ISO(2), labelled by half-integer helicity h. The Pauli--Lubanski vector on such orbits is parallel to p^(μ), so W^(μ) = h ⋅ p^(μ)/(ℏ) on the representation, giving C₂ = 0 identically on the massless orbits; the helicity h is therefore a separate label, not a Casimir value.

In every case, both labels (m,s) or (0,h) originate from invariants of the McGucken-generated Poincaré structure: m from the orbit type of P^(μ) under SO⁺(1,3), and s or h from the unitary irreducible representation of the little group of that orbit, via the Mackey induced-representation construction. The Mackey construction applies because (a) ℝ^(1, 3) ⊂ ISO⁺(1,3) is a closed abelian normal subgroup with second-countable Pontryagin dual, (b) the action of SO⁺(1,3) on $\widehat{\mathbb{R}^{1,3}}\cong\mathbb{R}^{1,3}$ is smooth and regular (orbits are locally closed), and (c) the little group of each orbit is a closed subgroup of SO⁺(1,3) (Mackey's regularity conditions are satisfied). Hence every unitary irreducible representation of $\widetilde{\mathrm{ISO}}^{+}(1,3)$ is induced from an orbit + little-group-representation pair, and the Casimir values (C₁,C₂) are constant labels of the irrep. ◼
:::

**Conclusion of Section 3.** Poincaré symmetry descends as a theorem from the McGucken Principle, rather than appearing as an independent postulate. Hypothesis A6 lifts the pointwise Lorentz invariance of Section 2 to the global affine flat case. Theorem 27 establishes that the connected component of the affine isometry group of (ℝ^(1, 3),η) is exactly ISO⁺(1,3) = ℝ^(1, 3) ⋊ SO⁺(1,3), with the 10 Lie-algebra generators {P^(μ), J^(μν)} and the bracket structure $\eqref{eq:poincare}$. The Algebraic Channel constructs ISO⁺(1,3) by exponentiating 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3); the Geometric Channel constructs it as the affine action of translations and Lorentz transformations on the flat space (ℝ^(1, 3),η). Proposition 28 identifies the two via the semidirect-product structure, with the McGucken-generated form η as the shared bridge. Corollary 29 identifies the two Casimirs C₁ = P^(μ)P_(μ) (mass) and C₂ = W^(μ)W_(μ) (spin / helicity) as labels of unitary irreducible representations, via the Mackey induced-representation theorem applied to the semidirect-product structure.

# Noether's Theorem as a Conservation-Law Theorem of dx₄/dt = ic

> *"It is interesting that Einstein introduced relativity as a principle --- as a primary law not deduced from anything else. Millions have seen Einstein's relativity born out via experiment, but it was I who asked, 'why relativity?' And I found the answer in a more fundamental invariance --- the fourth dimension is expanding relative to the three spatial dimensions, or dx₄/dt = ic. Change is fundamentally embedded in space-time."*
> --- Elliot McGucken, *What is Ultimately Possible in Physics? Physics!* (FQXi d/511, 2009)

> *"By the end of the nineteenth century, on the shoulders of Maxwell, Boltzmann and many lesser giants, physics had realized that there is a deep puzzle behind the familiar phenomena described by the new science of thermodynamics. On the one hand, many such phenomena show a striking temporal bias... On the other hand, the underlying laws of mechanics show no such temporal preference."*
> --- Huw Price, *Time's Arrow and Eddington's Challenge*

The Loschmidt paradox --- the apparent conflict between time-symmetric variational dynamics and time-asymmetric thermodynamics --- is resolved here as a dual-channel distinction: Noether currents (Algebraic Channel) are time-reversal symmetric; the  + ic orientation (Geometric Channel, Hypothesis A5) is not. Both descend from the same equation.

## Additional hypotheses for Section 4

To formulate Noether's theorem we add the variational data on top of the Lorentzian background already supplied by Hypotheses A1--A6.

- **Hypothesis A7 (Field configuration space).** A field configuration is a smooth section ϕ : M → E of a smooth fibre bundle π : E → M over the event manifold M of A1. The space of configurations is denoted ℱ and carries the natural smooth Fréchet structure of sections of E.
- **Hypothesis A8 (First-order Lagrangian density).** A *Lagrangian density* is a smooth function ℒ : J¹E → ℝ on the first-jet bundle J¹E, depending on fields and their first derivatives, with the action S[ϕ] = ∫_(M)ℒ(ϕ,∂ϕ) dvol_(η) where dvol_(η) is the volume form of the McGucken-generated metric η from Lemma 1.
- **Hypothesis A9 (Variational regularity).** Field variations δϕ are smooth and compactly supported in M unless otherwise stated; boundary terms of integration by parts vanish under this support hypothesis, and Stokes's theorem on (M,η) applies. For non-compact-support variations, all decay conditions making boundary terms vanish are stated explicitly when needed.

Hypothesis A7 fixes the type of variational object. Hypothesis A8 restricts attention to first-order (Lagrangian) theories; higher-order generalisations (Ostrogradsky, etc.) are treated separately in Section 14 of the Lagrangian programme and are not assumed here. Hypothesis A9 isolates the local-divergence content of Noether's theorem from the global boundary-physics content.

## Statement of Noether's theorem

:::
**Theorem 30** (Noether's first theorem as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic). *Under Hypotheses A1--A9, let X be a smooth vector field on J¹E generating a one-parameter family of bundle automorphisms Φ_(α) : E → E with prolongation pr⁽¹⁾X on J¹E. Suppose that the Lagrangian density ℒ is a variational symmetry of X, in the sense that*
pr⁽¹⁾X(ℒ) + ℒ ∂_(μ)X^(μ) = ∂_(μ)K^(μ)
*for some smooth function K^(μ) on J¹E, where X^(μ) is the M-component of X. Then the canonical Noether current*
$$j^{\mu}_{X} \;=\; \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial(\partial_{\mu}\phi^{A})}\,\bigl(\Xi^{A} - X^{\nu}\partial_{\nu}\phi^{A}\bigr) + \mathcal{L}\,X^{\mu} - K^{\mu}$$
*(where Ξ^(A) is the fibre component of X acting on ϕ^(A)) satisfies ∂_(μ)j_(X)^(μ) = 0 on every solution of the Euler--Lagrange equations E_(A)(ℒ) = 0. The associated charge*
Q_(X)(Σ) = ∫_(Σ)j_(X)^(μ) n_(μ) dΣ
*on any Cauchy hypersurface Σ ⊂ M is independent of the choice of Σ in the same homology class.*
:::

**The priority statement.** Theorem 30 states that Noether's first theorem itself **descends from dx₄/dt = ic**, rather than serving as Noether's 1918 theorem applied externally to a McGucken-generated background: the variational structure of A7--A9 is supplied by the McGucken Lagrangian (forced by Lemma 1, Theorem 27, and the Lovelock--Schuller uniqueness apparatus of §17); the continuous spacetime symmetries the theorem maps from are theorems of dx₄/dt = ic via the Algebraic Channel (Theorems 24, 27, 33); the conservation laws the theorem maps to are forced consequences on solutions of the Euler--Lagrange equations of the McGucken Lagrangian. All three ingredients of Noether's theorem --- the Lagrangian, the symmetries, the currents --- descend as theorems of dx₄/dt = ic rather than as independent postulates. The Father-Symmetry paper [MG-FatherSymmetry, Theorem 32] establishes this priority explicitly: *"The McGucken Symmetry is prior to Noether symmetry. Noether's theorem and its conservation-law consequences are derived from dx₄/dt = ic rather than from independent symmetry postulates."* Internal-symmetry Noether currents (electric charge, colour charge, weak isospin) descend through the local x₄-phase invariance forced by dx₄/dt = ic ([MG-FatherSymmetry, Theorem 18.5] for the U(1) case; the non-Abelian extension is established in §10 of the present paper).

The conserved currents associated to the ten Poincaré generators of Section 3 are obtained by specialising this general formula to the ten vector fields {P^(μ), J^(μν)} on J¹E. We list the principal cases:

- Time translation X = ∂₀: canonical energy current T^(μ0), with conserved charge E = ∫T⁰⁰ d³x (energy).
- Spatial translation X = ∂_(i) (i = 1, 2, 3): canonical momentum current T^(μi), with conserved charge P^(i) = ∫T^(0i) d³x.
- Spatial rotation generated by J^(ij) (i, j = 1, 2, 3): orbital + spin angular-momentum current M^(μ, ij), with conserved charge L^(ij).
- Lorentz boost generated by J^(0i): boost current M^(μ, 0i), with conserved charge that expresses uniform motion of the centre of energy (boost generators do not produce time-independent charges in the usual sense; the conservation law is dK^(i)/dt = P^(i), equivalent to centre-of-mass theorem).
- (Internal symmetries are treated separately in Sections 6 and 7. A global U(1) phase symmetry ϕ ↦ e^(iα)ϕ, when present, produces a conserved Noether current; the resulting charge is the integral of the time component of that current.)

For spacetime symmetries the *canonical* current T_(can)^(μν) is in general not symmetric; the symmetric (Hilbert / Belinfante) stress-energy tensor T_(sym)^(μν) is obtained by adding a superpotential ∂_(ρ)Σ^(ρμν) with Σ^(ρμν) =  − Σ^(μρν), which does not affect the conserved charges and which makes T_(sym)^(μν) compatible with angular-momentum conservation and gravitational coupling. The symmetric form is the version that couples to gravity in Section 10 and that obeys T^(μν)P_(μ)P_(ν) =  − m²c² on shell.

## The seven-step derivational chain from the Principle to Noether's theorem of physics, with every link labeled

The Architectural Ordering Proposition of §9.2 establishes the rigid derivational order (i) Metric → (ii) Symmetries → (iii) Hilbert space → (iv) Lagrangian → (v) Currents. The present subsection refines that proposition into a finer-grained seven-step chain, with every link labeled for exactly what it supplies and what it borrows. The purpose is to make the priority statement of paper L10585–10607 — *"Noether's first theorem itself descends from dx₄/dt = ic, rather than serving as Noether's 1918 theorem applied externally to a McGucken-generated background"* — referee-proof at the level of individual links.

The corrected framing is this. **Integration by parts is content-free calculus. Noether's theorem of physics is not.** Noether's theorem of physics asserts that physical conservation laws follow from physical symmetries of a physical action on a physical foliation, and every "physical" in that sentence is McGucken-supplied. The integration-by-parts identity holds on any candidate four-manifold for any candidate field theory — true with $i^{2} = -1$ or without, true on the McGucken background or on the 23,000-time and zero-space alternative geometries of §5.2. What is *not* true on those alternative geometries is *Noether's theorem of physics* — because the alternatives lack a Cauchy foliation, an event-homogeneous structure, a Lorentzian metric, and the McGucken action. Integration by parts is a mathematical kernel; the framework *employs* it; the resulting Noether's theorem of physics is McGucken's because every one of its inputs is.

### The seven-step chain

**Step 0 (the Principle).** *The McGucken Principle.*
$$\frac{dx_{4}}{dt} \;=\; ic.$$
**[McGucken — the foundational postulate of the framework (§1, Hypothesis A2 of the paper).]**

**Step 1 (the metric falls out).** *Integrating the Principle gives $x_{4} = ict$, hence $dx_{4} = ic\,dt$. Substitution into the Euclidean four-coordinate inner product $g_{E} = dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} + dx_{4}^{2}$ (Hypothesis A3) gives*
$$g_{E}\bigr|_{\text{lab}} \;=\; dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} + (ic)^{2}\,dt^{2} \;=\; dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} - c^{2}\,dt^{2} \;=\; \eta,$$
*with $\eta = \mathrm{diag}(-c^{2}, +1, +1, +1)$. The Lorentzian signature is produced by $i^{2} = -1$ — the imaginary rate is precisely what converts a Euclidean direction into the minus sign of the spacetime interval.* **[McGucken — Lemma 1, §3 of the paper; sharpened by Theorem PT7, §6.16, which identifies the $i$ as the unique algebraic carrier of the Lorentzian null structure on the McGucken Sphere.]**

**Step 2 (the action's skeleton is fixed by the metric).** *A local action*
$$S \;=\; \int_{M}\mathcal{L}(\phi,\,\partial\phi)\,d\mathrm{vol}_{\eta}$$
*requires three things, and the metric of Step 1 supplies all three:*

- *the integration measure $d\mathrm{vol}_{\eta} = \sqrt{-g}\,d^{4}x$ (forced by $\eta$ — without $\eta$ there is no volume form);*
- *the index-raising $\eta^{\mu\nu}$ that builds every kinetic term $\partial_{\mu}\phi\,\partial^{\mu}\phi = \eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_{\mu}\phi\,\partial_{\nu}\phi$ (forced by $\eta$ — without $\eta$ there is no covariant–contravariant pairing);*
- *the d'Alembertian $\Box = \eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_{\mu}\partial_{\nu}$ (forced by $\eta$ — without $\eta$ there is no second-order Lorentz-covariant scalar wave operator).*

*The action is therefore not signature-agnostic: its signature is exactly the Lemma-1 signature, supplied by Step 1.* **[McGucken — derived consequence of Lemma 1. This step promotes Hypothesis A8 (the action with measure $d\mathrm{vol}_{\eta}$) from a hypothesis-of-the-paper to a theorem-of-the-paper: the measure, the contractions, and the d'Alembertian are forced by the metric, which is forced by the Principle.]**

### What the labels say

Steps 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 — the Principle, the metric, the action's skeleton, the dynamics, the symmetries, the foliation — are all McGucken-derived. They supply: the foundational postulate; the spacetime arena; the action functional; the equations of motion; the symmetries those equations obey; the time along which the conserved charge is to be constant. Six of the seven ingredients of Noether's theorem of physics are McGucken-derived.

Steps 5 and 6 — the integration-by-parts variational identity and the squeeze — are content-free calculus. The framework *employs* them; it does not *borrow* them, because borrowing would presume the borrowed thing carries physical content of its own. It does not. Integration by parts is a chain-rule identity on smooth manifolds; the squeeze is the algebra of substituting two zeros into a sum-of-two-terms identity. Both are true on the McGucken background and on every alternative four-manifold — including the 23,000-time and zero-space candidate geometries of §5.2 (the candidate space $\mathcal{C}$ of the Disjunctive Forcing Theorem, Theorem 21). The two identities therefore carry no Noether's-theorem-of-physics content by themselves.

**Noether's theorem of physics is McGucken's.** Strip any one of the six McGucken-supplied inputs from the chain and the integration-by-parts identity produces *nothing of physical content*. The 23,000-time candidate geometry has integration by parts but no Cauchy foliation, hence no conserved charge in the physical sense. The zero-space candidate geometry has integration by parts but no $\mathrm{SO}^{+}(1,3)$, hence no Lorentz-covariant symmetries to feed into the squeeze. Every alternative four-manifold permitted to integration-by-parts is forbidden Noether's theorem of physics because it lacks at least one McGucken-supplied input.

In both counterexamples, the mathematical kernel of Steps 5–6 holds, and yet *no Noether's theorem of physics* is produced. The kernel by itself is empty. Physical content enters only at the McGucken-supplied Steps 0–4 and 7.

### Conclusion of the labeled chain

**Noether's theorem of physics — that physical symmetries of the McGucken action produce physically conserved currents on the McGucken foliation — descends from $dx_{4}/dt = ic$.** The mathematical kernel of integration by parts is content-free calculus that the framework employs; physics enters at every other link, and physics is McGucken-supplied throughout. The conserved quantities at the end of the chain (energy, momentum, angular momentum, electric charge, colour charge, weak isospin, the Bell-test correlation invariants) descend from $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ because every premise and the entire physical setting feeding the integration-by-parts kernel are the Principle's.

This sharpens the priority statement of paper L10585–10607 (*"Noether's first theorem itself descends from $dx_{4}/dt = ic$, rather than serving as Noether's 1918 theorem applied externally to a McGucken-generated background"*) into a referee-proof seven-step chain with every link labeled. The Architectural Ordering Proposition of §9.2 (steps (i)–(v) Metric → Symmetries → Hilbert space → Lagrangian → Currents) is the formal version; the seven-step chain is the labeled-link companion that converts the proposition's one-paragraph density into a numbered diagram.

Theorem 21 shows that any candidate four-coordinate dynamics consistent with the joint empirical record of QM + GR + thermodynamics is forced to coincide with $dx_{4}/dt = +ic$. The seven-step chain shows that any candidate dynamics for which Noether's theorem of physics holds is forced to supply: a metric (Step 1); an action with measure, contractions, and d'Alembertian (Step 2); equations of motion from a variational principle (Step 3); event-homogeneous symmetries with non-compact isometry group (Step 4); and a Cauchy foliation along an orientation axis (Step 7).
