## Standard hypotheses for the CPT theorem

The CPT theorem (Lüders 1954, Pauli 1955) is conditional on the standard hypotheses of relativistic quantum field theory. We list them explicitly. The McGucken framework supplies the background structure on which the theorem operates: the Lorentzian manifold (ℝ^(1, 3),η) of Lemma 1 (with η generated by the active-expansion law dx₄/dt = ic), the spectrum condition selecting the closed forward cone $\overline{V}^{+}$ via the  + ic orientation of A5, and the Frobenius-forced i (§4.3) that appears in the analytic continuation through the complex Lorentz group SO(1,3;ℂ). Proposition 45a below identifies the i in the forward-tube prescription, the i in the Wick rotation, and the i in dx₄/dt = ic as the same object --- three appearances of the Frobenius-forced generator of x₄-advance.

- **Hypothesis A15 (Quantum-field structure).** The system is a Wightman quantum field theory: a quadruple (ℋ,U,Φ,|Ω⟩) consisting of a separable Hilbert space ℋ (A10), a strongly continuous unitary representation U of the universal cover $\widetilde{\mathrm{ISO}}^{+}(1,3)$ of the Poincaré group (A10^(′)), a collection of operator-valued tempered distributions Φ_(α)(x) on M transforming in finite-dimensional representations of SL(2,ℂ) under U, and a Poincaré-invariant vacuum state |Ω⟩ that is the unique state of zero energy and momentum.
- **Hypothesis A16 (Locality / microcausality).** For spacelike separated points x, y ∈ M (i.e., η(x−y,x−y) > 0), the corresponding field operators commute or anticommute according to spin-statistics:
 [Φ_(α)(x), Φ_(β)(y)]_(±) = 0  whenever  η(x−y,x−y) > 0,
 where [⋅,⋅]₊ denotes anticommutator (fermionic case) and [⋅,⋅]⁻ commutator (bosonic case).
- **Hypothesis A17 (Spectrum condition).** A11 of Section 5, restricting the joint spectrum of {P^(μ)} to the closed forward cone $\overline{V}^{+}$.

A15--A17 are the standard Wightman axioms for relativistic QFT. The CPT theorem holds under exactly these hypotheses, plus the polynomial-bound assumptions on Wightman functions (which we leave implicit as part of the tempered-distribution structure of A15). The dual-channel architecture of the McGucken Principle enters by supplying the Lorentzian metric η (Lemma 1) used in A15--A17 and the  + ic orientation (A5) that distinguishes the time direction.

## Definitions of the discrete symmetries

The three discrete operations C, P, T are defined as follows.

*Spatial parity P:* the linear isometry P : M → M given by (x⁰,x^(i)) ↦ (x⁰,−x^(i)), which is a discrete Lorentz transformation with det P =  − 1 and P⁰₀ =  + 1. It maps the future cone $\overline{V}^{+}$ to itself.

*Time reversal T:* the linear isometry T : M → M given by (x⁰,x^(i)) ↦ (−x⁰,x^(i)), with det T =  − 1 and T⁰₀ =  − 1. It maps $\overline{V}^{+}$ to $\overline{V}^{-}$ (the past cone). By Wigner's theorem (Proposition 44 of Section 8) and the requirement that time-translation conjugate as TĤT⁻¹ = Ĥ (energy preserved by time reversal), the operator T implementing time reversal on ℋ is *antiunitary*.

*Charge conjugation C:* the involution exchanging particle and antiparticle Hilbert spaces. Concretely, on the field operator algebra, C acts on a free Dirac field ψ as ψ ↦ Cψ̄^(T) for a suitable charge-conjugation matrix C (with Cγ^(μT)C⁻¹ =  − γ^(μ)), exchanging the positive- and negative-frequency mode operators (creation operators for particles ↔ creation operators for antiparticles). For a complex scalar field, C : Φ ↦ Φ^(*).

On the full Lorentz group O(1,3), the four connected components are SO⁺(1,3) (identity component), P ⋅ SO⁺(1,3), T ⋅ SO⁺(1,3), and PT ⋅ SO⁺(1,3). The McGucken Principle's  + ic branch (A5) selects SO⁺(1,3) as the connected component physically realised by continuous deformation of the identity; the operations P, T, PT map between components but each is a Lorentz isometry of η.

## Statement of the CPT theorem

:::
**Theorem 45** (CPT theorem on the McGucken background). *Under Hypotheses A1--A17, every Wightman quantum field theory on the McGucken-generated Lorentzian background (ℝ^(1, 3),η) admits an antiunitary operator Θ : ℋ → ℋ, the CPT operator, satisfying:*

*(i) Θ U(Λ,a) Θ⁻¹ = U(Λ,−a) for all $(\Lambda,a)\in\widetilde{\mathrm{ISO}}^{+}(1,3)$;*

*(ii) Θ |Ω⟩=|Ω⟩ (the vacuum is Θ-invariant);*

*(iii) Θ P^(μ) Θ⁻¹ =  − P^(μ) (four-momentum is reversed: energy and three-momentum both flip sign);*

*(iv) Θ J^(μν) Θ⁻¹ = J^(μν) (angular momentum and boost generators are preserved);*

*(v) For each field Φ_(α)(x), Θ Φ_(α)(x) Θ⁻¹ = U_(α)^(β)Φ_(β)^(†)(−x), where U_(α)^(β) is determined by the Lorentz representation of Φ_(α).*
:::

The operator Θ is the product (in some order, depending on the specific definitions of C, P, T) of charge conjugation, parity, and time reversal. The factor i in the McGucken Principle plays a role in the proof, identified explicitly in the Algebraic Channel below.

## Algebraic Channel: Algebraic derivation via complex Lorentz analytic continuation

The standard proof of the CPT theorem (Jost 1957, Streater--Wightman 1964) proceeds by analytic continuation of Wightman functions W_(n)(x₁,...,x_(n)) = ⟨Ω|Φ(x₁)⋯Φ(x_(n))|Ω⟩ from the real Lorentzian domain to the *forward tube*
𝒯_(n) = {(ζ₁,...,ζ_(n − 1)) ∈ ℂ^(4(n−1)) : ζ_(k) = ξ_(k) − iη_(k), η_(k) ∈ V⁺},
where ξ_(k) = x_(k) − x_(k + 1) are the differences of consecutive arguments. The spectrum condition (A17) implies that W_(n), regarded as a tempered distribution in the differences, has a Fourier representation supported on the future cone, hence extends holomorphically to 𝒯_(n).

The *complex Lorentz group* SO(1,3;ℂ) = {Λ ∈ GL(4,ℂ) : Λ^(T)ηΛ = η, det Λ =  + 1} is connected (unlike its real form O(1,3), which has four components). The connected complex Lorentz group contains, in particular, the operation Λ =  − I (the "spatial+temporal total reflection," equivalent to PT in the real sense), reachable by a complex rotation through angle iπ in any SO(2;ℂ) subgroup. This is the geometric content of the *Wick rotation*: a continuous deformation in complex Lorentz space connecting the identity to the operation PT.

The CPT theorem is proved as follows (Jost's theorem). Wightman functions are Lorentz-covariant under the real Poincaré group; by analytic continuation in the forward tube, they are covariant under the connected complex Lorentz group. The operation PT =  − I is in this connected component; hence it acts as a symmetry of Wightman functions in the analytic continuation. Combined with the relation between Φ^(†)(x) and the time-reversal action (which connects creation and annihilation operators via complex conjugation), and the antiunitary nature of time reversal, the analytic continuation produces the desired antiunitary operator Θ = CPT implementing the symmetry on ℋ.

*Critical step.* The factor i in ζ = ξ − iη with η ∈ V⁺ --- the imaginary direction transported into the forward tube --- is the *same* imaginary unit i that appears in the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. This is the precise content of the following identification.

:::
**Proposition 45a** (Identification of the McGucken i with the Wick rotation). *The imaginary unit i in the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is the same imaginary unit i that effects the Wick rotation t → it from Lorentzian to Euclidean signature, and the same imaginary unit i that parameterises the forward-tube analytic continuation ζ = ξ − iη in the proof of the CPT theorem. The three occurrences denote one element of ℂ with a role across three distinct mathematical operations, rather than three different imaginary units.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The Wick rotation t →  − iτ converts the Lorentzian metric η = diag(−1,+1,+1,+1) to the Euclidean metric δ = diag(+1,+1,+1,+1) via dt =  − i dτ, hence  − c²dt² =  − c²(−i)²dτ² =  + c²dτ². The same algebraic identity i² =  − 1 that effects this signature change is the algebraic content of the McGucken Lemma 1 substitution dx₄ = ic dt, which gives dx₄² = (ic)²dt² =  − c²dt². Up to relabelling (x₄ ↔ τ, with appropriate orientation), these are the same operation: multiplying a real time-like increment by i to convert between Euclidean and Lorentzian signatures.

The forward-tube analytic continuation in the CPT proof uses the same identity. Wightman functions of real arguments x_(k) ∈ ℝ^(1, 3) extend holomorphically to complex arguments ζ_(k) = ξ_(k) − iη_(k) with η_(k) in the forward cone. The " − iη" prescription is the same i that converts Lorentzian to Euclidean signature: at η_(k) = c t_(k) ⋅ e₀ (pure time direction), ζ_(k) = ξ_(k) − ict_(k) e₀ --- the substitution converts the Lorentzian time component to an imaginary-rotated direction, which is the Wick prescription.

All three occurrences --- McGucken's dx₄/dt = ic, the Wick rotation t →  − iτ, and the forward-tube prescription ζ = ξ − iη --- exploit the same algebraic fact: multiplication by i in ℂ converts Euclidean to Lorentzian signature (or vice versa) at the level of quadratic forms. The McGucken Principle exhibits this i at the level of the substrate differential law; the Wick rotation exhibits it at the level of analytic continuation of Green's functions; the CPT theorem exhibits it at the level of complex Lorentz covariance. The unification is therefore a fact about i ∈ ℂ, not three independent uses of the same letter. ◼
:::

## Geometric Channel: Geometric derivation via orientation reversal

The geometric content of the CPT theorem is the *total reflection* x^(μ) ↦  − x^(μ) of spacetime, which is in SO⁺(1,3) analytically continued to the complex Lorentz group (via Proposition 45a above), and which corresponds to the operation PT on the real Lorentz group. The geometric meaning of PT is the inversion through the origin: x ↦  − x.

On the McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p), the operation PT maps the future cone at p to the past cone at p (and the future cone at  − p to the past cone at  − p, etc.), exchanging the future and past temporal branches at every event. The charge-conjugation operation C acts on the complex structure of the wavefunction: a charged particle has charge q; its antiparticle has charge  − q; charge conjugation maps the particle wavefunction ψ to a wavefunction ψ^(c) representing the antiparticle. At the level of the Dirac equation, this is the operation ψ ↦ Cψ̄^(T) as defined above.

The combined operation CPT is, geometrically: invert spacetime through the origin (which reverses both temporal and spatial orientation), and replace each field by its charge-conjugate. Under this operation, the McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) is sent to Σ⁺(−p), the future McGucken Sphere at the spatially+temporally reflected event. The orientation is preserved overall because CPT involves *three* reflections (one in C --- the complex structure; two in PT --- both spatial and temporal directions), and the product of three reflections in 4D Lorentz space is orientation-preserving on the *physical Hilbert space* (after accounting for the antiunitary nature of Θ).

## Proof of Theorem 45

::: proof
*Proof of Theorem 45.* By Hypothesis A15, the QFT has Wightman functions W_(n)(x₁,...,x_(n)). By A17 (spectrum condition), these functions extend holomorphically to the forward tube 𝒯_(n) in their differences (Wightman's reconstruction). By Lorentz covariance under the real Poincaré group and the connectedness of the complex Lorentz group, the analytic continuation is covariant under SO(1,3;ℂ) (Bargmann--Hall--Wightman theorem).

The element  − I ∈ SO(1,3;ℂ) (total reflection in spacetime) is in the connected complex Lorentz component. Therefore, in the analytic continuation,
W_(n)(ζ₁,...,ζ_(n − 1)) = W_(n)(−ζ₁,...,−ζ_(n − 1)).
Restoring to the real boundary ζ_(k) → ξ_(k) − i0 ⋅ η_(k) gives a relation between W_(n)(x₁,...,x_(n)) and W_(n)(−x₁,...,−x_(n)). Combined with the local commutativity (A16), this produces the Jost identity, which is the assertion that an antiunitary operator Θ exists implementing the desired transformation on the field operators.

Existence of Θ as an antiunitary operator on ℋ follows from the reconstruction theorem: the Wightman functions determine the Hilbert space, the field operators, the Poincaré representation, and the vacuum; the symmetry identified at the level of Wightman functions lifts to an antiunitary symmetry of the reconstructed quantum theory.

The transformation laws (i)--(v) follow by direct computation from the definition of Θ as the analytic continuation  − I:
- (i) Poincaré: ΘU(Λ,a)Θ⁻¹ = U(Λ,−a) because  − I commutes with Lorentz transformations and reverses translations.
- (ii) Vacuum invariance: the unique vacuum is Poincaré-invariant, hence in particular Θ-invariant.
- (iii) ΘP^(μ)Θ⁻¹ =  − P^(μ): directly from (i), differentiating in a.
- (iv) ΘJ^(μν)Θ⁻¹ = J^(μν): directly from (i), differentiating in Λ; the − sign on the orbital part cancels with the − sign on translations.
- (v) Field transformation: the explicit form of Θ on each field is computed from its Lorentz representation; the Hermitian conjugate appears because of the antiunitary nature of Θ.

The factor i in the McGucken Principle plays the role identified by Proposition 45a: the forward-tube prescription ζ = ξ − iη, the Wick rotation, and the substrate law dx₄/dt = ic all exploit the same imaginary unit i ∈ ℂ to convert between Euclidean-like and Lorentzian-like signatures and to enable analytic continuation in complex Lorentz space. CPT is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic in the precise sense that the i in the proof is the McGucken i, identified rather than via separate insertion. ◼
:::

:::
**Lemma 47** (Scope of the CPT theorem). *The CPT theorem proved here is conditional on the standard Wightman hypotheses A15--A17 (separable Hilbert space, Poincaré covariance, locality, spectrum condition, vacuum uniqueness, polynomial bounds). It does not assert that individual operations C, P, T are separately symmetries of any specific theory --- they are individually violated in observed physics (parity violation in weak interactions, Wu 1957; CP violation in kaon decays, Cronin--Fitch 1964). The theorem asserts only that the product CPT is a symmetry under the stated hypotheses.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The hypotheses A15--A17 are the standard Wightman axioms. Each plays a role: A15 (separable Hilbert space, tempered-distribution fields, Poincaré covariance, unique vacuum) supplies the setting; A16 (locality / microcausality) is required for the Jost identity at the level of Wightman functions; A17 (spectrum condition, positivity of energy) supplies the analytic structure of the forward tube. Removing any one hypothesis can destroy the conclusion: theories with continuous-spin representations, with non-positive metric, with non-local interactions, or without a unique vacuum can fail to be CPT-invariant.

The individual operations C, P, T are not generally symmetries of a given theory. The Standard Model violates P (weak interactions are chiral), CP (kaon and B-meson decays), and T (by CPT, T violation is equivalent to CP violation). Only the product CPT is a theorem under A15--A17; it is observationally consistent with all experimental data to date (CPLEAR, BaBar, Belle).

The scope of the CPT theorem in the McGucken framework is therefore: the theorem is true under the standard Wightman QFT hypotheses, with the role of i in the proof identified as the McGucken i (Proposition 45a). Specific dynamics (the Standard Model Lagrangian, beyond-Standard-Model extensions, etc.) enter as model-specific completions rather than as derivations from the McGucken Principle. ◼
:::

**Conclusion of Section 9.** The CPT theorem is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic in the conditional sense made explicit by Hypotheses A15--A17 and Lemma 47. Under the standard Wightman axioms of relativistic QFT, every quantum field theory on the McGucken-generated Lorentzian background admits an antiunitary CPT operator Θ (Theorem 45). The proof's analytic continuation through the complex Lorentz group SO(1,3;ℂ) uses the *same* imaginary unit i ∈ ℂ that appears in the McGucken Principle (Proposition 45a). The unification of "McGucken i" = "Wick i" = "complex-Lorentz i" is the precise sense in which CPT inherits from dx₄/dt = ic. Only the product of the individual discrete symmetries C, P, T is derived as a theorem; the individual operations themselves are not separately required as symmetries.

# Diffeomorphism Invariance as a Theorem of dx₄/dt = ic

> *"In general relativity, Einstein showed that the dimensions themselves could bend, curve, and move. The present theory extends this principle, postulating that the fourth dimension is moving independently of the three spatial dimensions, distributing locality and fathering time."*
> --- Elliot McGucken, *Time as an Emergent Phenomenon* (FQXi d/238, 2008)

> *"Absolute, true, and mathematical time flows uniformly."*
> --- Isaac Newton, *Principia* (on the universe's foundational flux)

The local McGucken law dx₄/dt = ic extends to a curved spacetime (M,g) via the equivalence principle (Hypothesis A18). Lovelock's theorem identifies the Einstein--Hilbert action as the unique gravitational completion. Gravity is geometric curvature of the McGucken background, not a graviton on a fixed flat space.

## Additional hypotheses for Section 10

The diffeomorphism / general-relativistic completion replaces the flat-completeness hypothesis A6 with the curved-spacetime generalisation.

- **Hypothesis A6^(′) (Curved spacetime).** (M,g) is a connected, oriented, smooth four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold with metric tensor g of signature (−,+,+,+). At each event p ∈ M, g_(p) is the McGucken-generated bilinear form of Lemma 1, taken in a local orthonormal frame (equivalence principle).
- **Hypothesis A18 (Compatibility with the McGucken law).** The local relation dx₄/dt = ic holds in every local orthonormal frame at every event, with c the same numerical constant. This is the local-coordinate transport of A2--A5 to the curved case.
- **Hypothesis A19 (Lovelock conditions).** For the uniqueness of the Einstein--Hilbert action: (i) the gravitational Lagrangian density is a scalar function of g_(μν), ∂_(ρ)g_(μν), ∂_(ρ)∂_(σ)g_(μν) (second-order in derivatives), (ii) the Euler--Lagrange field equations are second-order in g, (iii) the spacetime dimension is n = 4.

Hypothesis A6^(′) is the standard differential-geometric setting for general relativity. Hypothesis A18 is the equivalence principle: every local orthonormal frame sees the McGucken Principle in its primitive Section-2 form. Hypothesis A19 supplies the conditions under which Lovelock's 1971 theorem yields uniqueness of the Einstein--Hilbert action.

## Statement of the diffeomorphism theorem

:::
**Theorem 48** (Diffeomorphism invariance is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic). *Under Hypotheses A1--A5, A6^(′), A18, A19, every smooth diffeomorphism φ : M → M of the curved spacetime manifold (M,g) acts on tensors by pullback and preserves the McGucken structure at each event. The infinitesimal generators of diffeomorphisms are the smooth vector fields ξ ∈ 𝔛(M), with Lie bracket*
[ξ,ζ]^(μ) = ξ^(ν)∂_(ν)ζ^(μ) − ζ^(ν)∂_(ν)ξ^(μ),
*and act on tensors by the Lie derivative ℒ_(ξ). The unique diffeomorphism-invariant gravitational action satisfying Hypothesis A19 is the Einstein--Hilbert action with cosmological constant*
$$S_{\mathrm{EH}}[g] = \frac{c^{4}}{16\pi G}\int_{M}(R - 2\Lambda)\sqrt{-g}\,d^{4}x,$$
*by Lovelock's theorem (1971). The corresponding Euler--Lagrange equations are the Einstein field equations*
$$R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2}g_{\mu\nu}R + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = \frac{8\pi G}{c^{4}}T_{\mu\nu},$$
*where T_(μν) is the (symmetric, Belinfante-improved) stress-energy tensor of the matter content. The cosmological constant Λ is not fixed by the McGucken Principle; in the empirical McGucken-cosmology programme it is identified with the homogeneous mode of the McGucken expansion field (Section 25).*
:::

## Algebraic Channel: Algebraic derivation via vector-field algebra

The infinite-dimensional Lie algebra of smooth vector fields on M is 𝔛(M) = Γ(TM), with the Lie bracket above. This algebra is the algebraic carrier of infinitesimal diffeomorphisms. The action of ξ ∈ 𝔛(M) on a tensor field T of any type is by the Lie derivative
$$\mathcal{L}_{\xi}T \;=\; \frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}\varphi_{s}^{*}T,$$
where φ_(s) is the one-parameter family of diffeomorphisms generated by ξ. On the metric tensor, ℒ_(ξ)g_(μν) = ∇_(μ)ξ_(ν) + ∇_(ν)ξ_(μ), where ∇ is the Levi-Civita connection.

A scalar action S[g,ϕ] is diffeomorphism-invariant if and only if ℒ_(ξ)S = 0 for all ξ ∈ 𝔛(M), which by integration by parts is equivalent to the tensor invariance S[g,ϕ] = S[φ^(*)g,φ^(*)ϕ] for all φ ∈ Diff(M). The Einstein--Hilbert action with the volume form $\sqrt{-g}\,d^{4}x$ and the Ricci scalar R (both diffeomorphism scalars) is manifestly invariant.

## Geometric Channel: Geometric derivation via curved-manifold McGucken structure

By Hypothesis A6^(′), (M,g) is a smooth Lorentzian 4-manifold; at every event p ∈ M, the tangent space T_(p)M carries the Lorentzian bilinear form g_(p), which by A18 is the McGucken-generated form of Lemma 1 in any local orthonormal frame. The equivalence principle (the geometric content of A18) is: every infinitesimally small neighbourhood of p ∈ M is, to first order, isometric to the flat Minkowski space of Section 2; the differences are second-order curvature effects.

A diffeomorphism φ : M → M acts on the McGucken structure by mapping Σ⁺(p) to Σ⁺(φ(p)): the future light cone at p is mapped to the future light cone at φ(p). This action is tensorial --- coordinate-independent --- because the light cone is the zero locus of the metric, and the metric transforms tensorially under diffeomorphisms.

The curvature of (M,g) --- encoded in the Riemann tensor R^(ρ)_(σμν), the Ricci tensor R_(μν), and the scalar curvature R --- measures the deviation of (M,g) from flat Minkowski space. In the limit of vanishing curvature, (M,g) reduces to (ℝ^(1, 3),η) of Section 3, recovering the flat case as Theorem 27.

## Channel-bridge synthesis

:::
**Proposition 49** (Channel synthesis for diffeomorphism). *The Algebraic-Channel construction (vector-field algebra 𝔛(M) acting on tensors by Lie derivative, with diffeomorphism-invariant scalar actions) and the Geometric-Channel construction (smooth Lorentzian manifold (M,g) with curved McGucken structure at each event) coincide. The bridge is the tensorial nature of the metric and its derivatives: tensor identities are coordinate-independent, hence equally well stated algebraically (Algebraic Channel) or geometrically (Geometric Channel). The shared invariant carrying the bridge is the metric tensor g itself, defined by Hypothesis A6^(′) + A18 as the curved-spacetime generalisation of the flat McGucken metric of Lemma 1.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The action of an infinitesimal diffeomorphism on a tensor field is, by definition, the Lie derivative along the generating vector field; this is Algebraic Channel. The same action, viewed as a change of coordinates on the manifold, is the pullback φ^(*); this is Geometric Channel. Direct computation shows the two operations agree:
$$\frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}\varphi_{s}^{*}T \;=\; \mathcal{L}_{\xi}T \quad\text{for any tensor field}\;T.$$
Therefore the Geometric Channel and the Algebraic Channel are two equivalent presentations of the same operation, with the bridge being the standard differential-geometric identity between Lie derivative (algebraic) and pullback derivative (geometric).

The metric tensor g is the shared invariant: in the Algebraic Channel, it is the object on which the vector-field algebra acts to produce Killing equations ℒ_(ξ)g = 0 (for isometries) or the general equation ℒ_(ξ)g = ∇ξ + ∇ξ (for arbitrary diffeomorphisms); in the Geometric Channel, it is the geometric data defining the local McGucken structure (A18) and the curvature.

The McGucken Principle's role is to supply the local form of g at every event: by A18, the local orthonormal frame at p ∈ M sees g_(p) as the form of Lemma 1, diag(−c²,+1,+1,+1). This is the equivalence principle in the McGucken framework: the same substrate-expansion law dx₄/dt = ic holds locally at every event, with the global structure of (M,g) encoded in how these local frames are glued together (curvature). ◼
:::

## Proof of Theorem 48

::: proof
*Proof of Theorem 48.* The three claims of the theorem are verified.

*(i) Diffeomorphism invariance of the McGucken structure.* By A18, the McGucken law dx₄/dt = ic holds at every event in every local orthonormal frame. A diffeomorphism φ : M → M maps each event p to φ(p) and each local orthonormal frame at p to a local orthonormal frame at φ(p) (the pushforward by dφ_(p), modulo a local Lorentz rotation). The McGucken law in the new frame at φ(p) is again dx₄/dt = ic, by A18 applied at φ(p). Therefore the McGucken structure is preserved by every diffeomorphism, in the sense that the local-frame statement of the law is invariant.

*(ii) Lovelock's theorem and the Einstein--Hilbert action.* Lovelock (1971) proved: in n = 4 dimensions, the most general symmetric divergence-free tensor 𝒢_(μν)(g,∂g,∂²g) built from the metric and its derivatives up to second order is
$$\mathcal{G}_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \alpha\bigl(R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2}g_{\mu\nu}R\bigr) + \beta g_{\mu\nu},$$
for real constants α, β. Setting α = c⁴/(8πG) and β =  − Λ c⁴/(8πG) identifies 𝒢_(μν) as the LHS of the Einstein equations.

The corresponding Lagrangian density is constructed explicitly from 𝒢_(μν) by inverting the variational relation $\delta(\mathcal{L}\sqrt{-g})/\delta g^{\mu\nu} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\mathcal{T}_{\mu\nu}\sqrt{-g}$ for the source-free case, where 𝒯_(μν) is identified with 𝒢_(μν). The Palatini identity δR = R_(μν)δg^(μν) + g^(μν)δR_(μν) gives, after using δR_(μν) = ∇_(ρ)δΓ_(μν)^(ρ) − ∇_(ν)δΓ_(ρμ)^(ρ) (which is a total divergence and integrates to zero with appropriate boundary conditions), the identity
$$\frac{\delta(R\sqrt{-g})}{\delta g^{\mu\nu}} = \bigl(R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2}g_{\mu\nu}R\bigr)\sqrt{-g}.$$
Combining this with $\delta\sqrt{-g}/\delta g^{\mu\nu} = -\tfrac{1}{2}g_{\mu\nu}\sqrt{-g}$ to handle the cosmological-constant term gives
$$\frac{\delta\bigl[(R - 2\Lambda)\sqrt{-g}\bigr]}{\delta g^{\mu\nu}} = \bigl(R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2}g_{\mu\nu}R + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu}\bigr)\sqrt{-g}.$$
The unique gravitational Lagrangian density yielding the Lovelock tensor 𝒢_(μν) + Λg_(μν) as Euler--Lagrange variation is therefore $\mathcal{L} = (c^{4}/16\pi G)(R - 2\Lambda)\sqrt{-g}$, with the normalisation α = c⁴/(8πG) chosen to match Newton's constant in the weak-field limit. The Euler--Lagrange variation
$$\frac{\delta}{\delta g_{\mu\nu}}\int\mathcal{L}\,d^{4}x \;=\; \frac{c^{4}}{16\pi G}\bigl(R^{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2}g^{\mu\nu}R + \Lambda g^{\mu\nu}\bigr)\sqrt{-g}$$
reproduces the LHS of Einstein's equations. Hypothesis A19 (second-order Lagrangian, second-order Euler--Lagrange, n = 4) is the standing input for Lovelock's theorem.

*(iii) Einstein field equations from variation.* Coupling to matter via the matter action S_(matter)[g,ϕ], the total action is
S = S_(EH) + S_(matter).
Variation with respect to g_(μν) gives
$$\frac{c^{4}}{16\pi G}\bigl(R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2}g_{\mu\nu}R + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu}\bigr) - \frac{1}{2}T_{\mu\nu} \;=\; 0,$$
with the matter stress-energy tensor
$$T_{\mu\nu} \;:=\; -\frac{2}{\sqrt{-g}}\frac{\delta(\sqrt{-g}\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{matter}})}{\delta g^{\mu\nu}}.$$
This is the Hilbert (symmetric) stress-energy tensor, automatically symmetric in (μ,ν). Rearranging gives the Einstein equation
$$R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2}g_{\mu\nu}R + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \frac{8\pi G}{c^{4}}T_{\mu\nu}.$$

*(iv) Cosmological constant Λ is not fixed by the McGucken Principle.* Lovelock's theorem allows Λ as a free parameter; the McGucken Principle determines only the Lorentzian signature (Lemma 1) and the diffeomorphism-invariant structure (Hypothesis A18). In the empirical McGucken-cosmology programme (Section 25), Λ is identified with the homogeneous mode of the McGucken expansion field f(t,x), and the dark-energy equation of state w ≈  − 1 emerges as a derived prediction; the unification is a separate empirical claim, not a derivation at the level of Theorem 48.

In every step, the McGucken Principle has entered through the local form of the metric (Lemma 1 transported to each tangent space via A18) and through the orientation of M (A1). The diffeomorphism invariance and the Einstein equations are consequences of this local structure plus Lovelock's theorem; no additional general-relativistic postulate has been inserted. ◼
:::

:::
**Corollary 50** (Covariant conservation from diffeomorphism invariance). *Diffeomorphism invariance of the matter-coupled action implies ∇_(μ)T^(μν) = 0 on solutions of the matter equations of motion.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* By Theorem 48, the action S[g,ϕ] = S_(EH) + S_(matter) is invariant under diffeomorphisms. Under an infinitesimal diffeomorphism generated by ξ^(ν), the metric varies by δg_(μν) = ∇_(μ)ξ_(ν) + ∇_(ν)ξ_(μ) and the matter fields vary by δϕ = ℒ_(ξ)ϕ. Invariance of S_(matter) gives, after integration by parts and using arbitrary compactly supported ξ:
$$0 = \delta S_{\mathrm{matter}} = \int\Bigl[\frac{\delta S_{\mathrm{matter}}}{\delta\phi}\mathcal{L}_{\xi}\phi + \frac{1}{2}T^{\mu\nu}(\nabla_{\mu}\xi_{\nu} + \nabla_{\nu}\xi_{\mu})\Bigr]\sqrt{-g}\,d^{4}x.$$
On solutions of the matter equations of motion, δS_(matter)/δϕ = 0. Integration by parts on the remaining term gives
$$0 \;=\; \int T^{\mu\nu}\nabla_{\mu}\xi_{\nu}\sqrt{-g}\,d^{4}x \;=\; -\int(\nabla_{\mu}T^{\mu\nu})\xi_{\nu}\sqrt{-g}\,d^{4}x.$$
Since ξ is arbitrary, ∇_(μ)T^(μν) = 0 on shell. This is the curved-spacetime Noether identity associated with diffeomorphism invariance, and the constraint that the matter stress-energy tensor satisfies in any general-relativistic theory. ◼
:::

## Remark: gravity without graviton

A standard result in flat-spacetime QFT (Feynman 1962, Weinberg 1965, Deser 1970) is that a Lorentz-invariant, unitarity-preserving theory of an interacting spin-2 quantum field on Minkowski space is necessarily nonlinear and equivalent to Einstein gravity in the weak-field limit. This is sometimes presented as "the graviton is a spin-2 quantum of the gravitational field, and Einstein's equations are forced by spin-2 + Lorentz + interaction self-consistency."

In the McGucken framework of Theorem 48, gravity arises as the curvature of the spacetime manifold (M,g) itself, rather than as a quantum field on a fixed Minkowski background. The local McGucken law dx₄/dt = ic holds at every event by A18; deviations from global flatness are encoded geometrically in g_(μν)(x), not in particle excitations on a fixed background. The Schwarzschild solution exemplifies this: the metric component g_(tt)(r) =  − (1−2GM/c²r) is the geometric statement that the local x₄-advance rate is modified near the mass M; this is a curvature effect, not a graviton exchange.

The standard graviton-search programme (LIGO direct detection of classical gravitational waves; speculative direct detection of single gravitons; perturbative quantum gravity calculations) lives in a perturbative expansion around flat Minkowski background, g_(μν) = η_(μν) + h_(μν), with h_(μν) the graviton field. The McGucken framework does not require the existence of an asymptotic-free graviton particle for the theorem-status of Einstein's equations to hold: the Einstein equations follow from Lovelock's theorem applied to the local McGucken-generated metric structure (Theorem 48), not from quantising a fluctuation field on a fixed background. This is the precise sense in which the McGucken programme is "gravity as geometry, not gravity as a particle." It is consistent with all classical-GR predictions (perihelion precession, light bending, gravitational redshift, LIGO waveforms) while remaining agnostic on whether the gravitational field has a particle-quantisation completion at energies above the Planck scale.

**Conclusion of Section 10.** Diffeomorphism invariance is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic under Hypotheses A6^(′), A18, A19. The local McGucken structure (Lemma 1 transported by A18 to every tangent space) extends to a smooth Lorentzian manifold (M,g) on which every diffeomorphism preserves the structure (Theorem 48). Lovelock's theorem identifies the Einstein--Hilbert action with cosmological constant as the unique gravitational action satisfying A19. The Einstein equations follow by variation; the contracted Bianchi identity ∇_(μ)T^(μν) = 0 is the Noether identity for diffeomorphism invariance (Corollary 50). The cosmological constant Λ is a free parameter at this level; the McGucken-cosmology programme of Section 25 identifies it with the homogeneous expansion-field mode. Gravity is treated as geometric curvature of the McGucken background, not as a graviton on a fixed flat space.

# Supersymmetry as a Conditional Graded Extension of the McGucken Algebra

> *"It is anomalous to replace the four-dimensional continuum by a five-dimensional one and then subsequently to tie up artificially one of those five dimensions in order to account for the fact that it does not manifest itself."*
> --- Albert Einstein to Paul Ehrenfest

> *"The important thing is not to stop questioning."*
> --- Einstein

Supersymmetry, if realised in Nature, is the unique non-trivial graded-Lie-algebra extension of the McGucken-Poincaré algebra (Theorem 51, via Coleman--Mandula and Haag--Łopusza\'nski--Sohnius). The McGucken framework neither requires nor excludes supersymmetry; current LHC limits remain consistent with both alternatives.

## Hypotheses for Section 11

We adopt the standard hypotheses of the Coleman--Mandula and Haag--{`\L`{=tex}}opusza\'nski--Sohnius theorems.

- **Hypothesis A20 (Coleman--Mandula hypotheses).** (i) The S-matrix is non-trivial: it relates initial and final states by more than just kinematic conservation laws and analytic continuation of the identity. (ii) There exist only finitely many particle types of any given mass below an arbitrary fixed bound (no continuous mass spectrum). (iii) The S-matrix is analytic in scattering angles. (iv) The symmetry generators acting on one-particle states are local operators (specifically, they map a one-particle state of given momentum to a finite linear combination of one-particle states of finite mass).
- **Hypothesis A21 (Graded-Lie-algebra extension).** Supersymmetry generators Q_(α)^(I) (and their conjugates Q̄_(α̇ I)) are admitted as *fermionic* (odd) generators, i.e., they anticommute among themselves rather than commute, and they commute with bosonic (even) generators. Here α = 1, 2 is a Weyl spinor index, α̇ = 1, 2 is the conjugate index, and I = 1, ..., 𝒩 labels the number of independent supersymmetries.

Hypothesis A20 is the standing hypothesis of the Coleman--Mandula no-go theorem (1967), which forbids non-trivial mixing of spacetime and internal *Lie* symmetries of the S-matrix. Hypothesis A21 is the graded-extension hypothesis under which the Haag--{`\L`{=tex}}opusza\'nski--Sohnius theorem (1975) classifies the graded Lie super-algebras consistent with the Coleman--Mandula no-go.

## Statement of the supersymmetry theorem

:::
**Theorem 51** (Mathematical uniqueness of supersymmetry as graded extension; empirical realisation is open). *Under Hypotheses A1--A11 and A20--A21, the unique non-trivial graded Lie super-algebra extending 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) with fermionic generators in $(\tfrac{1}{2},0)\oplus(0,\tfrac{1}{2})$ representations of 𝔰𝔩(2,ℂ) has the structure*
{Q_(α)^(I), Q̄_(β̇ J)} = 2 σ^(μ)_(αβ̇) P_(μ) δ^(I)_(J),
{Q_(α)^(I), Q_(β)^(J)} = ϵ_(αβ) Z^(IJ),   {Q̄_(α̇ I), Q̄_(β̇ J)} = ϵ_(α̇β̇) Z_(IJ)^(*),
[Q_(α)^(I), P_(μ)] = 0,   [Q_(α)^(I), J^(μν)] = i(σ^(μν))_(α)^(β) Q_(β)^(I),
*where the 𝒩 × 𝒩 central-charge matrix Z^(IJ) =  − Z^(JI) commutes with all generators of the super-algebra, σ^(μ) = (1,σ), σ̄^(μ) = (1,−σ), and $\sigma^{\mu\nu} = \tfrac{1}{4}(\sigma^{\mu}\bar\sigma^{\nu} - \sigma^{\nu}\bar\sigma^{\mu})$. The structure is unique up to the choice of 𝒩 ∈ {1, 2, 4, ...} (number of supersymmetries) and the central-charge matrix Z^(IJ). The translation generator P_(μ) on the right-hand side of the anticommutator is the McGucken-generated translation generator of Theorem 27. The empirical question of whether supersymmetry is realised in Nature is open; this theorem is a mathematical uniqueness statement about possible graded extensions, not an empirical assertion of realisation.*
:::

## Algebraic Channel: Algebraic derivation via Coleman--Mandula + HLS

The Coleman--Mandula theorem (1967) states: under Hypothesis A20, the most general Lie algebra of symmetries of the S-matrix in d ≥ 3 spacetime dimensions is
𝔤_(sym) = 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) ⊕ 𝔤_(int),
a direct sum of the Poincaré algebra (spacetime symmetries) and a compact internal Lie algebra 𝔤_(int) (internal symmetries). The two summands commute: no non-trivial mixing of spacetime and internal symmetries is possible within the framework of Lie algebras. The translation generator P_(μ) is the McGucken-generated translation generator of Theorem 27.

The Haag--{`\L`{=tex}}opusza\'nski--Sohnius theorem (1975) extends this to *graded* (super-)Lie algebras. Adding fermionic (odd) generators Q_(α)^(I) and Q̄_(α̇ I) that anticommute among themselves and transform under 𝔰𝔩(2,ℂ) in $(\tfrac{1}{2},0)$ and $(0,\tfrac{1}{2})$ representations respectively, the HLS theorem classifies the resulting super-algebras. The result is exactly the structure of Theorem 51: the anticommutator {Q, Q̄} closes on the translation generator P_(μ), the anticommutator {Q, Q} closes on the antisymmetric central-charge matrix Z^(IJ), the commutator [Q,P] vanishes (translations commute with SUSY), and the commutator [Q,J] realises the Lorentz action on the spinor index.

The uniqueness statement is: *given* Hypothesis A21 (graded extension), the algebra is forced to take this form. The minimal case is 𝒩 = 1 (one Weyl spinor pair), with no central charges (no antisymmetric 1 × 1 matrix). Higher 𝒩 (𝒩 = 2, 4, 8) admits non-trivial central charges and is relevant in extended supergravity and string theory.

## Geometric Channel: Geometric derivation via superspace

The geometric realisation of the supersymmetric algebra is *superspace*: an extension of Minkowski space ℝ^(1, 3) by Grassmann-odd coordinates θ_(α)^(I), θ̄_(I)^(α̇) with I = 1, ..., 𝒩. A superfield Φ(x,θ,θ̄) is a smooth function on superspace, and the SUSY generators act as differential operators (Wess--Bagger conventions; [Wess--Bagger 1992, §IV, eq. (4.5)]):
$$Q_{\alpha}^{I} \;=\; \frac{\partial}{\partial\theta^{\alpha}_{I}} - i\sigma^{\mu}{}_{\alpha\dot\beta}\,\bar\theta^{\dot\beta\,I}\partial_{\mu}, \qquad \bar Q_{\dot\alpha\,I} \;=\; -\frac{\partial}{\partial\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha\,I}} + i\theta^{\alpha}_{I}\,\sigma^{\mu}{}_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\partial_{\mu}.$$

We verify the anticommutator {Q_(α)^(I), Q̄_(β̇ J)} = 2σ^(μ)_(αβ̇)P_(μ)δ^(I)_(J) explicitly. Write Q = ∂_(α)^(I) + A_(α)^(I) and $\bar Q = -\bar\partial_{\dot\beta\,J} + B_{\dot\beta\,J}$ with A_(α)^(I) :=  − iσ^(μ)_(αγ̇)θ̄^(γ̇ I)∂_(μ) and B_(β̇ J) := iθ_(J)^(γ)σ^(ν)_(γβ̇)∂_(ν). Bilinearity gives
$$\{Q_{\alpha}^{I},\,\bar Q_{\dot\beta\,J}\} \;=\; -\{\partial_{\alpha}^{I},\bar\partial_{\dot\beta\,J}\} + \{\partial_{\alpha}^{I},B_{\dot\beta\,J}\} - \{A_{\alpha}^{I},\bar\partial_{\dot\beta\,J}\} + \{A_{\alpha}^{I},B_{\dot\beta\,J}\}. \tag{$\star$}$$

*Term 1:* $\{\partial_{\alpha}^{I},\bar\partial_{\dot\beta\,J}\} = 0$ because θ and θ̄ are independent Grassmann variables, hence their derivatives anticommute to zero.

*Term 2:* {∂_(α)^(I), B_(β̇ J)}. Using the Grassmann Leibniz rule with sign for odd ∂_(α)^(I) acting on odd θ_(J)^(γ),
∂_(α)^(I)(θ_(J)^(γ)⋅X) = (∂_(α)^(I)θ_(J)^(γ)) X − θ_(J)^(γ) ∂_(α)^(I)X = δ_(α)^(γ) δ^(I)_(J) X − θ_(J)^(γ) ∂_(α)^(I)X.
Setting X = iσ^(ν)_(γβ̇)∂_(ν)f (Grassmann-even, since ∂_(ν) is bosonic) and using [∂_(α)^(I),∂_(ν)] = 0, the operator ∂_(α)^(I)B_(β̇ J) + B_(β̇ J)∂_(α)^(I) acts on f as
δ^(I)_(J) iσ^(ν)_(αβ̇)∂_(ν)f − θ_(J)^(γ) iσ^(ν)_(γβ̇)∂_(ν)∂_(α)^(I)f + θ_(J)^(γ) iσ^(ν)_(γβ̇)∂_(ν)∂_(α)^(I)f = i δ^(I)_(J) σ^(ν)_(αβ̇)∂_(ν)f.
So {∂_(α)^(I), B_(β̇ J)} = i δ^(I)_(J) σ^(ν)_(αβ̇)∂_(ν).

*Term 3:* $\{A_{\alpha}^{I},\,\bar\partial_{\dot\beta\,J}\}$. By the analogous Grassmann Leibniz computation with $\bar\partial$ acting on θ̄,
$$\{\bar\theta^{\dot\gamma\,I}\partial_{\mu},\,\bar\partial_{\dot\beta\,J}\} \;=\; \delta^{\dot\gamma}{}_{\dot\beta}\,\delta^{I}{}_{J}\,\partial_{\mu}.$$
Substituting into A_(α)^(I):
$$\{A_{\alpha}^{I},\bar\partial_{\dot\beta\,J}\} \;=\; -i\sigma^{\mu}{}_{\alpha\dot\gamma}\,\delta^{\dot\gamma}{}_{\dot\beta}\,\delta^{I}{}_{J}\,\partial_{\mu} \;=\; -i\,\delta^{I}{}_{J}\,\sigma^{\mu}{}_{\alpha\dot\beta}\,\partial_{\mu}.$$
Hence $-\{A_{\alpha}^{I},\bar\partial_{\dot\beta\,J}\} = +i\,\delta^{I}{}_{J}\,\sigma^{\mu}{}_{\alpha\dot\beta}\,\partial_{\mu}$.

*Term 4:* {A_(α)^(I), B_(β̇ J)}. Both contain a single θ or θ̄ outside the bosonic derivative. Since {θ̄^(γ̇ I), θ_(J)^(γ)} = 0 (independent Grassmann variables) and the bosonic derivatives commute with both θ and θ̄, expanding gives
{A_(α)^(I), B_(β̇ J)} = σ^(μ)_(αγ̇) σ^(ν)_(γ′β̇) {θ̄^(γ̇ I)∂_(μ), θ_(J)^(γ′)∂_(ν)} =  − σ^(μ)_(αγ̇) σ^(ν)_(γ′β̇) {θ̄^(γ̇ I), θ_(J)^(γ′)} ∂_(μ)∂_(ν) = 0.

Summing (⋆):
{Q_(α)^(I), Q̄_(β̇ J)} = 0 + i δ^(I)_(J) σ^(ν)_(αβ̇)∂_(ν) + i δ^(I)_(J) σ^(μ)_(αβ̇)∂_(μ) + 0 = 2i σ^(μ)_(αβ̇) δ^(I)_(J) ∂_(μ).

To identify the right-hand side with 2σ^(μ)_(αβ̇)P_(μ)δ^(I)_(J) as stated in Theorem 51, the relevant superspace translation-generator convention is P_(μ) := i∂_(μ) (Wess--Bagger 1992, eq. (4.4); also Bagger--Lambert 2007 §2). Under this identification,
{Q_(α)^(I), Q̄_(β̇ J)} = 2σ^(μ)_(αβ̇)P_(μ)δ^(I)_(J),
in agreement with the Algebraic-Channel statement of Theorem 51.

`\emph{Sign-convention remark.}`{=tex} The Wess--Bagger SUSY-superspace convention P_(μ) = i∂_(μ) differs by an overall sign from the QM Hermitian-generator convention P_(μ) =  − i∂_(μ) used in §3 of the present paper (where T_(a) = e^(−ia^(μ)P_(μ)) and T_(a)ψ(x) = ψ(x−a)). Both conventions describe the same translation group ℝ^(1, 3); they differ only in which sign of i∂_(μ) is called P_(μ). The Algebraic-Channel statement of Theorem 51 --- derived from Coleman--Mandula + HLS --- is convention-independent at the level of the abstract algebra; only its explicit differential-operator representation on superspace depends on the convention. With the alternative QM convention P_(μ) =  − i∂_(μ), the corresponding differential operators for Q, Q̄ are obtained by flipping the sign of the inhomogeneous terms ( − iσθ̄∂ becomes  + iσθ̄∂, and similarly for Q̄), and the same explicit computation then yields {Q, Q̄} =  − 2iσ^(μ)∂_(μ) = 2σ^(μ)P_(μ)δ^(I)_(J). We adopt the Wess--Bagger convention for this section to match standard SUSY-superspace literature.

The geometric content of supersymmetry on the McGucken background is that the McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) is extended by Grassmann-odd directions. The "super-McGucken-sphere" has bosonic 3-volume directions, a temporal direction, and additional Grassmann-odd "directions" whose square roots are the bosonic spacetime translations. This is the geometric statement of {Q, Q̄} = 2σ ⋅ P: odd directions in superspace, squared, give bosonic translations along the McGucken background.

## Channel-bridge synthesis

:::
**Proposition 52** (Channel synthesis for supersymmetry). *The Algebraic-Channel super-algebra of Theorem 51 and the Geometric-Channel superspace differential-operator realisation are equivalent representations of the same graded extension of 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3). The shared invariant carrying the bridge is the translation generator P_(μ), which is the McGucken-generated translation generator of Theorem 27 in both channels.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The Algebraic-Channel abstract super-algebra is uniquely determined by Theorem 51 (via Coleman--Mandula + HLS). The Geometric-Channel superspace differential-operator realisation provides an explicit representation: substituting the differential-operator formulae for Q_(α)^(I), Q̄_(α̇ I), P_(μ), and J^(μν) (Poincaré generators on ℝ^(1, 3) extended trivially in θ) into the anticommutators and commutators of Theorem 51 verifies them as operator identities on the space of smooth functions of (x,θ,θ̄).

The shared invariant is P_(μ): in the Algebraic Channel, it is the bosonic generator on the right-hand side of {Q, Q̄} = 2σ ⋅ P; in the Geometric Channel, it is the differential operator  − i∂_(μ) acting on superfields. Both occurrences are the same McGucken-generated translation generator of Theorem 27. The two channels therefore meet at the same algebraic object.

The uniqueness of supersymmetry in the dual-channel architecture is: given the Coleman--Mandula no-go for Lie algebras and the graded-extension hypothesis A21, the unique resulting super-algebra is Theorem 51's, and its geometric realisation is superspace. Whether Nature realises this extension is an empirical question --- the mathematical uniqueness is independent of physical realisation. ◼
:::

## Proof of Theorem 51

::: proof
*Proof of Theorem 51.* The Coleman--Mandula theorem (under A20) gives 𝔤_(sym)^(Lie) = 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) ⊕ 𝔤_(int) as the unique Lie-algebra symmetry of the S-matrix.

The HLS theorem (under A20 + A21) gives the unique graded-Lie-algebra extension by fermionic generators in $(\tfrac{1}{2},0)\oplus(0,\tfrac{1}{2})$ representations of 𝔰𝔩(2,ℂ). The defining relations are derived as follows.

*Anticommutator {Q, Q̄}.* The generators Q_(α)^(I) and Q̄_(β̇ J) transform in $(\tfrac{1}{2},0)$ and $(0,\tfrac{1}{2})$ of 𝔰𝔩(2,ℂ). Their anticommutator transforms in the tensor product $(\tfrac{1}{2},0)\otimes(0,\tfrac{1}{2}) = (\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{2})$, which is the four-vector representation of 𝔰𝔬(1,3). The unique vector-valued generator in the algebra 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) ⊕ 𝔤_(int) is P_(μ). Therefore {Q_(α)^(I), Q̄_(β̇ J)} is proportional to σ^(μ)_(αβ̇)P_(μ), with a possible diagonal matrix M^(I)_(J) in the SUSY-index space. Hermiticity (Q^(†) = Q̄) and the requirement that the algebra closes consistently force M^(I)_(J) = 2δ^(I)_(J) (after normalisation), giving {Q_(α)^(I), Q̄_(β̇ J)} = 2σ^(μ)_(αβ̇)P_(μ)δ^(I)_(J).

*Anticommutator {Q, Q}.* The product Q_(α)^(I)Q_(β)^(J) transforms in $(\tfrac{1}{2},0)\otimes(\tfrac{1}{2},0) = (0,0)\oplus(1,0)$. The symmetric part (1,0) has no available bosonic generator in 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) ⊕ 𝔤_(int) (no self-dual antisymmetric tensor generator exists in the Poincaré algebra). The antisymmetric part (0,0) is a scalar in spacetime indices but a 𝔤_(int) tensor in the SUSY indices. This scalar generator is a *central charge* Z^(IJ), antisymmetric in (I,J) by the Grassmann-odd anticommutator structure (the anticommutator {Q_(α)^(I), Q_(β)^(J)} is symmetric under simultaneous exchange of both index pairs (α,I) ↔ (β,J); with {Q, Q} = ϵ_(αβ)Z^(IJ) and ϵ_(αβ) antisymmetric, Z^(IJ) must be antisymmetric in (I,J) for the total expression to be symmetric). Therefore {Q_(α)^(I), Q_(β)^(J)} = ϵ_(αβ)Z^(IJ) with Z^(IJ) =  − Z^(JI). For 𝒩 = 1, the only matrix entry is Z¹¹, and antisymmetry Z¹¹ =  − Z¹¹ forces Z¹¹ = 0; no central charges are admitted. For 𝒩 ≥ 2, antisymmetric 𝒩 × 𝒩 matrices have 𝒩(𝒩−1)/2 independent entries, and non-trivial central charges are allowed.

*Commutator [Q,P].* The commutator transforms in $(\tfrac{1}{2},0)\otimes(\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{2}) = (1,\tfrac{1}{2})\oplus(0,\tfrac{1}{2})$. The $(1,\tfrac{1}{2})$ part has no available generator. The $(0,\tfrac{1}{2})$ part could be Q̄, but the resulting bracket would conflict with the spin-statistics structure of the algebra (HLS uses the no-go argument here in detail). The conclusion is [Q_(α)^(I),P_(μ)] = 0: SUSY generators commute with translations.

*Commutator [Q,J^(μν)].* This is fixed by the requirement that Q_(α)^(I) transform in the spinor representation: [J^(μν),Q_(α)^(I)] =  − i(σ^(μν))_(α)^(β)Q_(β)^(I) (equivalently [Q_(α)^(I),J^(μν)] = i(σ^(μν))_(α)^(β)Q_(β)^(I)).

These four relations, together with the commutator of central charges with all generators (they commute with everything, as is verified by Jacobi identities), define the supersymmetry algebra. Uniqueness is the content of the HLS theorem: any graded extension of 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) by fermionic generators satisfying A20 + A21 reduces to this structure (up to choice of 𝒩 and Z^(IJ)). The translation generator P_(μ) that appears on the right-hand side of {Q, Q̄} is the McGucken-generated translation generator of Theorem 27, established from dx₄/dt = ic via Lemma 1 and the affine completion. ◼
:::

:::
**Lemma 54** (Empirical status of supersymmetry). *Theorem 51 is a mathematical uniqueness statement about graded-Lie-algebra extensions of 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3), conditional on Hypotheses A20 + A21. It does not assert that supersymmetry is realised in Nature. Current empirical status: searches at the Large Hadron Collider (ATLAS, CMS) have not produced evidence for superpartners up to TeV-scale masses; the simplest weak-scale supersymmetric extensions of the Standard Model face increasing experimental tension. The McGucken Principle's derivations of the Standard Model symmetries, gravity, and quantum mechanics proceed without supersymmetric extension; supersymmetry, if found, is an additional layer compatible with the McGucken framework but not required by it.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The mathematical content of Theorem 51 is the uniqueness of the graded extension under A20--A21, established via Coleman--Mandula + HLS. This is a theorem about Lie super-algebra structure; it does not depend on whether physical states organised into supermultiplets exist in Nature.

The empirical status as of the current writing: the ATLAS and CMS collaborations at the LHC have searched extensively for the production of supersymmetric particles in proton--proton collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ and 14 TeV centre-of-mass energy. No statistically significant deviation from Standard Model expectations has been observed. The Particle Data Group's compilation of constraints sets lower limits on gluino masses above  ∼ 2 TeV, squark masses above  ∼ 1.5 TeV, and various electroweakino masses depending on assumed decay channels. These limits exclude many supersymmetric models that were considered well-motivated on naturalness grounds before LHC Run\~2.

The McGucken framework's derivations of Sections 2--10 (Lorentz, Poincaré, Noether, Wigner, U(1) gauge, non-Abelian gauge, unitary, CPT, diffeomorphism) make no use of supersymmetry. The Standard Model with three generations of fermions and the SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1) gauge group is a non-supersymmetric quantum field theory, and the McGucken derivation programme for it (companion papers, see Bibliography) proceeds without supersymmetric content. Theorem 51 therefore serves as a statement: *if* supersymmetry is realised, *it is necessarily of this form*. Empirical confirmation or refutation is independent of the theorem. ◼
:::

## The Geometric-Channel Emptiness Argument for Supersymmetry

The Geometric Channel given in §11 above proceeds by *postulating* a Grassmann-odd extension of the McGucken Sphere --- the introduction of fermionic coordinates θ_(α)^(I), θ̄_(I)^(α̇) adjoined to the four bosonic axes (x₁,x₂,x₃,x₄) of ℳ. This is mathematically well-defined as a graded-Lie-algebra extension (Theorem 51 establishes the uniqueness up to the HLS classification), but it is distinct from the Geometric-Channel derivations of the nine principal symmetries of Sections 2--10. In each of those nine cases, the Geometric-Channel geometric content is *forced* by dx₄/dt = ic acting on ℳ: the McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) at each event is the locus reachable by x₄-expansion at rate c in time Δt (Lorentz, Poincaré, Wigner); the wavefront propagation of Huygens construction is forced by spherical x₄-expansion from every event (quantum-unitary, U(1) gauge, non-Abelian gauge); the spatial three-block of the McGucken Sphere carries all dynamical curvature with the x₄-axis gauge-fixed (diffeomorphism); the analytic continuation through the complex Lorentz group is forced by the reality of x₄ (CPT); and the variational symmetry structure descends from the McGucken Lagrangian forced by Lemma 1 (Noether). In none of these nine cases is an additional structure adjoined to the McGucken background.

This subsection states the fact that makes supersymmetry different and explains the empirical consequence.

:::
**Definition 53′** (Geometric-Channel forcing). *A symmetry S on the McGucken background is said to have a* Geometric-Channel-forced derivation *if there exists a geometric construction Γ_(S) on the McGucken manifold ℳ, using only the bosonic four-axis structure (x₁,x₂,x₃,x₄) and the active-expansion law dx₄/dt = ic, such that Γ_(S) produces the geometric carrier of S without the adjunction of additional fields, coordinates, or algebraic structures. A symmetry S has* Geometric-Channel-postulated *content if the geometric carrier of S requires the adjunction of structure beyond the bosonic four-axis content of ℳ.*
:::

:::
**Proposition 53′ A** (The nine principal symmetries are Geometric-Channel-forced). *Each of the symmetries Lorentz (Theorem 24), Poincaré (Theorem 27), Noether (Theorem 30), Wigner (Theorem 33), U(1) gauge (Theorem 36), non-Abelian gauge (Theorem 39), quantum-unitary (Theorem 42), CPT (Theorem 45), and diffeomorphism (Theorem 48) is Geometric-Channel-forced in the sense of Definition 53′. The geometric carrier in each case is constructed from the McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) and the bosonic four-axis structure of ℳ alone.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Inspection of the Geometric-Channel sections of Sections 2--10. In each case, the construction uses only (i) the four bosonic axes (x₁,x₂,x₃,x₄), (ii) the active-expansion law dx₄/dt = ic, (iii) the McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) at each event p ∈ ℳ, and (iv) standard mathematical completion theorems (Frobenius integrability, Stone's theorem, Huygens's construction, Lovelock's theorem, Bargmann-Hall-Wightman analytic continuation). No fermionic coordinate, no compact direction beyond the four bosonic axes, and no auxiliary algebraic structure is adjoined. The geometric carrier in each case is therefore Geometric-Channel-forced. ◼
:::

:::
**Proposition 53′ B** (Supersymmetry's Geometric Channel is postulated, not forced). *The Geometric-Channel realisation of supersymmetry given in §11 --- the extension of ℝ^(1, 3) by Grassmann-odd coordinates θ_(α)^(I), θ̄_(I)^(α̇) to form superspace --- is Geometric-Channel-postulated in the sense of Definition 53′. The Grassmann-odd directions are adjoined to the McGucken Sphere; they are not produced by dx₄/dt = ic acting on the bosonic four-axis structure of ℳ.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) is, by Theorem 16 of [McGuckenExperimental2026] and the foundational-atom analysis of [Wick34, §12], the two-sphere of radius c Δt in the spatial three-slice Σ_(t), generated by spherically symmetric x₄-expansion at rate c in time Δt. The four axes generating this geometric structure are (x₁,x₂,x₃,x₄), all bosonic (commuting). The superspace extension introduces Grassmann-odd coordinates θ_(I)^(α) satisfying {θ^(α), θ^(β)} = 0 as an *additional* algebraic structure not present in the bosonic four-axis content of ℳ.

The McGucken Sphere does not have *room* for a Grassmann-odd direction in the sense of Definition 53′: every direction at every point on Σ⁺(p) is a tangent vector to one of the four bosonic axes or a linear combination thereof. No additional direction exists that could be identified with θ^(α). Consequently the superspace extension is adjoined rather than produced by Γ_(S) acting on ℳ. The Geometric Channel given in §11 is therefore Geometric-Channel-postulated. ◼
:::

:::
**Remark 53′** (Asymmetry between SUSY and the nine confirmed symmetries). The asymmetry made precise by Propositions 53′ A and 53′ B is the reason supersymmetry occupies a different empirical status from the nine principal symmetries of Sections 2--10. For each of the nine confirmed symmetries, dx₄/dt = ic acting on ℳ produces both the Algebraic-Channel algebraic content and the Geometric-Channel geometric content; the two channels are independent derivations meeting at the same theorem (the dual-channel disjointness of [Wick34, Theorem 30] and [McGuckenDualityDeepest2026, §IX]). For supersymmetry, dx₄/dt = ic produces only the Algebraic-Channel content (the Coleman--Mandula no-go theorem and HLS uniqueness classification operating on the McGucken-generated 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3)); the Geometric-Channel content requires adjunction.
:::

:::
**Theorem 53′ C** (Geometric-Channel-emptiness as a prediction). *Under the present paper's hypothesis stack A1--A23, the Geometric-Channel-postulated character of supersymmetry (Proposition 53′ B) supplies a prediction in the following precise sense:*

*(i) If supersymmetry is empirically realised in Nature (e.g., if superpartners are eventually observed at sufficient collider energy or in cosmological data), then the McGucken Sphere must admit a geometric extension that supplies the fermionic directions θ^(α) as Geometric-Channel content forced by dx₄/dt = ic on ℳ rather than adjoined. The framework then requires identification of the fermionic substrate from ℳ-structure; current corpus work does not exhibit this substrate.*

*(ii) If supersymmetry is not empirically realised in Nature, then the Geometric-Channel-postulated character of Proposition 53′ B is the reason: the McGucken Sphere does not admit fermionic-direction extension as Geometric-Channel-forced content, so the Algebraic-Channel graded extension of 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) is a mathematically consistent but physically unrealised possibility. The McGucken framework is consistent with this empirical outcome without revision.*

*In both empirical outcomes, the Geometric-Channel-postulated character of supersymmetry's geometric content is the mechanism connecting the empirical status to the framework's mathematical structure.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* (i) Suppose supersymmetry is realised in Nature with superpartner masses m_(f̃) observable in collider or cosmological data. Then there exists a physical mechanism generating the fermionic generators Q_(α)^(I) with non-trivial action on physical states. Under Hypothesis A1 (dx₄/dt = ic is the foundational physical principle from which all physics descends), the existence of physical Q_(α)^(I) must trace to ℳ-structure. Since ℳ has bosonic four-axis content, the trace either (a) identifies Q_(α)^(I) with a derived structure on the bosonic four-axes (an extension of the Cartan-square-root machinery of [MG-Dirac], where spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ is derived as a theorem of x₄-rotation), or (b) reveals additional substrate structure on ℳ not currently identified. Option (a) is how spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ enters the McGucken framework (as the universal cover of the McGucken-Sphere SO(3) acting on Cl(1,3)⁺ Weyl-spinor doublets, per [MG-SMGauge2026, Part I]); this mechanism produces fermionic *fields* on bosonic spacetime but does not produce fermionic *coordinates* on the substrate manifold itself. Option (b) requires identification of a fermionic substrate that current corpus work does not exhibit. The empirical observation of supersymmetry would therefore force one of these two routes to be completed.

(ii) Suppose supersymmetry is not realised in Nature, and superpartners are not observed at any energy accessible to experiment or cosmological inference. Then the Algebraic-Channel graded extension of 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) (Theorem 51) is a mathematical statement about possible algebraic extensions of the McGucken-Poincaré algebra without physical realisation. The McGucken framework's derivation programme --- Sections 2 through 10 of the present paper, the 24 GR theorems and 23 QM theorems of [McGuckenExperimental2026], the SM gauge sector of [MG-SMGauge2026], the McGucken cosmology of [MG-Cosmology2026], and the broader corpus --- proceeds without supersymmetric content. The framework is consistent with the non-realisation of supersymmetry without revision; the Geometric-Channel-postulated character of Proposition 53′ B is the reason this consistency holds. ◼
:::

:::
**Remark 53′′** (The prediction is unique to the McGucken framework). *After a comprehensive survey of the prior art* --- covering the major operational-reconstruction programs (Hardy 2001, Chiribella--D'Ariano--Perinotti 2010s, Masanes--Galley--Müller 2019), the superspace and supergravity literature from Salam--Strathdee 1974 and Wess--Zumino 1974 forward, the LHC phenomenology constraint catalogues (PDG 2024), and the standard SUSY-mathematics canon --- Theorem 53′ C has no analogue. Standard symmetry programmes --- for which symmetries are postulated as algebraic constraints without a geometric substrate --- have no analogue of Theorem 53′ C. Within those programmes, supersymmetry is either added as a postulate (and so must be confirmed empirically to justify its inclusion) or omitted (and so cannot be excluded on the framework's own grounds). The McGucken framework, by deriving the nine confirmed principal symmetries as Geometric-Channel-forced theorems of dx₄/dt = ic on ℳ, supplies a notion of *Geometric-Channel emptiness* that is well-defined for any candidate additional symmetry. A candidate symmetry is Geometric-Channel-forced if and only if its geometric carrier can be constructed from the bosonic four-axis structure of ℳ alone; otherwise it is Geometric-Channel-postulated. The Geometric-Channel-postulated character of a candidate symmetry is a precise reason, rather than a metaphysical preference, for treating the symmetry's empirical realisation as a separate question from the framework's mathematical consistency.

The prediction recorded as Theorem 53′ C is therefore not "supersymmetry must exist" or "supersymmetry cannot exist." It is the conditional fact: the empirical status of supersymmetry is connected to whether the McGucken Sphere admits a fermionic-coordinate extension as forced rather than postulated. This connection is unique to the McGucken framework; no standard symmetry programme makes it. The author would be delighted to learn of any precedent and invites communication of bibliographic detail to drelliot@gmail.com.
:::

**Conclusion of Section 11.** Supersymmetry, viewed as an algebraic extension, is the unique non-trivial graded Lie super-algebra extension of 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) consistent with the Coleman--Mandula no-go theorem (Theorem 51, via Coleman--Mandula + HLS). The translation generator on the right-hand side of {Q, Q̄} = 2σ ⋅ P is the McGucken-generated P_(μ) of Theorem 27. The Algebraic-Channel super-algebra and Geometric-Channel superspace differential-operator realisation are formally equivalent (Proposition 52), but the Geometric-Channel realisation is *postulated* rather than *forced* by dx₄/dt = ic acting on ℳ (Proposition 53′ B); the Grassmann-odd directions θ^(α) are adjoined to the bosonic four-axis structure of ℳ, in contrast to the nine confirmed principal symmetries of Sections 2--10, whose geometric carriers are Geometric-Channel-forced (Proposition 53′ A). This asymmetry supplies the prediction recorded as Theorem 53′ C: the empirical status of supersymmetry is connected to whether ℳ admits a fermionic-direction extension as forced rather than postulated. Whether supersymmetry is physically realised is an empirical question (Lemma 54); current LHC data sets stringent constraints but does not rule out heavier supersymmetric scenarios. The McGucken framework's derivations of the principal symmetries of physics (Sections 2--10) proceed without supersymmetry; the latter, if found, is a Algebraic-Channel enhancement compatible with the McGucken Principle, with the geometric substrate of its Geometric-Channel content remaining to be identified.

# String-Theoretic Dualities as Geometric-Channelridge Theorems

The string-theoretic dualities (T, S, U, mirror, AdS/CFT) are accommodated as channel-bridge theorems over the McGucken-generated Lorentzian base, conditional on the string-theoretic framework describing physical structures. The McGucken Principle's derivations of Sections 2--10 do not depend on string theory; the empirical status of string theory remains open.

## Hypothesis for Section 12

The string-theoretic dualities are statements about quantum-mechanical equivalences between distinct mathematical descriptions of putative physical systems. Their content within the McGucken framework proceeds as follows: each duality has a Algebraic-Channel invariant (spectrum, partition function, BPS index, etc.) and a Geometric-Channel geometric carrier (target geometry, compactification manifold, bulk/boundary structure), with the two coinciding via the invariant. The empirical realisation of string theory itself is an open question; the content of the dualities is independent of this empirical question.

- **Hypothesis A22 (String-theoretic data).** A duality between two descriptions D₁, D₂ of a physical system is specified by (i) a list of observable quantities 𝒪₁, 𝒪₂ computed in each description, and (ii) an isomorphism ι : 𝒪₁ → 𝒪₂ such that the values of corresponding observables agree. The isomorphism ι is the *invariant* of the duality.

Under A22, the channel-bridge theorem for dualities is: each duality is a Algebraic-Channel/Geometric-Channel correspondence over a McGucken-generated Lorentzian background, with the invariant ι as the bridge. The McGucken Principle's role is to supply the four large noncompact dimensions of every string-theoretic compactification; the duality structure on the remaining (compact, internal, or bulk) directions is built on top of this base.

| Duality | Algebraic Channel (algebraic) | Geometric Channel (geometric) | Shared invariant |
|---|---|---|---|
| T-duality | ℤ/2 exchange n ↔ w of momentum/winding quantum numbers on S¹ | Equivalence of target circles of radius R and α^(′)/R | Closed-string mass spectrum |
| S-duality | SL(2,ℤ) action on complex coupling τ = θ/2π + i/g² | Equivalence of strong- and weak-coupling regimes | BPS state spectrum |
| U-duality | Exceptional duality group E_(n(n))(ℤ) | Equivalence of higher-dimensional supergravity compactifications | BPS state lattice |
| Mirror symmetry | Exchange of Hodge numbers h^(1, 1) ↔ h^(2, 1) on Calabi--Yau pair (X,X̃) | Equivalence of two distinct CY 3-folds | Topological string partition function |
| AdS/CFT (holographic) | Boundary conformal-field-theory generating functional Z_(CFT)[J] | Bulk gravitational partition function Z_(grav)[ϕ|_(∂)=J] | Z_(CFT)[J] = Z_(grav)[ϕ|_(∂)=J] |

*In each case the duality is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic in the sense that the four large noncompact dimensions are the McGucken-generated Lorentzian background of Lemma 1, the Algebraic Channel / Geometric Channel pattern is the McGucken dual-channel architecture, and the shared invariant is the data preserved by the duality. The conclusion is conditional on the string-theoretic framework being a description of physical structures; the McGucken framework's principal derivations (Sections 2--10) do not depend on this empirical question.*
