## T-duality

*Algebraic Channel.* For a closed bosonic string compactified on a circle S¹ of radius R, the centre-of-mass momentum along the circle is quantised as p = n/R for n ∈ ℤ (Kaluza--Klein momentum), and the string can wind around the circle w ∈ ℤ times. The mass-squared of a string state with quantum numbers (n,w) and oscillator excitations N, Ñ is
$$\alpha^{\prime}M^{2}(n,w) \;=\; \frac{\alpha^{\prime}n^{2}}{R^{2}} + \frac{w^{2}R^{2}}{\alpha^{\prime}} + 2(N+\tilde N - 2),$$
where α^(′) is the Regge slope (squared inverse string tension). Under the substitution R → α^(′)/R and n ↔ w, the spectrum is invariant. This is a ℤ/2 symmetry, not a continuous symmetry.

*Geometric Channel.* Geometrically, the target spaces ℝ^(1, d − 1) × S_(R)¹ and ℝ^(1, d − 1) × S_(α^(′)/R)¹ are *not* isometric as Riemannian manifolds --- they have different radii. The duality is the statement that *closed-string physics* on the two backgrounds is the same: scattering amplitudes, correlation functions, and partition functions coincide. The geometric content of the duality is therefore the equivalence of two distinct geometric backgrounds under string probes, rather than a target-space isometry.

*Channel synthesis.* The shared invariant is the closed-string mass spectrum (and, more generally, all closed-string scattering amplitudes). The McGucken Principle supplies the ℝ^(1, d − 1) noncompact base. The compact circle S¹ is an additional structure (the compactification data) not derived from the McGucken Principle; what *is* a McGucken theorem is the underlying Lorentzian causal structure of the noncompact dimensions, on which the string is propagating.

## S-duality

*Algebraic Channel.* The complexified coupling of 𝒩 = 4 super Yang--Mills (or Type IIB string theory) is
$$\tau \;=\; \frac{\theta}{2\pi} + \frac{i}{g^{2}},$$
where g is the gauge coupling (or string coupling) and θ is the topological theta-angle. The S-duality conjecture is that the theory is invariant under the SL(2,ℤ) action
$$\tau \;\mapsto\; \frac{a\tau + b}{c\tau + d}, \qquad \begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z}),$$
with appropriate transformations of states under the modular group. In particular, the generator τ →  − 1/τ corresponds to strong/weak coupling inversion: g → 1/g at θ = 0.

*Geometric Channel.* Geometrically, the duality is interpreted as a non-trivial geometric identification on the moduli space ℳ_(coupling) of complex couplings, with quotient by SL(2,ℤ). The physical regimes "strong coupling" and "weak coupling" are points on opposite sides of the fundamental domain of SL(2,ℤ) in the upper half plane.

*Channel synthesis.* The shared invariant is the BPS spectrum (states that preserve some fraction of supersymmetry). BPS states are exact under the duality (their masses are determined by a central-charge formula and are SL(2,ℤ)-covariant). The McGucken Principle supplies the underlying ℝ^(1, 3) on which 𝒩 = 4 SYM lives.

## U-duality

In compactifications of 11-dimensional supergravity (M-theory) on a torus T^(n), the resulting low-energy effective theory has a global duality group E_(n(n))(ℤ) --- an exceptional Lie group acting on the discrete charge lattice. For n = 4 (compactification to 7 dimensions): E₄₍₄₎(ℤ) ≅ SL(5,ℤ). For n = 5: E₅₍₅₎ ≅ Spin(5,5). For n = 6: E₆₍₆₎. For n = 7: E₇₍₇₎. The duality unifies T- and S-dualities into one large symmetry group acting on the full BPS state spectrum.

*Algebraic Channel.* The action of E_(n(n))(ℤ) on the discrete charge lattice of BPS states.

*Geometric Channel.* The action on the moduli space of supergravity compactifications: different points in the moduli space, related by E_(n(n))(ℤ), describe the same physical theory.

*Channel synthesis.* Shared invariant: the BPS lattice and its associated partition functions. The McGucken Principle supplies the ℝ^(1, 3) noncompact base of the dimensional reduction.

## Mirror symmetry

*Algebraic Channel.* For a Calabi--Yau 3-fold X, the two relevant Hodge numbers are h^(1, 1)(X) (dimension of Kähler moduli space) and h^(2, 1)(X) (dimension of complex structure moduli space). Mirror symmetry asserts the existence of a mirror CY 3-fold X̃ with
h^(1, 1)(X) = h^(2, 1)(X̃),   h^(2, 1)(X) = h^(1, 1)(X̃).
The A-model topological string on X (which depends only on Kähler structure) is equivalent to the B-model topological string on X̃ (which depends only on complex structure), and vice versa.

*Geometric Channel.* Geometrically, X and X̃ are typically *distinct* Calabi--Yau 3-folds (different topology, different Hodge structures), related by the Strominger--Yau--Zaslow conjecture as T-duality on a T³ fibration.

*Channel synthesis.* The shared invariant is the topological string partition function (and, more generally, the Gromov--Witten invariants of X matching the period integrals of X̃). The McGucken Principle supplies the ℝ^(1, 3) base; the Calabi--Yau 3-fold is an additional compactification structure.

## AdS/CFT (holographic duality)

*Algebraic Channel.* A d-dimensional conformal field theory on the boundary ∂(AdS_(d + 1)) is described by a generating functional
Z_(CFT)[J] = ∫𝒟ϕ e^(−S_(CFT)[ϕ]+∫Jϕ),
encoding all correlation functions of operators 𝒪 (dual to sources J) in the CFT.

*Geometric Channel.* A (d+1)-dimensional gravitational theory in the AdS bulk is described by a partition function
Z_(grav)[ϕ|_(∂)=J] = ∫𝒟g 𝒟ϕ_(bulk) e^(−S_(grav))|_(ϕ(∂AdS) = J),
with the bulk field ϕ taking specified boundary values J on the conformal boundary.

*Channel synthesis.* The AdS/CFT correspondence (Maldacena 1997, GKP--Witten 1998) is the identification
Z_(CFT)[J] = Z_(grav)[ϕ|_(∂)=J].
The shared invariant is the partition function itself, encoded by correlation functions on the boundary side and by gravitational saddles in the bulk. Both the boundary conformal group SO(d,2) and the bulk AdS isometry group SO(d,2) are realised; their coincidence is the symmetry-group fingerprint of the duality, but the duality content is the partition-function equality, not the group coincidence.

The McGucken Principle's role in AdS/CFT is as follows: the boundary ℝ^(1, d − 1) (or its conformal compactification) is the Lorentzian base on which the CFT lives; the bulk AdS_(d + 1) is a curved generalisation of the McGucken background. For the d = 4 case (AdS₅ × S⁵ / 𝒩 = 4 SYM on ℝ^(1, 3)), the boundary is exactly the McGucken-generated four-dimensional Minkowski space.

:::
**Remark 56**. *String theory remains empirically uncertain: no direct experimental confirmation of string-theoretic predictions has been made to date. The McGucken framework accommodates string-theoretic dualities as channel-bridge theorems if they describe physical structures (Hypothesis A22); the derivations of QM, GR, the Standard Model, and thermodynamics from dx₄/dt = ic in Sections 2--10 proceed without compactification or string-theoretic content. The dualities of this section are therefore presented as channel-bridge theorems applicable conditionally on the string framework, not as derivations on which the McGucken programme depends.*
:::

## Channel-bridge synthesis (general)

:::
**Proposition 57** (Duality-invariant criterion as channel-bridge theorem). *A quantum-mechanical equivalence between two descriptions D₁, D₂ of a physical system is a channel-bridge theorem in the McGucken dual-channel architecture if and only if there exists a shared invariant ι (spectrum, partition function, BPS index, correlation function, moduli-space invariant, or topological invariant) such that:*

*(i) Algebraic Channel: D₁ supplies an algebraic computation of ι (via charges, generators, modular orbits, or representation theory).*

*(ii) Geometric Channel: D₂ supplies a geometric computation of ι (via target geometry, moduli space, or bulk/boundary structure).*

*(iii) The two computations yield the same numerical / result: ι_(A) = ι_(B).*

*The five string-theoretic dualities of Theorem 55 are explicit instances of this pattern. The McGucken Principle's role is to supply the underlying Lorentzian noncompact base on which the dualities are formulated.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The "only if" direction is the definition of a quantum-mechanical duality: two descriptions are dual exactly when they compute the same physical observables, which is the existence of ι with ι_(A) = ι_(B).

The "if" direction (channel-bridge identification): given such an ι, the algebraic-computation side is by definition Algebraic Channel (algebra of charges, generators, representations), and the geometric-computation side is by definition Geometric Channel (geometry, moduli, bulk structure). Each of the five named dualities (T, S, U, mirror, AdS/CFT) provides an explicit example of ι:
- T: ι = closed-string mass spectrum.
- S: ι = BPS state spectrum, computed algebraically via the modular orbit on τ, geometrically via moduli-space identifications.
- U: ι = full BPS charge lattice, with E_(n(n))(ℤ) action.
- Mirror: ι = topological string partition function, Gromov--Witten invariants on one side matching period integrals on the other.
- AdS/CFT: ι = boundary generating functional = bulk partition function with specified boundary conditions.

In each case the McGucken Principle enters as follows: the four large noncompact dimensions are the McGucken-generated Lorentzian base of Lemma 1. The compactification or curved generalisation is an additional structure on top of this base, supplied by the string-theoretic framework. The channel-bridge architecture is the algebra-geometry correspondence already operating in Sections 2--10 of this paper. ◼
:::

## The Geometric-Channel Emptiness Argument for the String-Theoretic Dualities

The analysis of Section 11 (Propositions 53′ A and 53′ B, Theorem 53′ C, and Remarks 53′ and 53′′) applies *mutatis mutandis* to the string-theoretic dualities of the present section. The geometric carriers of T-duality, S-duality, U-duality, mirror symmetry, and AdS/CFT --- compactification radii on circles or higher tori, moduli spaces of complex and Kähler structures on Calabi--Yau manifolds, bulk anti-de-Sitter geometries with conformal boundaries --- are not produced by dx₄/dt = ic acting on the bosonic four-axis structure of ℳ. They are *adjoined* to the McGucken background through the additional hypothesis A22 (the string-theoretic framework describes physical structures). Section 12 above states this explicitly: "The McGucken Principle supplies the underlying four large noncompact dimensions as the Lorentzian base of Lemma 1; the compactification or curvature is additional structure not derived from the McGucken Principle" (Conclusion of Section 12).

This subsection states the consequence and the parallel empirical prediction.

:::
**Proposition 57′ A** (The string-theoretic dualities have Geometric-Channel-postulated carriers). *Each of the five string-theoretic dualities of Theorem 55 (T, S, U, mirror, AdS/CFT) has a Geometric-Channel-postulated carrier in the sense of Definition 53′ (§11). Specifically:*

*(i) T-duality requires a compact direction S¹ of radius R, exchanged with α′/R. The compact circle is not produced by dx₄/dt = ic acting on the bosonic four-axis structure of ℳ.*

*(ii) S-duality requires a coupling constant g to be a modular parameter on the upper half-plane ℌ. The modular structure is not produced by ℳ.*

*(iii) U-duality requires the E₇₍₇₎ or higher exceptional duality group structure operating on compactified moduli. The exceptional structure is not produced by ℳ.*

*(iv) Mirror symmetry requires Calabi--Yau threefolds X, X^(∨) with swapped Hodge numbers. The Calabi--Yau geometry is not produced by ℳ.*

*(v) AdS/CFT requires an anti-de-Sitter bulk geometry AdS_(d + 1) with conformal boundary. The bulk-boundary structure beyond the four bosonic large axes of ℳ is not produced by ℳ.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* In each case the geometric carrier requires structure beyond the four bosonic axes (x₁,x₂,x₃,x₄) of ℳ. The compactification radii of (i), the modular structure of (ii), the exceptional duality group of (iii), the complex and Kähler moduli of (iv), and the additional bulk dimension of (v) are all adjoined structures, not produced by dx₄/dt = ic acting on the bosonic four-axis content of ℳ. The Geometric Channel given for each duality in §12 is therefore Geometric-Channel-postulated. ◼
:::

:::
**Remark 57′** (Why the McGucken Sphere does not supply the compact dimensions). It is sometimes suggested that the McGucken Sphere itself, being a 2-sphere of radius c Δt in the spatial three-slice, might play the role of the compact directions of string-theoretic compactification. This suggestion fails for a reason. The McGucken Sphere is a *dynamical* spherical wavefront generated by spherically symmetric x₄-expansion at rate c; it is parametrised by elapsed parameter Δt and grows without bound. String-theoretic compact directions are *static* compact manifolds with fixed periodicity. The McGucken Sphere does not have the compactness, static character, or moduli-space structure required for string-theoretic compactification.

A separate construction with additional structure beyond the McGucken Sphere --- e.g., a Kaluza--Klein-type circle of static radius identified with the x₄-oscillation period (cf. [Wick34, §14] for the Kaluza--Klein content of the corpus) --- could in principle supply such compact directions, but the construction is itself an additional adjunction beyond the bosonic four-axis content. The Geometric-Channel-postulated status of the string-theoretic dualities is therefore robust to the obvious attempts at derivation from ℳ alone.
:::

:::
**Theorem 57′ B** (Geometric-Channel-emptiness as a prediction for the string-theoretic dualities). *Under the present paper's hypothesis stack A1--A23, the Geometric-Channel-postulated character of the string-theoretic dualities (Proposition 57′ A) supplies a prediction in the following precise sense:*

*(i) If the string-theoretic framework describes physical structures and the dualities of Theorem 55 are realised in Nature, then the compact-direction substrate must be exhibited as Geometric-Channel-forced content of ℳ rather than adjoined. The framework then requires identification of the compactification substrate from ℳ-structure; current corpus work does not exhibit this substrate.*

*(ii) If the string-theoretic framework does not describe physical structures and the dualities of Theorem 55 are not realised in Nature, then the Geometric-Channel-postulated character of Proposition 57′ A is the reason: the McGucken background does not admit the compact-direction or Calabi--Yau extensions as Geometric-Channel-forced content, so the algebraic dualities of Theorem 55 are mathematically consistent but physically unrealised. The McGucken framework's derivations of Sections 2--10 are consistent with this empirical outcome without revision.*

*In both empirical outcomes, the Geometric-Channel-postulated character of the string-theoretic dualities' geometric content is the mechanism connecting their empirical status to the framework's mathematical structure.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The argument is parallel to the proof of Theorem 53′ C of §11, with the bosonic four-axis content of ℳ taking the place of the Grassmann-odd extension and the compact-direction or Calabi--Yau adjunction taking the place of the Grassmann-odd extension. In case (i), the empirical realisation of the dualities forces identification of the geometric substrate from ℳ-structure; in case (ii), the non-realisation of the dualities is consistent with the Geometric-Channel-postulated status without framework revision. ◼
:::

:::
**Remark 57′′** (The prediction is unique to the McGucken framework). *After a comprehensive survey of the prior art* --- covering the standard string-theory canon (Polchinski 1998, Green--Schwarz--Witten 1987, Becker--Becker--Schwarz 2007, and the holographic-duality literature from 't Hooft 1993 and Susskind 1995 through Maldacena 1997 and forward), the standard T-duality and S-duality literature, and the Calabi--Yau-and-mirror-symmetry programme --- the prediction recorded as Theorem 57′ B has no analogue in standard string-theoretic programmes. Within those programmes, the dualities are postulates of the framework, and their empirical realisation is not predictable from the framework itself; the framework can accommodate either realisation or non-realisation without internal modification. The McGucken framework, by deriving the nine confirmed principal symmetries as Geometric-Channel-forced theorems of dx₄/dt = ic on ℳ, supplies a notion of *Geometric-Channel emptiness* that is well-defined for any candidate string-theoretic structure. A candidate compactification is Geometric-Channel-forced if and only if its geometric carrier can be constructed from the bosonic four-axis structure of ℳ alone; otherwise it is Geometric-Channel-postulated. The Geometric-Channel-postulated character of the string-theoretic compactifications and dualities supplies a precise reason, rather than a metaphysical preference, for treating their empirical realisation as a separate question from the McGucken framework's mathematical consistency.

The prediction is therefore not "string theory must be right" or "string theory cannot be right." It is the conditional fact: the empirical status of the string-theoretic dualities is connected to whether the McGucken background admits a compact-direction extension as forced rather than postulated. This connection is unique to the McGucken framework; standard string-theoretic programmes do not make it because they have no Geometric-Channel notion to be empty of. The author would be delighted to learn of any precedent and invites communication of bibliographic detail to drelliot@gmail.com.
:::

**Conclusion of Section 12.** The five canonical string-theoretic dualities (T, S, U, mirror, AdS/CFT) are channel-bridge theorems in the McGucken dual-channel architecture (Theorem 55, Proposition 57). Each has a Algebraic-Channel algebraic invariant (spectrum, BPS lattice, partition function) and a Geometric-Channel geometric carrier (compactification radius, modular orbit, moduli space, bulk/boundary structure), with the shared invariant as the duality content. The Geometric-Channel carriers in each case are *postulated* rather than *forced* by dx₄/dt = ic acting on ℳ (Proposition 57′ A); the compact directions, modular structure, exceptional duality groups, Calabi--Yau moduli, and AdS-bulk geometry are all adjoined to the bosonic four-axis content of ℳ. This asymmetry --- parallel to the supersymmetry case of §11 --- supplies the prediction recorded as Theorem 57′ B: the empirical status of the string-theoretic dualities is connected to whether ℳ admits a compact-direction or Calabi--Yau extension as forced rather than postulated. The McGucken Principle supplies the underlying four large noncompact dimensions as the Lorentzian base of Lemma 1; the compactification or curvature is additional structure not derived from the McGucken Principle. The conclusion is conditional on the string-theoretic framework describing physical structures (Hypothesis A22, Remark 56); the McGucken Principle's principal derivations of Sections 2--10 do not depend on this empirical question.

# Hierarchy and Master Table

> *"A theory is the more impressive the greater the simplicity of its premises is, the more different kinds of things it relates, and the more extended is its area of applicability."*
> --- Albert Einstein

> *"Three Rules of Work: Out of clutter find simplicity; From discord find harmony; In the middle of difficulty lies opportunity."*

This section organises the principal symmetries derived in Sections 2--12 into a single classification table. Two readings of the table are useful. The first gives the **carrier reading**: each principal symmetry is identified with the carrier (interval, affine space, action, representation, bundle, etc.) on which its automorphism group acts. The second gives the **channel-bridge reading**: each symmetry is identified by its Algebraic-Channel algebraic content, its Geometric-Channel geometric content, and the shared invariant that bridges them. Both readings refer to the audited theorem statements of Sections 2--12; no claim is repeated here that was not proved there.

## Note on numbering

The eleven principal-symmetry sections audited in this paper are §2 (Lorentz), §3 (Poincaré), §4 (Noether), §5 (Wigner), §6 (U(1) gauge), §7 (non-Abelian SU(N) gauge), §8 (Quantum-Unitary evolution), §9 (CPT), §10 (Diffeomorphism invariance), §11 (Supersymmetry), §12 (String-theoretic dualities). Section 1 is the Historical Analysis. The references below to "Section n" use this numbering throughout.

## The carrier hierarchy

:::
**Definition 60** (Carrier hierarchy). *The eleven principal symmetries derived in Sections 2--12 are organised by the level of carrier on which they act, ordered by logical priority (each level presupposes the structures of all earlier levels):*

*Level 1. Spacetime geometry: Lorentz (§2), Poincaré (§3) --- automorphism groups of the McGucken-generated affine bilinear form.*

*Level 2. Variational dynamics: Noether (§4) --- conserved currents from variational symmetries.*

*Level 3. Quantum representations: Wigner (§5) --- unitary irreducible representations of the spacetime group.*

*Level 4. Internal symmetry: U(1) gauge (§6), non-Abelian gauge (§7) --- bundle connections over the McGucken base.*

*Level 5. Quantum dynamics: Quantum-unitary evolution (§8) --- Stone's theorem on the Hilbert-space representation of time-translation.*

*Level 6. Discrete completion: CPT (§9) --- antiunitary discrete-symmetry product.*

*Level 7. Local extension: Diffeomorphism invariance (§10) --- curved-manifold generalisation of Poincaré.*

*Level 8. Conditional extensions: Supersymmetry (§11), string dualities (§12) --- graded-algebra and quantum-equivalence extensions whose empirical realisation is open.*
:::

The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic sits beneath Level 1, supplying the foundational physical-geometric datum (the substrate-expansion law) from which the carriers of all eight levels are generated as theorems. The principle serves as the source of the hierarchy rather than as a member of it.

## Hypothesis for §14

- **Hypothesis A23 (Principal-symmetry class).** A *principal symmetry* is a symmetry of a fundamental physical theory satisfying all of the following: (i) it acts on the kinematic, dynamical, quantum, gauge, spacetime, or duality structure of the theory; (ii) it is not merely a finite subgroup, accidental degeneracy, perturbative approximation, or phenomenological mnemonic; (iii) it enters the formulation of the theory at the level of invariant structures, generators, bundles, representations, actions, or equivalence classes of backgrounds; (iv) it acts on a carrier from Definition 60's Level 1--8 enumeration.

Hypothesis A23 makes Definition 60's eight-level carrier enumeration explicitly the scope of what is meant by "principal symmetry" in the closure and uniqueness theorems below. Discrete subgroups (crystallographic point groups, parity in atomic spectra), approximate or emergent symmetries (isospin, flavour SU(3), chiral symmetry), and gauge-fixing or BRST symmetries are excluded by clauses (ii) and (iv); they are restrictions or representation-specific features of principal symmetries already in the catalog.

## Closure of the symmetry catalog

:::
**Theorem 58** (Closure). *Under Hypothesis A23, the eleven principal symmetries derived in Sections 2--12 --- Lorentz, Poincaré, Noether, Wigner, U(1) gauge, non-Abelian gauge, quantum-unitary, CPT, diffeomorphism, supersymmetry, and the string-theoretic dualities (T, S, U, mirror, holographic) --- exhaust the principal symmetries of physics that have been proposed in the 154-year arc from Klein 1872 to the present. Equivalently, every principal symmetry in the sense of Hypothesis A23 acts on one of the eight carrier levels of Definition 60, hence is either an entry in the catalog of Sections 2--12 or a sub-symmetry, representation, restriction, or breaking of such an entry.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Hypothesis A23 reduces the proof to an enumeration over carrier levels. Let G be a principal symmetry in the sense of A23. By clause (iv), G acts on one of the eight carrier levels of Definition 60. We verify that the principal symmetries derived in Sections 2--12 represent every carrier level.

*Level 1 (spacetime geometry).* The carriers are the bilinear form η at each tangent space and its global affine completion to flat Minkowski space. The connected automorphism group of η as a bilinear form is SO⁺(1,3) (Theorem 24, Section 2). The connected affine isometry group of (ℝ^(1, 3),η) is ISO⁺(1,3) (Theorem 27, Section 3). Any symmetry acting on Level 1 is therefore a subgroup or restriction of ISO⁺(1,3).

*Level 2 (variational dynamics).* The carrier is the action functional S[ϕ,g] on the McGucken background (with the background itself generated by the active-expansion principle dx₄/dt = ic); the automorphism algebra is the algebra of variational symmetries (Noether vector fields on J¹E). Theorem 30 (Section 4) establishes that every variational symmetry yields a conserved current and an associated Lie-algebra homomorphism from the symmetry algebra to the Poisson algebra of charges. The dual-channel architecture of [McGuckenDualityDeepest2026, Level 2] pairs this Algebraic-Channel conservation-law content with the Geometric-Channel strict-monotonicity content of §4.3 above: Noether's conserved currents (time-symmetric) and the strict Second Law dS/dt > 0 (time-asymmetric) are the two faces of the same Level-2 source-pair structure on the McGucken background. The internal U(1) phase symmetry (mentioned in Section 4 as a Noether symmetry on charged matter) is the Level 2 instance of an internal symmetry; its full geometric content is at Level 4.

*Level 3 (quantum representations).* The carrier is a unitary representation of the spacetime group + spectrum condition. Theorem 33 (Section 5) classifies unitary irreducible representations via Mackey induction; the classification is exhaustive on $\widetilde{\mathrm{ISO}}^{+}(1,3)$ under the spectrum condition A11. Every quantum-mechanical particle representation is an entry in this table.

*Level 4 (internal symmetry).* The carrier is a G-principal bundle over the McGucken base. Theorem 36 (Section 6) treats the abelian case G = U(1); Theorem 39 (Section 7) treats the non-abelian case for compact G. The Standard Model gauge group SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1) is the empirical content; the content (existence and uniqueness of the connection structure on the bundle) is the theorem.

*Level 5 (quantum dynamics).* The carrier is the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group implementing time evolution. Theorem 42 (Section 8) supplies Stone's theorem: U(t) = e^(−iĤt/ℏ) for unique self-adjoint Ĥ. Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures are unitarily equivalent presentations of this content.

*Level 6 (discrete completion).* The carrier is the full disconnected component structure of O(1,3) plus the discrete charge-conjugation involution. Theorem 45 (Section 9) establishes that CPT is a theorem of the standard Wightman QFT framework; individual C, P, T are not separately required.

*Level 7 (local extension).* The carrier is a smooth Lorentzian manifold (M,g) with curved-spacetime McGucken structure at each event. Theorem 48 (Section 10) establishes that Diff(M) preserves this structure and that Lovelock's theorem identifies the Einstein-Hilbert action as the unique gravitational completion satisfying A19.

*Level 8 (conditional extensions).* The carrier is either (a) a graded-Lie-algebra extension of 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) (Theorem 51, Section 11) or (b) a quantum-mechanical equivalence between distinct mathematical descriptions (Theorem 55, Proposition 57, Section 12). Both are conditional on additional hypotheses (A20--A22).

Since the eight carrier levels are mutually distinguished by the mathematical objects on which their automorphism groups act (bilinear forms, action functionals, Hilbert-space representations, principal bundles, unitary groups, disconnected Lorentz components, smooth manifolds, graded algebras / quantum equivalences), every principal symmetry under A23 falls into exactly one level and is covered by the corresponding entry of Sections 2--12. The catalog is therefore closed under the principal-symmetry criterion.

The excluded classes (finite subgroups, approximate symmetries, gauge-fixing symmetries, broken remnants) by A23(ii) sit outside the principal-symmetry category in the stipulated sense, appearing instead as physically useful restrictions or representation-specific features of the eleven principal entries: parity is the det  =  − 1 coset of O(1,3) relative to Lorentz; isospin is an approximate SU(2) acting on quark flavours, a representation-specific feature of the strong SU(3) gauge symmetry of Level 4; BRST symmetry is a gauge-fixing structure on top of Level 4. None of these introduces a new carrier level. ◼
:::

## Uniqueness of the McGucken father symmetry

:::
**Definition 61** (First-order single-equation foundational principle). *A *first-order single-equation foundational principle* is a single physical equation of the form*
$$\frac{d\phi}{dt} \;=\; f(\phi,t)$$
*involving one continuous parameter t (physical time), one derivative (d/dt, first order), and a right-hand side f that may contain real or complex constants, a finite-dimensional substrate ϕ, and the universal constant c. The principle is *physically interpretable* if it generates, as theorems under standard mathematical completions, the carriers of all eight levels of Definition 60.*
:::

:::
**Theorem 59** (Uniqueness of the McGucken father symmetry). *Under Hypothesis A23 and Definition 61, the McGucken Principle*
$$\frac{dx_{4}}{dt} \;=\; ic$$
*is the unique first-order single-equation foundational principle, up to additive origin of x₄ and reflection of the spatial axes, simultaneously generating all eight carrier levels of Definition 60 as theorems. The seven requirements are:*

*(1) Lorentzian metric signature (−,+,+,+) --- generated by the factor i via i² =  − 1 converting one signature direction to negative (Lemma 1).*

*(2) Invariant speed c --- fixed by the magnitude of the right-hand side.*

*(3) Quantum unitary structure --- the same i in the McGucken Principle is the i in unitary evolution U(t) = e^(−iĤt/ℏ) (Proposition 45a).*

*(4) Dynamical time-translation --- the derivative d/dt generates the one-parameter time-translation group of §3, §8.*

*(5) Fourth coordinate x₄ --- supplies the substrate-direction on which spherical expansion acts (Hypothesis A2).*

*(6) Temporal orientation --- the  + ic branch selects the future cone (Hypothesis A5), generating the Second Law (Section 4) and the spectrum condition (Hypothesis A11).*

*(7) Generation of every entry in the closure catalog (Theorem 58) --- each derived as a theorem via the standard mathematical completion of Section 2--12.*

*No weaker, alternative, or modified single-equation foundational principle in the class of Definition 61 satisfies all seven requirements simultaneously.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The argument has two parts: existence (the McGucken Principle satisfies all seven) and uniqueness (no other principle in the class does).

*Existence.* Requirements (1)--(7) are the content of Theorems 24, 27, 30, 33, 36, 39, 42, 45, 48, 51, 55, established in Sections 2--12. In particular, Lemma 1 produces the Lorentzian metric of signature (−,+,+,+) from substitution of dx₄ = ic dt into the Euclidean four-coordinate inner product (Requirement 1); the magnitude of c enters as the universal constant on the right-hand side (Requirement 2); Proposition 45a establishes the identification of the McGucken i with the unitary-evolution i and the Wick-rotation i (Requirement 3); the differential operator d/dt generates the one-parameter time-translation group exponentiated by Stone's theorem in Section 8 (Requirement 4); the fourth coordinate x₄ is the substrate-direction of A2 (Requirement 5); the + sign of  + ic selects the future temporal branch of A5 (Requirement 6); and the closure catalog of Theorem 58 is exhaustively derived in Sections 2--12 (Requirement 7).

*Uniqueness.* Let P be a first-order single-equation foundational principle in the class of Definition 61 satisfying all seven requirements. We deduce that P has the form dx₄/dt = ic up to the stated equivalences.

*Requirement 1 (Lorentzian signature)* forces the right-hand side of P to contain a factor i (or a complex unit equivalent to i under rotation): under substitution of P into a Euclidean four-coordinate inner product, the square of the right-hand side must produce a negative contribution to the metric, equivalently the right-hand side squared must be negative. The only real scalars squaring to a negative real are pure imaginaries; the unique imaginary unit (up to sign and complex rotation) is i.

*Requirement 2 (invariant speed)* fixes the magnitude of the right-hand side to be c: |f(ϕ,t)| = c for all ϕ, t in the domain. Combined with Requirement 1, this leaves f =  ± ic (up to a possible additional complex phase, eliminated below).

*Requirement 3 (quantum unitary structure)* requires the imaginary unit i in P to act as the imaginary unit in the unitary-evolution exponent e^(−iĤt/ℏ). By Wigner's theorem (Section 8, Proposition 44), this i is forced to be the canonical i of ℂ, not an arbitrary complex phase. Hence no additional complex phase e^(iθ) can be inserted: f =  ± ic.

*Requirement 4 (dynamical time-translation)* requires that the derivative on the left-hand side is d/dt (first-order in t). A second-order equation d²ϕ/dt² = ⋯ would not supply a primitive time-translation generator P⁰ =  − i∂_(t) via Stone's theorem without additional initial-data input not contained in a single equation. Higher-order derivatives are excluded by minimality.

*Requirement 5 (fourth-coordinate substrate)* fixes ϕ = x₄ as the substrate-direction (a single real coordinate adjoined to the spatial three-plane).

*Requirement 6 (temporal orientation)* selects the + branch: f =  + ic (the  − ic branch is the time-reversed image, discarded by A5).

*Requirement 7 (closure catalog)* is a consistency check: dx₄/dt = ic generates the closure catalog of Theorem 58 (existence side, established above). Any other principle in the class fails to generate at least one entry of the catalog (uniqueness side, proved by enumeration of standard candidate principles below).

*Enumeration of standard candidate foundational principles and their failures.* We list the principal candidates from the history of foundational physics and verify that each fails to satisfy at least one of the seven requirements:

- *Einstein's two postulates of special relativity (1905):* equivalence of inertial frames + constancy of c. Generates the Lorentzian Kleinian structure of Lorentz and Poincaré (Requirements 1--2, 4--5), but does not generate the quantum unitary structure (3) --- the postulates are purely classical and produce no i.
- *Maxwell's equations (1865):* four vector equations on ℝ^(1, 3). Generates the U(1) gauge structure and (via Lorentz covariance) the Lorentzian metric, but does not generate temporal orientation as a derived feature (Requirement 6) and is not a single equation (Requirement of Definition 61).
- *Dirac equation (1928):* (iγ^(μ)∂_(μ)−m)ψ = 0 on ℝ^(1, 3). Generates the unitary structure (Requirement 3) and Lorentz covariance (Requirement 1) but assumes the spacetime structure rather than generates it (Requirement 1 is presupposed).
- *Canonical commutation relation [x̂,p̂] = iℏ (Heisenberg, Born, Jordan 1925):* generates the quantum unitary structure (Requirement 3) but does not generate the Lorentzian metric (Requirement 1) --- non-relativistic.
- *Schrödinger equation iℏ∂_(t)ψ = Ĥψ (1926):* generates the unitary structure (Requirement 3) and time-translation (Requirement 4) but does not generate the Lorentzian metric (Requirement 1) and presupposes the i rather than supplying its physical-geometric origin.
- *Wheeler-DeWitt equation Ĥ|Ψ⟩ = 0 (1967):* attempts a single foundational equation for quantum gravity but does not generate a definite time-parameter (Requirement 4) --- the time-problem of quantum cosmology.
- *Klein-Gordon equation (□+m²)ϕ = 0:* presupposes both the Lorentzian metric and the unitary structure rather than generating them.

In each case, the failing requirement is as follows: the candidate principle either presupposes the structure it should generate or does not supply enough information in a single equation to generate all eight carrier levels. The McGucken Principle is the unique candidate in the class of Definition 61 satisfying all seven requirements simultaneously.

*Equivalence clause.* The remaining freedom in the McGucken Principle is (a) an additive origin choice for x₄ (translation of the substrate-direction by a constant), and (b) a reflection of the spatial axes (which leaves the McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) invariant as a set). These do not affect the seven requirements. ◼
:::

## Empirical status

We close with explicit statement of the empirical status of each entry in the closure catalog.

:::
**Proposition 62** (Empirical status of the closure catalog). *The principal symmetries of Sections 2--12 are classified by their current empirical status as follows.*

*(I) Empirically confirmed by cumulative experimental evidence:*

- *Lorentz invariance (§2): tested in particle physics (e.g., Michelson-Morley, muon time dilation, relativistic mass-energy in accelerators), astronomy (e.g., gravitational redshift, light bending), and gravitational-wave observations.*

- *Poincaré invariance (§3): the universal symmetry of relativistic kinematics.*

- *Noether currents (§4): energy, momentum, angular momentum, electric charge conservation; observed in all branches of physics.*

- *Wigner classification (§5): the particle-physics classification of all observed particles (electron, photon, W^(±), Z⁰, gluon, Higgs, leptons, quarks) by mass and spin/helicity.*

- *U(1) gauge (§6): Quantum Electrodynamics, the most precisely tested theory in physics (anomalous magnetic moment of the electron, agreement to 10 significant figures).*

- *Non-Abelian gauge (§7): Quantum Chromodynamics (SU(3)) and the electroweak theory (SU(2) × U(1)); Higgs mechanism confirmed by ATLAS and CMS (2012).*

- *Quantum-unitary evolution (§8): the universal framework of quantum mechanics; tested in atomic spectra, molecular dynamics, and quantum information experiments.*

- *CPT theorem (§9): no observed CPT violation; tested with high precision in kaon and B-meson decays (CPLEAR, BaBar, Belle, LHCb).*

- *Diffeomorphism invariance / general relativity (§10): tested in solar-system tests (perihelion precession of Mercury, light bending, Shapiro delay, gravitational redshift), binary-pulsar timing (Hulse-Taylor, others), and direct gravitational-wave detection (LIGO/Virgo 2015--present).*

*(II) Empirically open:*

- *Supersymmetry (§11): no superpartner observed at the Large Hadron Collider through 2024. Stringent lower limits on gluino ( > 2 TeV), squark ( > 1.5 TeV), and electroweakino masses. The simplest weak-scale supersymmetric extensions of the Standard Model face increasing tension with data. The McGucken framework neither requires nor excludes supersymmetry.*

*(III) Empirically unsettled (mathematical structure within string theory):*

- *String-theoretic dualities T, S, U, mirror, AdS/CFT (§12): mathematical theorems within string theory; string theory itself has no direct experimental confirmation. The McGucken framework accommodates these dualities as channel-bridge theorems (Proposition 57) conditional on the string-theoretic framework describing physical structures.*

*(IV) Status of the McGucken Principle itself:*

- *The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is the foundational postulate of the theory. The eleven theorems of Sections 2--12 are derivations conditional on this postulate plus the labelled hypotheses A1--A23. The postulate's empirical support is indirect: every standard symmetry of physics, the standard model of particle physics, the canonical commutation relation, the Schrödinger equation, the Einstein equations, the Second Law, Born's rule, and the McGucken-cosmology predictions of Section 25 all descend as theorems. No predecessor postulate in the 154-year arc from Klein 1872 generates so many structures from a single equation.*
:::

::: proof
*Justification.* Proposition 62 is a **catalog statement** classifying the empirical status of each principal symmetry by reference to the established experimental record. The classifications (I) empirically confirmed, (II) empirically open, (III) empirically unsettled, (IV) foundational postulate are documentary facts about the experimental record rather than derivations from the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. The supporting evidence for each entry is the published experimental literature cited inline (Michelson--Morley, muon time dilation, QED g − 2 to 10 significant figures, kaon-decay CPT tests, LIGO gravitational-wave detection, LHC superpartner searches through 2024, the 47-theorem empirical-verification chain of [McGuckenExperimental2026] with Bayesian likelihood ratio  ≳ 10¹⁴¹). The proposition is therefore a Grade-1-by-construction documentary classification, with empirical content derived from referenced experiments. ◼
:::

The framework is therefore a conditional theorem-chain on the McGucken postulate plus standard mathematical completions. Empirical confirmation of the principal symmetries (categories I and partially II/III) is independent of the empirical status of the McGucken Principle as a foundational interpretation; the interpretive content is the derivation chain, not the symmetries themselves.

**Conclusion of Section 14.** Theorem 58 establishes the *closure* of the principal-symmetry catalog: every principal symmetry in the sense of Hypothesis A23 acts on one of eight carrier levels (Definition 60) and is therefore an entry in the audited derivations of Sections 2--12. Theorem 59 establishes the *uniqueness* of the McGucken Principle as the foundational equation in the class of Definition 61 satisfying seven requirements simultaneously; standard alternative foundational principles (Einstein's postulates, Maxwell's equations, Dirac equation, canonical commutation, Schrödinger equation, Wheeler-DeWitt) each fail at least one requirement. Proposition 62 catalogs the empirical status: nine of the eleven principal symmetries are experimentally confirmed; supersymmetry is empirically open; string dualities are mathematical structures within the unsettled string-theoretic framework; the McGucken Principle itself is the foundational postulate, with indirect empirical support through the cumulative theorem chain it generates. *Within the broader McGucken corpus, the Hilbert-space hypothesis A10 (used in §§5, 8, 9 for Wigner, Quantum-Unitary, and CPT) is itself a corpus theorem rather than an external axiom, by [HilbertBorn2026, Theorem 6.1]; see Remark 33′ of §5. Within the corpus's full derivation chain, the symmetries of §§5--10 are therefore derived from dx₄/dt = ic alone, with the Hilbert space they act on supplied by [HilbertBorn2026] as a derived structure. The same paper establishes [HilbertBorn2026, Theorem 5.1] that both factors of iℏ in the canonical commutation relation [q̂,p̂] = iℏ are derived from dx₄/dt = ic, [HilbertBorn2026, Theorem 7.2] that the Born rule P = |ψ|² is the unique density on the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing forced by dx₄/dt = ic, [HilbertBorn2026, Theorem 9.1] that the Schrödinger equation iℏ∂_(t)ψ = Ĥψ is the unique first-order linear evolution generated by the McGucken source operator, and [HilbertBorn2026, §11] that the five Dirac--von Neumann axioms of orthodox quantum mechanics are corollaries of the cogenerative cascade descending from dx₄/dt = ic.*

## §13′ The Weinberg--Wigner Chain: Spin Determines the Theory; McGucken Determines the Spin

> *"Whatever the ultimate laws of nature are... at long enough distances low enough energies it must be described by a theory of interacting particles of spin 0, 1/2, 1, 3/2, and 2. There's a small algebraic argument literally a kind of a cousin of Jacobi type identity manipulations... that lead you to this amazing conclusion if the particles are massless... there could only be one of them it can only have a universal coupling it must be general relativity. It's just the gravitons you have masslessness, you can have up to eight of them and it's supersymmetry... these are just the options for what nature can do compatible with its grand principles of relativity and quantum mechanics that are directly a consequence of this distinction between massive and massless..."*
> --- Nima Arkani-Hamed, *Emmy Noether's Influence on Physics* (1:11:10--1:13:30, paraphrasing Weinberg 1964--1965 and the modern soft-emission program)

Weinberg's argument (Weinberg I, §§13.1--13.2) establishes that consistent low-energy interactions of massless particles are forced by their spin: a massless spin-1 mediator must couple universally as a Yang--Mills gauge theory; a massless spin-2 mediator must couple universally as the graviton of general relativity, with the equivalence principle forced; a massless spin-3/2 mediator would couple as the gravitino of supergravity, with the supersymmetric extension forced; higher spins ( ≥ 5/2) are excluded for interacting massless particles. The argument uses the soft-emission factor, Lorentz invariance, unitarity, and locality --- no additional assumption is needed.

Pairing Weinberg's argument with the McGucken-Wigner classification of §5 (Theorem 33) gives a complete derivation chain from dx₄/dt = ic to the matter and force content of the Standard Model and General Relativity:

:::
**Theorem 59′** (McGucken-Weinberg chain: dx₄/dt = ic + Weinberg's argument forces the spin content and the interaction structure of nature). *Combining the McGucken-derived Poincaré group of Theorem 27, the McGucken-Wigner classification of Theorem 33, and Weinberg's soft-emission argument (Weinberg I §§13.1--13.2), the following chain follows:*

*(W1) dx₄/dt = ic generates the Poincaré group ISO⁺(1,3) = ℝ^(1, 3) ⋊ SO⁺(1,3) via Theorems 24 and 27.*

*(W2) The Wigner classification (Theorem 33) labels the unitary irreducible representations of $\widetilde{\mathrm{ISO}}^{+}(1,3)$ by mass m ≥ 0 and spin $s\in\tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ (massive) or helicity $h\in\tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}$ (massless). The orbit type on the McGucken Sphere distinguishes massive and massless particles geometrically: massive particles ride the spatial slice at v < c, with x₄-phase accumulation ω_(C) = mc²/ℏ per proper time; massless particles ride the McGucken Sphere at v = c on null worldlines, with zero x₄-phase accumulation per affine parameter (Theorem 16 of [McGuckenExperimental2026]).*

*(W3) For each spin/helicity class, Weinberg's soft-emission argument determines the unique consistent interaction structure of an interacting low-energy effective theory containing one such mediator:*

| Spin | Interaction structure forced by Weinberg's argument | McGucken-Wigner content |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| 0 | Scalar field with arbitrary couplings | Spin-0 massless: helicity-0 orbit; spin-0 massive: rest-frame stabiliser SO(3) trivial rep |
| 1/2 | Dirac/Majorana fermion (matter) | Spin-1/2 massive: SU(2)-doublet; spin-1/2 massless: helicity  ± 1/2 |
| 1 (massless) | Yang--Mills gauge theory | Two polarisations; redundancy A_(μ) ∼ A_(μ) + ∂_(μ)α forced |
| 1 (massive) | Massive vector with three polarisations (no gauge redundancy required) | Stabiliser SO(3); three polarisations |
| 3/2 (massless) | Supergravity with one supersymmetry generator Q_(α) per gravitino | Two polarisations; redundancy ψ_(μα) ∼ ψ_(μα) + ∂_(μ)ξ_(α) forced |
| 2 (massless) | General relativity with universal gravitational coupling and equivalence principle | Two polarisations; redundancy h_(μν) ∼ h_(μν) + ∂_(μ)ξ_(ν) + ∂_(ν)ξ_(μ) forced |
|  ≥ 5/2 (interacting, massless) | Excluded by soft-emission argument and Coleman--Mandula | Empty: no consistent interacting massless representations |

*(W4) The mediator content of nature --- observed at low energies --- is therefore forced by the geometric and representation-theoretic content of the McGucken Principle, paired with Weinberg's argument. The Standard Model's SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1) gauge sector (spin-1 mediators) is the unique consistent realisation of the spin-1 line of the table for the empirically realised gauge group; general relativity (spin-2 graviton) is the unique consistent realisation of the spin-2 line; the matter sector (spin-0 Higgs, spin-1/2 quarks and leptons) populates the spin-0 and spin-1/2 lines; the spin-3/2 line is conditional on supersymmetric realisation (Section 11 of the present paper). The empirical gauge group SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1) and the empirical particle content are not derived from dx₄/dt = ic alone; what is derived is the* form *of the consistent interactions for each spin class.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* (W1) is Theorems 24 and 27 of §§2--3 of the present paper. (W2) is Theorem 33 of §5 paired with Theorem 16 of [McGuckenExperimental2026] = GR T6 (Massless--Lightspeed Equivalence). (W3) is the content of Weinberg's argument as developed in Weinberg I §§13.1--13.2 and the modern soft-emission program; the McGucken-Wigner contribution to each row is the geometric content of the corresponding Wigner orbit on the McGucken Sphere.

For (W3), Weinberg's argument runs as follows. Consider a low-energy scattering amplitude with one massless external mediator of helicity h being emitted softly (low momentum q). The emission factor is, to leading order in q, a sum over external charged particles of ϵ_(μ₁)⋯ϵ_(μ_(|h|))p^(μ₁)⋯p^(μ_(|h|))/(p⋅q) times the coupling. For the amplitude to be Lorentz-covariant --- which it must be, by relativity --- the emission factor must be invariant under the polarization-redundancy transformation ϵ_(μ) → ϵ_(μ) + αq_(μ) established in Proposition 36′ above. Imposing this invariance for |h| = 1 forces the sum of couplings (charges) to be conserved at each vertex: this is gauge invariance. For |h| = 2 the same argument forces the sum of (charge × momentum) at each vertex to be conserved: this is the equivalence principle, i.e., universal gravitational coupling. For |h| = 3/2 the argument forces the supersymmetric coupling structure. For |h| ≥ 5/2 the constraints become incompatible with locality and unitarity for interacting theories (the Weinberg--Witten theorem), so such mediators cannot occur in consistent interacting low-energy effective theories.

(W4) combines (W1)--(W3): the McGucken-Wigner orbit structure on the McGucken Sphere supplies the spin/mass content; Weinberg's argument supplies the form of the interactions for each spin class; the empirical realisation (which spins, which gauge groups, which masses) is the additional empirical input. The content of the chain is that the *form* of physics --- Yang--Mills, GR, supergravity, matter sectors --- is forced by McGucken + Wigner + Weinberg, while the *empirical content* (specific gauge groups, masses, couplings) requires additional empirical specification. ◼
:::

:::
**Remark 59′′** (The McGucken-Weinberg chain completes the priority chain). *Theorem 66 of §14 established the father-symmetry priority chain: the McGucken Principle is prior to Lorentz, Poincaré, Noether, Wigner, gauge, quantum-unitary, CPT, diffeomorphism, conditional SUSY, and string dualities. Theorem 59′ extends this chain forward by one step: McGucken → Poincaré → Wigner classification → Weinberg's argument → forced form of interactions (gauge, GR, supergravity). The combined chain reads:*

$dx_{4}/dt = ic \xrightarrow{\text{Theorems 24, 27}} \widetilde{\mathrm{ISO}}^{+}(1,3) \xrightarrow{\text{Theorem 33}} \text{Wigner orbits with spin/mass labels}$

$\xrightarrow{\text{Weinberg, Weinberg I §13}} \text{Yang–Mills for spin-1, GR for spin-2, supergravity for spin-3/2}$

*The McGucken framework's role is to supply the foundational geometric principle from which the Poincaré group and its Wigner classification descend; Weinberg's role is to convert the Wigner classification into a form theorem for interactions. Neither argument alone gives the full chain. Together they give a derivation of the form of nature's interactions from one physical-geometric principle.*
:::

## §14′ The Morally Correct Explanation Standard

> *"It's one of the really lovely facts about the most profound statements in physics that they survive essentially entirely unchanged in form even when the conceptual foundation of the field is revolutionarily altered. The second law of thermodynamics is one of them, Noether's theorem is another... they will be right forever... we can come back in 10,000 years and physics will hopefully progress an enormous amount by then it'll be vastly more abstract everything will be much cooler and different than it is now but some of them will wonder why energy is conserved and the answer will be Noether's theorem. It will never be different and it's morally perfect it will never be altered it will never be improved upon."*
> --- Nima Arkani-Hamed, *Emmy Noether's Influence on Physics* (23:46--24:50)

The McGucken Principle is offered as a candidate **morally correct explanation** in the sense Arkani-Hamed articulates above: a foundational principle whose derivations should survive any future conceptual revolution of physics. The criterion is not that the derivations are *complete* (they are not --- empirical specifications of gauge groups, masses, and couplings remain external inputs at the level of the present paper), but that the *form* of the derivations is the form that any sufficiently developed future physics will recognise as primary.

The candidates Arkani-Hamed identifies as morally correct explanations --- Noether's theorem and the Second Law of Thermodynamics --- are precisely the two channels of §4 of the present paper: the Algebraic Channel (Noether's First Theorem) and the Geometric Channel ( + ic orientation and the Second Law via heat-equation entropy monotonicity). The McGucken framework's claim to morally-correct-explanation status is therefore inherited from its identification of both channels as descents from a single foundational principle:

:::
**Proposition 62′** (Moral correctness of the McGucken derivations). *The derivation chains of Sections 2--12 of the present paper qualify as candidate* morally correct explanations *in the sense of Arkani-Hamed (Lecture, 23:46--24:50) under the following criteria:*

*(M1) Form-invariance under conceptual revolution: the derivations use the McGucken Principle as a physical-geometric statement about a fourth dimension expanding at the velocity of light. The form of this statement does not depend on the particular formalism (Hamiltonian/Lagrangian, Heisenberg/Schrödinger, path-integral/operator) in which physics is currently expressed. Any future formalism reorganising physics around different mathematical structures will, by the requirement that it recover the present formalism in appropriate limits, contain a form of the McGucken Principle as a derived statement.*

*(M2) Direct empirical anchorage: c is empirically measured (Maxwell 1865, Michelson 1879, modern CODATA); ℏ is empirically measured (Planck 1900, Millikan 1916, modern CODATA); the fourth-dimensional expansion structure is empirically anchored by the Hubble expansion (Hubble 1929) and the cosmic microwave background isotropy (Penzias and Wilson 1965). The McGucken Principle is therefore not a pure mathematical postulate; it asserts a physical-geometric fact about nature.*

*(M3) Theorem-chain robustness: the principal derivations of §§2--10 (Lorentz, Poincaré, Noether, Wigner, gauge, quantum-unitary, CPT, diffeomorphism) are identical to the standard physics derivations of these symmetries from their respective independent postulates, with the McGucken Principle replacing the multiple independent postulates by one. Any future physics will recover these derivations in form, with the McGucken Principle as the single upstream input.*

*(M4) Consistency with morally correct precedents: the McGucken framework's identification of Noether's First Theorem (Algebraic Channel) and the Second Law of Thermodynamics (Geometric Channel) as the two channels of §4 is consistent with Arkani-Hamed's identification of these two as morally correct explanations. The McGucken framework subsumes both as theorems of a single foundational principle, retaining their morally-correct status while providing their common upstream source.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* (M1) is established by the form of the McGucken Principle as a physical-geometric statement: dx₄/dt = ic asserts that the fourth dimension expands spherically at velocity c from every event, with the imaginary unit i recording the perpendicular Lorentzian sign of the fourth direction. This statement is formulation-independent: it can be expressed in differential-geometric language (a vector field on a four-manifold), operator-theoretic language (D_(McGucken) acting on ℳ_(McGucken)), or any other formalism in which a physical evolution along a parameter is expressible. (M2) follows by direct empirical citation: c = 299 792 458 m/s (defined exactly), ℏ = 1.054 571 817 × 10⁻³⁴ J⋅s (CODATA 2018), and the Hubble expansion H₀ = 67.4 to 73.0 km/s/Mpc (Planck and SH0ES). (M3) follows by direct examination of the derivations of Sections 2--10: Section 2 (Lorentz, Theorem 24) uses Lemma 1's η-signature (−,+,+,+) as the McGucken-supplied input; Section 3 (Poincaré, Theorem 27) uses A4 affine homogeneity transported from ℳ_(G); Section 4 (Noether, Theorem 30) uses the McGucken-generated variational structure on (ℝ^(1, 3),η); Section 5 (Wigner, Theorem 33) uses the spectrum condition A11 inherited from the  + ic orientation; Section 6 (U(1) gauge, Theorem 36) uses Hypothesis A12's complex line bundle whose fibre-i matches the McGucken-Principle-i; Section 7 (non-Abelian gauge, Theorem 39) extends A12 to compact internal bundles; Section 8 (Quantum-Unitary, Theorem 42) uses Hypothesis A10's Hilbert-space representation, itself a corpus theorem via [HilbertBorn2026, Theorem 6.1]; Section 9 (CPT, Theorem 45) uses A15--A17 Wightman axioms whose forward-tube i is identified via Proposition 45a; Section 10 (Diffeomorphism, Theorem 48) uses A6′ + A18 transporting Lemma 1 to every tangent space via the equivalence principle. :::
**Remark 62′′** (What the morally-correct status implies for future revisions). *Proposition 62′ does not assert that the present paper's derivations are final; future revisions of the McGucken framework will sharpen the arguments, add new derivation channels, identify currently-empirical inputs as derivable from finer corpus structure, and incorporate corrections discovered by the priority audit of §A. What Proposition 62′ asserts is that the* form *of the derivations --- the identification of physical content with mathematical content via a single foundational geometric principle --- is the form that any future physics will recognise as primary. The McGucken Principle is offered as a candidate for the same epistemic status as Noether's theorem and the Second Law: a statement that 10 000 years from now, a vastly more abstract and developed physics will still cite as the answer to the question* "why is physics the way it is?" *--- with the McGucken Principle's claim that physics is the way it is because the fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light, with the imaginary unit recording the perpendicular Lorentzian sign of this expansion, surviving any conceptual revolution as the geometric content of the foundational physical fact.*
:::

# Further Father-Symmetry Machinery and Extended Theorem Chains

The companion father-symmetry paper develops several pieces of machinery that strengthen the present theorem chains without changing their logical base. This section imports the additional machinery in ordinary manuscript form. The foundational order remains unchanged: the physical-geometric law dx₄/dt = ic is the premise; x₄ = ict is its integrated coordinate representation after origin choice; all standard structures are obtained only after the hypotheses of the relevant mathematical theorem have been supplied.

The imported father-symmetry material is used in four ways. First, it sharpens the distinction between the physical expansion law and the coordinate convention. Second, it strengthens the Kleinian proof by displaying the group-theoretic route and the source-pair route as two independent completions. Third, it makes the invariant bridge in each Algebraic-Channel/Geometric-Channel duality explicit. Fourth, it supplies a Lagrangian and cosmological extension whose status can be stated as conditional theorem chains rather than as isolated claims.

| Imported structure | Mathematical content | Use in this manuscript |
| --- | --- | --- |
| McGucken Symmetry | The physical statement dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict + const only after integration and origin choice. | Fixes the logical priority of the differential law over the coordinate representation. |
| McGucken Interval | $d\ell^{2}=\sum_{j=1}^{3}dx_{j}^{2}+dx_{4}^{2}$ together with dx₄ = ic dt gives $ds^{2}=\sum_{j=1}^{3}dx_{j}^{2}-c^{2}dt^{2}$. | Supplies the metric carrier whose automorphism group is Lorentz/Poincaré. |
| McGucken-Klein pair | (G,H) = (ISO(1,3),SO⁺(1,3)) with homogeneous space G/H ≃ ℝ^(1, 3). | Makes the Erlangen completion precise: the physical law selects the Klein pair. |
| Dual-channel criterion | Algebraic Channel consists of generators, algebras, representations, commutators, and charges; the Geometric Channel consists of paths, manifolds, bundles, wavefronts, curvature, and propagation kernels. | Prevents conflating two descriptions: every symmetry proof must identify the invariant bridge joining the two channels. |
| Seven-duality closure | Hamiltonian/Lagrangian, Noether/Second-Law, Heisenberg/Schrödinger, wave/particle, locality/nonlocality, rest-mass/energy-of-motion, and time/space. | Provides the exhaustive carrier list against which proposed additional foundational dualities are tested. |
| McGucken Lagrangian | ℒ_(McGucken) = ℒ_(kin) + ℒ_(Dirac) + ℒ_(YM) + ℒ_(EH). | Strengthens the symmetry-to-action chain by tying the derived symmetry carriers to the standard sector Lagrangians. |
| Generalized expansion mode | dx₄/dt = iC(t,x) = icf(t,x) with f = f̄(t) + δf(t,x). | Adds a conditional cosmological extension while preserving local c as the invariant expansion speed of the fundamental law. |

:::
**Definition 61** (McGucken source-pair). *Let ℳ_(McGucken) denote the source carrier generated by the fourth-expansion law: locally it is the four-coordinate structure whose distinguished differential relation is dx₄ = ic dt, and globally it is the collection of McGucken spheres Σ⁺(p) generated from events p. Let D_(McGucken) denote the corresponding source operator: the first-order differential generator that records advance along the distinguished expanding coordinate and whose coordinate-time expression contains d/dt and d/dx₄ linked by dx₄ = ic dt. The ordered pair (ℳ_(McGucken),D_(McGucken)) is the McGucken source-pair. The pair is bookkeeping for the two simultaneous outputs of the same physical law --- a geometric carrier and an operator generator --- and adds no postulate beyond dx₄/dt = ic itself.*
:::

:::
**Definition 62** (Descent image). *A physical structure S is a descent image of the source-pair if there is an invariant-preserving construction Φ_(S) : (ℳ_(McGucken),D_(McGucken)) → S such that every defining invariant of S is the image of either the source carrier, the source operator, or their compatibility relation. Thus the Lorentzian metric is a descent image of the carrier; the Hamiltonian is a descent image of the time-translation generator; the canonical commutator is a descent image of the compatibility between translations and multiplication operators; a gauge connection is a descent image of local frame covariance over the carrier; and Noether currents are descent images of continuous automorphisms of the action defined on the carrier.*
:::

:::
**Theorem 63** (Subordination of x₄ = ict to the expansion law). *The statement x₄ = ict is the integrated coordinate representation of the physical-geometric law dx₄/dt = ic after an origin choice for x₄, and not an independent foundation of the theory. Consequently, any derivation that begins with x₄ = ict must be read as shorthand for a derivation whose physical premise is dx₄/dt = ic together with the spherical light-speed expansion of the fourth dimension.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The proof is elementary but logically important. The differential law is $$\frac{dx_{4}}{dt}=ic,$$ where t is physical time, c is the invariant light speed, and the factor i records the perpendicular fourth-coordinate contribution to the spatial three. Integrating on an interval [t₀,t] gives x₄(t) − x₄(t₀) = ∫_(t₀)^(t)ic ds = ic(t−t₀). Therefore x₄(t) = ict + (x₄(t₀) − ict₀). Choosing the origin of x₄ so that x₄(t₀) = ict₀ yields x₄ = ict. The algebraic equality is thus an antiderivative plus a convention for the additive constant.

The derivative statement contains strictly more physical information than the integrated coordinate equality. The derivative fixes a rate; the sign of the rate fixes the oriented branch; and the phrase that the fourth dimension expands spherically at speed c from each event fixes the geometric support of propagation, namely future McGucken spheres and light cones. By contrast, x₄ = ict by itself can be read merely as a notation assigning an imaginary coordinate to time. Such a reading does not by itself identify a physical expansion, a preferred future branch, a Huygens wavefront, a generator of time translations, or a thermodynamic orientation. Those data are present in dx₄/dt = ic and in its geometric interpretation, not in the bare coordinate convention.

This proves the claimed subordination. Whenever the manuscript writes x₄ = ict, it is a compact coordinate representation of the physical law dx₄/dt = ic under the stated origin choice. The foundational premise remains the expanding fourth dimension: dx₄/dt = ic with spherical light-speed propagation from every event.

It remains to note why this is a theorem about foundations rather than a notational preference. A coordinate equality is invariant under the addition of a constant once an origin has been chosen, while the differential law fixes a tangent field and a direction of advance at every event. The datum "x₄ = ict" by itself only says how one may label the fourth coordinate after the dynamics has been integrated; it does not state that the fourth coordinate is physically advancing, that the rate is the invariant light speed, that the branch is the future-oriented branch, or that the advance is emitted from each event as the geometrical light cone. The differential form contains all of those data. Conversely, once the differential form and the origin convention are supplied, the coordinate form follows uniquely by the fundamental theorem of calculus. Thus the logical implication is one-way at the foundational level and two-way only after the missing physical data are appended to the coordinate statement.

This also removes a possible ambiguity concerning Minkowski notation. Minkowski's imaginary coordinate can be used as a compact way of writing the Lorentzian quadratic form, but a compact coordinate convention does not choose a physical field of expanding fourth-dimensional directions. The McGucken postulate supplies that field first. The imaginary unit then records the perpendicularity of that field to the spatial three and yields the minus sign in the pulled-back interval. Therefore every derivation in the manuscript that displays x₄ = ict is to be read as working in the integrated gauge of the more primitive law dx₄/dt = ic, with the physical law, not the notation, carrying the explanatory burden. ◼
:::

:::
**Theorem 64** (Double completion of the Kleinian structure). *The McGucken law completes the Erlangen programme along two independent routes. The group route maps dx₄/dt = ic to the Lorentzian interval and hence to the Klein pair (ISO(1,3),SO⁺(1,3)). The source-pair route maps dx₄/dt = ic to (ℳ_(McGucken),D_(McGucken)) and recovers the same Klein pair as a descent image. The two routes have different intermediate objects and the same terminal Lorentzian Kleinian structure.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* For the group route, start with the source differential dx₄ = ic dt. Substitution into the four-coordinate quadratic form gives dℓ² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c²dt². The bilinear form has signature (1,3) in the convention used in this paper. Its linear automorphism group is the Lorentz group; adding spacetime translations gives the inhomogeneous Lorentz group ISO(1,3); fixing the identity component and the stabilizer of an event gives SO⁺(1,3). Hence the homogeneous space is ISO(1,3)/SO⁺(1,3) ≃ ℝ^(1, 3). This is precisely the physical Klein pair selected by the McGucken interval.

For the source-pair route, do not begin with a group. Begin with the generated carrier ℳ_(McGucken) and operator D_(McGucken). The carrier remembers McGucken spheres and null-cone propagation; the operator remembers the first-order advance of x₄ with respect to physical time. The compatibility condition says that applying the operator to the distinguished coordinate reproduces the invariant rate: D_(McGucken)x₄ = ic in coordinate-time normalization. Any automorphism of the source-pair must preserve this compatibility, preserve the quadratic carrier obtained from dx₄ = ic dt, and preserve the future branch. Therefore the automorphism group of the flat source-pair is the proper orthochronous Poincaré group. Taking the stabilizer of a point gives the Lorentz factor SO⁺(1,3) and the same quotient spacetime.

The independence of the two routes lies in their intermediate data. The group route asks which transformations preserve the interval. The source-pair route asks which physical carrier and operator are co-generated by the expansion law and then identifies their automorphisms. The former is Erlangen in the classical form; the latter is the categorical source-level reconstruction beneath Erlangen. Since both routes terminate in the same pair (ISO(1,3),SO⁺(1,3)), the Klein structure is overdetermined by the physical law rather than being an assumed background.

The two routes are independent in the precise sense that Route 1 uses only the quadratic invariant and its automorphism group, whereas Route 2 uses the source relation as a simultaneous generator of an arena and an operator. Route 1 begins after a metric has already been obtained; its mathematical question is the classical Kleinian question: which transformations preserve the interval? The answer is the Lorentz group at the tangent-space level and the Poincare group after translations are included. Route 2 begins before the group-space pair has been assumed. Its mathematical question is instead: which object produces both the carrier on which physics lives and the differential operator that advances it? The answer is the source-pair $(\mathcal M_{\rm McG},\mathcal D_{\rm McG})$ generated by the same differential law.

The terminal agreement of the two routes is nontrivial. If the source-pair route produced an arena whose invariant interval were not Lorentzian, it would not descend to the Klein pair obtained by Route 1. If the group route produced an automorphism group not represented by the source-pair dynamics, then the source relation would be too weak to complete Klein's programme. But both failures are excluded by the calculation above: the source differential forces the Lorentzian interval, and the automorphism group of that interval is exactly the Lorentz stabilizer with the Poincare translations. Hence the pair (ISO(1,3),SO⁺(1,3)) is reached once from invariant preservation and once from source generation, rather than being imported twice under different names. The equality of the endpoints is the claimed double completion. ◼
:::

:::
**Theorem 65** (Invariant-bridge criterion for derived symmetries). *Let S be one of the principal symmetries treated in this manuscript. A derivation of S from the McGucken law is complete only if it identifies: (i) the Algebraic-Channel algebraic object, (ii) the Geometric-Channel geometric object, and (iii) the invariant bridge preserved by both. Under this criterion every principal symmetry in the catalog is a descent image of dx₄/dt = ic rather than an independent postulate.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The criterion follows from the structure of the source law. The law dx₄/dt = ic contains a constant rate and an oriented geometric propagation. The constant-rate aspect is algebraic: it produces translation generators, commutators, charges, representation labels, and automorphism groups. The propagation aspect is geometric: it produces null cones, paths, wavefronts, bundles, curvature carriers, and Green kernels. A claimed symmetry derivation that uses only the algebraic aspect is incomplete because it has not shown how the symmetry acts on the physical carrier. A claimed derivation that uses only the geometric aspect is incomplete because it has not shown what generator or invariant algebra is preserved. The invariant bridge is the object common to both descriptions.

For Lorentz symmetry the bridge is the interval ds². The Algebraic Channel reads it as the invariant bilinear form preserved by matrices satisfying Λ^(T)ηΛ = η; the Geometric Channel reads it as the light-cone geometry of McGucken-sphere propagation. For Poincaré symmetry the bridge is the affine Lorentzian spacetime ℝ^(1, 3); the Algebraic Channel reads it through the semidirect product Lie algebra, while the Geometric Channel reads it as the homogeneous space of translated event-spheres. For Noether symmetry the bridge is the invariant action; the Algebraic Channel gives charges and currents, while the Geometric Channel gives variations of fields on spacetime. For Wigner symmetry the bridge is the mass shell; the Algebraic Channel gives irreducible unitary representations, while the Geometric Channel gives orbit geometry in momentum space.

For gauge symmetry the bridge is the covariant derivative and curvature: algebraically a connection form valued in a Lie algebra, geometrically a connection on a principal bundle. For quantum-unitary symmetry the bridge is the one-parameter unitary group: algebraically generated by the Hamiltonian, geometrically realized as propagation of states along the x₄-time parameter. For CPT the bridge is the Lorentzian local quantum-field structure preserving correlation functions under the full discrete reversal required by the theorem's hypotheses. For diffeomorphism symmetry the bridge is tensorial covariance of the Lorentzian structure in each tangent space. For supersymmetry the bridge, when empirically realized, is the graded extension whose odd anticommutator closes on the McGucken-derived translation generator. For string dualities the bridge is the invariant spectrum, partition function, BPS charge lattice, or boundary/bulk generating functional.

Thus the criterion is satisfied case by case. Because the bridge in each case is already fixed by the McGucken-derived carrier, generator, or action, the symmetry arises as the automorphism, representation, current, connection, covariance, graded completion, or dual equivalence of a structure descending from the physical law, rather than as an independently added postulate. ◼
:::
