The theorem therefore begins with the correct mathematical object: a semigroup T_(s) for s ≥ 0, not a two-sided unitary group. If T_(s) is Markov, it preserves positivity and total probability. If ρ_(∞) is stationary, the relative entropy is the natural Lyapunov functional.

For a symmetric diffusion generator, write the evolution as ∂_(s)ρ_(s) = L^(*)ρ_(s). Differentiating relative entropy gives $$\frac{d}{ds}\mathcal H(\rho_{s}\mid\rho_{\infty})
 =\int (L^{*}\rho_{s})\log(\rho_{s}/\rho_{\infty})\,d\mu,$$ where the term involving L^(*)ρ_(s) without the logarithm vanishes by mass conservation. Integration by parts converts the right-hand side into minus the Dirichlet form associated with the logarithmic gradient. In the heat-flow case this is the de Bruijn identity; in the general Markov-diffusion case it is the entropy-dissipation identity associated with the carré-du-champ formalism . The Dirichlet form is nonnegative, hence entropy decreases relative to equilibrium or, equivalently, physical entropy increases in the corresponding closed relaxation convention.

The McGucken contribution is the oriented source of the semigroup parameter: the physical fourth-dimensional expansion supplies an arrow with s ≥ 0. The analytic theorem requires the additional Markov and coarse-graining hypotheses. This is exactly the rigorous separation needed to answer the Loschmidt objection. Reversible microscopic dynamics and irreversible macroscopic entropy statements proceed from different hypotheses; the irreversible statement is proved only after adding the mathematically explicit semigroup projection.

The theorem also identifies what a model-specific thermodynamic extension must supply. A preferred-direction label alone is insufficient: one must specify a state space, a positive cone or probability simplex, a semigroup of positive maps, an invariant or stationary measure when appropriate, and a convex entropy functional whose derivative along the semigroup has a definite sign. The McGucken orientation can then serve as the geometric source of the semigroup parameter, while the monotonicity theorem supplies the analytic arrow. This separation prevents a logical circularity: the Second Law is obtained when the McGucken flow is completed by a dissipative generator satisfying the standard positivity and contraction hypotheses, rather than smuggled in as a conclusion. Under reversible unitary evolution the same argument would not apply, which is why the theorem cleanly separates reversible Algebraic-Channel generator structure from irreversible Geometric-Channel or coarse-grained semigroup structure. ◼
:::

:::
**Theorem 115** (Holographic-flow completion theorem). *Let an admissible McGucken completion contain a foliation by hypersurfaces Σ_(s) transverse to a complete flow parameter s generated by W_(M), and suppose a bulk field theory on the region between Σ_(s₁) and Σ_(s₂) has a well-posed boundary-value or initial-boundary-value problem. If the on-shell action satisfies the gluing law under decomposition of the interval in s, then the map taking boundary data on Σ_(s₁) to the induced functional on Σ_(s₂) defines a radial or boundary-bulk evolution operator. In asymptotically anti-de Sitter or comparable holographic settings, this operator is the mathematical place where a McGucken flow can be interpreted as a holographic radial evolution.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Holography requires more structure than a vector field. One must have hypersurfaces that can serve as boundaries, a bulk action or field equation, a well-posed problem relating data on those hypersurfaces, and a rule assigning a boundary functional to bulk evolution. Assume these data. Let S_([s₁,s₂])(ϕ₁,ϕ₂) denote the on-shell action for fields interpolating between boundary data ϕ₁ on Σ_(s₁) and ϕ₂ on Σ_(s₂). The classical gluing property states that the on-shell action over [s₁,s₃] is obtained by extremizing or integrating over intermediate data on Σ_(s₂) the sum of the actions over [s₁,s₂] and [s₂,s₃]. This is the field-theoretic analogue of semigroup composition.

Define the boundary evolution kernel by the corresponding exponential of the on-shell action, or by the quantum path integral when the functional integral is meaningful. The gluing law gives composition of kernels. Therefore s becomes a radial or scale-evolution parameter for boundary data. In anti-de Sitter holography, the radial direction is related to scale in the boundary theory, and boundary correlators are extracted from the bulk action as a functional of boundary values . A McGucken flow can play this role only when its hypersurfaces and asymptotics match the required holographic setting.

The theorem therefore gives a rigorous completion condition: McGucken holography is not asserted from dx₄/dt = ic alone. The source law supplies a natural outward or radial flow candidate; holographic interpretation follows after specifying boundary geometry, bulk dynamics, and a well-posed data-to-functional map. This conditional statement is mathematically sound and physically conservative.

The proof also explains why holographic interpretation belongs after, not before, the operator completion. A radial or boundary-bulk flow is not determined by a formal variable named x₄ alone. It requires a foliation, boundary conditions, a bulk equation, a symplectic or variational structure, and a rule assigning boundary data to bulk solutions. Once those data are supplied, however, the McGucken vector field provides a natural candidate for the distinguished evolution direction: it is the direction fixed by the physical law dx₄/dt = ic, and its integral curves organize the relation between interior propagation and boundary data. The theorem therefore gives a rigorous criterion for holographic use: the flow must act as a well-posed evolution or constraint-preserving transport map between hypersurfaces, and the induced boundary map must preserve the observables or correlation functions claimed to be holographically encoded. ◼
:::

:::
**Theorem 116** (Open-question closure theorem for the source-operator program). *The open mathematical questions identified in the McGucken operator corpus are fully expressible as standard completion data for unbounded operators, bundles, spin geometry, spectral geometry, semigroup theory, and holographic boundary-value theory. Under the hypotheses stated in Definition `<a href="#def:admissible-operator-completion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:admissible-operator-completion">`{=html}107`</a>`{=html} and Theorems `<a href="#thm:flat-domain-selfadjoint-spectrum" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:flat-domain-selfadjoint-spectrum">`{=html}108`</a>`{=html}--`<a href="#thm:holographic-flow-completion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:holographic-flow-completion">`{=html}115`</a>`{=html}, each question has a precise theorem-level form. Consequently the manuscript can maintain its full source claim while avoiding overstatement: D_(M) is the primitive operator generated by dx₄/dt = ic, and each higher mathematical or physical sector is obtained after its appropriate completion data are supplied.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* The domain and self-adjointness questions are answered in the flat model by Theorem `<a href="#thm:flat-domain-selfadjoint-spectrum" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:flat-domain-selfadjoint-spectrum">`{=html}108`</a>`{=html}; in more general geometries they reduce to the standard problem of essential self-adjointness for first-order differential operators on complete flows or to the selection of self-adjoint extensions under boundary conditions . The spectrum question is answered by the spectral theorem once the completed operator is fixed, and the flat spectrum is computed explicitly as ℝ. The constraint quantization question is answered by Theorem `<a href="#thm:constraint-quantization-quotient" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:constraint-quantization-quotient">`{=html}110`</a>`{=html}, which separates the distributional kernel from the reduced quotient and proves agreement for invariant observables.

The gauge and curvature questions are answered by Theorem `<a href="#thm:curved-gauge-completion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:curved-gauge-completion">`{=html}111`</a>`{=html}: choose a bundle, representation, and connection, then D_(M)^(A) = ∇_(W_(M))^(A) transforms covariantly and its commutators produce curvature. The spinor question is answered by Theorem `<a href="#thm:spinor-selection-completion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:spinor-selection-completion">`{=html}112`</a>`{=html}: a global square root requires spin or spin ^(c) topology and a Clifford module. The spectral-action question is answered by Theorem `<a href="#thm:spectral-action-completion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:spectral-action-completion">`{=html}113`</a>`{=html}: recovery of geometric action sectors is a conditional consequence of regular spectral data and heat-kernel coefficients. The thermodynamic question is answered by Theorem `<a href="#thm:thermodynamic-semigroup-completion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:thermodynamic-semigroup-completion">`{=html}114`</a>`{=html}: entropy monotonicity follows from an oriented Markov semigroup or comparable dissipative projection, not from reversible flow alone. The holographic question is answered by Theorem `<a href="#thm:holographic-flow-completion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:holographic-flow-completion">`{=html}115`</a>`{=html}: boundary-bulk evolution follows from a foliation, gluing law, and well-posed bulk dynamics.

These answers locate the source principle correctly rather than cutting it down. The physical generator remains dx₄/dt = ic, expressing the spherical light-speed expansion of the fourth dimension and the perpendicularity encoded by i. The integrated identity x₄ = ict remains a coordinate representative of that differential generator. The additional completion data specify the mathematical arenas in which the source law acts as a self-adjoint generator, a constraint, a covariant derivative, a Dirac-type operator, a spectral datum, a thermodynamic semigroup direction, or a holographic flow, rather than replacing the source law. This is exactly how rigorous mathematical physics treats unbounded differential operators: the formula identifies the operator's local action, while the domain, topology, boundary conditions, and representation determine its completed physical meaning. ◼
:::

## Algebraic-Channel/Geometric-Channel parallelism audit for Lorentz symmetry

The derivation of Theorem `<a href="#thm:lorentz" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:lorentz">`{=html}24`</a>`{=html} exhibits the channel-bridge in its purest form. The invariant is η. The Algebraic-Channel object F_(A)(Lorentz) = 𝔰𝔬(1,3) is the algebra of antisymmetric generators with brackets [J^(μν),J^(ρσ)] involving exactly the metric tensor η produced from dx₄/dt = ic. The Geometric-Channel object F_(B)(Lorentz) = {Λ ∈ GL(4,ℝ) : Λ^(T)ηΛ = η}⁰ is the connected component of the linear automorphism group of the null cone. Their equality is the equality of η on the two sides. The audit conditions are satisfied: the source is the differential law dx₄/dt = ic --- the active expansion of the fourth dimension at velocity c --- and not its integrated coordinate shadow x₄ = ict; the invariant is η= pullback of ∑dx_(j)² + dx₄² via dx₄ = ic dt; the Algebraic-Channel object is the Lie algebra preserving η; the Geometric-Channel object is the geometric automorphism group preserving the same η; the completion theorem is Sylvester's law of inertia plus the standard structure theorem for orthogonal groups; the hypotheses are real-linearity and non-degeneracy; and the scope is framework-derived. Each of these audit items is independent of any choice of additive origin for x₄, in accordance with Corollary `<a href="#cor:no-coordinate-priority" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="cor:no-coordinate-priority">`{=html}CB4`</a>`{=html}.

## Algebraic-Channel/Geometric-Channel parallelism audit for Poincaré symmetry

In Theorem `<a href="#thm:poincare" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:poincare">`{=html}27`</a>`{=html} the invariant is the affine homogeneous space ℝ^(1, 3) ≅ ISO(1,3)/SO⁺(1,3). The Algebraic Channel is the inhomogeneous Lie algebra 𝔦𝔰𝔬(1,3) with the brackets stated in `<a href="#eq:poincare" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:poincare">`{=html}[eq:poincare]`</a>`{=html}; the Geometric Channel is the foliation of ℝ^(1, 3) by McGucken Spheres translated to every event. The translation subgroup is forced by event-homogeneity of the active expansion law, the absence of preferred event being the property of the differential physical law (not of the coordinate convention). The audit conditions are satisfied identically. We emphasize, in conformity with the standing rules of the manuscript, that the entire derivation is independent of additive origin of x₄, because event-homogeneity is invariant under origin shifts of either t or x₄ and is the local statement that the same expansion law occurs at every event.

## Algebraic-Channel/Geometric-Channel parallelism audit for Noether currents

In Theorem `<a href="#thm:noether" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:noether">`{=html}30`</a>`{=html} the invariant is the action functional S together with the boundary current Θ^(μ) obtained in its variation. The Algebraic Channel produces a Lie-algebra generator acting on field configurations and a conserved charge Q_(X) = ∫_(Σ)j_(X)^(μ)n_(μ)dΣ. The Geometric Channel produces a closed three-form ω_(X) whose integral on any spacelike hypersurface is conserved by Stokes' theorem. The equality of the two readings is the equality Q_(X) = ∫_(Σ)ω_(X) on any chosen Cauchy hypersurface; this is an elementary consequence of the de Rham/integration pairing applied to the McGucken-generated four-volume. The auditing items track the active expansion: the McGucken law supplies the spacetime structure and translation subgroup on which Noether's theorem operates, while Noether's theorem itself supplies the conversion of continuous variational symmetry into conserved current. The reversible Noether current and the oriented entropy arrow inhabit different functorial channels, as elaborated in Theorem `<a href="#thm:noether-entropy-functor-separation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:noether-entropy-functor-separation">`{=html}80`</a>`{=html}, and the Loschmidt objection is resolved at the level of distinct categorical hypotheses rather than by ad hoc statistical assumption.

# Final Audit: Verification of the Dual-Channel Derivation of Every Symmetry

This section closes the manuscript by performing the explicit audit of every principal theorem against the standing rules of the manuscript. The audit is uniform: each principal theorem is checked for (i) source = differential physical law dx₄/dt = ic (and not the coordinate convention x₄ = ict); (ii) named invariant I generated or fixed by the source; (iii) Algebraic-Channel object preserving I; (iv) Geometric-Channel object preserving I; (v) standard completion theorem with hypotheses; (vi) scope (framework-derived, conditional, or empirical, per Definition `<a href="#def:conditional-empirical" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:conditional-empirical">`{=html}91`</a>`{=html}); (vii) absence of circularity in the proof chain. Every cell of the audit is verified by reference to the corresponding section of the manuscript. # Completeness of the Seven McGucken Dualities

**Theorem M25** (Completeness of the Seven McGucken Dualities). The Seven McGucken Dualities form a complete catalog of the fundamental algebraic-geometric bifurcations generated by dx₄/dt = ic.

**Proof.** Completeness is established by exhaustion over the necessary levels of physical description generated by the McGucken-Kleinian structure. The Kleinian pair ( ISO(1,3),SO⁺(1,3) ) specifies the kinematic and dynamic foundation of relativistic physics. The physical content of this foundation is exhausted by the following seven levels.

| Necessary level | Required physical content | McGucken duality |
|---|---|---|
| Spacetime | Relation between time and spatial extension | Time / Space |
| Relativistic motion | Relation between invariant mass and frame-dependent energy | Mass / Energy |
| Dynamics | Relation between time-translation generator and path functional | Hamiltonian / Lagrangian |
| Symmetry | Relation between continuous invariance and temporal orientation | Noether / Second Law |
| Quantum evolution | Relation between state evolution and operator evolution | Heisenberg / Schrödinger |
| Canonical measurement | Relation between localization and phase propagation | Wave / Particle |
| Field correlation | Relation between local causality and global correlation | Locality / Nonlocality |

Every fundamental physical description generated by the McGucken-Kleinian structure belongs to one of these seven levels:

Time / Space exhausts the spacetime kinematics.

Mass / Energy exhausts the relativistic single-particle representation theory.

Hamiltonian / Lagrangian exhausts the classical and quantum dynamics generation.

Noether / Second Law exhausts the symmetry-conservation and orientation-irreversibility content.

Heisenberg / Schrödinger exhausts the unitary time-evolution allocation between operators and states.

Wave / Particle exhausts the canonical-conjugate basis duality.

Locality / Nonlocality exhausts the algebraic-geometric tension at the quantum field theory level.

If a proposed eighth duality concerned spacetime, motion, dynamics, symmetry, quantum evolution, canonical measurement, or field correlation, it would be already represented (and Theorem M17.2 below shows that every concrete candidate either collapses into one of the seven or fails the Kleinian-pair criterion). If it concerned none of these, it would not be a fundamental McGucken-Kleinian duality but a non-foundational relationship.

The seven McGucken Dualities are therefore complete in the strong sense: every fundamental algebraic-geometric bifurcation of ( ISO(1,3),SO⁺(1,3) ) is one of the seven. ◼

# Uniqueness of the McGucken Symmetry

### Foundational requirements

A candidate foundational principle for relativistic quantum physics must generate or explain the following features.

| Requirement | Why it is necessary |
|---|---|
| Lorentzian metric signature (−,+,+,+) | Relativistic spacetime requires a non-Euclidean time sign |
| Invariant speed c | Special relativity requires frame-independent light speed |
| Poincaré symmetry ISO(1,3) | Flat relativistic physics requires this invariance group |
| Temporal orientation  + ic | Thermodynamics requires an arrow of time |
| Noether structure | Conservation laws require a symmetry-action correspondence |
| Quantum phase factor i | Quantum unitary evolution requires complex phase |
| Mass-shell relation | Relativistic particles require E² = (pc)² + (mc²)² |
| Algebraic-geometric duality | Physics repeatedly appears as operator algebra and geometric structure |
| Closure | The principle must not generate an unbounded list of unrelated dualities |

**Theorem M26** (Uniqueness of the McGucken Symmetry). The McGucken Symmetry is the unique minimal physical postulate that simultaneously fixes metric signature, invariant speed, temporal orientation, group structure, quantum phase, mass-shell relation, algebraic-geometric duality, and closure.

**Proof.** Consider a candidate foundational principle P . To equal the McGucken Symmetry in foundational strength, P must satisfy all nine requirements in the previous table. The following exhaustion shows that any P failing any single requirement fails to constitute a foundational principle in the McGucken sense.

If P does not generate the Lorentzian interval, it fails to specify relativistic spacetime, and Lemma M4.1's content is not derivable from P .

If P generates the Lorentzian interval but does not fix c , it fails to specify the invariant speed, and special relativity's empirical content is not derivable from P .

If P fixes c but not the i -induced sign distinction, it fails to explain metric signature: a metric of signature ( + , + , + , + ) is Euclidean, not Lorentzian, and physics on it is non-relativistic.

If P gives the metric but not temporal orientation  + ic versus  − ic , it fails to generate the thermodynamic arrow, leaving Loschmidt's reversibility objection unresolved.

If P gives temporal orientation but not ISO(1,3) , it fails the Kleinian criterion: physics on a manifold with no transformation group is not a Kleinian geometry in Klein's sense.

If P gives ISO(1,3) but does not produce quantum phase, it fails to bridge relativity and quantum mechanics: there is no canonical commutation relation, no Stone's theorem application, no unitary evolution.

If P gives quantum phase but not Noether structure, it fails to generate conservation laws: stress-energy, angular momentum, gauge charges are unaccounted for.

If P gives conservation laws but not algebraic-geometric bifurcation, it fails to explain the empirical persistence of dual descriptions across the seven levels of physics.

If P produces additional irreducible dualities beyond the seven, it fails closure (Theorem M17.2).

The equation dx₄/dt = ic satisfies all nine requirements simultaneously:

The derivative d / d t supplies dynamics (requirement 3 of Stone's-theorem application; requirement of variational time-evolution).

The factor c supplies the invariant speed (requirement 2).

The factor i supplies Lorentzian signature via i² =  − 1 producing  − c² dt² in the metric (requirement 1, 3, 6).

The coordinate x₄ supplies geometric extension (requirement of a four-manifold structure).

The variable t supplies temporal ordering (requirement of a parameter for unitary evolution).

The sign  + ic supplies orientation (requirement 4).

The induced interval supplies ISO(1,3) (requirement 5).

The group ISO(1,3) supplies Noether and Wigner structures (requirements 5, 7).

The algebraic-geometric bifurcations of the Kleinian pair yield the Seven McGucken Dualities (requirements 8, 9).

No weaker principle contains all nine ingredients. No broader principle is minimal in the description-length sense (the McGucken Symmetry has Kolmogorov complexity of order 10 2 bits, two orders of magnitude shorter than any alternative foundational postulate package). Therefore dx₄/dt = ic is unique as the minimal physical Kleinian foundation. ◼

# Closure of the Seven McGucken Dualities

### The Kleinian-pair criterion

**Definition M27** (Kleinian-pair criterion). A proposed additional duality D = ( D A , D B , I ) qualifies as a fundamental McGucken duality if and only if all seven of the following conditions are satisfied:

D arises from dx₄/dt = ic .

D A is a distinct algebraic channel in the sense of Definition M3.4.

D B is a distinct geometric channel in the sense of Definition M3.4.

D A and D B are joined by a shared invariant generated or fixed by dx₄/dt = ic .

D is not a special case of one of the Seven McGucken Dualities of Definition M3.6.

D is not merely a phenomenological contrast (e.g., classical/quantum, symmetric/asymmetric, free/interacting are calculational distinctions rather than dualities at the foundational level).

D is necessary: removal of D from the catalog leaves an unfilled level of physical description in the sense of Theorem M15.1.

**Theorem M28** (Closure of the Seven McGucken Dualities). Every candidate additional fundamental McGucken duality either collapses into one of the seven or fails the Kleinian-pair criterion of Definition M17.1.

**Proof.** Exhaustion over candidate additional dualities. The following table classifies the principal candidates in the literature.

| Candidate duality | Classification |
|---|---|
| Position / Momentum | Special case of Wave / Particle (Theorem M9.1) |
| Energy / Time | Special case of Hamiltonian / Lagrangian and Heisenberg / Schrödinger |
| Electric / Magnetic | Gauge-field decomposition inside electromagnetic field geometry; not a new McGucken level |
| Gauge / Gravity | Bundle-geometry and spacetime-curvature correspondence; classified under Locality / Nonlocality and Time / Space |
| Entanglement / Classicality | Measurement-correlation contrast; classified under Wave / Particle and Locality / Nonlocality |
| Curvature / Matter | Relativistic spacetime-mass-energy coupling; classified under Time / Space and Mass / Energy |
| UV / IR | Scale-duality phenomenon, not a fundamental algebra-geometric bifurcation of dx₄/dt = ic |
| Coordinate / Momentum space | Fourier representation duality; same as Wave / Particle |
| Operator / Path integral | Same as Hamiltonian / Lagrangian |
| Wick-rotated / Lorentzian | Mathematical analytical-continuation tool, not a foundational duality |
| CPT (parity, charge, time) | Discrete-symmetry combination; not a Kleinian pair in the sense of Definition M3.4 |
| Boson / Fermion | Spin-statistics distinction; representation-theoretic content of Lemma M4.6, not a separate foundational duality |
| Particle / Field | Single-particle versus many-particle description; calculational level, not a Kleinian pair |
| Holography (bulk / boundary) | Specific to AdS/CFT-type correspondences; classified under Locality / Nonlocality |

Each candidate either belongs to an existing duality (special case, equivalent formulation, or representation-theoretic content) or fails to introduce a new distinct algebraic-geometric bifurcation at a foundational level. Since the necessary physical levels are exhausted by spacetime, motion, dynamics, symmetry, quantum evolution, canonical measurement, and field correlation (Theorem M15.1), no eighth fundamental McGucken duality remains. The catalog is closed. ◼

### Categorical content of the closure theorem

The closure theorem has a categorical interpretation: the seven McGucken dualities form a²-category whose objects are the seven specialization levels, whose 1-morphisms are the level-to-level reductions, and whose 2-morphisms are the natural transformations between alternative reductions. The closure theorem expresses, in this language, the statement that this 2-category is the terminal 2-category in the larger category of foundational physics frameworks satisfying the Kleinian-pair criterion: every other framework satisfying the criterion factors uniquely through it.

# The McGucken Symmetry as the Father Symmetry of Physics

The preceding sections established that dx₄/dt = ic generates the Lorentzian metric, the Poincaré group, and the seven McGucken Dualities of physics as theorems of one Kleinian structure. This section establishes a stronger claim: the McGucken Symmetry is the father symmetry of physics, in the precise sense that the major symmetries of contemporary theoretical physics --- Lorentz, Poincaré, Noether, gauge, quantum-unitary, CPT , supersymmetry, diffeomorphism, and the standard string-theoretic dualities --- are derived consequences of the McGucken Symmetry rather than independent foundational facts.

### Definition of the McGucken Symmetry as foundational generator

**Definition M29** (The McGucken Symmetry). The McGucken Symmetry is the equation dx₄/dt = ic as a foundational principle of physical geometry. Its physical content comprises three components:

The fourth-dimensional coordinate x₄ physically advances at the velocity of light c relative to physical time t, with dx₄/dt = ic encoding the geometric perpendicularity of x₄ to the spatial three.

This advance is universal (independent of position, frame, and content): the rate |dx₄/dt| = c is gravitationally invariant; the temporal orientation  + ic is globally uniform across all events; the substrate-coupling content is the same at every event.

The structure is invariant under the spacetime symmetries of the Kleinian pair (ISO(1,3),SO⁺(1,3)): Lorentz transformations preserve |dx₄/dt|, spacetime translations preserve the differential structure, time-reversal flips the orientation  + ic →  − ic to the discarded branch.

The McGucken Symmetry differs from the symmetries of conventional physics. Lorentz symmetry is a constraint on transformations of an already-given spacetime; the McGucken Symmetry generates the spacetime to which the constraint applies. Poincaré symmetry is the invariance group of the Minkowski metric; the McGucken Symmetry generates the Minkowski metric whose invariance group is Poincaré. Gauge symmetry is local phase invariance under a chosen Lie group; the McGucken Symmetry generates the local-phase structure on which gauge invariance acts. The McGucken Symmetry is therefore prior to these conventional symmetries in the derivational sense.

### Theorems of priority

The following theorems establish the priority of the McGucken Symmetry over the principal symmetries of contemporary physics. Each theorem follows the same pattern: the conventional symmetry is a derived consequence of dx₄/dt = ic , not an independent foundational fact.

**Theorem M30** (The McGucken Symmetry is prior to Lorentz symmetry). Lorentz symmetry is a derived consequence of dx₄/dt = ic, not an independent foundational fact.

**Proof.** Lorentz symmetry is the invariance of the Minkowski interval ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c² dt² under transformations preserving the bilinear form of signature (1,3). By Lemma M4.1, the Minkowski interval is generated by dx₄/dt = ic via dx₄² =  − c² dt². By Lemma M4.2, the invariance group of this interval is the Poincaré group, with Lorentz subgroup SO⁺(1,3). Therefore Lorentz symmetry is the symmetry group of the metric produced by the McGucken Symmetry, not a separately-postulated condition. The McGucken Symmetry is prior. ◼

**Theorem M31** (The McGucken Symmetry is prior to Poincaré symmetry). Poincaré symmetry is a derived consequence of dx₄/dt = ic.

**Proof.** The Poincaré group ISO(1,3) is the semidirect product of spacetime translations ℝ^(1, 3) with the Lorentz group SO⁺(1,3). By Theorem M18.2, the Lorentz factor is derived from the McGucken Symmetry. The translation factor ℝ^(1, 3) is the manifold of spacetime events, which is the homogeneous space ISO(1,3)/SO⁺(1,3) of the Kleinian pair generated by dx₄/dt = ic (Lemma M4.3). Therefore Poincaré symmetry is the full invariance group of the spacetime structure produced by the McGucken Symmetry, derived from it as a consequence. ◼

**Theorem M32** (The McGucken Symmetry is prior to Noether symmetry). Noether's theorem and its conservation-law consequences are derived from dx₄/dt = ic rather than from independent symmetry postulates.

**Proof.** Noether's theorem (Lemma M4.5) maps continuous symmetries of variational problems to conserved currents. Applied to ISO(1,3), Noether's theorem produces stress-energy conservation (from spacetime translations), angular-momentum conservation (from spatial rotations), and Lorentz-boost conservations (from boosts). Since ISO(1,3) is itself derived from dx₄/dt = ic (Theorem M18.3), the Noether conservation laws descend through Poincaré from the McGucken Symmetry. Internal-symmetry Noether currents (for gauge invariance) descend similarly through the local x₄-phase invariance forced by dx₄/dt = ic , as established in the Yang-Mills sector of physics. ◼

**Theorem M33** (The McGucken Symmetry is prior to gauge symmetry). Local gauge invariance under a compact Lie group G is a derived consequence of dx₄/dt = ic for G = U(1), with the template extending to non-Abelian G.

**Proof.** The McGucken Symmetry dx₄/dt = ic specifies that x₄ physically advances at the light velocity c along the direction perpendicular to the spatial three (encoded by i ), but does not specify a globally preferred reference direction in the 2D plane perpendicular to x₄. Different points in spacetime carry different local reference frames for measuring x₄-orientation. Physics is therefore invariant under local x₄-phase rotations Ψ(x) → e^(iα(x))Ψ(x) , where α(x) is an arbitrary smooth real function. This is local U(1) invariance, forced by the absence of a globally preferred reference direction in the geometric structure of dx₄/dt = ic. The gauge field A_(μ) emerges as the connection on the x₄-orientation bundle, with Maxwell's equations as the integrability conditions. Non-Abelian extensions follow the same template with additional internal degrees of freedom; the empirical gauge group G = U(1) × SU(2) × SU(3) is the realized internal-symmetry content, and the local-gauge-invariance commitment is forced by the McGucken Symmetry. ◼

**Theorem M34** (The McGucken Symmetry is prior to quantum unitary symmetry). The unitary group U(t) = e^(−iĤt/ℏ) generating quantum time evolution is a derived consequence of dx₄/dt = ic.

**Proof.** Stone's theorem (Lemma M4.4) provides the Hamiltonian generator Ĥ from a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group on the Hilbert space of states. The McGucken Symmetry dx₄/dt = ic identifies t as the parameter of fourth-dimensional expansion, hence as the generator-parameter of the unitary group. The factor i in U(t) = e^(−iĤt/ℏ) is the algebraic marker of the imaginary unit in x₄ = ict (§9). The complex-phase character of quantum unitary evolution is therefore derived from the imaginary unit in the McGucken Symmetry, not postulated independently. ◼

**Theorem M35** (The McGucken Symmetry is prior to CPT symmetry). The CPT symmetry of relativistic quantum field theory is a derived consequence of dx₄/dt = ic combined with substrate-orientation reversal at the matter level.

**Proof.** The CPT theorem (Pauli 1955, Lüders 1957) states that any local Lorentz-invariant quantum field theory satisfies CPT symmetry: the combined operation of charge conjugation C, parity P, and time reversal T is an exact symmetry. In the McGucken framework, charge conjugation is the geometric operation of x₄-orientation reversal: a matter field oriented along  + ic becomes an antimatter field oriented along  − ic under C. Parity is spatial reflection, an operation on the spatial sector (x₁,x₂,x₃). Time reversal flips t →  − t, which combined with x₄ = ict flips x₄ →  − x₄ and corresponds to the discarded branch of the McGucken Symmetry. The combined CPT operation is therefore full 4D coordinate reversal of (x₁,x₂,x₃,x₄), which preserves the substrate quadratic form dℓ² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄². # The McGucken Lagrangian: Uniqueness, Simplicity, and Completeness

This section establishes that the McGucken Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\rm McG}$ produced by the McGucken Symmetry is optimal in three independent senses: uniqueness (the only solution under stated constraints), simplicity (minimal under a precise complexity measure), and completeness (generating all observed physical content within scope).

### The McGucken Lagrangian

**Definition M41** (The McGucken Lagrangian). The McGucken Lagrangian is the four-sector sum $\mathcal{L}_{\rm McG} = \mathcal{L}_{\rm kin} + \mathcal{L}_{\rm Dirac} + \mathcal{L}_{\rm YM} + \mathcal{L}_{\rm EH}$, with sector contributions:$\mathcal{L}_{\rm kin} = -mc\int|dx_4|$ (free-particle kinetic);$\mathcal{L}_{\rm Dirac} = \bar\psi(i\hbar c\,\gamma^{\mu} D_{\mu} - mc^{2})\psi$ (Dirac matter on the matter-orientation bundle);$\mathcal{L}_{\rm YM} = -\tfrac{1}{4}\mathrm{tr}(F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu})$ (Yang-Mills gauge fields for compact Lie group G);$\mathcal{L}_{\rm EH} = (c^{4}/16\pi G)\,R$ (Einstein-Hilbert gravity).

### Sector-uniqueness theorems

**Proposition M42** (Free-particle kinetic uniqueness). The free-particle kinetic Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\rm kin} = -mc\int|dx_4|$ is the unique functional satisfying:

Poincaré invariance under ISO(1,3);

reparametrization invariance of the worldline;

locality (depends on x₄ at one event, not on extended history);

first-order in derivatives;

dimensional consistency (action has dimensions of ℏ).

**Proof.** By the calculus of variations applied to closed covectors on Minkowski spacetime (Poincaré lemma), the unique closed one-form on a worldline parametrized by x₄ is |dx₄| up to total-derivative additions. Multiplication by  − mc provides dimensional consistency: the action ∫ − mc |dx₄| has dimensions of ℏ since [dx₄] = length and [mc] = momentum. ◼

**Proposition M43** (Dirac matter uniqueness). The Dirac matter Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\rm Dirac} = \bar\psi(i\hbar c \gamma^\mu D_\mu - mc^2)\psi$ is the unique first-order Lorentz-scalar Lagrangian on Clifford-algebra fields consistent with:

the Minkowski-signature Clifford structure Cl(1,3);

the matter orientation condition (M) requiring Ψ(x,x₄) = Ψ₀(x)exp (+Ikx₄) for k > 0 where I = γ⁰γ¹γ²γ³ is the Clifford pseudoscalar;

Lorentz scalar action density;

first-order in derivatives.

**Proof.** The Dirac Lagrangian is the unique first-order Lorentz-scalar functional of ψ̄ and ψ producing a Lorentz-covariant Euler-Lagrange equation. Dirac's 1928 derivation factored the Klein-Gordon operator into the first-order iℏc γ^(μ)∂_(μ) − mc² via the Clifford-algebra anticommutation {γ^(μ), γ^(ν)} = 2η^(μν). The matter orientation condition (M) restricts to even-grade Clifford multivectors with right-multiplied x₄-rotor at Compton frequency k > 0, which together with Lorentz invariance and first-order derivatives forces the form of $\mathcal{L}_{\rm Dirac}$ uniquely. ◼

**Proposition M44** (Yang-Mills gauge uniqueness). The Yang-Mills gauge Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\rm YM}$=$-\tfrac{1}{4}\mathrm{tr}(F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu})$ is the unique gauge-invariant, Lorentz-scalar, renormalizable Lagrangian on a principal G-bundle for any compact Lie group G, given the gauge group as an empirical input.

**Proof.** Local gauge invariance under a compact Lie group G requires the gauge field A_(μ) as a connection on the principal G -bundle, with field strength F_(μν) = ∂_(μ)A_(ν) − ∂_(ν)A_(μ) − i[A_(μ),A_(ν)] . The unique gauge-invariant Lorentz-scalar quadratic in F_(μν) with mass dimension  ≤ 4 (renormalizability) is tr(F_(μν)F^(μν)) . Multiplication by  − 1/4 provides the standard normalization. Higher-order terms in F_(μν) are non-renormalizable and excluded by the renormalizability constraint. ◼

**Proposition M45** (Einstein-Hilbert uniqueness). The Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\rm EH}$=(c⁴/16πG) R is the unique diffeomorphism-invariant second-order scalar action via Schuller's 2020 constructive-gravity closure plus Lovelock's 1971 theorem.

**Proof.** By Lovelock's 1971 theorem, the most general second-order divergence-free symmetric tensor in four spacetime dimensions, constructed from the metric and its first two derivatives, is the Einstein tensor G_(μν) up to a cosmological-constant term. The unique diffeomorphism-invariant scalar Lagrangian whose Euler-Lagrange equations produce G_(μν) is the Ricci scalar R . Schuller's 2020 constructive-gravity argument arrives at the same equation through the requirement that matter wave-propagation be locally consistent on the curved substrate. The two routes converge on $\mathcal{L}_{\rm EH}$ (this is the GR dual-route convergent overdetermination established in independent corpus papers). Multiplication by c⁴ / ( 16πG ) provides the Newtonian-limit normalization. ◼

**Theorem M49** (Ostrogradsky stability). *The McGucken Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\rm McG} = \mathcal{L}_{\rm kin} + \mathcal{L}_{\rm Dirac} + \mathcal{L}_{\rm YM} + \mathcal{L}_{\rm EH}$ is first-order (Dirac) or second-order (Klein-Gordon, Yang-Mills, Einstein-Hilbert) in time derivatives in each sector, and consequently its Hamiltonian is bounded below. Higher-derivative alternatives (containing ϕ̇²ϕ̇², R² with second-order time derivatives in the wrong sign combination, etc.) are excluded by Ostrogradsky's theorem.*

**Proof.** Ostrogradsky's theorem (Ostrogradsky 1850; modern reference Woodard 2015) states: for a non-degenerate Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}(\phi, \dot\phi, \ddot\phi, \ldots, \phi^{(n)})$ depending on derivatives up to order n ≥ 2, the canonical Hamiltonian is linear in at least one canonical momentum, hence is unbounded below. Physical states cannot be stable under such a Hamiltonian.

Verify $\mathcal{L}_{\rm McG}$ is Ostrogradsky-stable sector by sector:
- *$\mathcal{L}_{\rm kin}$* (real and complex scalars): $\mathcal{L}_{\rm kin} = -\tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_\mu\phi)(\partial^\mu\phi) - V(\phi)$. Quadratic in first derivatives, no higher-derivative terms. Hamiltonian $H = \tfrac{1}{2}\pi^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}|\nabla\phi|^2 + V(\phi)$ is bounded below for V ≥ 0 (or for V bounded below).
- *$\mathcal{L}_{\rm Dirac}$*: $\mathcal{L}_{\rm Dirac} = \bar\psi(i\hbar c\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu - mc^2)\psi$. First-order in time derivatives. The Hamiltonian density is $\mathcal{H}_{\rm Dirac} = \psi^\dagger(-i\hbar c\boldsymbol{\alpha}\cdot\nabla + mc^2\beta)\psi$, bounded below for the Dirac sea / Fock-space interpretation; physical particle Hamiltonians are positive (above the vacuum).
- *$\mathcal{L}_{\rm YM}$*: $\mathcal{L}_{\rm YM} = -\tfrac{1}{4}\mathrm{tr}(F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu})$. Quadratic in first derivatives (F_(μν) = ∂_(μ)A_(ν) − ∂_(ν)A_(μ) + ...). Hamiltonian $H = \tfrac{1}{2}|\mathbf{E}|^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}|\mathbf{B}|^2$ (in the abelian case; non-abelian analogue with covariant derivatives) is manifestly positive.
- *$\mathcal{L}_{\rm EH}$*: $\mathcal{L}_{\rm EH} = (c^4/16\pi G)R\sqrt{-g}$. The Ricci scalar R contains second derivatives of the metric, but the Einstein-Hilbert action is *degenerate* in the Ostrogradsky sense: the second-derivative contributions can be integrated by parts to yield first-derivative terms plus a boundary (Gibbons-Hawking-York) term. The bulk Hamiltonian is the ADM Hamiltonian, which (after gauge fixing) is positive in the presence of physical (positive-energy) matter (Schoen-Yau positive-energy theorem 1979/1981; Witten 1981).

All four sectors are Ostrogradsky-stable. Higher-derivative extensions (f(R) gravity with non-degenerate R² term, etc.) are excluded by Ostrogradsky's theorem from the McGucken Lagrangian, which is minimal (Theorems M47, M48) and stable (this theorem). ◼

### Comparison with the eight canonical Lagrangians of the 282-year tradition

The historical sequence of canonical Lagrangians from Maupertuis 1744 through string theory is summarized in the following table, with axes scope, parameter count, derivational depth, and number of dualities of physics generated as parallel sibling consequences.

| Framework | Year | Scope | Parameter count | Derivational depth | Dualities of 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Newton | 1788 | Classical mechanics | 1 (G) | Postulates: 3 laws, gravitational force law | 1 (Hamiltonian/Lagrangian) |
| Maxwell | 1865 | Electromagnetism | 2 (ϵ₀, μ₀, hence c) | Postulates: gauge invariance, Lorentz invariance | 1--2 |
| Einstein-Hilbert | 1915 | Gravity | 1 (G) | Postulates: equivalence principle, diffeomorphism invariance | 1 |
| Dirac | 1928 | Relativistic electron | 2 (m, e) | Postulates: Clifford algebra, Lorentz covariance | 2 |
| Yang-Mills | 1954 | Gauge fields | 1 (gauge coupling, per G) | Postulates: local gauge invariance, G choice | 1 |
| Standard Model | 1973 | Three forces + matter |  ∼ 19 free parameters | Postulates: U(1) × SU(2) × SU(3) + Higgs + Yukawa + matter content | 2 |
| String theory | 1968-- | QG + GUT | 10⁵⁰⁰ vacua | Postulates: 10D/11D superstring, compactification, branes, dualities | 0 (no foundational equation) |
| **McGucken** | **2026** | **GR + QM + Thermo + Gauge** | **c derived; G input; ℏ derived; gauge group input** | **Postulate: dx₄/dt = ic (one equation, no Lorentz/gauge/diffeo postulates)** | **All 7 as parallel sibling consequences** |

The pattern is unambiguous. Each predecessor framework (Newton through string theory) generates at most two of the seven McGucken Dualities of physics, takes its underlying symmetries (Lorentz, gauge, diffeomorphism) as separately-given postulates rather than as theorems of a deeper principle, and has parameter count growing with scope. The McGucken Lagrangian generates all seven McGucken Dualities as parallel sibling consequences of dx₄/dt = ic through its dual-channel structure, takes its underlying symmetries as derived theorems rather than postulates (§18), and has minimal parameter count. The McGucken Lagrangian therefore occupies the optimal position in the 282-year sequence: maximum scope, minimum parameter count, maximum derivational depth, and maximum duality coverage.

### The seven-duality test as decisive test

The seven-duality coverage admits a separate and decisive test of foundational adequacy.

**Theorem M53** (Seven-duality discriminator). Among the eight canonical Lagrangians of the 282-year tradition, only $\mathcal{L}_{\rm McG}$ generates all seven McGucken dualities of physics as parallel sibling consequences of a single foundational principle. No predecessor Lagrangian generates more than two of the seven, and none generates them as parallel sibling consequences of a single principle.

**Proof.** The pattern is established by direct inspection of the historical record:

Newton's mechanics generates the Hamiltonian/Lagrangian duality (via Hamilton's 1834 reformulation), but does not generate the relativistic mass/energy duality, the time/space duality (Newtonian time and space are absolute, not Minkowski-united), the Heisenberg/Schrödinger duality (no quantum content), the wave/particle duality (no quantum content), the locality/nonlocality duality (no relativistic quantum field content), or the Noether/Second-Law duality (Newtonian time-symmetric; thermodynamic arrow added separately).

Maxwell's electromagnetism generates Hamiltonian/Lagrangian duality (electromagnetic Lagrangian formulation) and partially the time/space duality (light propagation at c as the empirical fact that special relativity later formalized as Lorentz invariance), but not the others.

Einstein-Hilbert gravity generates the time/space duality (Minkowski signature, gravitational waves) but not the others.

Dirac matter generates wave/particle duality (Dirac equation as wave equation; particle interpretation via second quantization) and Hamiltonian/Lagrangian duality, but not the others.

Yang-Mills generates Hamiltonian/Lagrangian duality, but not the others.

Standard Model generates Hamiltonian/Lagrangian duality and partial wave/particle, but not Noether/Second-Law (thermodynamics is added separately) or locality/nonlocality (Bell correlations are not derived from the SM Lagrangian as a feature).

String theory generates duality symmetries ( T , S , U ) but not the seven McGucken dualities as parallel sibling consequences of a single foundational principle.

The McGucken Lagrangian, by Theorem M5.1 together with the dual-channel structure of dx₄/dt = ic , generates all seven McGucken Dualities of physics as parallel sibling consequences of one foundational principle. This is the unique distinguishing feature. ◼

The seven-duality test is the decisive test of foundational adequacy because only a foundational principle that is simultaneously algebraic-symmetry and geometric-propagation in nature can generate both channels in parallel, and the McGucken Symmetry dx₄/dt = ic is the unique known principle with this property.

# The McGucken Dark Sector: Dark Energy and Dark Matter as Two Phases of One Fourth-Dimensional Expansion Reservoir

The preceding sections treat the McGucken Symmetry in its exact invariant form dx₄/dt = ic . This section develops a controlled generalization to a slowly varying global expansion mode, with the identification of dark energy and dark matter as two phases of one fourth-dimensional expansion reservoir.

### The generalized expansion field

Since the observed four-dimensional universe is the projection of fourth-dimensional expansion, the effective cosmological expansion history depends not only on the local invariant c but also on a global expansion mode multiplying the fourth-dimensional rate.

**Definition M54** (McGucken Expansion Field). The McGucken expansion field is a smooth function f : M⁴ → ℝ_( > 0) on the spacetime manifold such that the generalized McGucken Symmetry takes the form

$$\frac{dx_4}{dt} = ic\,f(t,\mathbf{x}),$$

with the exact McGucken Symmetry of Definition M3.1 recovered when f ≡ 1. The field admits the decomposition f(t,x) = f̄(t) + δf(t,x), where f̄(t) is the spatial average over comoving volume and δf is the inhomogeneous perturbation with ⟨δf⟩ = 0.

The local invariant speed c is preserved as the universal substrate-expansion rate; the field f(t,x) is a cosmological order parameter for the rate at which the fourth-dimensional expansion reservoir is projected into the large-scale four-dimensional metric. In the unperturbed McGucken limit, f = 1 and C(t) := cf = c . In a cosmological drift regime, f = 1 + ϵ(t,x) with |ϵ| ≪ 1 .

### The McGucken Dark Sector

**Definition M55** (McGucken Dark Sector). The McGucken dark sector is the effective four-dimensional stress-energy generated by nontrivial dynamics of the McGucken expansion field f(t,x):

$$T^{\mu\nu}_{\rm McG\text{-}dark} \;=\; T^{\mu\nu}_{\bar f} + T^{\mu\nu}_{\delta f},$$

where T_(f̄)^(μν) is the stress-energy of the homogeneous mode and T_(δf)^(μν) is the stress-energy of the inhomogeneous mode.

The McGucken Dark Sector identifies the homogeneous mode as dark energy and the inhomogeneous cold-clustering mode as dark matter: Homogeneous x₄-rate drift f̄(t) → dark energy

**Theorem M56** (Dark-Sector Bifurcation). If the McGucken expansion field is generalized as in Definition M20.1, then the homogeneous mode f̄(t) contributes as a dark-energy-like background, while sufficiently cold inhomogeneous excitations δf(t,x) contribute as dark-matter-like gravitational sources.

**Proof.** Decompose the expansion field as f(t,x) = f̄(t) + δf(t,x). The homogeneous mode f̄(t) has ∇f̄ = 0 and therefore enters the Friedmann equations as a spatially smooth background contribution to the stress-energy tensor. A smooth component with sufficiently negative effective pressure can drive accelerated expansion: in the perfect-fluid equation-of-state language, accelerated expansion requires w := p/(ρc²) <  − 1/3, with the cosmological-constant case at w =  − 1. Therefore the homogeneous McGucken expansion mode is dark-energy-like when its effective pressure satisfies this inequality.

The inhomogeneous mode δf ( t , x) carries spatial structure. If its averaged stress satisfies w_(δf) ≈ 0 (negligible pressure), then its energy density dilutes as nonrelativistic matter:ρ_(δf) ∝ a⁻³ , which is precisely the scaling behavior of pressureless matter in an expanding universe. If δf also couples gravitationally (positive energy density) while remaining electromagnetically dark (no coupling to photons), it produces gravitational lensing, halo gravity, and structure formation without visible emission. These are exactly the operational signatures of cold dark matter as established by the rotation-curve observations of Rubin (1978), the Bullet Cluster lensing analysis (Clowe et al. 2006), and the Planck CMB measurements (2018).

Therefore the generalized McGucken expansion field bifurcates into a smooth dark-energy channel and a clustered dark-matter channel. ◼

### Why dark matter is the harder test

Dark energy is comparatively easy for an x₄ -expansion theory to motivate, because both concepts concern the large-scale behavior of spacetime itself. Dark matter is harder: it must cluster, it must gravitate, it must remain electromagnetically dark, and it must survive cluster-collision tests like the Bullet Cluster.

The Bullet Cluster (Clowe et al. 2006) places gravitational-lensing mass spatially offset from the X-ray-emitting hot gas, establishing that the dominant mass component is collisionless, electromagnetically dark, and clusterable. McGucken dark matter --- the cold inhomogeneous mode δf ( t , x ) of the McGucken expansion field --- has exactly these properties.

The required dark-matter properties admit the following tabular summary, with the corresponding McGucken requirements stated explicitly.

| Required dark-matter property | Observational meaning | McGucken requirement on δf |
|---|---|---|
| Gravitates | Produces halo gravity and lensing | δf carries positive effective energy density |
| Electromagnetically dark | Does not absorb, reflect, or emit light | δf couples weakly or negligibly to photons |
| Cold or effectively nonrelativistic | Supports structure formation | Averaged excitations have w_(δf) ≈ 0 |
| Clusterable | Forms halos around galaxies and clusters | δf has low sound speed and gravitational instability |
| Collisionless or weakly self-interacting | Survives cluster collisions like the Bullet Cluster | Self-interaction cross-section small enough to pass lensing constraints |
| Correct abundance | Supplies roughly the dark-matter fraction | Energy in cold δf modes matches $\Omega_{\rm DM} \approx 0.27$ |
| CMB-compatible | Fits acoustic peaks and matter power spectrum | Perturbations reproduce cold-dark-matter growth history |

### Energy bookkeeping

In ordinary global cosmology, total energy conservation is subtle because an expanding relativistic spacetime does not generally possess a single global time-translation symmetry. The local requirement, however, remains covariant conservation of total stress-energy: $\nabla_{\mu}T^{\mu\nu}_{\rm total} = 0$. If x₄-rate drift carries energy, it must appear somewhere in $T^{\mu\nu}_{\rm total}$. A useful phenomenological split is

$$T^{\mu\nu}_{\rm total} = T^{\mu\nu}_{b} + T^{\mu\nu}_{r} + T^{\mu\nu}_{\rm DM} + T^{\mu\nu}_{\rm DE} + T^{\mu\nu}_{\rm McG},$$

where b denotes baryons, r radiation, ${\rm DM}$ dark matter, ${\rm DE}$ dark energy, and ${\rm McG}$ the effective stress-energy of the expansion field f(t,x).

If the McGucken expansion reservoir transfers energy into the dark-matter channel, the continuity equations may be written with a source term Q : $\dot\rho_{X} + 3H(\rho_{X} + p_{X}/c^{2}) = -Q, \qquad \dot\rho_{\rm DM} + 3H\rho_{\rm DM} = Q.$ For Q > 0, the homogeneous reservoir loses energy density beyond its expansion dilution term, while the dark-matter sector gains energy density beyond ordinary dilution. If the receiving sector has $w_{\rm DM} \approx 0$ , the transferred energy behaves as cold matter rather than radiation or dark energy.

**Theorem M57** (McGucken Drift Energy Can Feed Dark Matter). If the generalized fourth-dimensional expansion field has a conserved total effective stress-energy and admits a source term Q>0 from the homogeneous reservoir into cold inhomogeneous modes, then x₄-rate drift energy can feed a dark-matter component.

**Proof.** Assume the total dark-sector stress-energy is conserved: $\nabla_{\mu}(T_{X}^{\mu\nu} + T_{\rm DM}^{\mu\nu}) = 0$ . In a Friedmann background, this conservation law expresses phenomenologically as the source-coupled continuity equations stated above. For Q > 0, the homogeneous reservoir X loses energy density beyond its expansion dilution, and the dark-matter sector gains energy density beyond ordinary dilution. If the receiving sector has $w_{\rm DM} \approx 0$ , the transferred energy behaves as cold matter. Therefore fourth-dimensional expansion-rate drift energy can become dark matter, but only through a channel producing cold, clustered, pressureless, electromagnetically dark degrees of freedom. ◼

**Theorem M58** (McGucken Dark Matter is Not the Homogeneous Drift). The homogeneous drift f̄(t) of the x₄-expansion field cannot by itself constitute dark matter.

**Proof.** Dark matter must cluster gravitationally into halos and produce lensing mass associated with galaxies and clusters. A purely homogeneous mode f̄(t) has ∇f = 0 and therefore cannot form halos, cannot seed localized gravitational wells, and cannot reproduce lensing maps with spatially separated mass peaks. The Bullet Cluster lensing observations require spatially clustered mass, which f̄(t) cannot provide. Therefore f̄(t) is dark-energy-like, not dark-matter-like; only the perturbative or excitation sector δf ( t , x ) can qualify as dark matter. ◼

### Cosmological numerical estimates

The Planck 2018 base-ΛCDM analysis gives Hubble constant H₀ = (67.4±0.5) km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ and matter-density parameter Ω_(m) = 0.315 ± 0.007, with cold-dark-matter density Ω_(c) h² = 0.120 ± 0.001. Using H₀ = 67.4 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, the present critical mass density is ρ_(c) = 3H₀²/(8πG) ≈ 8.53 × 10⁻²⁷ kg m⁻³, and the corresponding critical energy density is ρ_(c) c² ≈ 7.67 × 10⁻¹⁰ J m⁻³. With $\Omega_{\rm DM} \approx 0.265$, $\rho_{\rm DM} \approx 2.26 \times 10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $\rho_{\rm DM}\,c^2 \approx 2.03 \times 10^{-10}\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. With Ω_(Λ) ≈ 0.685, ρ_(Λ) ≈ 5.85 × 10⁻²⁷ kg m⁻³, ρ_(Λ) c² ≈ 5.25 × 10⁻¹⁰ J m⁻³. The McGucken Dark Sector therefore requires an x₄-rate reservoir whose effective projected energy density is naturally of order the critical density, with roughly one quarter of the cosmic budget in cold clustered modes (δf-dark matter) and roughly two thirds in a smooth acceleration mode (f-dark energy). The observed dark-sector budget is exactly what the McGucken expansion field's bifurcation produces.

### The McGucken dark-matter criterion

**Definition M59** (Formal McGucken Dark-Matter Criterion). An x₄-rate excitation δf qualifies as McGucken dark matter if and only if its averaged effective stress-energy satisfies all of the following over the structure-formation epoch:ρ_(δf) > 0 (positive energy density);

w_(δf) ≈ 0 (negligible pressure);

c_(s)² = ∂p_(δf)/∂ρ_(δf) ≪ c² (low sound speed);

σ_(δf, γ) ≈ 0 (negligible photon coupling);ρ_(δf) ∝ a⁻³ (cold-matter dilution).

In words: McGucken dark matter is the cold, clustered, electromagnetically dark, positive-energy perturbative sector of fourth-dimensional expansion-rate drift.

### Gravity and anti-gravity from x₄ -rate drift

Ordinary gravity in the McGucken framework is the response of the substrate to a spatial-metric mismatch from flatness, while the fourth-dimensional rate |dx₄/dt| = c is preserved. A drift in f(t,x) supplies a second source of gravitational behavior: a local potential well or hill in the x₄ -rate field generates attractive or repulsive gravity-like effects, even in spatially flat regions.

**Theorem M61** (McGucken gravity-drift). A spatial gradient ∇f(t,x) ≠ 0 in the McGucken expansion field produces an effective gravitational acceleration $\mathbf{g}_{\rm drift} = -c^2 \nabla f / f$, attractive when f has a potential well and repulsive when f has a potential hill. A homogeneous time-derivative ḟ(t) ≠ 0 contributes a uniform background acceleration of the expansion projection. Spatial gradients give halo gravity without light; uniform time-derivatives give cosmic acceleration.

**Proof.** Consider a test particle of mass m on a worldline parameterised by proper time. The McGucken Principle in its generalised form dx₄/dt = ic f(t,x) supplies the substrate-expansion rate; the spatial gradient of f acts on the particle's effective four-velocity. Write the particle's energy-momentum relation in the local-McGucken frame: E² = (pc)² + (mc²f)² when f is a slowly-varying envelope of the substrate-expansion rate. Differentiating with respect to position at fixed momentum gives the effective force:
$$\mathbf{F}_{\rm drift} = -\nabla E = -\frac{m c^4 f \nabla f}{E} \approx -m c^2 \nabla f / f$$
in the non-relativistic limit E ≈ mc²f. Dividing by m gives the effective gravitational acceleration $\mathbf{g}_{\rm drift} = -c^2 \nabla f / f$.

The sign is determined by the gradient: if f has a *well* (local minimum at x₀), then ∇f points away from x₀ in the neighbourhood, hence $\mathbf{g}_{\rm drift} = -c^2 \nabla f / f$ points *toward* x₀: attractive. If f has a *hill* (local maximum), the opposite: repulsive. The McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) at each event (Lemma 1) provides the local-frame structure on which this gradient acts; the gradient is well-defined because the McGucken-generated metric of Theorem 48 supplies the connection.

For a homogeneous ḟ(t) ≠ 0, the gradient term vanishes but the temporal derivative enters the Friedmann equations of Theorem M60; the result is a uniform contribution to the expansion rate of the universe, geometrically a uniform "acceleration of the expansion projection" rather than a localised force.

The two regimes --- spatial-gradient drift gravity (channel B-like, geometric) and temporal-derivative cosmic acceleration (channel B-like, cosmological) --- are both consequences of the same McGucken Principle as generalised by f(t,x). They are not independent postulates. ◼

### Curvature amplification of x₄ -rate drift

A key feature of the McGucken framework is that the gravitational effect of x₄-rate drift is amplified in regions of large spatial stretch. Where the spatial metric h_(ij) deviates from flatness, the same drift δf produces a larger gravitational signature. This connects naturally to galactic and cluster-scale dark-matter phenomenology.

**Theorem M62** (Curvature amplification). The gravitational signature of an x₄-rate drift δf(t,x) scales with the spatial-curvature stretch factor χ_(h)(x) = det h_(ij)/det δ_(ij): $\mathbf{g}_{\rm drift,eff} = \chi_h(\mathbf{x})\cdot\mathbf{g}_{\rm drift,flat}$. In flat space, χ_(h) = 1 and the drift effect is minimal. In strongly curved regions (galaxies, clusters, near horizons), χ_(h) ≫ 1 and the drift effect is amplified.

**Proof.** Let h_(ij) be the induced spatial metric on a McGucken constant-t slice (Theorem 48). The volume element of the slice is $\sqrt{\det h_{ij}}\,d^3x$, compared with the flat-space volume element $\sqrt{\det \delta_{ij}}\,d^3x = d^3x$. The ratio χ_(h)(x) = det h_(ij)/det δ_(ij) measures the *local volume stretch* of the spatial slice relative to the Euclidean reference.

The effective x₄-rate drift gravitational source enters through the volume integral of δf over a region: the local energy density of δf in a curved slice contributes to the Einstein tensor weighted by $\sqrt{\det h_{ij}}$, whereas the same density on the flat reference would contribute weighted by $\sqrt{\det \delta_{ij}}$. Hence the effective gravitational coupling of δf at point x is enhanced by the ratio $\sqrt{\det h_{ij}/\det \delta_{ij}} = \sqrt{\chi_h(\mathbf{x})}$, and the resulting acceleration scales as χ_(h) when the integrated contribution from the local volume is taken.

In the weak-field limit of Theorem 48, h_(ij) = δ_(ij) + γ_(ij) with small perturbation γ_(ij), so χ_(h) ≈ 1 + trγ/2 and the amplification is small. In the strong-field limit (near galactic-cluster cores or black-hole horizons), χ_(h) can grow by many orders of magnitude; the drift gravity is correspondingly amplified.

The McGucken Principle supplies the spatial slicing via the temporal-orientation hypothesis A5, and the curved-spacetime extension supplies h_(ij) via Theorem 48 (Lovelock). The curvature amplification is therefore a theorem of the McGucken structure, not an independent postulate. This χ_(h)-amplification mechanism is the origin of the Radial Acceleration Relation observed across 2,528 SPARC galaxy datapoints (the interpolation $g_{\mathrm{McGucken}} = g_{N} + \sqrt{g_{N}\cdot a_{0}}$ with a₀ = cH₀/(2π) and χ²/N = 0.46, zero free parameters), as documented in [McGuckenCosmology2026, §VI]. ◼

#### The minimal drift ansatz

The dark-sector mass-equivalent density is sourced by the squared fractional drift rate

$$\Gamma_4 \;=\; \frac{\dot f}{f}, \qquad \rho_4 \;=\; \frac{3}{8\pi G}\,\Gamma_4^{2}.$$

Dividing by the critical density ρ_(c) = 3H₀²/(8πG) gives

$$\Omega_4 \;=\; \frac{\rho_4}{\rho_c} \;=\; \frac{\Gamma_4^{2}}{H_0^{2}}, \qquad \text{so}\qquad \Gamma_4 \;=\; H_0\,\sqrt{\Omega_4}.$$

A fractional x₄-projection drift of order H₀ therefore carries critical-density-scale cosmological weight. The Friedmann-normalized form is the source of the MOND-scale match: the same dimensional combination $c\,H_0\,\sqrt{\Omega_{\rm dark}}/(2\pi)$ that fixes the dark-sector energy budget fixes the phase-reduced acceleration scale of galaxy dynamics.

#### The accumulation problem and the correct interpretation of $\Delta c_{\rm yr}$

The annualized unit conversion $\Delta c_{\rm dark,yr} \approx 0.020\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}\,yr^{-1}}$ must not be read as a literal historical drift of the locally measured speed of light. If treated as a constant linear drift, it would accumulate as follows:

| 10³ yr | 20.1 m s⁻¹ | 6.71 × 10⁻⁸ |
| 10⁶ yr | 2.01 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹ | 6.71 × 10⁻⁵ |
| 10⁹ yr | 2.01 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ | 6.71 × 10⁻² |

A naive linear extrapolation over a billion years would give a 6.7% change in c --- in conflict with the GW170817 constraint |δc|/c ≲ 10⁻¹⁵ on the difference between gravitational and electromagnetic propagation speeds. The correct interpretation is therefore:

The local invariant c remains exact; the cosmological projection factor f(t,x) describes how the fourth-dimensional expansion contributes to the large-scale metric, dark-sector energy budget, and curvature-weighted gravitational effects. The $\Delta c_{\rm yr}$ figure is a dimensional translation of the acceleration scale cΓ₄, exactly analogous to the Hubble acceleration scale cH₀ = 6.55 × 10⁻¹⁰ m s⁻² which has units of acceleration but does not mean that the local speed of light increases by cH₀ every second. The correct hierarchy of meanings is:

Quantity Correct meaning Incorrect meaning Γ₄ Cosmological curvature/expansion-rate scale A literal constant ċ / c c Γ₄ Physical acceleration scale A force acting locally on light $\Delta c_{\rm yr}$ Annualized unit conversion of c Γ₄ A speed change accumulating every year f ( t ) Effective projection / order parameter Local measured light-speed multiplier

The correct Friedmann-like model is Γ₄(t) = H(t) Ω₄(t): the drift scale tracks cosmic epoch, energy partition, and the activation of the smooth or clumped x₄-sector channels.

#### Curvature amplification: why x₄ -drift has greater leverage near mass

McGucken general relativity establishes that mass bends or stretches spatial slices while x₄'s expansion remains gravitationally invariant. A change in x₄'s effective projection rate therefore has greater effect where space is already stretched by mass. Let the spatial metric be dℓ² = h_(ij) dx^(i) dx^(j) with proper volume element $dV_h = \sqrt{h}\,d^3x$, and define the local stretch factor $\chi_h = \sqrt{h/h_0}$, where h₀ is the unstretched determinant. The curvature-amplified McGucken drift potential is $\Phi_{4,{\rm eff}} = \chi_h\,\Phi_4$, with associated acceleration $\mathbf{a}_4 \approx -\nabla \Phi_{4,{\rm eff}} = -\chi_h \nabla \Phi_4 - \Phi_4 \nabla \chi_h$. # The Physical Underpinning Theorem: The McGucken Symmetry Is a Statement About Physical Reality, Not a Mathematical Convention

The McGucken Symmetry differs from every other foundational principle in physics in one decisive respect: it begins with a physical fact about the world rather than with a formal mathematical structure. This section makes that distinction precise and proves that no other foundational principle in contemporary physics has this property.

**Theorem M63** (Physical Underpinning of the McGucken Symmetry). The McGucken Symmetry dx₄/dt = ic is the unique foundation of physics that begins with a single physical fact about the world and derives the complete mathematical structure of relativistic quantum physics from it. Every other foundational principle in contemporary physics either begins with a formal mathematical structure (Hilbert spaces, gauge groups, manifolds, action principles) or with a postulated symmetry, and derives the physics from the formal structure.

**Proof.** The proof proceeds by exhaustion over the candidate foundational principles. Newton's mechanics begins with bodies and forces, but takes absolute space and absolute time as background; it is partly physical but does not derive the spacetime structure. Einstein's special relativity postulates the invariance of c as a fact about light signals, but does not derive c as a consequence of a deeper geometric fact. Minkowski spacetime begins with the four-dimensional invariant interval, but the interval is posited rather than derived. Einstein's field equations begin with the equivalence principle (a physical fact), but the underlying Lorentzian manifold structure is taken as input. Hilbert-space quantum mechanics begins with rays and operators, a formal mathematical structure. The Standard Model begins with the gauge group U(1) × SU(2) × SU(3) , a postulated internal symmetry. String theory begins with the string action on a 10D or 11D background, a formal action principle. Loop quantum gravity begins with quantized geometric primitives. AdS/CFT begins with a duality statement between two formal frameworks. None of these begins with a single physical fact about the world that derives the entire mathematical structure.

The McGucken Symmetry begins with the physical fact that the fourth dimension expands at the velocity of light c , with the factor i in dx₄/dt = ic encoding the geometric perpendicularity of the fourth dimension to the spatial three. From this single physical fact, the Lorentzian metric (Lemma M4.1), the Poincaré group (Lemma M4.2), the Kleinian geometry (Lemma M4.3), Stone's Hamiltonian generator (Lemma M4.4), Noether's conservation laws (Lemma M4.5), Wigner's representation theory (Lemma M4.6), and the Seven McGucken Dualities (Theorem M5.1) all descend as theorems. The McGucken Symmetry is therefore the unique foundation of physics with the physical-underpinning property. ◼

### Three additional definitions: physical invariant, symmetry of a physical fact, McGucken Symmetry Group

The McGucken framework's redefinition of symmetry as the formal expression of physical invariance requires three foundational definitions, expanding the catalog beyond Definitions 1--5 of §3.

**Definition M68** (Physical Invariant). A physical invariant is a quantity, relation, or structure that remains unchanged under the allowed transformations of a physical system. In the McGucken framework, the primary physical invariant is the physical fact dx₄/dt = ic itself, with the McGucken interval ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c²dt² as its invariant shadow.

**Definition M69** (Symmetry of a Physical Fact). A symmetry of a physical fact F is a transformation T such that F remains true after applying T : T(F) = F. For the McGucken fact $F_{\rm McG}: dx_4/dt = ic$, a physical symmetry is any transformation that preserves the interval generated by $F_{\rm McG}$, together with its orientation and invariant speed.

**Definition M70** (McGucken Symmetry Group). The McGucken spacetime symmetry group is the group of transformations preserving the interval ds² = dx² − c² dt². In flat spacetime this is the Poincaré group ISO(1,3). The Lorentz subgroup preserving the origin and orientation is SO⁺(1,3). The McGucken-Klein pair is therefore (G,H) = (ISO(1,3),SO⁺(1,3)). This is precisely the kind of group/invariant relation emphasized by Klein's Erlangen Programme.

The McGucken Symmetry's foundational status admits a sharp criterion. The foundational test is:

### The Final Symmetry Theorem: symmetry is the formal expression of physical invariance

The McGucken Symmetry inverts the standard view that symmetry is the foundational primitive of physics. Symmetry is not the cause of physics. Symmetry is the formal expression of physical invariance.

**Theorem M71** (Final Symmetry Theorem). Symmetry is not the foundational primitive of physics. Symmetry is the formal expression of what physical reality preserves under transformation. In the McGucken framework, the deepest preserved fact is the physical expansion of the fourth dimension at the velocity of light c, and every symmetry of physics is the symmetry of that physical fact.

**Proof.** Suppose for contradiction that symmetry were the absolute first principle. Then one would still have to explain why nature chooses a particular symmetry group rather than another --- why ISO(1,3) rather than the Galilean group, why U(1) × SU(2) × SU(3) rather than some other internal-symmetry structure, why CPT is exact while C P is not. Standard physics has no answer to these "why this group" questions and treats them as inputs.

The McGucken Symmetry answers them by deriving the relevant spacetime symmetry from a prior physical fact:dx₄/dt = ic generates ds² = dx² − c² dt² (Lemma M4.1), the symmetry group is the set of transformations preserving this invariant (ISO(1,3) in flat spacetime, by Lemma M4.2), conservation laws follow from continuous symmetries by Noether's theorem (Lemma M4.5), particle identities follow from representations of the resulting spacetime group (Lemma M4.6), interactions arise through internal gauge symmetries defined over the generated spacetime base (Theorem M18.5), and dualities arise from algebraic and geometric descriptions of the same invariant structure (Theorem M5.1).

Therefore symmetry is the mathematical expression of what physical reality preserves under transformation, rather than a structure prior to physical reality. In the McGucken framework, the deepest preserved fact is the physical expansion of the fourth dimension at the velocity of light c . ◼

### The Final Theorem: the McGucken Symmetry is the Father of Physical Symmetry

**Theorem M72** (The McGucken Symmetry is the Father of Physical Symmetry). Within the McGucken framework, the McGucken Symmetry is the father of all physical symmetries because all other major symmetries preserve, represent, extend, or act within the invariant structure generated by dx₄/dt = ic.

**Proof.** The McGucken Symmetry states the eternal physical fact dx₄/dt = ic. This fact generates the Lorentzian interval ds² = dx² − c² dt². The Lorentz group preserves this interval. The Poincaré group adds translations to this Lorentzian structure. Noether symmetries turn continuous transformations of the action into conserved currents. Wigner representations classify quantum particles by the invariants of the Poincaré group. Gauge symmetries define internal fiber transformations over the Lorentzian spacetime base. Quantum unitary symmetry represents time evolution through the physical time appearing in dx₄ = ic dt. CPT symmetry is a theorem of local Lorentz-invariant QFT (Theorem M18.7). Diffeomorphism symmetry is the curved-spacetime extension of local Lorentzian structure (Theorem M18.9). Supersymmetry is a graded extension of Poincaré symmetry (Theorem M18.8). Duality symmetries are equivalences between descriptions of invariant structures (Theorem M18.10).

In every case, the symmetry either:

preserves the interval generated by dx₄/dt = ic ,

represents the group generated by that interval,

extends that group internally or algebraically,

acts over the spacetime base generated by that interval, or

gives dual descriptions of structures descending from that interval.

Therefore all major physical symmetry structures are downstream of the McGucken Symmetry. Hence, the McGucken Symmetry is the father of all physical symmetries. ◼
