# Appendix A: Reading the McGucken Principle — A Note on $dx_{4}/dt$, $dx_{4}/d\tau$, and the Photon — Clarifying Common Reader Misconceptions

*About this appendix.* Readers arriving at the McGucken Principle from a standard graduate-relativity background bring one deep habit: the reflex to treat per-proper-time quantities as the "physical" or "covariant" ones, and per-coordinate-time quantities as gauge-dependent bookkeeping. That habit points the wrong way here, because the Principle is a statement about the manifold itself — an expansion happening at every event, at the same rate, regardless of which worldline crosses that event. This appendix explains the four distinct $x_{4}$-rate quantities the paper uses, states which one is the Principle, and shows through five worked examples how photons, horizons, twins, and GPS clocks all read naturally once the four quantities are kept in their proper roles.

## A.0 The Physical Fact

Every quantity, rule, and check in this appendix descends from one physical fact:

> The fourth dimension $x_{4}$ is expanding in a spherically symmetric manner at the rate of $c$ from every spacetime event, or $dx_{4}/dt = ic$.

That is the McGucken Principle. Before any of its consequences are unpacked, its status must be stated plainly, because it is the point on which every reading in this appendix turns: $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ is an ontological claim — a statement about what physically is — and not a coordinate convention, a formal device, or a notational choice. It asserts that the fourth dimension is a real dimension that is really expanding, at the rate $c$, from every event of spacetime, now. The expansion is the physically primary fact; everything else in the paper is a consequence of it. Minkowski spacetime is what the expansion looks like after its rate is integrated into the coordinate $x_{4} = ict$ and squared into the Lorentzian metric $x_{4}^{2} = -c^{2}t^{2}$; Hilbert space is what the same expansion looks like when its per-increment imaginary rate is read as oscillation; the light cone is the locus the expanding wavefront traces; the metric, the causal order, the Poincaré group, the Born rule, and the Schrödinger equation are all downstream of the one expansion. None of these is postulated independently. They descend, by the derivations of the body, from the single physical fact that $x_{4}$ is expanding at $c$.

This is the reversal the reader must hold onto throughout. Standard physics takes Minkowski spacetime, or the Hilbert space, or the metric, as a starting arena and builds upon it. Here the arena is a result rather than a starting point: the starting point is the physical expansion $dx_{4}/dt = ic$, and the arena is what that expansion generates. When the appendix below insists that $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ is primary and the per-proper-time quantities are constructed from it, this is a claim about which fact is physically prior, distinct from a preference among equivalent formalisms. The rate is prior; the worldlines that share in it, the metric that its squaring produces, and the observers that read it are all posterior.

The imaginary unit $i$ in $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ records the algebraic perpendicularity of the $x_{4}$-axis to the three spatial axes on which the expansion casts its projection. Its geometric realisation at each event $p \in \mathcal{M}_{G}$ is the McGucken Sphere $\mathcal{M}_{p}^{+}(t)$ — the spherical wavefront of radius $ct$ swept out around $p$ by the $x_{4}$-expansion. The Sphere is what distinguishes the Principle from Minkowski's constant four-velocity norm $u^{\mu} u_{\mu} = -c^{2}$: the norm is a scalar constraint carrying no group action and no measure, and it survives here as a theorem of the Principle (the chain-rule pullback of the Sphere's expansion rate).

The Sphere carries $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant content that supplies the Born rule downstream by two independent routes: the rank-2 metric bilinearity route (Theorem 7.2; §9.5.13) and the Haar-measure route (the unique $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant measure on the Sphere). That these two derivationally-disjoint derivations return the same Born density $|\psi|^{2}$ is an instance of the convergent overdetermination documented in §17.5bis; see Remark A.0.1.

**Remark A.0.1 (Two independent derivations of the Born rule).** The Born density $P = |\psi|^{2}$ is derived in this framework by two routes that share no premises beyond the McGucken Sphere itself:

(i) *The rank-2 metric bilinearity route* (Theorem 7.2; §9.5.13; [MG-Born] Lemma 4.1, Theorem 4.2). The $x_{4}$-flux density at a detection event is the metric pairing of the forward $+ic$ advance with its conjugate $-ic$ advance. The Minkowski metric induced by $x_{4} = ict$ is a rank-2 tensor, so the pairing is bilinear in $(\psi, \psi^{*})$; $\mathrm{U}(1)$ phase invariance, reality, non-negativity, and normalization then force $P = |\psi|^{2}$ uniquely. The exponent 2 is the rank of the metric.

(ii) *The Haar-measure route* (Theorem 7.2 scholium; §7). The McGucken Sphere at the detection event carries the action of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$; the unique $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant normalized measure on the 2-sphere is the Haar (rotation-invariant) measure, and the probability of detection in a solid-angle element is fixed by that measure. Applied to the wavefront amplitude, this returns $P = |\psi|^{2}$.

Route (i) proceeds from the rank of the metric; route (ii) proceeds from the symmetry group of the Sphere. Neither uses the other's premise — one needs only that the metric is rank 2, the other only that the Sphere carries an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ action — so their agreement on $P = |\psi|^{2}$ is a genuine convergence rather than a single argument told twice. This is the sense in which the Born rule is convergently overdetermined by $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ (§17.5bis): the same downstream fact is fixed by two upstream properties of the Sphere that are logically independent of each other.

## A.1 The Four $x_{4}$-Rate Quantities

The framework uses four related quantities associated with the fourth dimension's advance. Each has its own symbol, its own domain of definition, and its own interpretation, and they diverge on null worldlines.

**(R1) The coordinate rate** $dx_{4}/dt = ic$, parameter: coordinate $t$; range: fixed value $ic$; universal — holds at every event of $\mathcal{M}_{G}$. *The Principle.* With the integrated shadow $x_{4} = ict$, this rate holds identically along every worldline of $\mathcal{M}_{G}$ — timelike, null, accelerated, at any gravitational potential — because $x_{4}$ is a coordinate function of $t$ alone. Every statement about the universality of the expansion, its metric-independence (GR T2), or its exception-freeness is a statement in (R1).

**(R2) The Sphere-tangent share** $v_{x_{4}} \equiv \sqrt{c^{2} - v^{2}}$ (the worldline's share of the $x_{4}$-expansion, per coordinate time); parameter: coordinate $t$; range: $[0, c]$; worldline-dependent. A bounded quantity (Lemma 5.1.3.2). The partition $v^{2} + v_{x_{4}}^{2} = c^{2}$ holds for every worldline, null ones included: at spatial rest $v_{x_{4}} = c$; on a null worldline $v = c$ gives $v_{x_{4}} = 0$. On timelike worldlines, $v_{x_{4}}$ coincides with the standard time-dilation factor of special relativity: $v_{x_{4}} = c\, d\tau/dt = c/\gamma$ for $0 \leq v < c$. The identity $v_{x_{4}} = c\, d\tau/dt$ is a theorem about $v_{x_{4}}$ — $\tau$ appears as output, not as the differentiation parameter. At $v = c$ (the null limit) all three expressions give $v_{x_{4}} = 0$: the $\sqrt{c^{2} - v^{2}}$ form by direct substitution, the $c\, d\tau/dt$ form as the ratio $c \cdot 0/dt$ with $d\tau = 0$, and the $c/\gamma$ form as the limit $\gamma \to \infty$. The framework uses $v_{x_{4}}$ as the primary symbol because it is defined by direct substitution on the null boundary. Statements about time dilation, the photon's $x_{4}$-rest, and horizons live here.

**(R3) The Lorentzian temporal component** $u^{4} = dx_{4}/d\tau = ic\gamma$; parameter: proper $\tau$; unbounded, undefined on null worldlines; a chain-rule consequence. Derived from (R1) by the chain rule (Theorem 5.1.2.8): $dx_{4}/d\tau = (dx_{4}/dt)(dt/d\tau) = ic\gamma$. Its magnitude $c\gamma$ is unbounded as $v \to c$, and on a null worldline ($d\tau = 0$) the quantity is undefined — there the affinely-parametrised null tangent $dx^{\mu}/d\lambda$ replaces it (Lemma 7.2.2.1a).

**(R4) The accumulated $x_{4}$-advance along $\gamma$**, $X_{4}[\gamma] \equiv \int_{\gamma} ic\, d\tau = ic\, \tau[\gamma]$; a worldline functional, path-dependent. Distinct from the coordinate $x_{4}$. Two worldlines sharing endpoints share $\Delta x_{4} = ic\, \Delta t$ but generally differ in $X_{4}$. Along a null worldline $X_{4}$ is constant; around any closed curve $\oint dx_{4} = 0$ identically. Statements about differential aging (the twins) live in (R4). The bridge to (R2): $dX_{4} = ic\, d\tau = i\, v_{x_{4}}\, dt$.

## A.2 Which One Is the Principle

The Principle is $dx_{4}/dt = ic$: the coordinate-time reading (R1). Because $x_{4}$ is a coordinate function of $t$ alone, the rate $dx_{4}/dt$ takes the same value $ic$ at every event of $\mathcal{M}_{G}$ — an expanding photon-event, a horizon event, an event on any accelerated worldline. The reading $dx_{4}/d\tau = ic$ is available too, but only where $d\tau = dt$: on a worldline at spatial rest, the chain rule collapses and (R1) coincides with the value of (R3). This is Lemma 4.7 (the rest-frame reverse-reading equivalence), and the qualification $d\tau = dt$ is what makes it valid. On a moving worldline the chain rule gives $ic\gamma$; on a null worldline the quantity does not exist. The coordinate-time reading is primary because $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ is a physical fact — the expansion itself is prior to any worldline, and $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ records it directly.

## A.3 Reading the Photon, the Horizon, and the Time-Dilation Formula

### A.3.1 What is the photon's $x_{4}$-rate?

The photon's share in the expansion is zero: $v_{x_{4}} = 0$ (the $v = c$ limit of $v^{2} + v_{x_{4}}^{2} = c^{2}$), obtained by direct substitution of $v = c$ into $v_{x_{4}} = \sqrt{c^{2} - v^{2}}$. The reader may be tempted to write "$dx_{4}/dt = 0$ for the photon" or "$dx_{4}/d\tau = 0$." Neither is available. The first is the coordinate rate (R1), which is $ic$ at every event of $\mathcal{M}_{G}$ including the photon's — what vanishes is the photon's share, not the expansion. The second is $0/0$: proper time is not defined for a photon ($d\tau = 0$ pointwise). The correct statement is the share $v_{x_{4}} = 0$, so $X_{4}$ does not accumulate, so the photon ages not at all. The Principle continues to hold at every event the photon crosses.

### A.3.2 What does "the $x_{4}$-rate at the horizon" mean?

The rate is gravity-rigid: $\partial(dx_{4}/dt)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (GR T2). The rate $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ takes the same value near the horizon as at infinity. What varies with potential is the share: $v_{x_{4}}(r) = c\, d\tau/dt = c\sqrt{1 - r_{s}/r}$ (static Schwarzschild observer), vanishing at $r = r_{s}$. On the infaller's own clock $d\tau = dt$ locally and Lemma 4.7 applies: the local rate is the full $ic$ throughout. Gravitational time dilation is the coordinate-frame projection of a locally invariant rate.

### A.3.3 Which identity is "$c^{2}$ through spacetime"?

*Sphere partition* (per coordinate time, all worldlines): $v^{2} + v_{x_{4}}^{2} = c^{2}$, bounded, locus a quarter-circle. *Lorentzian four-velocity norm* (per proper time, massive worldlines): $u^{\mu} u_{\mu} = |dx_{4}/d\tau|^{2} - |d\vec{x}/d\tau|^{2} = -c^{2}$, unbounded in each term, signature difference fixing the invariant. The Euclidean per-proper-time sum $|dx_{4}/d\tau|^{2} + |d\vec{x}/d\tau|^{2}$ equals $c^{2}$ only in the instantaneous rest frame; elsewhere $c^{2}\gamma^{2}$. Plus-sign identities belong to (R2); minus-sign identities to (R3).

### A.3.4 How does the twin paradox read?

Coordinate accumulation is path-independent: both twins accumulate $\Delta x_{4} = ic\, \Delta t$. Differential ageing is read from $X_{4} = \int ic\, d\tau$, advancing at real magnitude $v_{x_{4}}$ per unit coordinate time. On the traveling leg $v_{x_{4}} < c$, so the traveler accumulates less $X_{4}$, so less proper time. The stay-at-home twin retains $v_{x_{4}} = c$ and accumulates the maximal $X_{4}$. The CTC question closes the same way: $\oint dx_{4} = 0$ identically, so a CTC cannot run on the coordinate; the impossibility lives in $X_{4}$.

### A.3.5 $\gamma$-projection and rapidity

A boost is hyperbolic: rapidity $\phi$ with $\cosh\phi = \gamma$. The Sphere-partition projection is circular: Sphere angle $\theta$ with $\sin\theta = v/c$, $\cos\theta = v_{x_{4}}/c = 1/\gamma$. Related by the Gudermannian, $\theta = \mathrm{gd}(\phi)$, so $\cos\theta = \mathrm{sech}\, \phi$. The $1/\gamma$ projection is about $\theta$; unbounded component growth is about $\phi$.

## A.4 Why Nothing of Relativity Is Lost

The fourth dimension advances at the same rate at every event of $\mathcal{M}_{G}$; worldlines differ only in how much of that advance they share in. Massive at rest shares fully ($v_{x_{4}} = c$); moving shares less ($v_{x_{4}} = \sqrt{c^{2} - v^{2}}$, clock slowed by the Lorentz factor); photon does not share at all ($v_{x_{4}} = 0$, ageless, no $X_{4}$). Lorentz invariance survives entire because the invariant content — the norm $u^{\mu} u_{\mu} = -c^{2}$ and the metric — is a theorem of the Principle (the metric is the pullback of the Euclidean form along $x_{4} = ict$, the $-c^{2}$ from $(ic)^{2}$). Lorentz transformations preserve that derived metric; $\gamma$, time dilation, length contraction, $E = \gamma m c^{2}$, the null cone, and the mass-shell all come out unchanged. The foliation quantities $v_{x_{4}}$ and $X_{4}$ are additional bookkeeping frame-anchored to the cosmic-comoving foliation (the CMB rest frame); the Cloaking Theorem (Theorem 39) explains why local metrology cannot detect them. GR survives by the invariant/deformable split: the rate is gravity-rigid; gravity deforms the spatial sector. Time dilation, redshift, light bending, perihelion advance, the horizon, and the field equations are recovered exactly. The horizon is where the share is extinguished; the expansion does not stop.

## A.5 Worked Examples

### A.5.1 The twin paradox

Traveler at speed $v$ for coordinate time $\Delta t$. Coordinate accumulation: $\Delta x_{4} = ic\, \Delta t$ for both. Traveler's share: $v_{x_{4}} = c\sqrt{1 - v^{2}/c^{2}}$. Accumulated: $\Delta X_{4}^{\mathrm{trav}} = ic \sqrt{1 - v^{2}/c^{2}}\, \Delta t$ vs $\Delta X_{4}^{\mathrm{stay}} = ic\, \Delta t$. Differential aging: $\Delta \tau^{\mathrm{trav}} - \Delta \tau^{\mathrm{stay}} = \Delta t (\sqrt{1 - v^{2}/c^{2}} - 1) < 0$: the traveler is younger by exactly the Lorentz factor.

### A.5.2 GPS clock rate

Satellite at radius $r$, speed $v$, mass $M$. Principle: $dx_{4}/dt = ic$. Gravitational share: $v_{x_{4}}^{\mathrm{grav}}/c = \sqrt{1 - 2GM/rc^{2}}$; kinematic factor $\sqrt{1 - v^{2}/c^{2}}$. Total: $v_{x_{4}}^{\mathrm{sat}}/c \approx 1 - GM/(rc^{2}) - v^{2}/(2c^{2})$. Ground: $\approx 1 - GM/(R_{\oplus}c^{2})$. Fractional difference $\approx GM(1/R_{\oplus} - 1/r) - v^{2}/(2c^{2})$, matching the $+4.5 \times 10^{-10}$ pre-launch offset at $r = 26{,}600$ km, $v = 3.87$ km/s.

### A.5.3 Schwarzschild gravitational redshift

Photon from $r_{1}$ to $r_{2} > r_{1}$. Principle: $dx_{4}/dt = ic$. Local clock rate: $v_{x_{4}}(r)/c = \sqrt{1 - r_{s}/r}$. Frequency ratio $\nu_{2}/\nu_{1} = \sqrt{(1 - r_{s}/r_{1})/(1 - r_{s}/r_{2})}$; weak-field $\Delta \nu / \nu \approx -GM(1/r_{2} - 1/r_{1})/c^{2}$, matching Pound–Rebka 1959. Photon: $v_{x_{4}} = 0$ throughout, no $X_{4}$. The redshift is about the clock rates at emitter and receiver, rather than about the photon.

### A.5.4 Hawking temperature

At $r = r_{s}$, local share $v_{x_{4}}(r) \to 0$. Surface gravity $\kappa = c/(2 r_{s})$; compactification circumference $L_{H} = 4\pi r_{s} = c\hbar \beta_{H}$; temperature $T_{H} = \hbar c^{3}/(8\pi G M k_{B})$. The expansion does not stop at the horizon; the share is extinguished on the static foliation, and compactification of the Euclidean-section $x_{4}$-axis at $L_{H}$ produces the thermal spectrum.

### A.5.5 Bell's spaceship

Rockets $A$, $B$ at proper distance $L_{0}$, accelerating identically. Coordinate rate: $dx_{4}/dt = ic$. Share: $v_{x_{4}}(t) = c\sqrt{1 - v(t)^{2}/c^{2}}$, decreasing. Accumulated: $X_{4}^{A} = X_{4}^{B}$, so both age identically. Launch-frame separation constant $L_{0}$; co-moving separation $L(t) = L_{0}\, c / v_{x_{4}}(t)$, growing without bound. The string breaks: the budget shifts into the spatial sector identically on each rocket, so no differential ageing; the paradox lives in the spatial-sector geometry, the string breaking as co-moving distance grows as $1/v_{x_{4}}$.

# Appendix B: The Five Foundational Papers (2008--2013)

The McGucken Principle and Moving Dimensions Theory were established in five papers submitted to the Foundational Questions Institute (FQXi) essay contests. The five papers constitute the historical priority record for the principle and its consequences, and they are recapitulated here for reference. Full bibliographic URLs are in the Bibliography.

1. *Time as an Emergent Phenomenon: Traveling Back to the Heroic Age of Physics* (2008, FQXi d/238). The originating paper. Derives the Lorentz transformation from dx₄/dt = ic, unifies all arrows of time (radiative, thermodynamic, cosmological, causal, quantum), resolves the EPR paradox and the Gödel block-universe problem, and identifies x₄ = ict from Einstein's 1912 *Manuscript on Relativity* as the integrated form of the substrate-expansion law.

2. *What is Ultimately Possible in Physics? Physics! A Hero's Journey with Galileo, Newton, Faraday, Maxwell, Planck, Einstein, Schrödinger, Bohr, and the Greats towards Moving Dimensions Theory. E pur si muove!* (2009, FQXi d/511). The hero's-journey paper. Quotes the founding fathers of physics throughout. Derives Einstein's two postulates of Special Relativity from the single dx₄/dt = ic postulate; addresses Schrödinger's "characteristic trait of QM" (entanglement) as the agelessness of two photons that remain in the same place in x₄ as x₄ expands.

3. *On the Emergence of QM, Relativity, Entropy, Time, iℏ, and ic from the Foundational, Physical Reality of a Fourth Dimension x₄ Expanding with a Discrete (Digital) Wavelength ℓ_(p) at c Relative to Three Continuous (Analog) Spatial Dimensions* (2011, FQXi d/873). The discrete-analog paper. Identifies the unified algebraic role of i in the canonical commutation relation qp − pq = iℏ (Born--Heisenberg) and the substrate-expansion law dx₄/dt = ic (Einstein--Minkowski) --- both with differentials on the left and i on the right --- as Bohr noted.

4. *MDT's dx₄/dt = ic Triumphs Over the Wrong Physical Assumption That Time is a Dimension* (2012, FQXi d/1429). The corrective paper. Identifies the historical misreading of x₄ = ict as a coordinate convention. Time, as measured on a watch, is a scalar parameter that emerges from x₄'s expansion, rather than being itself the fourth dimension. Answers Eddington's Challenge: "Something must be added to the geometrical conceptions comprised in Minkowski's world before it becomes a complete picture of the world as we know it." That something is dx₄/dt = ic.

5. *It from Bit or Bit From It? What is It? Honor! Where is the Wisdom we have lost in Information? Returning Wheeler's Honor and Philo-Sophy --- the Love of Wisdom --- to Physics* (2013, FQXi d/1879). The honour-and-wisdom paper. Frames the McGucken programme as a return to the heroic tradition of empirical physics --- Galileo, Newton, Faraday, Maxwell, Planck, Einstein, Bohr, Wheeler, Feynman --- against the post-1973 drift of theoretical physics into untestable speculation.

The present paper completes the formal-mathematical articulation of the programme begun in these five essays. The mathematical apparatus is full Princeton-physics-PhD rigour; the spirit is Wheeler's, and the standard is the heroic age.

P. Woit, *Not Even Wrong: The Failure of String Theory and the Search for Unity in Physical Law* (Basic Books, 2006) [Woit2006]. Senior lecturer in mathematics at Columbia University, Peter Woit's book-length critique of post-1973 foundational physics, with focus on the failure of string theory to make experimental predictions and the postulational status of the standard model's symmetry content. The book argues that the central organising frame --- the standard model's specific symmetry choices remain without explanation, and the post-standard-model programmes (Grand Unification, supersymmetry, string theory) have failed either empirically or predictively --- is the diagnosis the present paper addresses via the Father-Symmetry derivation programme.

P. Woit, *String Theory and the Crisis in Physics* (Robinson's Podcast episode 224, May 2024), interview transcript [WoitPodcast2024]. Full URL: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0HfqRT29Gfs>. Two-hour interview engaging the symmetry critique of [Woit2006] alongside Woit's positive research programme on the geometry of spinors and twistors. Specific transcript timestamps cited in the present paper: 12:56 (representations not understood), 16:00 (group versus representation distinction elided), 28:38 (why U(1) × SU(2) × SU(3)?), 29:25 (symmetries as postulates), 30:42 (Higgs as tuned device), 38:30 (supersymmetry's superpartners-not-seen), 1:50:00 (spinors more fundamental than vectors).

P. Woit, *Euclidean Spinors and Twistor Unification* (2021), arXiv preprint. Cited as [Woit2021]. Woit's positive-programme paper developing a Euclidean twistor formulation of unification, in which the chiral structure of the Standard Model is read off the Euclidean Spin(4) ≅ SU(2)_(L) × SU(2)_(R) decomposition. Within this programme, the selection of SU(2,2) as primary and PT⁺ as physical requires a physical principle that Woit's framework does not internally supply; the McGucken framework, in the previously-developed corpus paper on the Woit--McGucken connection, identifies dx₄/dt = ic as supplying precisely this selection principle.

P. Woit, *Twistor Unification follow-up paper* (2023). Cited as [Woit2023]. The 2023 continuation of [Woit2021], with further development of the Euclidean twistor unification programme. The priority record between [Woit2021], [Woit2023], and the McGucken corpus is documented in the corpus paper on the Woit--McGucken connection (Wheeler-era Princeton → UNC 1998--99 → FQXi 2008--2013 establishes the McGucken priority of dx₄/dt = ic as the foundational physical relation). S. Weinberg, *The Quantum Theory of Fields, Vol. I: Foundations*, Cambridge University Press, 1995. Full URL: <https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/quantum-theory-of-fields/22986119910BF6A2EFE42684801A3BDF>; DOI full URL: <https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139644167>. Chapters 2 and 5 contain the formulation of Weinberg's theorem that consistent low-energy interactions of massless particles of spin 1, 3/2, and 2 are forced respectively to be Yang--Mills gauge theory, supergravity, and general relativity. The argument relies only on Lorentz invariance + unitarity + locality + the soft-emission factor, with the conclusion that the universal coupling of massless spin-2 forces the equivalence principle. The argument is invoked in §13′ of the present paper, paired with the McGucken-Wigner classification of the present §5 to give the derivation: McGucken Principle → Poincaré group → Wigner spin/mass orbits → Weinberg's argument → forced interaction structure (gauge for spin-1, GR for spin-2, supergravity for spin-3/2 if realised).

N. Arkani-Hamed, *Emmy Noether's Influence on Physics* (Lecture, ca. 2018--2023). Full URL: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8yi1H455Fhg>. Lecture at a conference celebrating Emmy Noether. Contains the explicit treatment of Noether's Second Theorem ("the technical content of the theorem is that when you have local symmetries instead of implying conservation laws they imply indeterminacies in the equations of motion... and so the system is uh uh indeterminate and you should instead think of them as redundancies of the description of the assist so that's the sort of key idea the word redundancy here which is something that she very clearly put her finger on" 2:46--3:21), the argument that the redundancy is *forced* on the field-theoretic description of massless spin-1 particles by Lorentz + unitarity + locality (Wigner-classification: stabilizer of null momentum in SO⁺(1,3) is ISO(2) with finite-helicity representations giving 2 polarizations vs. massive 3; physical states are equivalence classes ϵ^(μ) ∼ ϵ^(μ) + αp^(μ), position-space image A_(μ) ∼ A_(μ) + ∂_(μ)α "it's not a symmetry it's a redundancy but the redundancy is forced on us if we try to explain things" 1:09:16), the "morally correct explanations survive conceptual revolutions" epistemic claim ("it's one of the really lovely facts about the most profound statements in physics that they survive essentially entirely unchanged in form even when the conceptual foundation of the field is revolutionarily altered" 23:46--24:50), the Goldstone-bosons-from-spontaneous-symmetry-breaking argument ("whenever you're spontaneous symmetry breaking by exactly this argument you conclude that there must exist an excitation... the conservation law ∂ ⋅ J = 0 is literally the equation of motion is a wave equation for this excitation" 32:46--33:35), the Aharonov--Bohm effect as proof that the vector potential is physically meaningful ("Quantum mechanically we have to if we insist on describing physics in a way that's in a manifest agreement with the principles of locality" 1:00:35--1:00:50), and the Weinberg uniqueness theorem ("if you have any theory of massless spin one particle it must be described by a gauge theory if you have any consistent theory of massless spin two particle it must be described by general relativity... whatever the ultimate laws of nature are at long enough distances low enough energies it must be described by a theory of interacting particles of spin 0, 1/2, 1, 3/2, 2" 1:11:10--1:12:32). Cited in §4′ (Noether's Second Theorem as Bianchi identity), §6′ (gauge symmetry as redundancy), §6′′ (Aharonov--Bohm as empirical confirmation), §13′ (Weinberg-spin-determines-theory paired with McGucken Theorem 59), and §14′ (morally-correct-explanation epistemic standard) of the present paper.

Y. Aharonov and D. Bohm, *Significance of Electromagnetic Potentials in the Quantum Theory*, Physical Review 115 (1959) 485--491. Full URL: <https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.115.485>. The original theoretical paper establishing that the vector potential A_(μ) has direct physical significance independent of the electric and magnetic fields E and B: an electron passing through a region where E = B = 0 but A ≠ 0 (specifically, a region containing the curl of A around an inaccessible solenoid) acquires a measurable phase shift e^(ieΦ/ℏ) where Φ is the magnetic flux through the loop. The effect was experimentally confirmed by R. G. Chambers (1960) and definitively by A. Tonomura et al. (1986) using a superconductive ring to magnetically shield the electron path. The Aharonov--Bohm effect is the canonical empirical proof that the U(1) gauge structure derived in Theorem 36 of the present paper is a physical structure of nature: classical electromagnetism can be formulated using only E and B, but quantum mechanics requires the connection one-form A_(μ) as primary, with the field strength F = dA as derived. Cited in §6′′ of the present paper.
